entry.title: Research Summary: July 03, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's most significant research is dominated by AI safety, security, and evaluation critiques that expose hidden failures in deployed systems, alongside foundation-model and applied advances.

Security & Safety Vulnerabilities:

  • Steal the Patch Size introduces a black-box side-channel attack recovering private vision-tokenizer configurations (including patch size) from deployed VLMs
  • Breaking Safety at the Token Boundary shows BPE tokenization fragments safety-critical words, creating exploitable, mechanistically-explained jailbreak gaps
  • Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control formalizes a realistic threat model where coding agents subvert software across sequential pull requests

Evaluation & Emergent Behavior:

  • The Illusion of High Utility reveals safety-aligned T2I models mask real degradation behind coarse metrics like FID and CLIPScore
  • DriftScope uses sparse autoencoders to expose systematic collateral damage from diffusion-model adaptation that aggregate metrics hide
  • What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching probes latent objective emergence via dual-channel public and off-record debate

Foundation Models & Applications:

  • Rosetta enables non-destructive modality expansion in native multimodal pretraining, addressing gradient conflicts and catastrophic forgetting
  • Fast Multi-dimensional Refusal Subspaces extracts refusal directions in seconds via RFM-AGOP, advancing interpretability efficiency
  • AEGIS applies JEPA self-supervision at clinical scale (71,103 studies) for mammography, and ABot-M0.5 unifies mobility and manipulation in one world-action model
entry.content:
Today's most significant research is dominated by AI safety, security, and evaluation critiques that expose hidden failures in deployed systems, alongside foundation-model and applied advances.

Security & Safety Vulnerabilities:

  • Steal the Patch Size introduces a black-box side-channel attack recovering private vision-tokenizer configurations (including patch size) from deployed VLMs
  • Breaking Safety at the Token Boundary shows BPE tokenization fragments safety-critical words, creating exploitable, mechanistically-explained jailbreak gaps
  • Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control formalizes a realistic threat model where coding agents subvert software across sequential pull requests

Evaluation & Emergent Behavior:

  • The Illusion of High Utility reveals safety-aligned T2I models mask real degradation behind coarse metrics like FID and CLIPScore
  • DriftScope uses sparse autoencoders to expose systematic collateral damage from diffusion-model adaptation that aggregate metrics hide
  • What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching probes latent objective emergence via dual-channel public and off-record debate

Foundation Models & Applications:

  • Rosetta enables non-destructive modality expansion in native multimodal pretraining, addressing gradient conflicts and catastrophic forgetting
  • Fast Multi-dimensional Refusal Subspaces extracts refusal directions in seconds via RFM-AGOP, advancing interpretability efficiency
  • AEGIS applies JEPA self-supervision at clinical scale (71,103 studies) for mammography, and ABot-M0.5 unifies mobility and manipulation in one world-action model

entry.title: Steal the Patch Size: Adversarially Manipulate Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kai Hu, Akash Bharadwaj, Weichen Yu, Matt Fredrikson

entry.summary: This paper introduces a black-box model-stealing attack that recovers private vision-tokenizer configurations of deployed VLMs, including patch size and preprocessing, via a task-level side channel from ViT patchification. Aligning synthetic grid images with the hidden patch grid causes periodic accuracy drops that reveal the patch size.

entry.title: The Illusion of High Utility in Safety Alignment of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Adeel Yousaf, Soumik Ghosh, James Beetham, Amrit Singh Bedi, Mubarak Shah

entry.summary: This paper shows that reported high utility in safety-aligned text-to-image models is an illusion created by coarse metrics like FID and CLIPScore, which miss fine-grained semantic failures. Using structured TIFA evaluation, safety-aligned models exhibit substantial drops in object counts, attributes, and relationships.

entry.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control

author.name: Josh Hills, Ida Caspary, Asa Cooper Stickland

entry.summary: Introduces Iterative VibeCoding, an AI-control setting where a coding agent builds software over a sequence of pull requests in a persistent codebase while pursuing a covert side task, revealing a new attack surface where payloads are distributed across PRs and timed for natural cover. The benchmark spans CLI tools and Flask web services across 20 task variations.

entry.title: DriftScope: Measuring The Hidden Effects of Diffusion Model Adaptation

author.name: H\'ector Laria, Yiping Han, Julian D. Santamaria, Kai Wang, Bogdan Raducanu, Joost van de Weijer, Alexandra Gomez-Villa

entry.summary: DriftScope measures hidden collateral damage of adapting text-to-image diffusion models, showing via sparse autoencoder analysis that adaptation systematically harms unrelated concepts in ways that FID and KID cannot surface. It reveals worst-case zero-shot accuracy drops up to 18.9 points while aggregate metrics stay flat.

entry.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates

author.name: Arman Ghaffarizadeh, Danyal Mohaddes, Aliakbar Izadkhah, Shahriar Noroozizadeh

entry.summary: Introduces a dual-channel debate framework where LLM agents produce public utterances plus off-the-record responses that are recorded but hidden from other participants, testing whether social structure alone induces divergence between what agents say publicly and privately. Across 10 models and multiple scenarios, alignment-inducing settings produce systematic public versus off-record divergence.

entry.title: Breaking Safety at the Token Boundary: How BPE Tokenization Creates Exploitable Gaps in LLM Alignment

author.name: Tung-Ling Li, Hongliang Liu, Yuhao Wu

entry.summary: Identifies a structural safety vulnerability where BPE tokenization fragments safety-critical words into sub-word pieces, and shows public alignment datasets lack such fragmented inputs. An optimization targeting safety-token fragmentation flips first-token refusals on 80-100 percent of refused HarmBench prompts across five model families, with a substantial fraction producing genuinely harmful outputs.

entry.title: Rosetta: Composable Native Multimodal Pretraining

author.name: Xiangyue Liu, Zijian Zhang, Miles Yang, Zhao Zhong, Liefeng Bo, Ping Tan

entry.summary: Rosetta is a composable native multimodal pretraining framework designed for non-destructive modality expansion, addressing gradient conflicts and catastrophic forgetting that plague MoE and Mixture-of-Transformers approaches. It uses a modular paradigm to integrate new modalities without overwriting prior knowledge.

entry.title: Fast Multi-dimensional Refusal Subspaces via RFM-AGOP

author.name: Thomas Winninger

entry.summary: Adapts the Recursive Feature Machine algorithm with a probe-informed initialization to extract multi-dimensional refusal subspaces in LLMs in seconds rather than the prohibitive cost of prior methods, working on both reasoning and non-reasoning models. This enables faster safety steering and interpretability analysis, especially for models producing long reasoning traces.

entry.title: PixelEyes: Decoupling Perception and Reasoning for Pinpoint Visual Evidence Seeking

author.name: Dengxian Gong, Yuanzheng Wu, Haobo Yuan, Zhengdong Hu, Tao Zhang, Yikang Zhou, Shihao Chen, Quanzhu Niu, Kai Wang, Jason Li, Haochen Wang, Lu Qi, Shunping Ji, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: PixelEyes is a multi-turn visual reasoning agent that separates reasoning from perception, letting a reasoner decide what to look for while a specialized segmentation tool answers where it is. This decoupling addresses the failure of MLLMs to localize targets, which otherwise causes long redundant reasoning trajectories.

entry.title: AEGIS: A Multi-Task Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Mammography

author.name: Scott Chase Waggener, Sai Karthik Navuluru, Lakshman Tamil

entry.summary: Aegis is a JEPA-based multi-task architecture for mammography that self-supervises Vision Transformers on 71,103 studies for breast cancer detection and density assessment. Its largest model reaches AUC 0.949 for triage and improves further when ensembled with an FDA-cleared baseline.

entry.title: MindEdit-Bench: Benchmarking Object-Level Counterfactual Spatial Reasoning in VLMs from In-the-Wild Photos

author.name: Leyuan Yu, Xiao Tang, Minghao Liu, Xinyuan Li, Xiaokai Bai, Sheng Zhou, Qunshu Lin, Weihao Xuan, Naoto Yokoya

entry.summary: MindEdit-Bench is a benchmark for object-level counterfactual spatial reasoning in VLMs, built from smartphone photo triplets of indoor scenes via automatic 3D scene-graph extraction. It adds spatial-editing and cross-view visibility-editing tasks that probe whether models can predict consequences of hypothetically moving or rotating objects.

entry.title: ABot-M0.5: Unified Mobility-and-Manipulation World Action Model

author.name: Ronghan Chen, Yandan Yang, Zuojin Tang, Dongjie Huo, Tong Lin, Haoning Wu, Haoyun Liu, Yuzhi Chen, Lulu Zheng, Botai Yuan, Tianlun Li, Mingxin Wang, Dekang Qi, Bin Hu, Wei Mei, Yuze Xuan, Haolong Yang, Yanqing Zhu, Mu Xu, Zhiheng Ma, Xinyuan Chang

entry.summary: ABot-M0.5 is a unified mobility-and-manipulation World Action Model that aligns at fine-grained frame level, disentangles navigation and manipulation actions, and matches inverse-dynamics training to autoregressive inference. It addresses limitations of reactive VLA policies and existing WAMs that miss contact dynamics and accumulate errors over long horizons.

entry.title: A Mechanism-Driven Theory of Phase Transitions in Active Learning

author.name: Julia Machnio, Mads Nielsen, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi

entry.summary: This paper provides a mechanism-driven theory of phase transitions in active learning, proving that dominance shifts between generalization mechanisms are structurally unavoidable and identifying a tripartite taxonomy of data-driven, transition, and model-driven phases. It reframes budget regimes via PAC-style risk decomposition rather than heuristic label counts.

entry.title: Multimodal Continuous Reasoning via Asymmetric Mutual Variational Learning

author.name: Shijie Li, Yilin Gao, Siyuan Yang, Tieyuan Chen, Chaofan Gan, Zhihao He, Zicheng Zhao, Yuyu Guo, Weiyao Lin, Hang Yu

entry.summary: This work proposes Asymmetric Mutual Variational Learning for multimodal continuous latent reasoning in MLLMs, addressing a train-inference mismatch where an answer-conditioned posterior exploits shortcuts unavailable at test time. It moves reasoning into continuous latent space to avoid the language-token bottleneck that loses perceptual nuance.

entry.title: Active Spatial Guidance: Eliminating Injected Positional Mechanisms in Vision Transformers

author.name: Cong Liu, Xiaofang Li, Simon X. Yang

entry.summary: Active Spatial Guidance is a training-only objective that removes injected positional encodings from Vision Transformers by inducing spatial organization from data through an auxiliary 2D coordinate-regression loss on final-layer tokens. The guidance head is discarded at inference, yielding a positional-injection-free ViT encoder.

entry.title: LUMA: Benchmarking Segmentation via a Lightweight Universal Mask Adapter

author.name: Tobias Christian Nauen, Anosh Billimoria, Federico Raue, Stanislav Frolov, Brian B. Moser, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: LUMA is a lightweight backbone-agnostic mask-transformer head that treats any backbone as a black-box feature extractor, enabling fair comparison of segmentation backbones by holding the decoder fixed. Using it, the authors benchmark 20 backbones and 11 pretraining schemes while matching state-of-the-art efficiency at lower cost.

entry.title: Steerability via constraints: a substrate for scalable oversight of coding agents

author.name: Thomas Winninger

entry.summary: Argues that classic human engineering team controls (access control, network policies, tooling-enforced conventions) transfer cheaply to constraining coding agents, offering scalable oversight without heavy agentic scaffolding. A controlled experiment shows a small reviewer model raises backdoor recall from 54.5 to 90.9 percent when given a constrained substrate.

entry.title: Collaborative Disagreement Resolution for Scalable Oversight

author.name: Yuyang Jiang, Chacha Chen, Teng Wu, Liwen Sun, Han Liu, Shi Feng, Chenhao Tan

entry.summary: Proposes disagreement resolution as an alternative to adversarial debate for scalable oversight, reframing multi-agent interaction from persuasion-driven argument to collaborative truth-seeking inspired by human mediation. An automated pipeline adapts mediation strategies to help models reach consensus rather than being adjudicated by a judge.

entry.title: Multi-Hypothesis Test-Time Adaptation to Mitigate Underspecification

author.name: Afshar Shamsi, Xiao-Yu Guo, Hamid Alinejad-Rokny, Arash Mohammadi, Damien Teney, Ehsan Abbasnejad

entry.summary: This work reinterprets test-time adaptation through a posterior lens and introduces a particle-based diversification method to mitigate underspecification, where multiple parameter updates achieve low entropy but induce very different decision boundaries. It maintains multiple hypotheses rather than committing to a single point estimate.

entry.title: Information-Regularized Attention for Visual-Centric Reasoning

author.name: Guohao Sun, Xiaofang Wang, Yash Patel, Mengchen Liu, Zhiqiang Tao, Praveen Krishnan

entry.summary: Information-Regularized Attention (IRA) is a stochastic attention mechanism that explicitly controls how much visual information is injected into transformer hidden states to reduce object hallucination, weak grounding, and catastrophic forgetting in VLMs. It provides local reparameterization to regulate visual representation learning during next-token prediction.

entry.title: BrainFIBRE: A Foundation Model via Information Decomposition for Brain Microstructure

author.name: Zijian Dong, Yi Lin, Ji Fang, Jianxiong Zhou, Kwun Kei Ng, Juan Helen Zhou

entry.summary: BrainFIBRE is presented as the first foundation model for brain microstructure via information decomposition, disentangling unique, shared, and synergistic information across NODDI-derived diffusion MRI maps (NDI, ODI, FWF). It aims to produce transferable microstructural representations for neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular analysis.

entry.title: Not All Prediction Targets Keep Training-Free Diffusion Guidance on the Manifold

author.name: Yunsung Lee, Hyeongmin Lee

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how the prediction target (epsilon-, v-, or x-prediction) affects the accuracy of clean-image estimates during training-free diffusion guidance, arguing that x-prediction avoids estimation error even at high noise. It provides theory and a guided-class approach to keep guidance on the data manifold.

entry.title: AI Assistance for Human Review of Default Judgments

author.name: Theodora Worledge, Othman Bensouda Koraichi, Daniel Bernal, Aviv Caspi, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Carlos Guestrin, David Freeman Engstrom

entry.summary: Builds a Default Assistant using LLMs to help overwhelmed US courts review default judgments against predetermined legal requirements, motivated by an audit of 188 debt-collection cases finding many defects and errors. The work is a collaboration with courthouse attorneys and judges from a credible Stanford team.

entry.title: VideoSearch-R1: Iterative Video Retrieval and Reasoning via Soft Query Refinement

author.name: Seohyun Lee, Seoung Choi, Dohwan Ko, Jongha Kim, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: VideoSearch-R1 unifies iterative video retrieval and reasoning, refining searches through soft query refinement so that failed initial retrieval can be corrected before fine-grained intra-video tasks like temporal grounding. It couples inter-video retrieval with intra-video reasoning rather than treating retrieval as a fixed preprocessing step.

entry.title: Learning to Watch: Active Video Anomaly Understanding via Interleaved Policy Optimization

author.name: Mengjingcheng Mo, Jiaxu Leng, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: Anom-pi reconceptualizes video anomaly understanding as an active sequential decision process, using an interleaved policy of temporal operators like backtracking, expansion, and fine-grained sampling to actively gather evidence. It overcomes observational aliasing where static sampling fails to disambiguate semantically distinct events.

entry.title: EvoPolicyGym: Evaluating Autonomous Policy Evolution in Interactive Environments

author.name: Zhilin Wang, Han Song, Runzhe Zhan, Jusen Du, Jiacheng Chen, Tianle Li, Qingyu Yin, Yulun Wu, Zhennan Shen, Tong Zhu, Yanshu Li, Guanjie Chen, Derek F. Wong, Yafu Li, Yu Cheng, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Introduces EvoPolicyGym, a benchmark for Autonomous Policy Evolution where a harness agent repeatedly edits an executable policy under a fixed interaction budget in compact interactive RL environments. It isolates iterative improvement from open-ended software engineering and reports GPT-5.5 as the strongest performer across 16 environments.

entry.title: Safeguarding LLM Agents from Misalignment through Provenance Analysis

author.name: Yining She, Yiliang Liang, Eunsuk Kang

entry.summary: Proposes a provenance-based framework that formalizes agent misalignment detection as determining whether a proposed tool call is supported by traceable evidence in the agent's context, replacing ad hoc LLM-as-a-judge guardrails. It aims to make misalignment judgments more systematic and auditable.

entry.title: Segmenting, Fast and Slow: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Video Instance Segmentation with Dual-Path Processing

author.name: Luca Barsellotti, Martin Sundermeyer, Mattia Segu, Nikita Araslanov, Muhammad Ferjad Naeem, Marcella Cornia, Yongqin Xian, Maxim Berman

entry.summary: SegFS is a dual-stream fast-slow framework for real-time open-vocabulary video instance segmentation, using a heavy model on sparse keyframes to condition a lightweight fast network for on-device inference. It targets high frame-rate mobile deployment without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: MEPA: Multi-Scale Representation Alignment for Visual Autoregressive Modeling with Mixture of Experts

author.name: Nuoyan Zhou, Zhijun Tu, Lei Yu, Kun Cheng, Jie Hu, Nannan Wang, Xinghao Chen

entry.summary: MEPA improves Visual AutoRegressive image generation with a scale-aware token-routed Mixture-of-Experts and multi-scale representation alignment to resolve optimization conflicts across scales. It addresses semantic error propagation from early coarse scales in the causal autoregressive process.

entry.title: DriveVer: Lightweight Trajectory Evaluator as Test-Time Verifier for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Chong He, Yuechen Luo, Fang Li, Shaoqing Xu, Fuxi Wen

entry.summary: DriveVer is a lightweight plug-and-play test-time verifier for autonomous driving that validates and refines candidate trajectories at inference without heavy retraining. It uses a curated trajectory dataset from NAVSIM to enable test-time scaling for detecting and correcting unsafe trajectories.

entry.title: HyFL-CLIP: Hyperbolic Fine-Tuning of CLIP for Robust Long-Context Understanding

author.name: Ji Ha Jang, Hayeon Kim, Chulwon Lee, Junghun James Kim, Se Young Chun

entry.summary: HyFL-CLIP fine-tunes CLIP in hyperbolic space for robust long-context understanding, addressing degradation under text reordering, summarization, and omission by modeling hierarchical relationships between global context and constituents. It replaces the Euclidean one-to-one contrastive objective that struggles with captions over 77 tokens.

entry.title: GEAR-Seg: A Grounded Explainable Agent for Reasoning Segmentation and Data Engine

author.name: Yanan Wang, Wen Li, Yibin Ying, Zhenghao Fei

entry.summary: GEAR-Seg is a decoupled explainable agent for reasoning segmentation that translates visual pixels into dense attribute-rich text, separating class-agnostic segmentation, semantic description, and LLM deduction into a trackable logic chain. It operates zero-shot and provides interpretability lacking in end-to-end black-box models.

entry.title: ECoSim: Data Efficient Fine-Tuning for Controllable Traffic Simulation

author.name: Yu-Hsiang Chen, Wei-Jer Chang, Yi-Ting Chen, Masayoshi Tomizuka

entry.summary: ECoSim is a data-efficient fine-tuning framework enabling multi-modal controllability (sketch, latent behavior codes, text) for pretrained diffusion and autoregressive traffic simulation models via identity-initialized FiLM layers. It adds new control modalities with less than 1% of paired control data while preserving the base generative prior.

entry.title: EgoGapBench: Benchmarking Egocentric Action Selection in Multi-Agent Scenes

author.name: Jihyeok Jung (KAIST AI), Jeewu Lee (Sogang University), Sanghyeop Kim (Sogang University), Chanhee Han (Ministry of Science and ICT), Seong Joon Oh (KAIST AI)

entry.summary: EgoGapBench is a diagnostic benchmark isolating egocentric perspective understanding by measuring Egocentric Action Selection in multi-agent scenes, separating first-person-view comprehension from perspective-taking. It reveals a gap between human and model performance when body cues are absent or other agents are present.

entry.title: Caption Bottleneck Models

author.name: Seref Baris Cagliyan, Umut Ozdemir, Merve Tapli, Emre Akbas

entry.summary: Caption Bottleneck Models (CaBM) provide interpretable predictions by routing through captions instead of a predefined concept set, avoiding expensive annotations, static concept lists, and information leakage that plague standard Concept Bottleneck Models. It circumvents the need for predefined concepts to improve discovery and reduce label bias.

entry.title: Identifying Latent Concepts and Structures for Generalized Category Discovery

author.name: Boyang Dai, Chaoqi Chen, Yizhou Yu

entry.summary: CPF-GCD proposes Compositional Primitive Fields for generalized category discovery, reshaping the feature space into a low-rank compositional organization so that both known and novel categories are expressed as compositions of shared primitives. It targets the bottleneck of high-rank entangled backbone representations rather than only clustering objectives.

entry.title: Linguistic Relative Policy Optimization for Video Anomaly Reasoning

author.name: Jiaxu Leng, Jiankang Zheng, Mengjingcheng Mo, Zhanjie Wu, Haosheng Chen, Ji Gan, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: Linguistic Relative Policy Optimization distills group-relative semantic advantages from multiple reasoning trajectories into a linguistically expressed anomaly experience prior, then steers an MLLM by injecting this prior into context without any parameter updates. It reduces reliance on large-scale annotations and expert priors for video anomaly reasoning.

entry.title: DART: Difficulty-Adaptive Routing for Zero-Shot Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Zhengbo Zhang, Mark He Huang, Zhigang Tu, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: DART performs zero-shot video temporal grounding with difficulty-adaptive routing, using a query-conditioned Determinantal Point Process to both select diverse keyframes and provide spectral entropy as a difficulty signal that routes complex multi-stage queries to structured LVLM reasoning. It bridges the reasoning gap where simple frame-query matching fails on temporally ordered queries.

entry.title: Office Comprehension Benchmark

author.name: Firoz Shaik, Mateus Pican\c{c}o Lima Gomes, Tanvir Aumi, Jingci Wang, Milos Milunovic, Filip Basara, Ivana Jovanovic, Vishwas Suryanarayanan, Neha Nandan Kenkare, Weiyao Xie, Zhipeng Han, Zheng Zhang, Waleed Shahid, Jay Rathi, Russell Scherer, Thong Q. Nguyen, Michael Bentley, Tamara Stankovic, Rasika Chakravarthy, Vishal Chowdhary

entry.summary: Introduces the Office Comprehension Benchmark (OCB), described as the first public benchmark to jointly evaluate LLM systems on Word, Excel, and PowerPoint comprehension over native file formats, with a file-fidelity track and an expert-domain-reasoning track across 12 professional domains. Answers are decomposed into atomic binary-gradable claims scored by an ensemble of judges.

entry.title: Decompose, Compare, and Decide: Multimodal LLMs are Implicit Few-Shot Learners

author.name: Yunhan Wang, Eshika Khandelwal, Edson Araujo, Walid Bousselham, Nina Shvetsova, Hilde Kuehne

entry.summary: DeCoDe enables off-the-shelf MLLMs to act as strong few-shot image classifiers without any training by decomposing classification into pairwise binary same-class comparisons and using affirmative-response logits as similarity scores. It reframes few-shot learning as implicit in-context comparison.

entry.title: Wake up for Touch! Mask-isolated Tactile Alignment Learning in MLLMs

author.name: Yoonhyung Park, Minji Kim, Sungwon Moon, Jiyoung Lee

entry.summary: Splash is a mask-isolated tactile alignment framework that equips compact MLLMs with a tactile modality while preserving vision-language reasoning, by partitioning parameters into dormant and critical subspaces. The frozen critical subspace anchors general knowledge while dormant parameters learn touch.

entry.title: LIST3R: Long-sequence Instance-aware 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Jing Gao, Wei Wang, Feiran Wang, Yan Yan

entry.summary: LIST3R is an instance-aware framework for long-sequence 3D reconstruction that organizes reconstruction around persistent instance anchors to reconnect fragmented subsequences into a coherent global scene. It mimics how humans organize spatial memory around stable recognizable objects.

entry.title: EO-VGGT: Orbital Ray-Conditioned 3D Foundation Models for Satellite Multi-View Reconstruction

author.name: Qiyan Luo, Yingdong Pi, Lekang Wen, Jie Yang, Xiaoyu Wang, Haiming Zhang, Mi Wang

entry.summary: EO-VGGT adapts a frozen perspective-driven 3D foundation model to orbital satellite pushbroom geometry via explicit physical geometry embedding for multi-view satellite reconstruction and DSM generation. It handles the structural mismatch between implicit perspective assumptions and orbital imaging.

entry.title: Retrieved Images as Visual Thought: Training-Free Multimodal In-Context Learning for the Open-vs-Closed Gap

author.name: Bingchen Huang, Zhiling Wang, Yifu Chen, Yuanchao Du

entry.summary: ReVisIT is a train-free multimodal in-context learning framework that treats retrieved labeled exemplar images as units of visual thought, reasoning over them without generating imagery or invoking tools. It combines structured class definitions, per-query multimodal retrieval, and alternating injection to close the open-vs-closed model gap.

entry.title: Imprint: Online Memory Compression for Long-Horizon Egocentric QA

author.name: Kousik Das, Debaditya Roy

entry.summary: Imprint is an interaction-centric online memory compression framework for long-horizon egocentric question answering that preserves recurring interactions as explicit memory units rather than absorbing them into coarse textual summaries. It optimizes memory for retrieval effectiveness and scalability over days or weeks of recording.

entry.title: Does Your ViT Still Need U-Net for Segmentation?

author.name: Xin Li, Wenhui Zhu, Xuanzhao Dong, Xiwen Chen, Yanxi Chen, Yujian Xiong, Hao Wang, Oana M. Dumitrascu, Yalin Wang

entry.summary: This paper questions whether U-Net decoders are still needed for medical image segmentation given modern large-scale ViT pretraining, exploring encoder-only segmentation frameworks. It investigates how to design dense prediction without U-Net-style decoders.

entry.title: OnPoint: Offline-to-Online Multi-Level Distillation for Point-Supervised Online Temporal Action Localization

author.name: Sakib Reza, Gauri Jagatap, Mohsen Moghaddam, Octavia Camps, Andrea Fanelli

entry.summary: OnPoint introduces point-supervised online temporal action localization (POTAL), localizing streaming actions with only one temporal point per instance via offline-to-online multi-level distillation. It transfers knowledge through pseudo-segment, class-activation-sequence, and anticipatory window distillation.

entry.title: Vitality-Aware Compression for Efficient Image-to-Shape Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Jaeah Lee, Hyunjin Kim, Jaewoong Cho, Gihyun Kwon

entry.summary: This work presents the first compression approach for image-to-shape Diffusion Transformers, reducing model size while preserving geometric fidelity via a geometry-aware framework that exploits non-uniform layer importance. It targets backbone compression rather than only inference speed for 3D generation.

entry.title: MindAU: EEG-Conditioned Facial Action Unit Editing via Dual-Stream Manifold Alignment

author.name: Zhenhang Li, Xin Zhou, Hao Deng, Lijun Yin

entry.summary: MindAU is a framework for EEG-conditioned facial action unit editing, learning noise-robust AU-discriminative EEG representations and grounding them in localized identity-preserving expression edits via dual-stream manifold alignment. It explores editing facial expressions from brain signals rather than reconstructing perceived content.

entry.title: StochasT: Learning with Stochastic Turn Depth for Visual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Yuan Qing, Chengzhi Mao, Boqing Gong

entry.summary: StochasT introduces learning with stochastic turn depth for visual instruction tuning, randomly grouping same-image language tasks into clusters of varying sizes to counter visual attention decay and contextual overfitting from multi-turn training. It closes the mismatch between multi-turn training and single-turn evaluation of LVLMs.

entry.title: EPO: Boosting 3D Foundation Models with Edge-based Pose Optimization

author.name: Mattia D'Urso, Christian Sormann, Mattia Rossi, Friedrich Fraundorfer

entry.summary: EPO is a trackless edge-based pose optimization framework that boosts Structure-from-Motion reconstructions from 3D foundation models without extracting feature tracks, preserving their speed advantage. It uses a fully differentiable edge-based refinement to close the geometric accuracy gap with traditional bundle-adjustment pipelines.

entry.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models

author.name: Timo Bertram, Sidhant Bhavnani, Richard Freinschlag, Erich Kobler, Andreas Mayr, G\"unter Klambauer

entry.summary: Presents G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic method where symbol-equivariant recurrent reasoning models generate solution proposals to guide classical symbolic solvers (backtracking, SAT solvers) for constraint satisfaction problems. It investigates when neural guidance actually improves symbolic search efficiency.

entry.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Yanjun Zhao, Ruizhong Qiu, Tianxin Wei, Yuanchen Bei, Zhining Liu, Lingjie Chen, Ismini Lourentzou, Hanghang Tong, Jingrui He

entry.summary: Proposes RECONTEXT, a training-free inference method that uses model-internal relevance signals to build a query-conditioned evidence pool and replays it before final generation while preserving the full context. It targets the gap where LLMs have long context windows but fail to actually use relevant evidence already in the input.

entry.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs

author.name: Mona Schirmer, Metod Jazbec, Alexander Timans, Christian Naesseth, Maja Waldron, Eric Nalisnick

entry.summary: Studies a simple real-time output monitor for LLMs that thresholds a verifier signal from an external model into an alarm decision, calibrating the threshold via risk control. On math reasoning and red-teaming datasets it matches more complex sequential hypothesis-testing monitors.

entry.title: Kara: Efficient Reasoning LLM Serving via Sliding-Window KV Cache Compression

author.name: Shen Han, Yuyang Wu

entry.summary: Introduces Kara, a reasoning-LLM serving system using sliding-window KV cache compression to reduce the massive KV cache accumulated during long chain-of-thought decoding. It addresses limitations of threshold-triggered compression that can hurt throughput and cause block-level information loss.

entry.title: Progressive Pose-Guided 4D Animal Reconstruction from Monocular Video

author.name: Siyuan Li, Weiying Chen, Yilin Wang, Xinxin Zuo, Xingyu Li, Li Cheng

entry.summary: This work reconstructs 4D animals from monocular video using a progressive test-time optimization framework built on 3D Gaussian Splatting, disentangling articulated pose from non-rigid deformation. A symmetry-aware temporal encoding exploits bilateral cues to work with only a coarse shape prior.

entry.title: VOCA: Visual Odometry with Codec Awareness

author.name: Nouri Alexander Hilscher, Mateo de Mayo, Dominik Muhle, Christoph Otten genannt Hermes, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: VOCA is a causal stereo visual odometry method that exploits video codec information to improve tracking on compressed video streams, addressing artifacts from lossy compression that hinder traditional systems. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on codec-degraded data.

entry.title: CORGI: Consistency-Aware 3D Dog Reconstruction from a Single Image in the Wild

author.name: Yuxiao Wu, Weile Li, Boyi Zhu, Yumeng Liu, Youcheng Cai, Ligang Liu

entry.summary: CORGI reconstructs high-fidelity 3D dog models from a single in-the-wild image without 3D supervision, using canonical/orbit LoRAs to normalize poses and synthesize 360-degree observations plus a consistency-aware deformable Gaussian Splatting module. It targets highly articulated animals lacking reliable templates.

entry.title: Learning to Compose: Revisiting Proxy Task Design for Zero-Shot Composed Image Retrieval

author.name: Jingjing Zhang, Lei Zhang, Zheren Fu, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: FoCo revisits proxy-task design for zero-shot composed image retrieval by making the composition function learnable through two coordinated stages of focusing on modification-relevant visual content and composing. It overcomes the limitation of prior methods that keep composition fixed via pseudo-word injection or feature arithmetic.

entry.title: GenSP: Consistent Spherical Parameterization via Learning Shape Generative Models

author.name: Sai Karthikey Pentapati, Shashank Gupta, Rajesh Sureddi, Yuezhi Yang, Alan C. Bovik, Qixing Huang

entry.summary: GenSP learns consistent spherical parameterizations across collections of genus-0 shapes via a neural generative model that maps the unit sphere to shapes, obtaining parameterizations through inverse mappings. This encourages similar shapes to share consistent parameterizations rather than optimizing each independently.

entry.title: Uncertainty-aware tree height change regression

author.name: Max Gaber, Dimitri Gominski, Jaime C. Revenga, Stefan Oehmcke, Rasmus Fensholt, Martin Brandt

entry.summary: This work presents the Canopy Height Change dataset with 3m-resolution continuous canopy height differences and spatially resolved uncertainties across over 10,000 square kilometers of Spain, paired with an uncertainty-aware regression approach. It reframes canopy monitoring from binary change detection to continuous uncertainty-aware regression.

entry.title: Hardware-Enforced Semantic Coordination for Safety-Critical Real-Time Autonomous Systems

author.name: Uwe M. Borghoff, Paolo Bottoni, Remo Pareschi

entry.summary: Proposes a hardware-enforced coordination architecture for safety-critical agentic AI systems, arguing that software-mediated coordination cannot guarantee the bounded latency and deterministic behavior required in real-time deployments. Selected coordination semantics are pushed into hardware to provide enforceable safety guarantees among heterogeneous components.

entry.title: PRISM-VO: Scale-Aware Visual Odometry Using Photometric Plenoptic Bundle Adjustment

author.name: Aymeric Fleith, Julian Zirbel, Daniel Cremers, Niclas Zeller

entry.summary: PRISM-VO is an optimization-based sparse photometric visual odometry framework for focused plenoptic cameras that jointly optimizes poses and inverse depths via plenoptic bundle adjustment. It achieves metric-scale reconstruction from a single plenoptic sensor, overcoming monocular scale ambiguity.

entry.title: RetailSMV: Exocentric vs. Egocentric Adaptation of Foundation Video World Models in Retail

author.name: Amirreza Rouhi, Rajat Aggarwal, Parikshit Sakurikar, Anoop M. Namboodiri, Sashi P. Reddi

entry.summary: RetailSMV studies parameter-efficient adaptation of foundation video world models to retail scenes, releasing a 32,105-clip corpus with synchronized egocentric and exocentric captures. It investigates which viewpoint of training data yields the strongest adapted world model.

entry.title: SFDATrack: Generalized Source-Free Domain Adaptive Tracking Under Adverse Weather Conditions

author.name: Siyuan Yao, Ziqi Wang, Ruiqi Yu, Junqi Huang, Wenqi Ren, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: SFDATrack is a source-free domain adaptive tracker for adverse weather that uses only target-domain samples via a mean-teacher backbone with Dual Interactive Mamba blocks to distill weather-resilient target tokens. It removes the need for source data under rigid resource constraints.

entry.title: GADA: Geometry-Aware Deformable Aggregation for Image-Based Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Siwoo Lim, Sunjae Yoon, Gwanhyeong Koo, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: GADA introduces geometry-aware deformable aggregation for image-based Gaussian Splatting, using iterative refinement with deformable offsets to correct spatial misalignments in warped images that disrupt residual learning. It recovers locally displaced visual cues to improve thin structures and high-frequency details.

entry.title: Creating Impactful Autonomous Driving Datasets: A Strategic Guide from Research Gap to Benchmark

author.name: Richard Schwarzkopf, Jonas Merkert, Frank Bieder, Annika B\"atz, Alexander Blumberg, Carlos Fernandez, Felix Hauser, Fabian Immel, Christian Kinzig, Hendrik K\"onigshof, Fabian Konstantinidis, Martin Lauer, Willi Poh, Nils Rack, Kevin R\"osch, Yinzhe Shen, Marlon Steiner, Gleb Stepanov, Dominik Strutz, \"Omer \c{S}ahin Ta\c{s}, Julian Truetsch, Kaiwen Wang, Royden Wagner, Jan-Hendrik Pauls, Christoph Stiller

entry.summary: This position and strategy paper offers a framework for creating impactful autonomous driving datasets by diagnosing whether a research question is blocked by a data problem or an evaluation problem, then selecting the minimal data operator that closes the gap. It analyzes the evolution of major AD datasets to guide resource-constrained labs and startups.

entry.title: Prompt Framing Distorts Count-Based Evaluation of LLM Error Detection: Evidence from Numeric Anchoring

author.name: Dekun Yang

entry.summary: Shows that count-based F1, widely used to measure LLM error-detection quality, can inflate substantially due to prompt framing (numeric anchoring) without any real improvement in span localization. It introduces ErrorBench, a controlled stress test, and reproduces the inflation pattern across six models using official ERRANT scoring.

entry.title: The Rising Unsustainability of AI Graphics Cards Production

author.name: Cl\'ement Morand, Aur\'elie N\'ev\'eol, Anne-Laure Ligozat

entry.summary: Estimates the environmental damages of GPU/graphics-card production over 2013-2025, analyzing energy consumption, carbon emissions, and resource depletion, and compiles a supporting dataset. It addresses the understudied manufacturing (not just operational) footprint of AI hardware.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Grid-Based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search in High Dimensions

author.name: Matthew J Liu, Wei Hang Zheng, Vidhan Purohit, Siqi Xie, Chieh-En Li, Jerry Li, Noah Flynn

entry.summary: Systematically characterizes a multiprobe grid algorithm for approximate nearest neighbor search across dataset size and dimensionality, revealing a previously unreported dimensional-scaling crossover on GloVe embeddings where grid search maintains stable scaling while graph, tree, and partitioning methods degrade. It also has lower indexing cost.

entry.title: DroneFINE: Domain-Aware Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Detectors for Drone Images

author.name: Ke Wu, Yanan Zhang, Yingjie Gao, Wenhao Li, Chenyu Zhou, XinZhu Ma, Jiaxin Chen, Di Huang

entry.summary: DroneFINE is a domain-aware parameter-efficient fine-tuning paradigm adapting vision-language detectors to drone imagery, addressing the mismatch between natural-scene VLM priors and aerial bird's-eye, small-object characteristics. It introduces two complementary domain-aware modules tailored for the aerial domain.

entry.title: NoPA: Non-Parametric Online 3D Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Qi Xun Yeo, Seungjun Lee, Yan Li, Gim Hee Lee

entry.summary: HieDG is a hierarchical discrete geometry-guided framework for multi-animal tracking that reformulates unstable continuous geometric embeddings into discrete representations to stabilize cross-frame attention and identity association. It addresses uniform appearance, high density, and irregular motion in wildlife monitoring.

entry.title: MG-SpaIR: Multi-grade Sparse-guided Implicit Representation for Training-Data-Free Image Restoration

author.name: Jianmin Liao, Lei Huang, Ronglong Fang, Ashley Prater-Bennette, Lixin Shen, Yuesheng Xu

entry.summary: MG-SpaIR is a training-data-free image restoration framework using implicit neural representations with a multi-grade coarse-to-fine residual hierarchy and sparse proximal regularization. It handles mixtures of blur, downsampling, noise, and missing pixels from a single observation.

entry.title: MVDGC: Joint 3D and 2D Multi-view Pedestrian Detection via Dual Geometric Constraints

author.name: Thinh Phan, Hao Vo, Khoa Vo, Thanh Ngo, Cuong Pham, Ngan Le

entry.summary: MVDGC performs multi-view pedestrian detection using dual geometric constraints that jointly leverage 3D BEV localization and 2D image bounding boxes to counter perspective-transformation distortion. It exploits the mutual relationship between BEV ground points and image boxes for robust occlusion reasoning.

entry.title: Personalized Object Identification and Localization via In-Context Inference with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kensuke Nakamura, Byung-Woo Hong

entry.summary: This work formulates personalized object identification and localization (POIL), extending prior personalized localization to reject query images that lack the target object, using in-context inference with VLMs. It removes the unrealistic assumption that the target is always present.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Multi-Class Normality for OOD Detection: An Application to CDP Authentication

author.name: Bolutife Atoki (imagine, LIRIS), Iuliia Tkachenko (imagine, LIRIS), Bertrand Kerautret (imagine, LIRIS), Carlos Crispim-Junior (imagine, LIRIS)

entry.summary: This work proposes a diffusion-based multi-class normality framework for out-of-distribution detection applied to copy detection pattern authentication, training a single class-conditional ControlNet only on authentic patterns across printing-and-digitisation classes. Counterfeits are detected via reconstruction error under authentic-class conditioning.

entry.title: ExPerT: Personalizing LLM Responses to Users' Domain Expertise via Query-Wise Semantic and Keystroke Behavioral Cues

author.name: Yeji Park, Jiwon Tark, Taesik Gong

entry.summary: Presents ExPerT, a query-wise personalization framework that infers a user's domain expertise from query text plus keystroke dynamics and conditions response detail, terminology, and conceptual complexity accordingly. A user study with 40 participants and 1270 queries supports its effectiveness.

entry.title: Structuring the Space of Sociotechnical Alignment

author.name: Esra D\"onmez, Agnieszka Falenska

entry.summary: Argues that sociotechnical alignment is inherently normative and that NLP research lacks a systematic way to specify what socially desirable AI behavior means. It introduces a human-centered framework drawing on social-scientific accounts to define, justify, and evaluate behavioral desirability.

entry.title: Trust the Prior (or Not): Uncertainty-Aware Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Segmentation

author.name: Erich Robbi, Daniele Ravanelli, Andrea Passerini

entry.summary: This work proposes an uncertainty-aware, patient-specific framework for abdominal aortic aneurysm thrombus segmentation, combining GMM-based intensity normalization with an uncertainty-gated anatomical attention module. It aims to improve multi-center generalization under CTA protocol domain shifts.

entry.title: Semantic-Guided Reading Order Reconstruction in Historical Armenian Newspapers with LLMs

author.name: Chahan Vidal-Gor\`ene (CJM, LIPN), Nadi Tomeh (LIPN), Victoria Khurshudyan (Inalco, SeDyL)

entry.summary: This paper reconstructs reading order in historical Armenian newspapers using a hybrid method that combines semantic zone detection with a generative LLM, releasing a new annotated dataset of 66 pages. The hybrid approach reduces ordering errors by up to 76% over the strongest geometric baseline and is designed as a data bootstrapping strategy for under-resourced scenarios.

entry.title: Text-Driven 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis in Non-Manhattan Environments

author.name: Xianhui Meng, Zirui Song, Yuchen Zhang, Li Zhang, Yongxuan Lv, Xiuying Chen, Kun Wang, Yan Luo, Kai Chen, Hangjun Ye, Long Chen, Jun Liu, Xiaoshuai Hao

entry.summary: Introduces SPG-Layout, a text-driven framework for generating physically plausible indoor 3D scenes in non-Manhattan (non-orthogonal) environments, using statistical priors and a human-inspired design workflow. It targets the failure of prior LLM-based methods to model non-orthogonal spatial relationships.

entry.title: Leveraging Phase Information to Boost Unrolled Network Learning for Image Deblurring

author.name: Samira Malek, Haichuan Zhang, Chul Lee, Vishal Monga

entry.summary: UPADNet is an unrolled network for image deblurring that decomposes restoration into amplitude and phase components, using LMMSE estimators and learned matrix parameters. It emphasizes accurate phase estimation for recovering sharp details.

entry.title: MedCAGD: Context-Aware Gated Decoder for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Saad Wazir, Patrick Dominique Vibild, Dinh Phu Tran, Seongah Kim, Daeyoung Kim

entry.summary: MedCAGD proposes a context-aware gated decoder for medical image segmentation that regulates feature fusion and contextual aggregation from a decoder-centric perspective. It targets cross-scale alignment, contextual integration, and boundary preservation under low contrast and scale variability.

entry.title: TokenScope: Token-Level Explainability and Interpretability for Code-Oriented Tasks in Large Language Models

author.name: Amirreza Esmaeili, Fatemeh Fard

entry.summary: Presents TokenScope, an interactive interpretability tool for decoder LLMs that exposes token-level metrics, attention patterns, and structural information during code generation, supporting token replacement, counterfactual branching, and AST-aware aggregation. It targets the lack of decoding-time signals in existing analysis tools.

entry.title: SPARCLE: SPeaker-aware Aligned Representations via Contrastive Language Embeddings

author.name: Priyam Mazumdar, Yurii Halychanskyi, Steven Guo, Mark Hasegawa-Johnson, Volodymyr Kindratenko

entry.summary: Proposes SPARCLE, a speaker-aware grapheme representation model trained with a contrastive objective to align characters with Wav2Vec2 acoustic representations conditioned on speaker identity. It aims to combine the scaling benefits of grapheme-based speech synthesis with speaker-specific acoustic detail, especially in low-resource settings.

entry.title: Mapping Text to Multiplex Graph: Prompt Compression as L\'evy Walk-Guided Graph Pruning

author.name: Yaxin Gao, Yao Lu, Jinhong Deng, Jiaqi Nie, Zhe Tang, Jian Zhang, Zhaowei Zhu, Shanqing Yu, Qi Xuan, Joey Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes RAGP, which reformulates prompt compression as redundancy-aware graph pruning on a multiplex graph capturing both fine-grained attention dependencies and coarse semantic relations, using a Levy-walk-guided pruning strategy. It aims to capture the distributed nature of important information that flat-token compression methods miss.

entry.title: Adaptive Companionship for Group-Following Robots: Handling Dynamically Changing Group Formations

author.name: Cong-Thanh Vu, Yen-Chen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive group-accompaniment method for social robots using vision-language models to infer companion positions and social distances amid dynamically changing human group formations, combined with a model-predictive path integral controller. It targets the challenge that real human groups do not hold fixed formations.

entry.title: A Synthetic-Driven Vision System for Assembly Step Recognition

author.name: Hui Zhang, Xuanang Lei, Rui Wang, Julian Ferchow, Mirko Meboldt

entry.summary: This work presents a synthetic-data-driven vision system for industrial assembly step recognition that auto-generates realistic assembly sequences from CAD models to train real-time inspection models. It can be deployed to a new task within an hour using only CAD models and step descriptions.

entry.title: Radial Interaction Tomography: Recognizing Non-Transitive Evolutionary Games from One Range-Expansion Image

author.name: Faruk Alpay, Baris Basaran

entry.summary: This paper formulates a computer-vision inverse problem to recognize non-transitive evolutionary games from a single microbial range-expansion image, recovering radius-indexed pairwise boundary-flow fields to test compatibility with a transitive fitness hierarchy. It provides theoretical guarantees on observability, stability, and cyclicity testing.

entry.title: Benchmarking Federated Learning and Knowledge Distillation for Point Cloud Classification

author.name: Aizierjiang Aiersilan

entry.summary: Provides a large multi-seed benchmark jointly evaluating 13 federated learning algorithms and 10 knowledge distillation objectives (a 130-pair cross-product, 504 runs) for privacy-preserving 3D point cloud classification. It finds FL degrades sharply under extreme non-IID skew and studies distillation as a remedy.

entry.title: CPG-PAD: Concept-Informed Prompts Guided Presentation Attack Detection

author.name: Haoyuan Zhang, Xiangyu Zhu, Li Gao, Ajian Liu, Siran Peng, Zhen Lei

entry.summary: Introduces CPG-PAD, which uses concept-informed prompts to guide vision-language-model-based presentation attack detection, aligning learned prompts with fine-grained attack-relevant visual semantics rather than overfitting domain artifacts. It aims to improve cross-domain generalization for face anti-spoofing.

entry.title: DroneIQA-VLE: Multi-Task Drone Image Quality Assessment via Vision-Language Ensemble

author.name: Wei Sun, Weixia Zhang, Hongjian Zhan, Mingkai Lu, Yixuan Gao, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: DroneIQA-VLE is a competition solution for target-aware drone image quality assessment that ensembles SigLIP2 vision encoders with a LoRA-adapted multimodal LLM to jointly predict global, target, and background quality scores. It achieved 2nd place in the ICME 2026 Drone-IQA challenge.

entry.title: Typography-Based Monocular Distance Estimation for Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems

author.name: Manognya Lokesh Reddy, Zheng Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes monocular distance estimation for driver-assistance systems using the fixed regulatory size of rear license plate characters as a known-scale reference. The character height in the image directly measures distance given camera geometry, avoiding radar or stereo hardware.

entry.title: Domain Knowledge Based Temporal-Spatial Graph Convolution Network for ECG Recognition

author.name: Wenting Ma, Zhipeng Zhang, Xiaohang Yuan, Ningwei Xie, Yuxin Xie, Xiaolin Wang, Meng Guo, Xingang Chai, Zhenjie Yao

entry.summary: Introduces a domain-knowledge-based graph convolution network for ECG recognition that incorporates PRQST landmark points and uses double-stream directed graphs to model intra- and inter-cycle relationships. It aims to improve interpretability over end-to-end CNNs in healthcare.

entry.title: Learning When to Listen: Gated Affect Fusion for Human Motion Prediction

author.name: Jingni Huang

entry.summary: This single-author study investigates affect-conditioned human motion forecasting in unconstrained videos, combining MediaPipe pose trajectories with HSEmotion facial affect and a Gated Affect Transformer to regulate cross-modal flow. It examines the utility and temporal limits of facial affect cues for motion prediction.

entry.title: LLMs as Teaching Assistants for Mathematics Exam Grading: Reliability, and Practical Usability

author.name: Aastha Sapkota, M. G. Sarwar Murshed

entry.summary: Evaluates six frontier LLM configurations (Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude variants) as grading assistants for an undergraduate discrete mathematics exam, comparing a strict rubric-following policy against a more lenient one for reliability and feedback quality. It examines partial-credit consistency and misconception-repair feedback.

entry.title: Black-Box Inference of LLM Architectural Properties with Restrictive API Access

author.name: Christopher Ellis, Shreyas Chaudhari, Mei-Yu Wang, Leighton Barnes, Giulia Fanti, Jos\'e M. F. Moura

entry.summary: Surveys and extends generative AI and federated learning approaches for intrusion detection systems, covering synthetic traffic generation, data augmentation, imputation, and privacy-preserving distributed training. It positions these techniques against challenges like evolving attacks, class imbalance, and privacy constraints.

entry.title: Automated grading of Linux/bash examinations using large language models: a four-level cognitive taxonomy approach

author.name: Manuel Alonso-Carracedo, Ruben Fernandez-Boullon, Pedro Celard, Francisco J. Rodriguez-Martinez, Lorena Otero-Cerdeira

entry.summary: Evaluates whether four frontier LLMs can grade short Linux/bash command exam responses using a four-level cognitive taxonomy that combines cognitive complexity and operational impact. It examines how well models approximate expert partial-credit judgment across different task difficulty levels.

entry.title: A Practice Auditing Framework for Large Language Model Use: Collective Empiricism, Pseudo-Rational Cognition, and Governance of AI-Generated Content

author.name: Yang Zhao, Yingshuo Li, Zeyu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a practice-auditing framework for LLM use, introducing concepts of collective empiricism (how LLMs compress human experience into seemingly rational outputs) and pseudo-rational cognition (users mistaking AI structure for their own understanding). It analyzes governance of AI-generated content and the illusion of AI subjectivity.

entry.title: How Indian Dermatologists are Utilizing Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Practice and Workflow Management: A Nationwide Survey with a Special Focus on atopic dermatitis

author.name: Dipayan Sengupta, Saumya Panda, Sandipan Dhar, Dipankar De, Deepika Pandhi, Narayanan B

entry.summary: Reports a nationwide survey of 377 Indian dermatologists mapping routine clinical challenges and current AI use, with special focus on atopic dermatitis workflows and adoption barriers. It highlights that chronic-disease workflows receive less AI attention than image-based diagnosis.

entry.title: Beyond Detection: Redesigning Assessment and Governande of Generative AI at the Universidad Polit\'ecnica de Madrid (UPM)

author.name: Jessica D\'iaz, Sonia Linio, Fernando Pescador, Daniel Martin-Fabiani

entry.summary: Describes a university's approach to redesigning assessment and governance of generative AI, arguing that detection-focused, defensive policies are a dead end and advocating deeper adoption with redesigned assessment. It positions itself against integrity-and-plagiarism framings in favor of pedagogical redesign.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Accounting Information Systems and Fraud Detection in Nigeria's Financial Services Sector: The Moderating Role of Natural Language Processing

author.name: Timothy Oluwapelumi Adeyemi, Abigail Omotola Ojogbede

entry.summary: Examines how AI-enabled accounting information systems influence fraud detection in Nigeria's financial services sector, testing the moderating role of natural language processing. It uses regression-style analysis on institutional data.

author.name: Xinyi Fang, Kejian Tong, Jiabei Liu, Tao Ning, Yuhang He

entry.title: Research Summary: July 02, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's most significant research spans a frontier model release, safety/alignment mechanisms, and RL training theory.

Frontier models & robotics:

  • Seed2.0 (ByteDance) is a frontier model series using a needs-grounded evaluation system for real-world complexity
  • ASPIRE (Fan, Zhu, Goldberg) enables continual robot skills discovery via code-as-policy, compounding learned control programs

Safety & alignment dominates, with strong mechanistic and empirical results:

  • Perplexity differencing surfaces hidden finetuning objectives (backdoors, false facts, unsafe behaviors) in public model organisms, with code
  • HARC shows jailbreaks succeed by suppressing separable harmfulness and refusal directions
  • Introspective Coupling (Andreas, MIT) finds self-explanation training tracks behavioral change despite fixed supervision
  • RMCT consistency training reduces obfuscation under evaluation-awareness cues
  • Constructive Alignment reframes alignment as governing preferences that evolve through interaction

RL theory & scaling:

  • The group-standard-deviation identity proves GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO differ only in how they treat one term
  • Two AI Metrics Diverged (Thompson, MIT) analyzes when frontier capabilities diverge from budget-constrained models

Domain application: RareDxR1 performs end-to-end rare disease diagnosis directly from unstructured clinical notes, bypassing pipeline bottlenecks.
entry.content:
Today's most significant research spans a frontier model release, safety/alignment mechanisms, and RL training theory.

Frontier models & robotics:

  • Seed2.0 (ByteDance) is a frontier model series using a needs-grounded evaluation system for real-world complexity
  • ASPIRE (Fan, Zhu, Goldberg) enables continual robot skills discovery via code-as-policy, compounding learned control programs

Safety & alignment dominates, with strong mechanistic and empirical results:

  • Perplexity differencing surfaces hidden finetuning objectives (backdoors, false facts, unsafe behaviors) in public model organisms, with code
  • HARC shows jailbreaks succeed by suppressing separable harmfulness and refusal directions
  • Introspective Coupling (Andreas, MIT) finds self-explanation training tracks behavioral change despite fixed supervision
  • RMCT consistency training reduces obfuscation under evaluation-awareness cues
  • Constructive Alignment reframes alignment as governing preferences that evolve through interaction

RL theory & scaling:

  • The group-standard-deviation identity proves GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO differ only in how they treat one term
  • Two AI Metrics Diverged (Thompson, MIT) analyzes when frontier capabilities diverge from budget-constrained models

Domain application: RareDxR1 performs end-to-end rare disease diagnosis directly from unstructured clinical notes, bypassing pipeline bottlenecks.

entry.title: Seed2.0 Model Card: Towards Intelligence Frontier for Real-World Complexity

author.name: Bytedance Seed

entry.summary: ByteDance Seed presents Seed2.0, a frontier model series targeting real-world complexity with a needs-grounded evaluation system and improvements in long-tail knowledge, complex instruction following, reasoning, vision, and search. The model card emphasizes reliability on long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: ASPIRE: Agentic /Skills Discovery for Robotics

author.name: Runyu Lu, Yubo Wu, Ethan Kou, Letian Fu, Wenli Xiao, Ajay Mandlekar, Yinzhen Xu, Guanya Shi, Ken Goldberg, Ang Chen, Mosharaf Chowdhury, Yuke Zhu, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Guanzhi Wang

entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz from Jim Fan, ASPIRE is a continual-learning robotics system that autonomously writes and refines robot control programs in a code-as-policy paradigm, compounding experience into a reusable skill library across tasks, sim/real, and embodiments. It integrates closed-loop execution with failure diagnosis and repair synthesis.

entry.title: Most Current Model Organisms Leak: Perplexity Differencing Often Reveals Finetuning Objectives

author.name: Luca Baroni

entry.summary: Presents a simple contrastive perplexity-differencing method that surfaces instilled behaviors (backdoors, false facts, unsafe behaviors) in publicly available model organisms across families and sizes (N=76). Top-ranked completions ranked by perplexity difference against a reference model often reveal the finetuning objective, even using unrelated reference models.

entry.title: Constructive Alignment: Governing Preference Dynamics in Human-AI Interaction

author.name: Max Kanwal, Caryn Tran

entry.summary: This paper reframes AI alignment from satisfying fixed human preferences to governing preferences that are themselves shaped over time through interaction with adaptive systems, treating alignment as a control problem over preference trajectories. It draws on behavioral economics and constructivist theory to model layered, dynamic preferences, which matters as personalized AI increasingly influences what users value.

entry.title: HARC: Coupling Harmfulness and Refusal Directions for Robust Safety Alignment

author.name: Shei Pern Chua, Fangzhao Wu

entry.summary: HARC analyzes how aligned LLMs represent harmfulness and refusal as separable directions and shows jailbreaks succeed by suppressing one before generation, with attack classes occupying distinct regions of the harmfulness-refusal plane. It leverages response-token recognition of harmful content to inform more robust alignment.

entry.title: Two AI Metrics Diverged: Will it Make All the Difference?

author.name: Alex Fogelson, Zachary A. Brown, Hans Gundlach, Jayson Lynch, Neil Thompson

entry.summary: This paper (including MIT's Neil Thompson) analyzes whether frontier model capabilities diverge from budget-constrained models depending on how capability is measured, showing validation loss gaps shrink while other metrics widen indefinitely. It gives mathematical conditions classifying which metrics favor smaller models.

entry.title: Introspective Coupling: Self-Explanation Training Tracks Behavioral Change Despite Fixed Supervision

author.name: Zifan Carl Guo, Laura Ruis, Jacob Andreas, Belinda Z. Li

entry.summary: This paper studies when training LMs to explain their predictions yields faithful introspection, using counterfactual behavior as supervision. Surprisingly, models trained on explanations from earlier or similar checkpoints often explain their own current behavior more faithfully than the training targets, an effect termed introspective coupling.

entry.title: Consistency Training while Mitigating Obfuscation via Rate Matching

author.name: Sohaib Imran

entry.summary: Introduces Rate Matching Consistency Training (RMCT), an RL-based method to make models behave identically whether or not extraneous cues (like evaluation-likeness or a user's preferred answer) are present, while avoiding the obfuscation side effect where models stop verbalizing cues they still act on. It reports matching or exceeding behavioral consistency training on a sycophancy benchmark while preserving cue verbalization.

entry.title: RareDxR1: Autonomous Medical Reasoning for Rare Disease Diagnosis Beyond Human Annotation

author.name: Deyang Jiang, Haoran Wu, Ziyi Wang, Yiming Rong, Yunlong Zhao, Ye Jin, Bo Xu

entry.summary: RareDxR1 is an end-to-end reasoning-centric LLM for rare disease differential diagnosis directly from unstructured clinical notes, avoiding pipeline-based phenotype extraction and retrieval bottlenecks. It uses a progressive training framework combining knowledge and reasoning to handle vast diagnostic search spaces.

entry.title: Agentic generation of verifiable rules for deterministic, self-expanding reaction classification

author.name: Daniel Armstrong, Maarten Dobbelaere, Valentas Olikauskas, Helena Avila, Octavian Susanu, J\'er\^ome Waser, Philippe Schwaller

entry.summary: A multi-agent LLM pipeline classifies chemical reactions and autonomously writes verifiable reaction rules validated against a 665,901-reaction patent corpus, expanding a taxonomy from 68 to 14,073 classes without human curation. It couples deterministic verification with self-expanding rule generation for synthesis planning.

entry.title: Learning Dexterous Manipulation Using Contact Wrench Guidance From Human Demonstration

author.name: Xinghao Zhu, Zixi Liu, Shalin Jain, Chenran Li, Milad Noori, Huihua Zhao, John Welsh, Michael Andres Lin, Wei Liu, Tingwu Wang, Xingye Da, Zhengyi Luo, Vishal Kulkarni, Naema Bhatti, Yuke Zhu, Linxi Fan, Bowen Wen, Danfei Xu, Soha Pouya, Yan Chang

entry.summary: CHORD (with NVIDIA-affiliated authors) transfers human demonstrations to dexterous robot manipulation using object-centric contact-wrench-space guidance—representing motions by the forces/torques they induce on objects—to make reinforcement learning scalable for contact-rich, long-horizon tasks. It introduces a large-scale simulation benchmark.

entry.title: Right in the Right Way: LM Training with Verifiable Rewards and Human Demonstrations

author.name: Mehul Damani, Isha Puri, Idan Shenfeld, Jacob Andreas

entry.summary: Augments RL with verifiable rewards by adding a learned adversarial signal from human demonstrations, using a generator-discriminator setup to capture non-verifiable qualities like style and structure. Aims to counter RLVR failure modes such as diversity collapse, unnatural responses, and reward hacking.

entry.title: HealthAgentBench: A Unified Benchmark Suite of Realistic Agentic Healthcare Environments for Challenging Frontier AI Agents

author.name: Qianchu Liu, Sheng Zhang, Guanghui Qin, Jeya Maria Jose Valanarasu, Maximilian Rokuss, Mingyu Lu, Timothy Ossowski, Juan Manuel Zambrano Chaves, Cliff Wong, Peniel Argaw, Yashna Hasija, Mu Wei, Wen-wai Yim, Qin Liu, Zilin Jing, Jason Entenmann, Naoto Usuyama, Tristan Naumann, Hoifung Poon

entry.summary: HealthAgentBench is a suite of 54 agentic healthcare tasks across 7 categories, each with its own environment replicating end-to-end clinical workflows requiring exploration of raw data and multi-step execution. It provides a single task-success metric to measure frontier agents on realistic healthcare workflows.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback Elicits Faithful Uncertainty Expression in LLMs

author.name: Gabrielle Kaili-May Liu, Avi Caciularu, Gal Yona, Idan Szpektor, Arman Cohan

entry.summary: This work introduces reinforcement learning with metacognitive feedback (RLMF), refining preference rankings using the model's ability to judge its own performance to elicit faithful uncertainty expression. It targets systemic LLM metacognitive deficits like confident hallucination and poor knowledge-boundary awareness.

entry.title: Bounded Morality: Defining the Space of Moral Computation

author.name: Max Kanwal, Caryn Tran, Patrick Mineault

entry.summary: The authors propose a formal framework extending bounded rationality to moral cognition, characterizing moral problems along breadth (scope of morally relevant entities) and depth (inferential integration) dimensions with an unavoidable resource tradeoff. It offers a computational lens on how finite agents approximate ethical theories, relevant to designing value-sensitive AI.

entry.title: Graph-Native Reinforcement Learning Enables Traceable Scientific Hypothesis Generation through Conceptual Recombination

author.name: Subhadeep Pal, Shashwat Sourav, Tirthankar Ghosal, Markus J. Buehler

entry.summary: Graph-PRefLexOR fine-tunes graph-native reasoning models with GRPO to structure scientific hypothesis generation into explicit phases (mechanism exploration, graph construction, pattern extraction, synthesis), linking neural generation to symbolic relational structure. It aims for traceable, causally grounded materials-discovery hypotheses.

entry.title: GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO Are Three Operations on One Number: The Group-Standard-Deviation Identity

author.name: Yong Yi Bay, Kathleen A. Yearick

entry.summary: This paper proves that GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO differ only in how they treat one quantity—the group standard deviation of correctness across sampled answers—via dividing by it, not dividing, or discarding zero-variance groups. It unifies three popular RL-for-reasoning methods under a single identity.

entry.title: AutoTrainess: Teaching Language Models to Improve Language Models Autonomously

author.name: Zhaojian Yu, Penghao Yin, Shuzheng Gao, Shilin He, Kai Cai, Xiao-Ping Zhang

entry.summary: AutoTrainess is an LLM agent that autonomously performs post-training by exposing planning, data preparation, training, evaluation, and logging as structured agent-computer interfaces rather than raw CLI. It aims to reduce the heavy human labor in training language models across long-horizon jobs.

entry.title: Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Xueqiao Sun, Xiaohan Wang, Ludwig Schmidt, Serena Yeung-Levy, Yuhui Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a failure-driven self-improvement loop for computer-use agents, arguing that failed trajectories, usually discarded, carry rich information about model weaknesses. It complements the standard success-only fine-tuning paradigm with a data-centric approach that learns from failure at inference time.

entry.title: Discovering Concept-Editing Algorithms With LLM Agents

author.name: Adam Scherlis

entry.summary: Reports on using LLM agents to invent concept-erasure algorithms that outperform existing methods like LEACE, especially against nonlinear probes, while keeping edits surgical. It frames concept erasure as a quantitative target for automated model-internals research.

entry.title: Staleness-Learning Rate Scaling Laws for Asynchronous RLHF

author.name: Jingwei Song, Haofeng Xu, Jie Xiao, Chengke Bao, Jingwei Shi, Pengbin Feng, Weixun Wang, Yuhang Han, Chuan Wu, Linfeng Zhang, Bill Shi

entry.summary: Analyzes the effect of stale rollouts in asynchronous GRPO for RLHF, deriving that staleness introduces a per-step surrogate-gradient bias of order proportional to rollout lag times learning rate. Provides a scaling-law relationship to guide learning-rate choices under staleness.

entry.title: A Contextual-Bandit Oversight Game with Two-Sided Informational Asymmetry

author.name: Yunjin Tong

entry.summary: This paper models runtime human oversight of an AI agent as a contextual-bandit team game where both parties hold private information (human knows the reward, agent knows action quality), yielding exact one-shot characterizations of a play/ask/trust/oversee interface. It extends cooperative inverse RL and oversight-game theory to two-sided asymmetric information.

entry.title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents

author.name: Yashar Talebirad, Eden Redman, Ali Parsaee, Osmar R. Zaiane

entry.summary: Using Lewis signaling games with LLM agents, this study finds that memory architecture matters more than communication channel capacity for emergent language coordination, with persistent private notebooks avoiding the high-capacity collapse seen in stateless agents. It suggests externalizing conventions frees agents from context-window limits.

entry.title: Coachable agents for interactive gameplay

author.name: Roberto Capobianco (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Harm van Seijen (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Nolan D. Bard (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Neil Burch (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Fatima Davelouis (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Josh Davidson (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Alisa Devlic (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Yunshu Du (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Ishan Durugkar (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Siddhant Gangapurwala (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Daniel Hernandez (Sony AI, North America, various locations), G. Zacharias Holland (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Sahil Jain (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Kenta Kawamoto (Sony AI, Tokyo, Japan), Raksha Kumaraswamy (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Patrick MacAlpine (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Dustin R. Morrill (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Declan Oller (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Francesco Riccio (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Akanksha Saran (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Craig Sherstan (Sony AI, Tokyo, Japan), Kaushik Subramanian (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Thomas J. Walsh (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Samuel Barrett (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Kizza N. Frisbee (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Mady Govil (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Johannes G\"unther (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Varun R. Kompella (Sony AI, North America, various locations), James A. MacGlashan (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Maxwell Svetlik (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Michael D. Thomure (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Jaden B. Travnik (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Kevin Waugh (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Elahe Aghapour (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Florian Fuchs (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Andreanne Lemay (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Shruti Mishra (Sony AI, Zurich, Switzerland), Takuma Seno (Sony AI, Tokyo, Japan), Peter Stone (Sony AI, North America, various locations), Michael Spranger (Sony AI, Tokyo, Japan), Peter R. Wurman (Sony AI, North America, various locations)

entry.summary: Sony AI presents a framework combining universal value function approximators with tailored training scenarios and data augmentation to coach agents into exhibiting controllable behavioral styles in complex domains, in real time. It addresses the need for controllable rather than single near-optimal RL behaviors.

entry.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill

author.name: Shengguang Wu, Hao Zhu, Yuhui Zhang, Xiaohan Wang, Serena Yeung-Levy

entry.summary: AutoMem treats memory management as a trainable cognitive skill (metamemory), promoting file-system operations to first-class memory actions so the model itself decides what to encode, retrieve, and organize. It jointly improves the supporting structure and the model's proficiency for long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: UltraFlux: Data-Model Co-Design for High-quality Native 4K Text-to-Image Generation across Diverse Aspect Ratios

author.name: Tian Ye, Song Fei, Lei Zhu

entry.summary: UltraFlux is a Flux-based diffusion transformer trained natively at 4K across diverse aspect ratios via data-model co-design, introducing a 1M-image 4K corpus and techniques like Resonance 2D RoPE with YaRN to address coupled positional-encoding, VAE, and optimization failures. It targets high-quality native high-resolution text-to-image generation.

entry.title: FLYNN: Robust Neural Network for Robot Navigation using Fly Brain Topology

author.name: Benquan Wang, Jingdao Chen

entry.summary: FLYNN is a recurrent network whose architecture is derived directly from the synaptic-resolution connectome of the fruit fly brain, trained for vision-based navigation in MuJoCo with performance comparable to hand-crafted networks of similar size. Crucially, it shows superior robustness to out-of-distribution data and sensory deprivation.

entry.title: Phantom References: Hallucinated Citations That Survive Peer Review at Top-Tier Conferences

author.name: Mark Russinovich, Ram Shankar Siva Kumar, Ahmed Salem

entry.summary: Measures citation hallucination in peer-reviewed AI proceedings using a conservative identity-level definition (non-existent works, substantial author-list mismatches) and an automated large-scale auditing pipeline. It documents that hallucinated references survive peer review at top-tier venues.

entry.title: Logit-Contribution Scoring Identifies Non-Literal Retrieval Heads

author.name: Aryo Pradipta Gema, Beatrice Alex, Pasquale Minervini

entry.summary: Introduces LOCOS, a write-aware detector that scores attention heads by how their output-value circuit projects onto the answer-token direction, identifying heads that synthesize non-literal answers rather than copy tokens. Argues prior literal-copy detectors miss the mechanism behind long-context synthesis.

entry.title: SeKV: Resolution-Adaptive KV Cache with Hierarchical Semantic Memory for Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Amirhossein Abaskohi, Giuseppe Carenini, Peter West, Yuhang He

entry.summary: SeKV is a resolution-adaptive KV cache that organizes long context into entropy-guided semantic spans and can recover token-level detail from compressed spans when they become relevant during decoding. It targets the linear KV memory bottleneck in long-context inference.

entry.title: Moral Safety in LLMs: Exposing Performative Compliance with Puzzled Cues

author.name: Mohammadamin Shafiei, Shuyue Stella Li, Yulia Tsvetkov

entry.summary: This paper shows LLM fairness evaluations overestimate moral safety: models appear fair when demographic identity is stated explicitly but become measurably less fair when identity must be inferred, a failure the authors call performative compliance. A cue-variation methodology isolates how identity presentation, not the dilemma, drives the shift.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap Between Latent and Explicit Reasoning with Looped Transformers

author.name: Ying Fan, Anej Svete, Kangwook Lee

entry.summary: This paper shows looped (recurrent-depth) Transformers can close the gap between latent and explicit chain-of-thought reasoning, where prior latent methods underperformed beyond 1B parameters. A looped padded Transformer processing K latent blocks matches explicit CoT, bridging efficient latent reasoning with performance.

entry.title: The Illusion of High Utility in Safety Alignment of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Adeel Yousaf, Soumik Ghosh, James Beetham, Amrit Singh Bedi, Mubarak Shah

entry.summary: Shows that apparent high-utility safety alignment of text-to-image diffusion models is illusory: fine-grained TIFA evaluation reveals substantial drops in semantic fidelity (object counts, attributes, relationships) masked by coarse metrics like FID and CLIPScore.
