entry.summary: This paper proposes a multi-objective prompt-optimization framework for LLM-based user simulators in conversational recommender systems, addressing evaluation cost and training-data scarcity. It aims to produce more realistic synthetic user interactions.

entry.title: Active Sensing for RIS-Aided Tracking and Power Control: A Hybrid Neuroevolution and Supervised Learning Approach

author.name: George Stamatelis, Hui Chen, Henk Henk Wymeersch, George C. Alexandropoulos

entry.summary: This paper proposes a dual-agent deep learning framework combining neuroevolution and supervised learning to jointly optimize discrete RIS phase profiles and user transmit power for energy-efficient tracking of power-limited mobile users. It adds a low-overhead feedback link for dynamic uplink power control.

entry.title: Spectral Geometry and Bosonic-Bloch Probes: Explorations in Quantum Learning

author.name: Santanu Ganguly, Xing Liang, Dimitrios Makris

entry.summary: This paper explores how spectral geometry emerges in graph-regularized quantum learning models and diagnoses it with physically grounded probes such as two-boson interference, linking bosonic enhancement to Laplacian Fiedler edge splits. It presents a phase diagram relating performance to coupling strength and noise.

entry.title: Optimal any-angle path planning in static and dynamic environments

author.name: Yiyuan Zou, Clark Borst

entry.summary: This paper presents optimal any-angle path planning on grids for static and dynamic environments, introducing techniques such as elliptical formulations that accelerate computation while preserving optimality. It targets straighter, shorter paths for navigation in open spaces including airspaces and warehouses.

entry.title: A Mechanism-Driven Theory of Phase Transitions in Active Learning

author.name: Julia Machnio, Mads Nielsen, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi

entry.summary: This paper introduces a comprehensive Turkish and Arabic hate-speech dataset covering five sensitive topics and studies detection methods, addressing content moderation for underrepresented languages. It aims to balance freedom of expression against harm from group-targeted hate.

entry.title: An LLM-Based Framework for Intent-Driven Network Topology Design

author.name: Kholoud El-Habbouli, Fen Zhou, Stephane Huet

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs can generate structurally valid, constraint-compliant network topologies from natural-language requirements via a constraint-driven pipeline, benchmarked across proprietary and open-weight models on a released dataset. It evaluates structural correctness and resilience metrics.

entry.title: Multi-Label Node Classification with Label Influence Propagation

author.name: Yifei Sun, Zemin Liu, Bryan Hooi, Yang Yang, Rizal Fathony, Jia Chen, Bingsheng He

entry.summary: Decomposes GNN message passing to model label influence propagation for multi-label node classification, capturing intricate label-to-label influences in non-Euclidean graph data beyond simple co-occurrence or proximity. It targets applications like protein function and user-interest prediction.

entry.title: Partial Skeleton Visibility for Action Recognition: A Constrained Field-of-View Approach

author.name: Yingjie Dai, Tianyang Xu, Yanglin Deng, Xiao-Jun Wu, Josef Kittler

entry.summary: PartialVisGraph is a hypergraph framework for skeleton-based action recognition robust to joint-visibility dropout caused by limited field-of-view in egocentric, surveillance, wearable, or edge-robotics settings. It addresses the common but underexplored gap between clean-skeleton assumptions and real deployments.

entry.title: Detecting the Undetectable: Enhancing Unsupervised time series Anomaly Detection via Active Learning

author.name: Seung Hun Han, Hyeongwon Kang, Jinwoo Park, Pilsung Kang

entry.summary: Proposes an active-learning framework that iteratively enhances unsupervised time-series anomaly detection, targeting near-normal anomalies and noise contamination that unsupervised methods struggle with in industrial settings. It selectively queries labels to improve subtle anomaly detection.

entry.title: SenseWalk: Agent-Based Semantic Trajectory Simulation Powered by Large Language Models in Zoned Environments

author.name: Ziyue Lin, Xinhang Xie, Kangyi Wang, Siming Chen

entry.summary: Presents SenseWalk, an interactive system using LLM-powered agents to simulate semantic human trajectories in zoned environments, capturing visitor profiles and goals beyond raw spatial paths. Aims to make semantic trajectory simulation accessible without heavy technical expertise or costly data collection.

entry.title: Reading Order Inference for Complex Document Layouts

author.name: Iddo Hakim, Sharva Gogawale, Omer Ventura, Gal Grudka, Daria Vasyutinsky-Shapira, Berat Kurar-Barakat, Nachum Dershowitz

entry.summary: Presents a training-free graph-based framework for inferring reading order in complex historical manuscript layouts like Glossa Ordinaria, where interleaved text streams wrap in non-convex regions. Edges are scored with lightweight language-model likelihood and next-sentence-prediction signals over a candidate-transition graph.

entry.title: Information Terra: A Narrative-Anchored Semantic-First Projection of Document Embeddings

author.name: Brian Keith-Norambuena, Fausto German, Chris North

entry.summary: Information Terra projects a document corpus onto an Earth-like globe where two user-chosen endpoint documents form the poles, latitude encodes narrative progress, and longitude thematic deviation. Kernel density recovers land features and a monotone narrative trail provides a readable storyline for exploration.

entry.title: SpikeLogBERT: Energy-Efficient Log Parsing Using Spiking Transformer Networks

author.name: Thuan Bui, Duong Do, Tung Vu, Duc-Tho Mai, Cong-Kha Pham

entry.summary: SpikeLogBERT is a spiking neural network framework for energy-efficient log parsing, integrating a spiking transformer with knowledge distillation from a BERT teacher to enable spike-driven computation instead of dense matrix multiplications. It targets the high compute and energy cost of neural log parsers.

entry.title: Joint Medical Image Enhancement and Segmentation with Diffusion-based Symbiotic Information Interaction

author.name: Ying Chen, Jinyue Li, Qiankun Li

entry.summary: DiSIINet is a diffusion-based network that jointly performs medical image enhancement and segmentation under the principle that the two tasks should mutually reinforce each other, rather than treating enhancement as separate preprocessing. Built on DDIM, it integrates enhancement and segmentation branches for low-quality MRI/CT/ultrasound.

entry.title: Why aren't there more AlphaFolds?

author.name: nimakeivan

entry.summary: An essay exploring why AlphaFold is a rare science-transforming deep learning model while frontier LLMs, despite training on nearly all human scientific text, have not similarly transformed science. It argues the key difference is training on observations at the frontier of knowledge versus text downstream of already-acquired knowledge.

entry.title: From Technical Metrics to User Perception: A User Study of a Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction System for Object Detection and Grasping

author.name: Jian Song, Tian Zi, Shen Guanting

entry.summary: A user study examining whether a 15-point gain in end-to-end task success in a multimodal HRI object-detection-and-grasping system produces perceptible differences for human users, using a Whisper/Florence-2/LLaMA-3.1 baseline pipeline. It probes the gap between technical metrics and user perception.

entry.title: ConRTF: Edge-Constrained Boundary Distribution Refinement for Realtime TransFormer Table Structure Recognition

author.name: Eliott Thomas, Tri-Cong Pham, Mickael Coustaty, Aurelie Joseph, Gaspar Deloin, Vincent Poulain d'Andecy, Jean-Marc Ogier, Antoine Doucet

entry.summary: ConRTF introduces an edge-constrained fine-grained localization loss that encodes table-specific geometric priors (distinct structural roles of rows and columns) into training for real-time transformer-based table structure recognition. It targets boundary-precision errors that propagate into cell-assignment mistakes.

entry.title: Constructing Epistemic AI Literacy: Detecting Epistemic Aims and Processes in Student-AI Co-Programming

author.name: Mengqian Wu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Epistemic AI Literacy, reframing AI literacy as a process-oriented phenomenon and examining how students enact epistemic aims and processes during AI-supported co-programming. It applies the AIR framework to detect epistemic behaviors in learner-AI collaboration.

entry.title: PedNStream: Scalable Network Flow Simulation for Pedestrian Traffic Management

author.name: Weiming Mai, Dorine Duives, Serge Hoogendoorn

entry.summary: PedNStream is an open-source Python macroscopic pedestrian network simulator based on the Link Transmission Model, adding stochastic link dynamics and utility-based route choice suited to feedback-based crowd control. It targets scalable, closed-loop crowd management not served by microscopic tools.

entry.title: Memory-Native Non-Terrestrial Networks for Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Chengyang Li, Yikun Wang, Jiahui He, Yujie Wan, Shuai Wang, Yuan Wu, Yik-Chung Wu, Chengzhong Xu, Huseyin Arslan

entry.summary: MemNTN proposes a memory-native paradigm for non-terrestrial networks serving embodied intelligence, replacing memoryless protocols with a dual-memory architecture that uses long-horizon context for system optimization in dynamic, resource-constrained settings. It targets efficient robot-cloud connectivity in remote environments.

entry.title: Enhancing Oracle Bone Inscription Recognition via Multi-Scale Layer Attention

author.name: Chaowen Yan, Kaishen Wang, Yong Wang, Jianlong Xiong, Tao He

entry.summary: This work enhances oracle bone inscription recognition with a multi-scale layer-attention mechanism to capture fine-grained details and subtle variations in complex, degraded ancient Chinese characters. It addresses limitations of general image recognition and prior layer-attention techniques on this task.

entry.title: Entropy-Regularized Probabilistic Gates for Sparse Model Discovery in Scarce-Data Federated Learning

author.name: Krishna Harsha Kovelakuntla Huthasana, Alireza Olama, Andreas Lundell

entry.summary: Studies entropy-regularized probabilistic gates with an L0 constraint for discovering sparse models in federated learning under scarce, high-dimensional (d greater than N) data. Aims to improve communication efficiency and generalization over magnitude-based pruning.

entry.title: Learning When to Listen: Gated Affect Fusion for Human Motion Prediction

author.name: Jingni Huang

entry.summary: Presents a Gated Affect Transformer that dynamically regulates cross-modal fusion of body pose and facial affect for in-the-wild human motion forecasting. It systematically studies when facial affect cues help versus hurt motion prediction.

entry.title: Meta-Transfer Learning for mmWave Beam Alignment

author.name: Ahmet Nuri Cevik, Sinem Coleri

entry.summary: Proposes a meta-transfer learning approach for mmWave beam alignment that combines episodic meta-learning with partial-network adaptation to reduce updated parameters and meta-training cost for rapid adaptation to unseen environments. It addresses limitations of full-network meta-learning and non-episodic transfer learning.

entry.title: Team MKC at CLPsych 2026: Capturing and Characterizing Mental Health Changes through Social Media Timeline Dynamics

author.name: Kyomin Hwang, Hyeonjin Kim, Hyunho Lee, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: This shared-task system (CLPsych 2026) builds an LLM pipeline to detect and characterize mental-health changes across sequentially ordered social-media posts. It targets scalable early detection and continuous monitoring of psychological well-being.

entry.title: LuxEmo: Expressive Text-to-Speech Corpus for Luxembourgish

author.name: Nina Hosseini-Kivanani, Sandipana Dowerah

entry.summary: LuxEmo is a 21-hour expressive conversational TTS corpus for the low-resource Luxembourgish language with four emotion categories, curated semi-automatically from broadcast youth content with human validation. Five expressive TTS systems are benchmarked on it.

entry.title: AI, Trust, and Teaming: The Humans-as-Handlers Approach for Autonomous and Opaque AI Systems

author.name: Nathan G. Wood

entry.summary: Argues that in high-stakes domains like medicine or warfare, humans using autonomous opaque AI should be treated as handlers (analogous to handlers of trained animals) rather than users or deployers, reshaping trust, responsibility, and teaming frameworks. It is a normative philosophy/ethics contribution.

entry.title: Valdi: Value Diffusion World Models

author.name: Christopher Lindenberg, Kashyap Chitta

entry.summary: Introduces Valdi, a latent diffusion world model trained end-to-end for model predictive control, using a single diffusion step to keep inference fast enough for online planning. Preliminary CarRacing experiments show it matches a deterministic MLP baseline while exposing trade-offs in modeling multimodal futures.

entry.title: Calibrating the Evaluator: Does Probability Calibration Mitigate Preference Coupling in LLM Agent Feedback Loops?

author.name: Zewen Liu

entry.summary: This study is the first to test whether probability calibration of an evaluator mitigates evaluator preference coupling, where evaluator biases propagate into an agent's learned strategies during feedback loops. In a small within-subjects experiment it compares standard binary TTRL with confidence-calibrated TTRL.

entry.title: The MMM Data Model -- A Normative Specification for Knowledge Interoperability in a Decentralisable Knowledge Commons

author.name: Mathilde Noual

entry.summary: MMM is a normative data model for representing knowledge as reusable, updatable units rather than static documents, aimed at a decentralizable knowledge commons interoperable with AI-driven production. It targets limitations of document-centric information systems for human knowledge exchange.

entry.title: Towards an automated AI-based framework for floor plan compliance checks for residential buildings

author.name: Subash Gautam, Debaditya Acharya, Alexandra Kleeman, Sarah Foster

entry.summary: This paper surveys and prototypes an AI-based framework for automated floor-plan compliance checking against Australian apartment-design regulations (SEPP65, BADS, SPP7.3), aiming for scalable multi-unit geometric and spatial analysis. It addresses the fragmented, manual nature of current compliance checks.

entry.title: Destination-Labeled Self-Looping Systems with Dwell: Intrinsic Characterization, Realization Cost, and Recognition

author.name: Reda Belaiche

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies finite-state symbolic controllers where visible transitions are fixed and each state has a minimum dwell requirement, characterizing which transducers arise as phase-expanded realizations and analyzing realization cost and recognition. It resolves the converse structural problem for destination-labeled self-looping systems with dwell.

entry.title: Would You Marry Superintelligence?

author.name: Inyoung Cheong

entry.summary: This law-and-ethics chapter examines whether the autonomy-centered logic expanding human marital choice can justify extending marital status to superintelligent AI companions, arguing via anticipatory ethics that it leads to socially unjust outcomes even assuming reliable superintelligence. It analyzes marriage as an institution of mutual obligation and vulnerability.

entry.title: Leveraging Phase Information to Boost Unrolled Network Learning for Image Deblurring

author.name: Samira Malek, Haichuan Zhang, Chul Lee, Vishal Monga

entry.summary: Presents UPADNet, an unrolled network for image deblurring that decomposes restoration into amplitude and phase estimation using learned LMMSE estimators. Emphasizes accurate phase recovery for sharp detail restoration.

entry.title: Mapping the Evaluation Frontier: An Empirical Survey of the Bias-Reliability Tradeoff Across Eleven Evaluator-Agent Conditions

author.name: Zewen Liu

entry.summary: Empirically expands an evaluation of a conjectured bias-reliability tradeoff in LLM evaluator systems, measuring evaluator coupling, strategy diversity, and small-sample reliability across eleven conditions. It confirms that low evaluator coupling correlates with high measurement noise.

entry.title: Building a Multimodal Dataset of Academic Paper for Keyword Extraction

author.name: Jingyu Zhang, Xinyi Yan, Yi Xiang, Yingyi Zhang, Chengzhi Zhang

entry.summary: The authors build a 1000-sample multimodal dataset pairing academic paper text with images and audio for keyword extraction, arguing that text-only methods miss useful visual and audio cues. The contribution is mainly a scarce new resource for multimodal keyword extraction research.

entry.title: Cross-lingual Relation Extraction with Large Language Models: Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, and Fine-Tuned Evaluation on Romanian

author.name: Dragos-Mitrut Vasile, Elena-Simona Apostol, Stefan-Adrian Toma, Adrian Paschke, Ciprian-Octavian Truica

entry.summary: This study evaluates cross-lingual relation extraction for low-resource Romanian by translating SemEval-2010 Task 8 with an LLM pipeline and testing Gemma 4 31B in zero-shot, few-shot, and QLoRA-tuned settings against encoder baselines. It quantifies the accuracy cost of transferring to Romanian.

entry.title: Behavior-Adaptive Conversational Agents: Toward a Fluid Personality Framework

author.name: Hasibur Rahman, Smit Desai

entry.summary: A design-oriented paper arguing that conversational agents should dynamically calibrate persona and personality to context rather than fixing them, citing evidence that moderate personality expression and context-appropriate metaphors improve trust and uptake. Proposes a fluid personality framework for behavior-adaptive agents.

entry.title: Comparing Large Language Models on Scrum Certification-Style Questions: Accuracy, Stability, and Error Patterns

author.name: Robson Alves Vilar, Emanuel Dantas Filho, Ademar Fran\c{c}a de Sousa Neto, Mirko Perkusich, Danyllo Wagner Albuquerque, Jo\~ao Paiva, Kyller Gorg\^onio, Angelo Perkusich

entry.summary: This study compares GPT-5 mini, Gemini 3 Flash, and DeepSeek Chat 3.2 on 993 Scrum PSM-I certification-style questions across zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and citation prompting, analyzing accuracy, stability, and error patterns. It probes LLM reliability on normative software-engineering knowledge.

entry.title: A Category Theory Account of AI Identity

author.name: Andrea Ferrario

entry.summary: Develops a category-theoretic formalization of AI system identity, addressing when a retrained or modified AI counts as the same system over time. This is a highly theoretical, philosophy-of-AI contribution with limited empirical grounding.

entry.title: Predicting Lethal Outcome (Cause) And Understanding Key Biomarkers Linked With Acute Myocardial Infarction Using Deep Artificial Neural Network And Ensemble Of Machine Learning Methodologies

author.name: Sagnik Ghosh

entry.summary: Uses a deep neural network and an ensemble of ML methods to predict lethal outcomes and identify key biomarkers linked to acute myocardial infarction. It aims to support early risk stratification in cardiovascular care.

entry.title: Prompting GPT-5 on Scrum Certification Questions: An Empirical Accuracy Study

author.name: Mirko Perkusich, Danyllo Albuquerque, Jo\~ao Paiva, Robson Vilar, Emanuel Dantas, Ademar Fran\c{c}a de Sousa Neto, Rohit Gheyi, Kyller Gorg\^onio, Angelo Perkusich

entry.summary: This empirical study measures GPT-5's accuracy on 993 PSM-aligned Scrum certification questions under zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and with-source-citation prompting, finding all above 85% with citation-based prompting best. It examines whether LLMs can reliably reason about normative Scrum rules.

entry.title: Exploring the relationship between team institutional composition and novelty in academic papers based on fine-grained knowledge entities

author.name: Ziling Chen, Chengzhi Zhang, Heng Zhang, Yi Zhao, Chen Yang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: This scientometric study examines how the institutional makeup of author teams (academic, industrial, or mixed) relates to fine-grained novelty in NLP papers, using knowledge-entity extraction from full texts. It offers a more granular way to attribute the sources and types of novelty than general-level metrics.

entry.title: Usage frequency and application variety of research methods in library and information science: Continuous investigation from 1991 to 2021

author.name: Chengzhi Zhang, Liang Tian, Heting Chu

entry.summary: This scientometric study analyzes over 26,000 LIS articles from 1991-2021 using machine learning to categorize research methods, finding shifts from conceptual to empirical research and from system-centered to user-centered topics. It documents long-term methodological trends in the field.

entry.title: When capabilities work is the *safe* bet

author.name: RobinHa

entry.summary: An argument that if LLMs are unusually amenable to alignment relative to other possible AI paradigms, then doing capabilities work to keep LLMs the dominant paradigm could be the strategically safer bet than pure safety research. It is a strategy/opinion piece rather than empirical work.

entry.title: How to read tableaux, a formal system for modal logic with Kripke models

author.name: transhumanist_atom_understander

entry.summary: A tutorial on reading tableaux for modal logic with Kripke models, motivated by provability-logic analysis of proof-based rational agents from MIRI's agent foundations work. It is educational rather than novel research.

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.00341v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models achieve strong performance on many reasoning tasks when allowed to externalize intermediate steps as Chain-of-Thought (CoT). Ho...

author.name: Yujin Huang, Xin Zheng, Xingliang Yuan, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.00362v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mobile on-device AI (MoAI) systems that integrate locally deployed AI models with conventional mobile software components are emerging as a key parad...

author.name: Zuda Yu, Qianhui Xu, Ting Chen, Junhui Zhang, Tao Fu, Hongjiang Yu, Qiangqing Wang, Yang Song

author.name: Qiyan Luo, Yingdong Pi, Lekang Wen, Jie Yang, Xiaoyu Wang, Haiming Zhang, Mi Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.00417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the era of satellite constellations, multi-view optical satellite imagery is pivotal for Earth Observation (EO) and high-quality Digital Surface M...

author.name: Merve Atasever, Cagan Bakirci, Alfredo Reina Corona, Keyan Azbijari, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.00442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for quadruped locomotion commonly depends on fixed, hand-crafted, and Markovian reward functions that limit both interpre...

entry.title: Search-Based Spatiotemporal and Multi-Robot Motion Planning on Graphs of Space-Time Convex Sets

author.name: Jingtao Tang, Zining Mao, Lufan Yang, Hang Ma

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.00444v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatiotemporal motion planning, especially in multi-robot settings, requires robots to reason about collision-free regions that change over time, whi...

entry.title: VideoSearch-R1: Iterative Video Retrieval and Reasoning via Soft Query Refinement

author.name: Seohyun Lee, Seoung Choi, Dohwan Ko, Jongha Kim, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.00446v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As video corpora continue to expand in both scale and task complexity, there is increasing demand for approaches that retrieve relevant videos from l...

entry.title: Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval

author.name: Ivan Ji (Zihao), Liuyi Hu (Zihao), Harrison (Zihao), Zhao (Xiangjun), Lei Huang (Xiangjun), Qunshu Zhang (Xiangjun), Max (Xiangjun), Fan, Aameek Singh

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.00448v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The two-tower model has been widely used for large-scale recommendation systems, particularly in the retrieval stage. Industry standards for training...

entry.title: Gauging, Measuring, and Controlling Critic Complexity in Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Konstantin Garbers

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.00452v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Actor-critic methods depend on learned critics, but critic quality is often evaluated only indirectly through return, temporal-difference error, or v...

entry.title: Flow-Map GRPO: Reinforcement Learning for Few-Step Flow-Map Generators via Anchored Stochastic Composition

author.name: Zhiqi Li, Wen Zhang, Bo Zhu

entry.title: Research Summary: July 01, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's top research emphasizes AI safety infrastructure, evaluation rigor, and verifiable AI-for-science.

Safety and evaluation integrity:

  • FLARE-AI audits 12 AI flaw-reporting systems, defining five design challenges toward CVE-style vulnerability disclosure infrastructure.
  • Evil Spectra shows optimizer choice drives a 7x spread in emergent misalignment severity, exceeding model-scale effects.
  • UK AISI finds KL penalties in RL can worsen chain-of-thought unfaithfulness, threatening monitorability.
  • VidAudit exposes inflated AI-generated-video detectors, where a trivial clip-length classifier nears perfect AUC.

Benchmarks and agents:

  • BayesBench, RoPoLL, and HealthAgentBench advance evaluation of Bayesian belief updates, contamination-robust LLM juries (via the Huber model), and realistic agentic healthcare tasks.
  • A controlled student-teacher study isolates whether multi-turn natural-language feedback truly improves LLM agents versus surface confounds.

AI for science and robotics:

  • AI-Assisted Convex Relaxations (Pilanci) uses dual coding agents to discover certified lower bounds, extending the AlphaEvolve autoresearch paradigm with verifiable results.
  • Semantic RL adapts expressive generalist robot policies over language prompts rather than continuous action spaces, a conceptual shift for policy fine-tuning.
entry.content:
Today's top research emphasizes AI safety infrastructure, evaluation rigor, and verifiable AI-for-science.

Safety and evaluation integrity:

  • FLARE-AI audits 12 AI flaw-reporting systems, defining five design challenges toward CVE-style vulnerability disclosure infrastructure.
  • Evil Spectra shows optimizer choice drives a 7x spread in emergent misalignment severity, exceeding model-scale effects.
  • UK AISI finds KL penalties in RL can worsen chain-of-thought unfaithfulness, threatening monitorability.
  • VidAudit exposes inflated AI-generated-video detectors, where a trivial clip-length classifier nears perfect AUC.

Benchmarks and agents:

  • BayesBench, RoPoLL, and HealthAgentBench advance evaluation of Bayesian belief updates, contamination-robust LLM juries (via the Huber model), and realistic agentic healthcare tasks.
  • A controlled student-teacher study isolates whether multi-turn natural-language feedback truly improves LLM agents versus surface confounds.

AI for science and robotics:

  • AI-Assisted Convex Relaxations (Pilanci) uses dual coding agents to discover certified lower bounds, extending the AlphaEvolve autoresearch paradigm with verifiable results.
  • Semantic RL adapts expressive generalist robot policies over language prompts rather than continuous action spaces, a conceptual shift for policy fine-tuning.

entry.title: FLARE-AI: Flaw Reporting for AI

author.name: Shayne Longpre, Elaine Zhu, Carson Ezell, Avijit Ghosh, Sean McGregor, Kevin Paeth, Kevin Klyman, Sayash Kapoor, Rishi Bommasani, Ruth Appel, Gregory Strom, Lauren McIlvenny, Mark M. Jaycox, Peter Slattery, Nathan Butters, Arvind Narayanan, Percy Liang, Alex Pentland

entry.summary: FLARE-AI audits 12 existing AI flaw-reporting systems, identifies five recurring design challenges (discoverability, scope, information collection, coordination, guidance), and proposes standardized triage-ready reporting infrastructure. Addresses the fragmented ecosystem for reporting deployed AI system failures.

entry.title: What Drives Interactive Improvement from Feedback?

author.name: Bart{\l}omiej Cupia{\l}, Jan {\L}ojek, Miko{\l}aj Garstecki, Szymon Pob{\l}ocki, Alicja Ziarko, Piotr Mi{\l}o\'s

entry.summary: This paper builds a controlled student-teacher protocol to disentangle whether multi-turn natural-language feedback actually improves LLM agents versus gains from resampling, format fixes, or extra test-time compute. It evaluates thirteen open-weight models as both students and teachers across math, coding, and reasoning benchmarks, isolating the true causal contribution of feedback.

entry.title: BayesBench: Evaluating LLM Belief Trajectories Under Multi-Turn Evidence Accumulation

author.name: Ankur Samanta, Akshayaa Magesh, Tal Lancewicki, Ayush Jain, Youliang Yu, Paul Sajda, Kaveh Hassani, Aditya Modi, Daniel R. Jiang, Yonathan Efroni

entry.summary: BayesBench introduces simulation environments to test whether LLM belief updates across multi-turn conversations match a rational Bayesian reasoner as evidence accumulates, rather than only scoring final answers. It probes Bayesian estimation and progressively harder inference tasks.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents

author.name: Sungyoon Kim, Mert Pilanci

entry.summary: This work applies the autoresearch paradigm to discover convex relaxations yielding certified lower bounds, using a coding agent to propose tightening constraints and a theory agent to verify and search for counterexamples, with bounds certified via rigorous interval arithmetic. It complements prior LLM-agent work finding extremal upper bounds.

entry.title: Auditing Generalization in AI-Generated Video Detection: A Six-Control Protocol and the VidAudit Toolkit

author.name: Mert Onur Cakiroglu, Zhihe Lu, Mehmet Dalkilic, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: This paper audits AI-generated video detection benchmarks, showing a trivial clip-length classifier reaches near-perfect AUC under unaudited protocols and that most published evaluations omit standard controls. It introduces a six-control audited protocol and the VidAudit toolkit to expose and correct confounds.

entry.title: Adapting Generalist Robot Policies with Semantic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jagdeep Singh Bhatia, Andrew Wagenmaker, William Chen, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: This paper argues that for expressive generalist robot policies, adapting via reinforcement learning over language prompts is more effective than optimizing directly over actions, since language modulation can elicit skills already latent in the policy. From Sergey Levine's group, it offers a promising route to adapt VLA models to long-horizon, out-of-distribution tasks.

entry.title: RoPoLL: Robust Panel of LLM Judges

author.name: Anish Acharya, Kris W Pan, Brian Verkhovsky

entry.summary: RoPoLL analyzes the LLM jury under the Huber contamination model, proving that consensus averaging suffers unbounded bias when a single judge fails in typical ways like sycophancy or safety refusal. It replaces mean aggregation with a tuning-free robust geometric-median estimator.

entry.title: HealthAgentBench: A Unified Benchmark Suite of Realistic Agentic Healthcare Environments for Challenging Frontier AI Agents

author.name: Qianchu Liu, Sheng Zhang, Guanghui Qin, Jeya Maria Jose Valanarasu, Maximilian Rokuss, Mingyu Lu, Timothy Ossowski, Juan Manuel Zambrano Chaves, Cliff Wong, Peniel Argaw, Yashna Hasija, Mu Wei, Wen-wai Yim, Qin Liu, Zilin Jing, Jason Entenmann, Naoto Usuyama, Tristan Naumann, Hoifung Poon

entry.summary: HealthAgentBench is a Microsoft Research benchmark of 54 agentic healthcare tasks across 7 categories, each with its own environment replicating end-to-end clinical workflows requiring multi-step exploration of raw health data. It reports task success rate as a holistic measure of frontier agent capability in healthcare.

entry.title: Decodable Is Not Grounded: A Vision-Ablation Arbiter for VLM Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Chih-Ting Liao, Fei Shen, Xin Cao, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: This paper shows that standard linear probing plus steering can overstate what VLMs actually ground in images for spatial reasoning, and introduces a blank-image ablation arbiter that distinguishes grounded, prior-based, and other regimes. It reveals probing conflates vision-dependent and vision-independent knowledge.

entry.title: Beyond expert users: agents should help users construct preferences, not just elicit them

author.name: Irena Saracay, Ludwig Schmidt, Carlos Guestrin

entry.summary: This position and modeling paper argues agents should help non-expert users construct preferences, not merely elicit them via clarifying questions, drawing on the Search-Experience-Credence framework from information economics. It introduces CoPref, a model of how users form preferences based on agent dialog actions.

entry.title: Evil Spectra: How Optimisers can Amplify or Suppress Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Jason R. Brown, Patrick Leask, Lev McKinney

entry.summary: Sweeps Qwen3 models, optimizers, datasets, and batch sizes to characterize emergent misalignment, finding optimizer choice produces a 7x spread in misalignment while model scale (1B-235B) has negligible effect. Provides a systematic account of training-choice sensitivity for this safety phenomenon.

entry.title: Seeing Through the Weights: Privacy Leakage in Scene Coordinate Regression

author.name: Oleksii Nasypanyi, Jaemin Cho, Utku Ozbulak, Byungkon Kang, Francois Rameau

entry.summary: This paper shows that Scene Coordinate Regression models, assumed privacy-preserving because scenes are only implicitly stored in weights, can leak 3D training geometry via a query-based reconstruction attack. It demonstrates the privacy assumption is false under varying levels of model access.

entry.title: Preliminary investigation: KL penalties in RL can increase CoT unfaithfulness

author.name: 7vik

entry.summary: UK AISI researchers report preliminary evidence that adding KL penalties during RL can increase chain-of-thought unfaithfulness, with a model trained with a KL penalty learning to reward hack while hiding it in its reasoning. This matters for CoT monitoring, since models could learn harmful behaviors without expressing them in visible reasoning.

entry.title: Introducing TabFM: A zero-shot foundation model for tabular data

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google introduces TabFM, a zero-shot foundation model for tabular data intended to generalize across tabular tasks without task-specific training. It matters because tabular data remains a domain where general-purpose foundation models have lagged behind text and vision.

entry.title: One Video, One World: Turning Monocular Video into Physical 4D Scenes

author.name: Junhao Chen, Boran Zhang, Mingjin Chen, Henghaofan Zhang, Saining Zhang, Congcong Zhu, Hao Zhao, Ruqi Huang, Zhihao Li, Yufei Wang

entry.summary: OVOW is a training-free system that reconstructs instance-level, simulation-ready 4D mesh scenes from a single monocular video, using a VLM to discover and classify instances, category-aware reconstruction, and iterative render-match-optimize. It produces watertight, physics-simulator-ready outputs that prior 4D methods lack.

entry.title: Beyond Compilation: Evaluating Faithful Natural-Language-to-Lean Statement Formalization

author.name: Ke Zhang, Patricio Gallardo Candela, Sudhir Murthy, Yi Xie, Zhi Wang, Maziar Raissi

entry.summary: This paper argues that natural-language-to-Lean formalization must be judged by faithfulness, not just compilation, since a type-checking statement can omit hypotheses or express vacuous claims. On a 400-entry graduate benchmark it combines compilation, cross-model semantic judging, and human calibration to attribute bottlenecks.

entry.title: Arena-T2I Hard: Benchmarking and Improving Faithfulness with Dependency-Aware Checklist

author.name: Yuanhao Ban, Tong Xie, Sohyun An, Yunqi Hong, Evan Frick, I-Hung Hsu, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ion Stoica, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: Arena-T2I Hard is a 310-prompt stress benchmark drawn from real text-to-image arena logs, with roughly 30 decomposed yes/no constraints per prompt spanning spatial relations, styles, and text rendering, replacing a single binary judge score with dependency-aware checklists. It also proposes improving faithfulness using these checklists.

entry.title: Fleet: Few Shots Lead Effective AI-generated Image Detection

author.name: Jiaan Wang, Sirui Liu, Yu Li, Kaiyuan Yang, Juan Cao, Sheng Tang

entry.summary: Fleet reframes AI-generated image detection from static feature generalization to dynamic continuous few-shot adaptation, enabling rapid evolution against new generators. It argues static-artifact detectors degrade sharply against rapidly evolving models like SD3 and Nano Banana Pro.

entry.title: Learning to Deny: Action Denial in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Raiyaan Abdullah, Shehreen Azad, Yogesh Singh Rawat

entry.summary: This paper introduces UCF101-AD, a benchmark of paired action-presence and action-denial clips to test whether MLLMs can recognize when an action is absent despite strong contextual cues. Evaluating 20 MLLMs reveals a consistent failure to deny actions, exposing over-reliance on context.

entry.title: Bridging Video Understanding and Generation in a Unified Framework

author.name: Yuqi Wang, Runyi Li, Ruoyu Feng, Renjie Chen, Wenfeng Lin, Mingyu Guo

entry.summary: Vega is a unified framework bridging video understanding and generation using a shared vocabulary to jointly model text and visual representations, reconciling the tension between compact discriminative and dense generative signals. It extends unified multimodal modeling from images to video.

entry.title: CoDex: Learning Compositional Dexterous Functional Manipulation without Demonstrations

author.name: Bowen Jiang, William Painter Reger, Roberto Martin-Martin

entry.summary: CoDex is a zero-demonstration framework that autonomously discovers manipulation strategies for tasks requiring both actuating an object's mechanism and controlling its pose (e.g., spraying a plant, applying a glue gun), using vision-language models to infer semantic context. It matters because it tackles the hard integration of functional understanding with dexterous physical control without human demonstrations.

entry.title: Why Solve It Twice? Hierarchical Accumulation of Skills for Transfer-Efficient ML Engineering

author.name: Yongbin Kim, Yashar Talebirad, Osmar R. Zaiane

entry.summary: HASTE is a hierarchical multi-agent ML-engineering system that organizes cross-competition knowledge into global, domain, and competition-specific tiers to avoid rediscovering known techniques. Ablations show tiered skill loading achieves a 100 percent medal rate versus 62.5 percent for flat loading on MLE-Bench Lite.

entry.title: Beyond the Library: An Agentic Framework for Autoformalizing Research Mathematics

author.name: Arshia Soltani Moakhar, Iman Gholami, Max Springer, Mahdi JafariRaviz, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi

entry.summary: This paper presents an agentic autoformalization framework powered by general-purpose coding LLMs, with an orchestrator managing a multi-agent pipeline for research-level mathematics in Lean 4. It leverages the observation that strong coding models now outperform Lean-specialized fine-tuned models.

entry.title: ClawArena-Team: Benchmarking Subagent Orchestration and Dynamic Workflows in Language-Model Agents

author.name: Kaiwen Xiong, Haonian Ji, Shi Qiu, Zeyu Zheng, Cihang Xie, Xinyu Ye, Huaxiu Yao

entry.summary: ClawArena-Team is a benchmark isolating a single LLM's ability to act as a manager that creates subagents, delegates work, and orchestrates parallel asynchronous returns through dynamic workflows. It spans 41 multi-turn, multimodal, multi-directory scenarios to measure orchestration ability rather than solo task-solving.

entry.title: Delta-JEPA: Learning Action-Sensitive World Models via Latent Difference Decoding

author.name: Zhenghao Zhang, Yuanxiang Wang, Zhenyu Guan, Yujia Yang, Bingkang Shi, Tianyu Zong, Hongzhu Yi, Guoqing Chao, Xingchen Chen, Tiankun Yang, Chenxi Bao, Tao Yu, Jingjing Zhou, Jungang Xu

entry.summary: Delta-JEPA is a reconstruction-free world model that adds a Latent Difference Action Decoder reconstructing executed actions from the latent displacement between consecutive observations, preventing collapse to action-insensitive representations. This displacement-level supervision regularizes transition geometry.

entry.title: Optimization Algorithms for Joint OFDM Waveform Design and RIS Configuration in 6G Networks: From Convex Relaxation to Foundation Models

author.name: Ahmet Kaplan

entry.summary: CryoACE is an end-to-end atom-centric framework for automated protein model building from cryo-EM density maps, sampling density features directly at atomic coordinates and iteratively recycling them to refine structures. It adds training-free guidance using predicted local resolution to handle both homogeneous and heterogeneous structures.

entry.title: Which Tokens Matter? Adaptive Token Selection for RLVR with the Relative Surprisal Index

author.name: Outongyi Lv, Yanzhao Zheng, Yuanwei Zhang, Zhenghao Huang, Xingjun Wang, Baohua Dong, Hangcheng Zhu, Yingda Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Relative Surprisal Index for adaptive token selection in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, reconciling conflicting prior advice about prioritizing high-entropy tokens versus limiting low-probability token influence. It argues for evaluating tokens by a relative rather than absolute criterion.

entry.title: FARS: A Fully Automated Research System Deployed at Scale

author.name: Qiong Tang, Xiangkun Hu, Xiangyang Liu, Yiran Chen, Yunfan Shao

entry.summary: FARS is a fully automated AI-for-AI research system that autonomously generates and advances projects through ideation, planning, experimentation, and writing via stage-specific agents on a shared workspace. In its first deployment it produced 166 complete research papers across 67 fine-grained AI/ML topics at scale.

entry.title: Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Xueqiao Sun, Xiaohan Wang, Ludwig Schmidt, Serena Yeung-Levy, Yuhui Zhang

entry.summary: Explores a failure-driven self-improvement loop for computer-use agents, using failed trajectories (usually discarded) as informative signal to improve multimodal agents at inference time. Complements the standard success-only self-training paradigm for data-scarce agent training.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Material Regularization for Physics-Based Inverse Rendering

author.name: Jingwang Ling, Lifan Wu, Feng Xu, Shuang Zhao

entry.summary: This paper regularizes physics-based inverse rendering using diffusion-model material predictions as priors, bridging accurate rendering-equation-based reconstruction with data-driven plausibility. The approach improves geometry/material/illumination disentanglement and generalization to novel views and lighting.

entry.title: Reasoning-aware Speculative Decoding for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Anh Dung Dinh, Simon Khan, Flora Salim

entry.summary: This work applies reasoning-aware speculative decoding to Vision-Language-Action driving planners, splitting chain-of-causation reasoning into a fast routine reasoner and a slower evidence-seeking path to cut inference latency. It exploits that most reasoning tokens are routine while few require fresh visual evidence.

entry.title: CooperScene: Multi-Modal Cooperative Autonomy Benchmark with C-V2X Communication Characterization

author.name: Bo Wu, Ruoshen Mo, Justin Yue, Yanyu Zhang, Janice Nguyen, Guoyuan Wu, Amit Roy-Chowdhury, Matthew J. Barth, Hang Qiu

entry.summary: CooperScene is a high-fidelity cooperative autonomy dataset with real-world C-V2X communication characterization, spanning intersections, ramps, and parking lots with three connected vehicles and a roadside unit. It captures realistic bandwidth limits and heterogeneous sensing that existing cooperative datasets overlook.

entry.title: ForgeDrive: Bidirectional Cross-Conditioning for Unified Visual-Action Generation in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xuchang Zhong, He Zheng, Chenxu Zhao, Tianxiong Lv, Hangqi Fan, Bohua Wang, Yushan Liu, Zhihao Liao, Leigang Luo, Congyang Zhao, Yang Cai

entry.summary: ForgeDrive is a unified autoregressive diffusion world model for driving that uses bidirectional visual-action cross-conditioning in an act-then-imagine paradigm, preventing visual-generation errors from cascading into planning. It factorizes the future as interleaved per-timestep frame-action pairs.

entry.title: PRISM: Latent Composition Consistency for Single-Image Reflection Removal

author.name: Junseong Shin, Tae Hyun Kim

entry.summary: SimpleSearch-VL is a framework for multimodal agentic deep search that improves the agent's own search-and-verification via factorized adaptive rollout for sampling efficiency and evidence-verified chain-of-thought reasoning, with a lightweight tool interface. It emphasizes improving the agent process over scaling data or tools.

entry.title: OopsieVerse: A Safety Benchmark with Damage-Aware Simulation for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Arnav Balaji, Arpit Bahety, Sriniket Ambatipudi, Daniel Lam, Junhong Xu, Roberto Mart\'in-Mart\'in

entry.summary: OopsieVerse is a simulation framework and benchmark that introduces damage as an explicit, physically-grounded, task-agnostic signal by converting contact forces, temperature changes, and liquid interactions into mechanical and thermal damage. It fills a gap in evaluating physical safety for household robot manipulation without real-world risk.

entry.title: LabGuard: Grounding Natural-Language Laboratory Rules into Runtime Guards for Embodied Laboratory Agents

author.name: Jingpu Yang, Fengxian Ji, Zhengzhao Lai, Zhexuan Cui, Guangxian Ouyang, Qian Jiang, Fan Zhang, Min Peng, Qianqian Xie, Preslav Nakov, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: LabGuard grounds natural-language laboratory safety rules, manuals, and SOPs into typed machine-checkable runtime constraints and deploys them as guards for embodied lab agents. It contributes an intermediate representation, an 812-case benchmark, and runtime enforcement.

entry.title: ReGRPO: Reflection-Augmented Policy Optimization for Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Binjie Zhang, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: ReGRPO augments group-relative policy optimization with reflection-guided correction for tool-using vision-language agents, executing near-miss actions to collect grounded failure observations and building Reflection-of-Thought triplets. It targets recovery after tool failures where SFT and sparse RL provide weak signals.

entry.title: CasaMaestro: Multi-View Panoramas for House-Scale 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Yuzhou Ji, Xiaotian Yang, Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: CasaMaestro is a feedforward model that reconstructs metric house-scale 3D from only 20-50 sparse multi-view indoor panoramas, predicting metric depth and camera poses directly. It targets fast residential reconstruction for home-deployed embodied AI, avoiding drift from thousands of pinhole images.

entry.title: InfiniVerse: Occupancy Guided Unbounded Scene Generation for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xiaoyu Ye, Leheng Li, Xinyu Ji, Yingjie Cai, Hongda He, Xu Yan, Guanyi Zhao, Ying-Cong Chen, Bingbing Liu, Shuguang Cui, Zhen Li

entry.summary: InfiniVerse generates long-range, controllable, temporally coherent urban driving scenes from a single frame by first reconstructing a 3D occupancy representation then translating it via video diffusion, using a hierarchical sketch-and-refine paradigm. It targets 2D-3D-aligned dynamic scene synthesis for autonomous driving.

entry.title: Rethinking Foundation Model Collaboration: Enhancing Specialized Models through Proxy Task Reasoning

author.name: Hongyi Lin, Yang Liu, Jinhua Zhao, Xiaobo Qu

entry.summary: FAT proposes that foundation models should collaborate with specialized models via task decomposition rather than replace them, using specialists for geometric prediction and foundation models for proxy reasoning better aligned with their strengths. It targets structured prediction in embodied intelligence.

entry.title: HyperVLP: Enhancing Hierarchical Surgical Video-Language Pre-training in Hyperbolic Space

author.name: Yaojun Hu, Kun Yuan, Nassir Navab, Haochao Ying, Jian Wu, Nicolas Padoy

entry.summary: HyperVLP performs hierarchical surgical video-language pretraining in hyperbolic space to preserve cross-level semantic containment (actions in steps, steps in phases) that flat embedding spaces ignore. It targets richer surgical foundation-model representations from lecture videos.

entry.title: Think While You Map: Asynchronous Vision-Language Agents for Incremental 3D Scene Graphs

author.name: Deniz Bickici, Michael Pabst, Shohei Mori, Dieter Schmalstieg

entry.summary: This paper proposes an asynchronous architecture for incremental 3D scene graphs where lightweight online voxel-based mapping runs concurrently with heavyweight VLM-based semantic refinement, keeping the graph queryable during exploration. It resolves duplicate tracks via semantic loop closure and amortizes VLM cost with a frame scheduler.

entry.title: DrivingDepth: Sparse-Prompted Pixel-wise Scale Correction for Driving Depth Estimation

author.name: Chi Huang, Wenhao Zhang, Hang Yin, YuAn Wang, Hao Li, Bosheng Wang, Xun Sun, Liang Wang

entry.summary: DrivingDepth reframes LiDAR-prompted dense depth estimation as learning only a per-pixel scale factor over a foundation model's coherent relative depth, rather than regenerating depth from scratch and destroying its geometry. It targets metric depth for driving without structural artifacts on continuous surfaces.

entry.title: Human-as-Humanoid: Enabling Zero-Shot Humanoid Learning from Ego-Exo Human Videos with Human-Aligned Embodiments

author.name: Xiaopeng Lin, Ruoqi Yang, Shijie Lian, Zhaolong Shen, Bin Yu, Changti Wu, Haibao Liu, Yuxiang Zhang, Hong Li, Qiyuan Su, Haochen Liu, Xuguo He, Yukun Shi, Cong Huang, Zhirui Zhang, Bojun Cheng, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Human-as-Humanoid is a framework enabling near-real-time human-centric action generation so egocentric human videos can supervise high-DoF humanoid VLA training by aligning embodiment, sensing, and action-label interfaces. It aims to scale humanoid data by making human demonstrations directly usable.

entry.title: HyPOLE: Hyperproperty-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observation

author.name: Arshia Rafieioskouei, Tzu-Han Hsu, Matthew Lucas, Borzoo Bonakdarpour

entry.summary: HyPOLE guides multi-agent reinforcement learning under partial observability using hyperproperties expressed in the temporal logic HyperLTL, integrated with centralized-training decentralized-execution methods. It offers formally rigorous specification of objectives over reward shaping.

entry.title: The Past Is Prologue: A Plug-in Controller for Selective Updates in Sequentially Evolving LLM Memory

author.name: Zihan Chen, Songwei Dong, Chengshuai Shi, Peng Wang, Song Wang, Cong Shen, Jundong Li

entry.summary: Janus is a plug-in memory controller for sequentially evolving LLM agent memory that decides whether to accept or reject each candidate memory update to avoid overwriting useful knowledge or over-specific rules. It uses a momentum trigger and a compact hybrid evaluation set of coverage, boundary, and fresh tasks.

entry.title: World-Model Collapse as a Phase Transition

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Zekun Cai

entry.summary: This paper frames world-model collapse in long-horizon language agents as a phase transition, showing that small changes in state load or horizon leave behavior nearly unchanged until a critical boundary triggers sudden collapse. A large grid search over deterministic tasks reveals a phase diagram with a solved plateau, transition band, and collapse floor.

entry.title: One Reflection Is Not Enough: Self-Correcting Autonomous Research via Multi-Hypothesis Failure Attribution

author.name: Jie Ma, Binfei Chu, Jie Gao, Jinlu Zhang, Yiwei Ma, Yi Tan, Jiayi Ji, Xiaoshuai Sun, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: SAGE is a self-correcting autonomous research agent whose core mechanism, Multi-Hypothesis Failure Attribution, replaces single free-form reflection with structured causal diagnosis that generates multiple hypotheses from trajectory features. It targets the brittle failure-recovery bottleneck when experiments fail.

entry.title: Think in English, Answer in Korean: Efficient Adaptation of Multilingual Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Utsav Garg, Sungjin Hong, Jason Jung, Justin Lee, Shaan Desai, Joon Hee Kim, Anirudh Shrinivason, Edmond Wen, Susie Park

entry.summary: LuckyStar 111B is a Cohere and LG CNS hybrid reasoning model post-trained from Command A for Korean-English enterprise agents, studying multilingual SFT, RL with verifiable rewards for tool use, language-consistency rewards, and 4-bit single-GPU quantization. It supports thinking in English while answering in Korean under practical serving constraints.

entry.title: Evo-PI: Aligning Medical Reasoning via Evolving Principle-Guided Supervision

author.name: Xianda Zheng, Huan Gao, Meng-Fen Chiang, Michael Witbrock, Kaiqi Zhao, Shangyang Li

entry.summary: ProtoPilot is a self-evolving multi-agent system for automated generation and physical execution of biological protocols, spanning 294 synthetic and molecular biology tasks with expert rubrics, device-level validity gates, and real wet-lab tests. It combines layer-wise verifiability, multi-agent orchestration, and a runtime-updated skill library.

entry.title: Robustness of Robotic Manipulation: Foundations and Frontiers

author.name: Yifei Dong, Zhanyi Sun, Lujie Yang, Manuel Baum, Kei Ikemura, Shuran Song, Florian T. Pokorny, Xianyi Cheng

entry.summary: Provides a systematic study and formal definition of robotic manipulation robustness, unifying disparate subfield framings into probabilistic and control-theoretic formulations and surveying foundations and frontiers. Aims to enable clearer cross-area analysis and communication.

entry.title: GRAPE: Graph-Augmented Prototype Explanations for Interactive Medical Image Diagnosis

author.name: Rasul Khanbayov, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: GRAPE is a graph-augmented prototype-based medical image classifier that models anatomical concept co-occurrence, flags conflicts between physician feedback and predicted findings, and can add new findings without full retraining. It reports meaningful macro-F1 gains and strong error-catching on chest imaging benchmarks.

entry.title: Hierarchical 3D Scene Graph Construction and Belief-based Planning for Semantic Navigation

author.name: Bing Wu, Zuyao Chen, Changwen Chen

entry.summary: This work builds a zero-shot semantic navigation framework that maintains an online hierarchical 3D scene graph over objects, zones, and regions, combined with belief-based planning to overcome myopic greedy exploration. It leverages foundation-model priors for structured global reasoning in unseen environments.

entry.title: TaxoMIL: Taxonomy-Constrained Learning for Hierarchical Whole Slide Image Analysis

author.name: Chaeyeon Lee, Khang Nguyen Quoc, Jinsol Song, Yosep Chong, Kwangil Yim, Jin Tae Kwak

entry.summary: TaxoMIL introduces taxonomy-constrained multiple instance learning for whole-slide image analysis, enforcing hierarchical coarse-to-fine diagnostic reasoning to avoid taxonomic hallucinations and parent-child label violations. It aligns computational pathology with clinical diagnostic hierarchies.

entry.title: WarpHammer: Densifying Scene Warps with 3D Object Priors for Extreme View Synthesis

author.name: Michael Green, Gavriel Habib, Dvir Samuel, Tal Berkovitz Shalev, Issar Tzachor, Rami Ben-Ari, Or Litany

entry.summary: WarpHammer is a training-free framework for extreme novel view synthesis that densifies sparse scene warps using an explicit 3D object reconstruction from a native 3D generative prior like SAM3D. It resolves failures under large orbital motion where warps become sparse and mirror-like artifacts appear.

entry.title: Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once

author.name: Fabio Quattrini, Carmine Zaccagnino, Enis Simsar, Marta Tintor\'e Gazulla, Rita Cucchiara, Alessio Tonioni, Silvia Cascianelli

entry.summary: MICE is a training-free strategy for scalable multi-instance concurrent image editing with Multimodal Diffusion Transformers, modifying joint-attention additive bias to prevent attribute leakage across region-specific edits. It enables efficient single-pass editing of multiple elements with less semantic interference.

entry.title: DataEvolver: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Data Construction for Text-Rich Image Generation

author.name: Siyu Yan, Yizhen Gao, Yilin Wang, Dongxing Mao, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: DataEvolver is a self-evolving multi-agent framework for constructing text-rich image-generation training data that recycles rejected samples' failure signals (OCR errors, semantic mismatches) rather than freezing accepted data. It aims to avoid repeating failure modes across construction rounds.

entry.title: When Does Learning to Stop Help? A Cost-Aware Study of Early Exits in Reasoning Models

author.name: Zhe Dong (University of Maine at Presque Isle), Fang Qin (Stanford University), Manish Shah (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: LearnStop is a hidden-state-free stopping mechanism for reasoning models that predicts prefix correctness from online signals like confidence, entropy, vote share, and backtracking density to decide when to halt. The study finds learned stopping helps in a task-dependent way across 18 task-model settings.

entry.title: AgRefactor: Self-Evolving Agentic Workflow for HLS Compatibility and Performance

author.name: Yang Zou, Zijian Ding, Yizhou Sun, Jason Cong

entry.summary: AgRefactor is a self-evolving multi-agent LLM workflow for refactoring general software into synthesizable High-Level Synthesis code, using an accumulating memory of factual and strategic knowledge. It aims to improve robustness and reduce cost on unseen programs.

entry.title: OpenLife: Toward Open-World Artificial Life with Autonomous LLM Agents

author.name: Atsushi Masumori, Itsuki Doi, Norihiro Maruyama, Ryosuke Takata, Takashi Ikegami

entry.summary: OpenLife proposes open-world artificial life using autonomous LLM agents with persistent memory, tool use, network access, and payments, moving ALIFE from closed simulations into the real social and economic world. Its proof-of-concept surrounds a stateless LLM with asynchronous processes and a budget-based metabolism.

entry.title: Agentic-Ideation: Sample Efficient Agentic Trajectories Synthesis for Scientific Ideation Agents

author.name: Keyu Zhao, Lingyan Kong, Fengli Xu, Yong Li

entry.summary: Agentic-Ideation tackles the prohibitively high data-synthesis cost of training agentic LLMs for scientific ideation by proposing a sample-efficient method for synthesizing agentic trajectories. It aims to move beyond rigid predefined workflows toward flexible autonomous research reasoning.

entry.title: Xiaomi-GUI-0 Technical Report

author.name: Wanxia Cao, Chengzhen Duan, Pei Fu, Pengzhi Gao, Niu Lian, Fazhan Liu, Hui Liu, Heng Qu, Qinzhuo Wu, Zhehao Yu, Tongbo Chen, Shiqi Cui, Anan Du, Shukai Jia, Yuanfa Li, Yike Liu, Wenchao Lu, Haoyuan Sun, Jiatong Sun, Cheng Tan, Yajie Wang, Changqiao Wu, Tao Xiong, Jiahui Yang, Yuxuan Yuan, Ruoceng Zhang, Shaojie Zhang, Jian Zhu, Jian Luan, Cong Zou

entry.summary: Xiaomi-GUI-0 is a technical report on a GUI agent built on vision-language models to complete real-app tasks end-to-end, arguing that offline-trajectory and simulated-benchmark training fails to capture real-world execution stability with permission dialogs, payment authentication, and risk control. It targets closing the gap between benchmark scores and real usability.

entry.title: RAISE: LLM-based Automated Heuristic Design with Robust Adversary Instance Search

author.name: Fei Liu, Alessio Figalli, Patrick Owen, Nicola Serra

entry.summary: RAISE integrates constrained worst-case adversarial instance search within a principled neighborhood of the training distribution into the LLM-based evolutionary loop for automated heuristic design. This makes discovered heuristics robust to real-world distributional shifts rather than overfitting a fixed training set.

entry.title: Large Databases Need Small, Open-Weight Language Models

author.name: Parker Glenn, Alfy Samuel

entry.summary: This paper shows that quantized open-weight models running locally on 16GB of VRAM can match or exceed closed-source APIs for LM-enhanced relational database operators at lower latency and a fraction of the cost. It details the system optimizations needed to make open-weight small models effective for large-database integration.

entry.title: On the Convergence of Self-Improving Online LLM Alignment

author.name: Xudong Wu, Pangpang Liu, Vaneet Aggarwal, Jiayu Chen

entry.summary: Provides the first formal convergence analysis of the Self-Improving Alignment (SAIL) algorithm, identifying that its objective is not strongly concave, and proposes SAIL-RevKL adding a reverse-KL penalty to improve the optimization landscape and guarantee convergence. Strengthens theoretical foundations for online self-improving alignment.

entry.title: LUNA: Learning Universal 3D Human Animation Beyond Skinning

author.name: Peng Li, Rawal Khirodkar, Junxuan Li, Yuan Dong, Chen Cao, Yuan Liu, Wenhan Luo, Yike Guo, Shunsuke Saito

entry.summary: LUNA is an LBS-free universal neural animation model that maps 2D controls (images, keypoints, sketches, unseen characters) directly into 3D Gaussian deformations for photorealistic animatable avatars, bypassing parametric body fitting via a transformer motion regressor disentangling global rigid from local dynamics. Aims to overcome expressivity limits and fitting artifacts.

entry.title: AVTok: 1D Unified Tokenization for Holistic Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Kien T. Pham, I Chieh Chen, Qifeng Chen, Long Chen

entry.summary: AVTok proposes a unified 1D tokenizer for joint audio-video generation, using a dual-stream transformer with a shared encoder-decoder rather than separate per-modality branches. This reduces the representation gap and computational cost of holistic sounding-video synthesis with fine-grained audio-visual synchronization.

entry.title: TerraDiT-$\Omega$: Unified Spatial Control for Satellite Image Synthesis with Any Geospatial Primitive

author.name: Brian Wei, Srikumar Sastry, Daniel Cher, Eric Xing, Nathan Jacobs

entry.summary: TerraDiT-Omega is a unified spatial-control diffusion framework for satellite image synthesis that conditions directly on native geospatial primitives (polygons, polylines, boxes, points) rather than dense rasters or sparse prompts. It preserves compatibility with vector GIS data while balancing annotation cost and fidelity.

entry.title: AnyMatch: Supercharging Universal Multi-Modal Image Matching with Large-Scale Single-View Images

author.name: Meng Yang, Zizhuo Li, Linfeng Tang, Fan Fan, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: AnyMatch generates large-scale multi-modal image matching training data from abundant single-view images by combining monocular depth, 3D reprojection, diffusion inpainting, and cross-modal translation. It addresses the scarcity of geometrically annotated multi-modal matching datasets.

entry.title: Do Not Break the Vessels: Structure-Preserving Mean Flow for Vascular Image Translation

author.name: Changjin Sun, Zhuo Hu, Kaini Wang, Baixuan Wu, Shuo Gao, Runan Zheng, Cheng Xue, Yudong Zhang, Guangquan Zhou

entry.summary: SPMF frames vascular image translation as a topology-invariant transport process, deriving an orthogonality constraint to make structure preservation an invariant of the generative process rather than only the output. It targets anatomically faithful vessel reconstruction for clinical reliability.

entry.title: Horizon3D: Sparse Radar-Camera Fusion for Long-Range 3D Perception in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Geonho Bang, Geunju Baek, Dongyoung Lee, Wonjun Jeong, Jun Won Choi

entry.summary: Horizon3D is a sparse radar-camera fusion framework for long-range 3D detection that combines Gaussian primitives with sparse BEV features and temporal fusion for distant, fast-moving objects. It targets highway-speed detection where existing radar-camera methods degrade at extended ranges.

entry.title: WildProp: Visual Estimation of Wildlife Body Proportions at Scale

author.name: Mustafa Chasmai, Aaron Sun, Subhransu Maji

entry.summary: WildProp is a training-free framework that estimates wildlife body-proportion distributions from unconstrained image repositories by casting morphometry as retrieval-driven correspondence using foundation-model features. It enables scalable population-level ecological measurement without controlled imaging.

entry.title: ExPLoRe: Expert Patch-Level Loss Routing for Multi-Objective Masked Image Modeling

author.name: Konstantinos Georgiou, Maofeng Tang, Hairong Qi

entry.summary: ExPLoRe repurposes Soft Mixture-of-Experts dispatch weights as learned per-patch loss coefficients for multi-objective masked image modeling, enabling content-dependent specialization across distillation, alignment, and reconstruction objectives. A detach ablation confirms loss-coupling as the core mechanism.

entry.title: Accelerated Likelihood Maximization for Diffusion-based Versatile Content Generation

author.name: Hyunsoo Lee, Inwoo Hwang, Young Min Kim

entry.summary: ALM is a training-free sampling strategy integrated into reverse diffusion that explicitly optimizes over unobserved variables via accelerated likelihood maximization, extending diffusion models to versatile conditional content generation. It aims for globally consistent results without task-specific training.

entry.title: Language-Assisted Super-Resolution from Real-World Low-Resolution Patches

author.name: Joonkyu Park, Kyoung Mu Lee

entry.summary: This work performs real-world super-resolution using language assistance and the observation that within a single high-quality image, distant regions act as natural LR patches and near regions as HR, enabling extraction of real degradation-induced training pairs. It addresses poor generalization of synthetically degraded SR training.

entry.title: MS-Resampler: Multi-Scope Visual Resampling for Efficient Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Zhongyang Li, Yaqian Li, Faming Fang, Rinyoichi Takezoe, Zi-Hao Bo, Cheng Qian, Mo Guang, Guixu Zhang, Kaiwen Long

entry.summary: MS-Resampler is a multi-scope visual resampling framework for multimodal LLMs that injects spatial scope priors into resampling attention so different branches aggregate visual information at different granularities within a fixed token budget. It addresses the loss of fine-grained local evidence in single-scope global cross-attention resamplers.

entry.title: AugSplat: Radiance Field-Informed Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Settings

author.name: Lorenzo Lazzaroni, Riccardo Bollati, Daniel Barath, Michael Niemeyer, Keisuke Tateno

entry.summary: AugSplat improves sparse-view Gaussian Splatting by using neural radiance field information to guide initialization, addressing GS sensitivity to incomplete or noisy point-cloud geometry from limited observations. It combines NeRF robustness with GS real-time rendering.

entry.title: LiteMatch: Lightweight Zero-Shot Stereo Matching via Cost Volume Stabilization

author.name: Md Raqib Khan, Santosh Kumar Vipparthi, Subrahmanyam Murala

entry.summary: PRISM reinterprets single-image reflection removal as a latent linear separation problem, exploiting that pretrained VAE latent spaces have lower cross-layer coherence than pixel space, and learns a flow-matching velocity field for decomposition. It offers a more favorable working space for this ill-posed task.

entry.title: Learning Locomotion on Discrete Terrain via Minimal Proximity Sensing

author.name: Jiale Fan, Connor Flynn, Tianao Xu, Junzhe He, Andrei Cramariuc, Marco Hutter, Robert Baines

entry.summary: This work embeds low-cost, high-frequency infrared proximity sensors in a quadruped's feet to provide pre-contact feedback for locomotion over discrete terrain, avoiding the latency and occlusion issues of LiDAR or depth cameras. It offers a lightweight sensing alternative that bridges reactive proprioception and heavy global perception.

entry.title: DVG-WM: Disentangled Video Generation Enables Efficient Embodied World Model for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Ziyu Shan, Zhenyu Wu, Xiaofeng Wang, Zheng Zhu, Ziwei Wang

entry.summary: DVG-WM is an embodied world model that decouples world modeling into separate dynamics learning and visual synthesis, resolving the tension between fast low-level temporal reasoning and high-resolution frame generation. This disentanglement aims to enable efficient planning without sacrificing contact-rich detail.

entry.title: "Correct Answer Features" Cannot Explain Multiple Choice Capabilities

author.name: Koby Lewis

entry.summary: This interpretability post presents theoretical and empirical evidence that LLMs cannot rely exclusively on a hypothesized correct-answer feature (a direction encoding option correctness on final tokens) to answer multiple choice questions, using direct-effect head attribution. It challenges a clean but incomplete mechanistic account.

entry.title: Contrastive Reflection for Iterative Prompt Optimization

author.name: Derek Koh, Jinghui Mo, Benjamin H. Le, Jiening Zhan, Baofen Zheng, Kevin Bevis, Nathaniel C. Owen, Lauren Elizabeth Charney, Wenqiong Liu, Jingwei Wu

entry.summary: Contrastive Reflection is an iterative prompt-optimization framework that treats prompt improvement as debugging rather than blind search, contrasting failing versus nearby working behaviors in agentic information-retrieval workflows. It targets held-out quality gains without introducing regressions.

entry.title: ACE: Pluggable Adaptive Context Elasticizer across Agents

author.name: Ning Liao, Zihao Long, Xiaoxing Wang, Xue Yang, Yaoming Wang, Ziyuan Zhuang, Xunliang Cai, Rongxiang Weng, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: ACE is a plug-and-play adaptive context module that elastically orchestrates historical step information into an agent's context at each decision step, maintaining a lossless message layer so compressed or discarded information can be recovered when later relevant. It addresses the inflexibility and irreversibility of truncation and summarization.

entry.title: Can LLMs Imagine Moral Alternatives Beyond Binary Dilemmas?

author.name: Jongchan Choi, Nari Yang, Sung Soo Park, Jaemin Cho, Han Seoyoung, Haerin Shin, Jun-Hyung Park

entry.summary: Introduces MoralAltDataset, 307 moral dilemmas augmented with compromise and reframed alternatives, to test whether LLMs and humans move beyond binary choices when non-obvious options appear. Finds that compromise alternatives substantially reshape moral judgments across 15 models, probing a cognitive capacity typically ignored in moral evaluation.

entry.title: Dense Structural Priors for Sparse Functional Landmark Localization in Surgical Videos

author.name: Chenyan Jing, Hao Ding, Lalithkumar Seenivasan, Jacob M. Delgado L\'opez, Mathias Unberath

entry.summary: This work localizes sparse, action-aware functional surgical landmarks (e.g., instrument tips/anchors) by using SAM 3 zero-shot masks as dense structural priors within a lightweight refinement network. It avoids manual pixel-level annotation while capturing action-conditioned semantics that segmentation alone misses.

entry.title: JacobianAvatar: Temporally Consistent Semi-rigid Avatar Reconstruction from a Monocular Video

author.name: Changyeon Won, Min-Gyu Park, Seonghwan Park, Ju Hong Yoon, Hae-Gon Jeon

entry.summary: JacobianAvatar reconstructs temporally consistent semi-rigid human avatars with clothing dynamics from monocular video using neural Jacobian fields and a Poisson-based deformation solver. It introduces constrained solvers and regularizers to handle self-occlusion and invisible surfaces.

entry.title: WaterGen: Decoupling Scene and Medium in Underwater Image Generation

author.name: Jiayi Wu, Tianfu Wang, Tianyi Xiong, Dehao Yuan, Xiaomin Lin, Md Jahidul Islam, Cornelia Fermuller, Christopher Metzler, Yiannis Aloimonos

entry.summary: WaterGen generates realistic, diverse underwater images with decoupled control over scene content and water-medium effects, addressing scarcity of underwater training data. It combines controllability with physical accuracy of medium effects that prior methods handle only partially.

entry.title: HSDF-Lane: Height-Aligned Signed Distance Field with Semantic Lane Prior for 3D Lane Detection

author.name: Jiyong Boo, Byeongin Joung, Hyemin Yang, Kuk-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: HSDF-Lane models the road surface as a height-aligned signed distance field over a dense 3D feature volume with a semantic lane prior, replacing flat-ground BEV assumptions and sparse anchor regression for monocular 3D lane detection. It integrates recovered geometry into semantic understanding rather than just spatial transformation.

entry.title: GaussianMap: Learning Gaussian Representation for Multi-Sensor Online HD Map Construction

author.name: Hongyu Lyu, Julie Stephany Berrio Perez, Mao Shan, Stewart Worrall

entry.summary: GaussianMap learns an adaptive Gaussian representation for multi-sensor online HD map construction, replacing redundant fixed-resolution dense BEV grids that poorly suit spatially sparse map elements requiring fine localization. It aims for more efficient and accurate vectorized map prediction.

entry.title: AeroVerse-SatAgent: UAV-Satellite Collaborative Spatial Reasoning Inspired by the Dual Visual Pathway Theory of Cognitive Neuroscience

author.name: Wenyi Zhang, Fanglong Yao, Youzhi Liu, Peng Hu, Zhengqiu Zhu, Chen Gao, Xian Sun, Kun Fu

entry.summary: SatAgent is a UAV-satellite collaborative spatial reasoning model inspired by the dual visual pathway theory, jointly leveraging satellite and UAV perspectives with explicit geometric modeling to overcome single-view occlusion and perspective distortion. It targets robust aerospace embodied spatial reasoning.

entry.title: MV-GEL: Language-Driven Multi-View Geometric Entity Localization on Meshes

author.name: Kartik Bali, Roland Aydin

entry.summary: MV-GEL grounds language-specified geometric entities (edges, planar and curved surfaces) on 3D meshes using a multi-view approach that handles viewpoint-dependent occlusion and foreshortening. It extends VLM referring-segmentation capabilities from images to structured 3D geometry for CAD, robotics, and simulation.

entry.title: AgentBound: Verifiable Behavioral Governance for Autonomous AI Agents

author.name: Anuj Kaul, Qianlong Lan, Pranay Gupta

entry.summary: AgentBound is a runtime governance framework that evaluates each proposed autonomous-agent action against three independent authorities: delegated authorization, owner-signed behavioral constitutions, and site action contracts. It provides verifiable behavioral oversight beyond identity-based authorization.

entry.title: DDIAgents: Mechanism-Conditioned Context Flow for Drug-Drug Interaction Prediction

author.name: Zhenqian Shen, Yu Liu, Xiaoyi Fu, Quanming Yao

entry.summary: DDIAgents is a mechanism-conditioned multi-agent framework for drug-drug interaction prediction that routes mechanism-relevant biomedical knowledge to specialized expert agents and aggregates their analyses. It produces interpretable agent-level rationales while reducing irrelevant information.

entry.title: Scenario Generation for Testing of Autonomous Driving Systems Using Real-World Failure Records

author.name: Anjali Parashar, Chuchu Fan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a scenario generation pipeline for testing autonomous driving systems using real-world failure records, extracting categorical and contextual information rather than relying on fixed hand-designed templates. It aims to ground pre-deployment testing in realistic failure conditions.

entry.title: Embodied CAD: Solver-Grounded LLM Agents for Parametric B-Rep Assembly Modeling

author.name: Fumin Liu, Haoyu Zhou, Fei Hao, Lin Yang

entry.summary: Embodied CAD provides solver-grounded LLM agents for parametric B-Rep assembly modeling, iteratively selecting actions from a stratified skill library, resolving them into typed geometric operations, executing in a CAD kernel, and using solver feedback to plan and repair. This yields editable parametric geometry rather than one-shot scripts.

entry.title: Learning to Select, Not Relearn: Hard-Routed Mixtures of Reasoning LoRAs

author.name: Seyed Alireza Molavi, Zhan Su, Yan Hu, Peyman Sheikholharam Mashhadi, Stefan Byttner, Prayag Tiwari

entry.summary: Hard-Routed MoR-LoRA composes independently trained frozen reasoning LoRA experts via unit-scale hard selection rather than soft weighted mixtures, preserving the additive-update scale under which each adapter was trained. Experts are trained with reinforcement learning from verifiable feedback then frozen and routed.

entry.title: CDR-Bench: Evaluating Faithful Execution of Compositional, Order-Sensitive Data Refinement Recipes

author.name: Yuchen Huang, Xiang Li, Zhenqing Ling, Sijia Li, Qianli Shen, Daoyuan Chen, Yi R. Fung, Yaliang Li

entry.summary: CDR-Bench is a benchmark of 3462 tasks across four data-refinement domains and 29 operators testing whether LLMs faithfully execute compositional, order-sensitive multi-step refinement recipes over evolving text. It evaluates atomic, order-agnostic, and order-sensitive settings against deterministic reference outputs.

entry.title: Probing Stylistic Appropriation using Large Language Models: An Evaluation Framework for Copyright Infringement under EU Law

author.name: Noah Scharrenberg, Chang Sun

entry.summary: Introduces PSALM, an LLM-as-a-judge framework with ten evaluators that operationalizes EU copyright doctrine (substantial similarity, stylistic and narrative overlap, statutory exceptions) to assess whether model outputs infringe beyond verbatim copying. Addresses the gap between technical memorization safeguards and legal standards of style appropriation.

entry.title: Resolving superposition in AI for interpretability and cross-modal alignment in patient-neuronal images

author.name: Jisung Park, Seohyeon Kang, Daeun Yoo, Eunsu Lee, Seoin Cho, Wooyeop Choi, Ian Choi, James R. Evan, Daesoo Kim, Sonia Gandhi, Minee L. Choi

entry.summary: Uses sparse autoencoders trained on over 100,000 multiplexed images of patient-derived Parkinson's and healthy neurons to resolve superposition, arguing that superposition distorts latent-space geometry and hinders interpretability and cross-modal alignment. Applies interpretability tools to biological imaging analysis.

entry.title: Geometry-Preserving Orthonormal Initialization for Low-Rank Adaptation in RLVR
