author.name: Ruijia Zhang, Jiacheng Zhu, Hanqing Zhu, Laixi Shi

entry.summary: Analyzes LoRA initialization under reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), showing structured variants like PiSSA and MiLoRA that excel under SFT can underperform and destabilize under RLVR, and proves orthonormal initialization minimizes the gap to full fine-tuning. Recommends geometry-preserving orthonormal init for RLVR.

entry.title: PiLoT v2: Pixel-to-Orthogonal Map Alignment for Free-view UAV Geo-localization

author.name: Xinyi Liu, Xiaoya Cheng, Rouwan Wu, Zhaochen Wang, Shen Yan, Maojun Zhang, Yu Liu

entry.summary: PiLoT v2 replaces heavy 3D-mesh-based UAV geo-localization with lightweight direct pixel-to-orthogonal-map registration using orthophoto maps and surface models. It drastically reduces storage and rendering costs for embedded deployment in GNSS-denied environments.

entry.title: AC3S: Adaptive Conditioning for 3D-Aware Synthetic Data Generation

author.name: Eric Ji, Qiran Hu, Wufei Ma, Sarthak Jain, Yingying Li, Minh N. Do, Yaoyao Liu

entry.summary: AC3S is a diffusion-based synthetic-data framework that enforces 3D structure and pose consistency via adaptive conditioning, using a self-supervised mechanism to avoid over-conditioning artifacts that degrade realism. It aims to produce photorealistic, 3D-aware training data.

entry.title: UHD-MFF: Shattering Barriers in Multi-Focus Ultra-High-Definition Image Fusion via Learnable Lookup Tables

author.name: Yibing Zhang, Xunpeng Yi, Qinglong Yan, Yeda Wang, Han Xu, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: UHD-MFF introduces the first large-scale ultra-high-definition multi-focus fusion dataset and UMF-LUT, a scale-specialized learnable lookup-table framework with coarse-region and detail-edge tables for efficient UHD fusion. It addresses data, adaptability, and deployment barriers for high-resolution multi-focus fusion.

entry.title: Deep Spectral Models for Robust Dental Shape Generation

author.name: Tibor Kub\'ik, Fran\c{c}ois Guibault, Michal \v{S}pan\v{e}l, Herv\'e Lombaert

entry.summary: ToothForge is a deep spectral generative framework that models dental crown geometry from compact intrinsic representations using synchronized spectral embeddings to handle varying mesh connectivity and stabilize Laplace-Beltrami eigenbases. It enables efficient shape generation from small datasets.

entry.title: Fully Automated High-Precision Segmentation of Retinal Atrophy and Ellipsoid Zone Thickness in OCT: A Reliable Tool for Real-World GA Monitoring

author.name: Wolf-Dieter Vogl, Hlynur Skulason, Oliver Leingang, Ursula Schmidt-Erfurth, Amir Sadeghipour, Ariadne Whitby

entry.summary: This paper presents a fully automated deep-learning pipeline for high-precision OCT segmentation of geographic atrophy biomarkers including RPE loss, ellipsoid zone loss, and EZ thinning, using three specialized segmentation models developed on 298 SD-OCT volumes. It aims to be a reliable tool for real-world GA monitoring.

entry.title: PrISM-IQA: Image Quality Assessment Made Practical for Smartphone Photography

author.name: Shuyan Zhai, Jiaqi He, Weixia Zhang, Liang Wang, Zhenjie Lee, Zufeng Zhang, Kede Ma

entry.summary: PrISM-IQA reformulates smartphone image quality assessment as a multi-issue ordinal diagnosis, predicting ordered severity levels (absent, minor, severe, critical) for each ISP-relevant issue rather than a single scalar score. It aligns IQA with practical image-signal-processor tuning workflows.

entry.title: Spatial Reasoning via Modality Switching Between Language and Symbolic Representation

author.name: Shreya Rajpal, Tanawan Premsri, Parisa Kordjamshidi

entry.summary: This paper studies whether grounding multi-hop textual-spatial stories into geometry-aware modalities like grids improves reasoning over natural language, and whether models can decide when to switch modalities. It introduces a switching metric based on trustworthiness and complexity signals.

entry.title: Modality-Driven Search with Holistic Trace Judging for ARC-AGI-2

author.name: Johan Land

entry.summary: This single-author solver for ARC-AGI-2 treats reasoning modalities as search operators, generating diverse candidates independently across text, image, and code channels, and uses context-preserving holistic judging that jointly compares all traces in one long-context prompt. This recovers correct minority hypotheses that self-consistency or majority voting miss.

entry.title: 3D HAMSTER: Bridging Planning and Control in Hierarchical Vision Language Action Models through 3D Trajectory Guidance

author.name: Dongyoon Hwang, Byungkun Lee, Dongjin Kim, Hyojin Jang, Hoiyeong Jin, Jueun Mun, Minho Park, Hojoon Lee, Hyunseung Kim, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: 3D HAMSTER upgrades hierarchical vision-language-action robotics by having the VLM planner output metrically reliable 3D end-effector trajectories instead of depth-ambiguous 2D guidance, matching the 3D point-cloud space of low-level policies. This closes a geometric mismatch that distorts trajectories.

entry.title: UniTac: A Unified Multimodal Model for Cross-Sensor Tactile Understanding and Generation

author.name: Jiahang Tu, Fengyu Yang, Chenyang Ma, Xihang Yu, Ziyao Zeng, Shaokai Wu, Hanbin Zhao, Zhi Tao, Chao Zhang, Hui Qian, Alex Wong

entry.summary: UniTac is presented as the first unified multimodal model for cross-sensor tactile understanding and generation, modeling touch as a non-contact to contact transition with a dual-level representation encoding sensor and object attributes. Supports tasks like object property description and sensor identification.

entry.title: Intrinsic decomposition and editing of 3D Gaussian splats

author.name: Alexandre Lanvin, Jeffrey Hu, Simon Lucas, Adrien Bousseau, George Drettakis

entry.summary: Extends intrinsic decomposition (albedo, shading, view-dependent residuals) to Gaussian-splatting radiance fields by modeling layers as independent Gaussian sets and using data-driven optimization to disentangle multi-view photographs, enabling relighting-preserving color and texture edits. Advances editable 3D scene representations.

entry.title: WorldRoamBench: An Open-World Benchmark for Long-Horizon Stability of Interactive World Models

author.name: Ting-Bing Xu, Jiacheng Sui, Zhe Gao, Kewei Shi, Wenjin Yang, Zhicheng Liu, Zhaoxu Sun, Mingchao Sun, Hongyu Pan, Fan Jiang, Mu Xu, Qi Fan, Yong Li, Baoquan Chen

entry.summary: WorldRoamBench is an open-world benchmark evaluating long-horizon stability of interactive world models across action, vision, physics, and memory, with metrics for per-frame action fidelity, mid-sequence drift, controllability-gated physics, and action-decoupled memory. Addresses gaps in trajectory-level-only evaluation of world models.

entry.title: No Adaptation Without Observation: Observability-Constrained Test-Time Prompt Tuning for LiDAR Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Linlian Jiang, Wentao Ju, Sadman Rakib Pinon, Jianwei Xian, Zhixiang Chi, Xinxin Zuo, Yang Wang

entry.summary: This work proposes an observability-constrained, geometry-aware test-time prompt tuning framework for LiDAR semantic segmentation, estimating per-location sensing reliability to avoid destabilizing global parameter updates. It tackles spatially heteroscedastic pseudo-label reliability under real-world sensor conditions.

entry.title: WarpI2I: Image Warping for Image-to-Image Translation

author.name: Shen Zheng, Anurag Ghosh, Gaurav Parmar, Srinivasa Narasimhan

entry.summary: WarpI2I proposes a saliency-guided warp-unwarp framework that reallocates latent spatial capacity toward salient regions before encoding, preserving fine structures in diffusion-based image-to-image translation. It also adds an outpainting-based scheme to handle boundaries after inverse warping.

entry.title: Domain Adaptive Object Detection via Dual-Stream Bilevel-Cycle Optimization

author.name: Yannan Chen, Wenqiang Wang, Ruoyu Chen, Jiancheng Wang, Mingbo Yang, Yaowei Wang, Wei Wang, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: This paper extends cycle self-training to domain-adaptive object detection via dual-stream bilevel-cycle optimization, addressing unreliable pseudo-labels from classification and localization errors. It tackles challenges specific to detection that classification-oriented CST does not handle.

entry.title: What Capable Agents Must Know: Why AI Consciousness May Be an Inevitable Byproduct of Capability

author.name: Aran Nayebi

entry.summary: Aran Nayebi argues, backed by a UAI 2026 paper, that certain signatures of consciousness (per theories like global workspace) may be inevitable byproducts of capability in capable agents, and proposes empirical falsifiable tests derived from neuroscience theories. It bridges NeuroAI and machine consciousness debates with a quantitative angle.

entry.title: Agentic RAG-VLM: Affordance-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Self-Reflective Planning for Robotic Grasping

author.name: Tao Chen, Lizheng Liu, Jiaxu Wang, Ziyue Jiang, Ruiqi Tian, JiGuang Huo, Zhongxue Gan

entry.summary: Agentic RAG-VLM integrates retrieval-augmented generation with vision-language models and self-reflective planning for robotic grasping, incorporating physical affordances like handle graspability and material fragility rather than relying on visual similarity alone. It enables closed-loop spatial reasoning and failure recovery.

entry.title: Long-term Traffic Simulation via Structured Autoregressive Modeling

author.name: Lingyu Xiao, Zexin Feng, Xintao Yan

entry.summary: This paper proposes structured autoregressive modeling for long-horizon traffic simulation, leveraging frozen small LLMs whose attention transferability and token-distribution consistency enable rapid adaptation to traffic sequences with dynamic agent counts. It positions traffic simulation as a world model for autonomous driving.

entry.title: Ask the World Before Acting: Budgeted Environment Probing for World-Model Calibration

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Zekun Cai

entry.summary: This paper proposes a budgeted probing operator letting long-horizon language agents query the environment about one belief field before acting and write the answer back into their world model, treating interaction as a scarce calibration resource. It distinguishes procedural beliefs repairable by targeted checks from more costly ones.

entry.title: FinPersona-Bench: A Benchmark for Longitudinal Psychometric Stability of Autonomous Financial Agents

author.name: Muhammad Usman Safder (Steve), Ayesha Gull (Steve), Rania Elbadry (Steve), Fan Zhang (Steve), Yankai Chen (Steve), Xueqing Peng (Steve), Xue (Steve), Liu, Preslav Nakov, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: FinPersona-Bench introduces a simulation benchmark measuring Mandate Salience Decay, the phenomenon where autonomous financial LLM agents gradually lose adherence to initial behavioral mandates over long horizons. Uses a synthetic market decoupling price from hidden value to falsifiably test failure modes like panic-selling and signal-less trading.

entry.title: ECHO: Prune to act, trace to learn with selective turn memory in agentic RL

author.name: Zijun Xie, Binbin Zheng, Enlei Gong, Jihua Liu, Yuyang You, Lingfeng Liu, Jiayao Tang, Guanqun Zhao, Aoqi Hu, Zeyu Chen

entry.summary: ECHO is an agentic RL method for long-horizon language agents that prunes context to act while keeping source-addressable turn memory for learning, so outcome-based RL can align policy updates with the specific evidence supporting successful answers. Addresses degraded evidence reuse from context truncation and summarization.

entry.title: FROST: Training-Free Few-Shot Segmentation with Frozen Features and Nonparametric Statistics

author.name: Junghwan Park

entry.summary: FROST performs training-free few-shot segmentation using frozen self-supervised features and nonparametric statistics, arguing a class is better modeled as a distribution than a single prototype. It targets remote-sensing where labels are scarce and imagery differs from pretraining data.

entry.title: Beyond Single Character: Evaluating MLLMs for Sentence-Level Oracle Bone Inscription Understanding

author.name: Ziqi Li, Zijian Chen, Tingzhu Chen, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: S-OBI introduces a benchmark for sentence-level oracle bone inscription understanding by multimodal LLMs, moving beyond character-level recognition to capture textual coherence and context in divination charges. It synthesizes clear standardized OBI instances via glyph substitution to evaluate MLLMs.

entry.title: Wavelet-Optimized Pseudo-3D Accelerated Diffusion Model for Truncated Computed Laminography

author.name: Genyuan Zhang, Junyao Wang, Chuandong Tan, Fenglin Liu, Yongning Zhou

entry.summary: This work proposes a wavelet-optimized pseudo-3D accelerated diffusion model for truncated computed laminography, extending reconstruction beyond the field of view and enforcing data consistency across data-complete, incomplete, and free regions. It targets severe truncation artifacts in nondestructive testing.

entry.title: RCL-Mamba: A Dual-domain State Space Model for Measurement-oriented Image Restoration in Rotational Sparse-View Scanning Computed Laminography

author.name: Xuyang Duan, Genyuan Zhang, Zhenjiang Dong, Chuandong Tan, Zihao Wang, Junyao Wang, Fenglin Liu

entry.summary: RCL-Mamba is a dual-domain state-space model for rotational sparse-view computed laminography that first corrects rotational blur in the projection domain then removes sparse artifacts in the image domain via cascaded joint processing. It addresses cross-domain degradations from rapid sparse-view scanning.

entry.title: MAPE: Defending Against Transferable Adversarial Attacks Using Multi-Source Adversarial Perturbations Elimination

author.name: Xinlei Liu, Jichao Xie, Tao Hu, Peng Yi, Yuxiang Hu, Shumin Huo, Zhen Zhang

entry.summary: MAPE defends against transferable adversarial attacks via multi-source adversarial perturbation elimination, combining a single-source elimination mechanism with a probabilistic scheduling algorithm over pretrained models. It targets the high stealthiness of transferable attacks that avoid reliance on target model outputs.

entry.title: HVPNet: A Bio-Inspired Network for General Salient and Camouflaged Object Detection

author.name: Jiawei Xu, Qiangqiang Zhou, Zhouping Li, Yanjiao Shi, Yugen Yi, Jiacong Yu

entry.summary: HVPNet is a bio-inspired network for unified salient and camouflaged object detection that draws on the human visual process to achieve simpler, efficient modeling instead of complex cross-modal fusion. It questions whether heavy fusion structures are necessary for accurate detection.

entry.title: Thinking Before Retrieving: Robust Zero-Shot Composed Image Retrieval via Strategic Planning and Self-Criticism

author.name: Gunho Jung, Jeong-Woo Park, Seon Bin Kim, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: This work improves zero-shot composed image retrieval by replacing single-pass query fusion with strategic planning and self-criticism, letting the model detect and correct semantic distortions between the reference image and modification text. It builds retrieval queries in a frozen vision-language embedding space at inference.

entry.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Floating-Point Error Classification

author.name: Lisa Taldir (LI-PaRAD), Muhammad Ahmad Saeed (LI-PaRAD), David Defour (LI-PaRAD), Pablo de Oliveira Castro (LI-PaRAD), Eric Petit

entry.summary: InterFLOPBench is a benchmark of 90 C kernels and 1130 samples for evaluating whether LLMs can statically detect and classify six categories of floating-point errors as multi-label classification. Recent reasoning models exceed 0.88 F1 overall.

entry.title: An Agentic AI Framework to Accelerate Scientific Discovery in Plant Phenotyping

author.name: Renan Souza, Daniel Rosendo, Kelsey Carter, John Lagergren, Fr\'ed\'eric Suter, Shelaine L. Curd, Gerald A. Tuskan, Rafael Ferreira da Silva, David Weston

entry.summary: This ORNL work presents an end-to-end agentic AI framework turning a high-throughput plant phenotyping facility into an interactive discovery platform, with a conversational Co-Scientist Agent translating natural-language questions into analysis. It addresses the bottleneck where trait extraction remains manual and post-hoc despite automated imaging.

entry.title: CSO-LLM: Class Subspace Orthogonalization for Post-Training Backdoor Detection and Trigger Inversion in LLMs

author.name: Zhengxing Li, David J. Miller, Guangmingmei Yang, George Kesidis

entry.summary: CSO-LLM proposes class subspace orthogonalization for post-training backdoor detection and trigger inversion in LLMs treated as classifiers, addressing the discrete input space and lack of blacklist tokens. It provides a plug-and-play detection paradigm adapted from image-domain methods.

entry.title: Visual Semantic Entropy: Do Vision Language Models Recognize Visual Ambiguity?

author.name: Ta Duc Huy, Trang Nguyen, Townim Chowdhury, Ankit Yadav, Minh-Son To, Zhibin Liao, Johan W. Verjans, Vu Minh Hieu Phan

entry.summary: Analyzes why Semantic Entropy underestimates uncertainty on visually ambiguous inputs, showing overconfident visual embeddings suppress output diversity, and that perturbation-based methods are dominated by textual rather than visual variability. Motivates uncertainty measures grounded in visual evidence for VLMs.

entry.title: Look But Don't Touch with Sparse Autoencoders for Unlearning in Diffusion Models

author.name: Enrico Cassano, Riccardo Renzulli, Rayyan Ahmed, Marco Grangetto, Stephan Alaniz

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates sparse autoencoders for concept unlearning in diffusion models, showing that while SAEs reliably detect and localize semantic concepts, direct latent intervention causes out-of-distribution activations and artifacts. Proposes using SAEs purely as detectors and replacing patch embeddings instead of directly steering latents.

entry.title: Z-1: Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Lang Cao, Renhong Chen, Luyi Li, Peng Wang, Mofan Peng, Yitong Li

entry.summary: Z-1 is an RL post-training framework for flow-based vision-language-action models built on pi_0.5, using task-wise GRPO across 24 RoboCasa tasks with only publicly released demonstrations for SFT, improving beyond behavior cloning. Focuses on efficient, stable online RL for robot manipulation policies.

entry.title: GR2 Technical Report

author.name: Yufei Li (Yongkang), Zaiwei Zhang (Yongkang), Mingfu Liang (Yongkang), Kavosh Asadi (Yongkang), Jay Xu (Yongkang), Jimmy Kim (Yongkang), Chongyang Bai (Yongkang), Jieyi Zhang (Yongkang), Hongye Xie (Yongkang), Prachi Agrawal (Yongkang), Dian Yu (Yongkang), Tianyi Chen (Yongkang), Jean-Pascal Billaud (Yongkang), Garret Buell (Yongkang), YK (Yongkang), Zhu (Yang), Sachin Patil (Yang), Brooke Bian (Yang), Zhou Fang (Yang), Kevin Huang (Yang), Shiva Sudanagunta (Yang), Yuzhen Huang (Yang), Emma Lu (Yang), Chris O'Brien (Yang), Yang Song (Yang), Lihong Li (Yang), Jacob Tao (Yang), Zhicheng Zhu (Yang), Chao Li (Yang), Gaoxiang Liu (Yang), Neil Wu (Yang), Zhongyin Hu (Yang), Li Han (Yang), Loki Chen (Yang), Ming Lei (Yang), Greg Rehm (Yang), Siyuan Song (Yang), Tianwei Zhang (Yang), Li Li (Yang), Ketan Singh (Yang), Yavuz Yetim (Yang), Ilyas Atishev (Yang), Satendra Gera (Yang), Ashkan Sadeghi (Yang), Rachel Yan (Yang), Nikko Mizutani (Yang), Shuaiwen Wang (Yang), Song Yang (Yang), Zhijing Li (Yang), Jiang Liu (Yang), Mengying Sun (Yang), Fei Tian (Yang), Xiaohan Wei (Yang), Chonglin Sun (Yang), Parish Aggarwal (Yang), Kaushik Rangadurai (Yang), Zhi Hua (Yang), Frank Shyu (Yang), Ruchit Sharma (Yang), Liyuan Li (Yang), Shike Mei (Yang), Wenlin Chen (Yang), Santanu Kolay (Yang), Ben Schulte (Yang), Deepak Chandra (Yang), Adam (Yang), Song, Sandeep Pandey, Xi Liu, Hamed Firooz, Luke Simon

entry.summary: GR2 is an industrial technical report on using LLMs with reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards for the re-ranking stage of large-scale recommendation systems, targeting carousel and grid displays and addressing the underexplored final funnel stage. It argues RL unlocks reasoning capabilities beyond zero-shot or supervised fine-tuning for re-ranking.

entry.title: Towards Flexible, Natural, Efficient Interaction for Conversational Talking Face Generation

author.name: Baiqin Wang, Sen Chen, Jiankuo Zhao, Xiangyu Liu, Zhen Lei, Xiangyu Zhu

entry.summary: InterTalk is an efficient framework for conversational talking-face generation supporting flexible multi-round, multi-participant dialogue with natural non-verbal feedback and real-time efficiency. It attempts to jointly satisfy flexibility, naturalness, and efficiency where prior methods fall short.

entry.title: No Prompt, No Leaks: A Robust Generative Steganography Framework via Prompt-Free Diffusion

author.name: Jingwen Cai, Fen Xiao, Shuhua Deng, Xieping Gao

entry.summary: This work proposes a prompt-free diffusion generative steganography framework using style semantic priors and a cascaded affine coupling module for bijective mapping between secret and stego images. It aims for higher-quality stego images and more accurate secret recovery than text-prompt-dependent LDM methods.

entry.title: Towards a foundational model for recognising diastematic Gregorian notation

author.name: Daniel Kurek, Jan Haji\v{c} jr

entry.summary: This paper designs a common S-GABC-based encoding to unify four differently-encoded Gregorian notation datasets and trains a shared end-to-end foundational model, achieving a new state of the art across all four. It advances optical recognition of diastematic Gregorian chant notation.

entry.title: Technical Report of RoboSpatial Challenge at CVPR 2026: Selective Reasoning Activation and Reference-Frame Disambiguation for Embodied Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Yuxiang Xie, Qi Lv, Jianming Xing, Zijian Hong, Xiang Deng, Weili Guan, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: RoboSpatialBrain, a CVPR 2026 challenge submission built on RoboBrain2.5-8B, combines two training-free inference-time mechanisms: forced prefix activation with task-specific post-prompts to elicit deliberate reasoning, and reference-frame redirection to resolve camera- versus object-centric ambiguity. It targets embodied spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Geometric Dyson Brownian Motions and the Free Log-Normal Limit for a Non-Square Product of Random Matrices

author.name: Mufan Li, Jaume de Dios Pont, Mihai Nica, Daniel M. Roy

entry.summary: This work analyzes the squared singular value spectrum of products of non-square random matrices, connecting it to feature covariance eigenvalues of deep linear networks at initialization, and derives a geometric Dyson Brownian motion and a Burgers-equation limit yielding a free log-normal law. It offers theoretical foundations for understanding deep network spectra.

entry.title: A Three-Phase Foundation Model for Tax-Aware Personalized Portfolio Management

author.name: Ramin Pishehvar

entry.summary: A three-phase deep RL system for personalized, tax-aware portfolio management that removes ticker lock-in via a self-supervised cross-asset encoder augmented by a frozen time-series foundation model (Chronos). It claims first use of a time-series foundation model in portfolio RL.

entry.title: Surprise as a Signal for Plasticity and Metacognition

author.name: Louis Mouchon

entry.summary: This paper studies whether a prediction-error surprise signal from a small predictor over a frozen encoder's latent space can gate plasticity and support metacognition, writing new episodic concepts only when surprise is high and consolidating via offline replay. On a 1000-class ImageNet stream it recovers substantial retention on the oldest classes.

entry.title: MultiUAV-Plat: An LLM-Oriented Platform, Benchmark and Framework for Multi-UAV Collaborative Task Planning

author.name: Sheng Zhang, Qinglin Li, Yuechao Zang, Xueqin Huang, Yijia Fu, Cheng Zhu

entry.summary: MultiUAV-Plat is a lightweight LLM-agent-oriented simulation platform and benchmark for multi-UAV collaborative task planning, exposing RESTful APIs, role-based information access, and hidden validation logic. It captures aerial constraints like partial observability and coordination often missing from prior simulators.

entry.title: Cross-Domain Feature Expansion for Tabular Medical Data via Knowledge Graphs Injection

author.name: Mengying Zhou, Yongjie Yin, Haoyan Xin, Guoping Liu, Yang Chen

entry.summary: MedKGTab is a knowledge-injected framework for cross-domain feature expansion in tabular medical data, inferring uncollected biomedical features from available ones using a row-column dual-attention mechanism operating directly on raw structured data. It integrates statistical priors with medical knowledge graphs.

entry.title: Wisdom Of The (AI) Crowd: Investigating Artificial Swarm Intelligence In Large Language Models

author.name: Justin Brenne, Christian Meske

entry.summary: This study tests whether artificial LLM swarms can approximate human swarm intelligence, running 960 prompts across GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 on eight estimation tasks with intra-model sampling and inter-model aggregation. It reports consistent error reductions up to 37 percentage points in MAPE.

entry.title: BP-TTA: Balanced and Prototype-Guided Test-Time Adaptation in Dynamic Scenarios

author.name: Shaoyang Huang, Yashi Zhu, Yichen Yu, Lei Zhang, Zhang Yi, Tao He

entry.summary: BP-TTA is a test-time adaptation method that combines batch-balanced sampling with prototype-guided adaptation to jointly handle class imbalance and continual domain shift, which typically co-occur and interact in real test-time streams. It targets a gap left by TTA methods that address drift alone.

entry.title: CSTrader: A Testbed for Language-Grounded Trading in a Community-Driven Virtual Asset Market

author.name: Yao Shi, Kingfung Luo, Nan Tang, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: CSTrader is a multi-agent testbed for language-grounded trading in the community-driven Counter-Strike 2 weapon-skin market, integrating heterogeneous signals and specialized agents for technical analysis, liquidity, events, and sentiment under realistic frictions. It studies how LLMs turn unstructured text into trading actions in a niche volatile market.

entry.title: CLOUDADV: Decision-Aligned Instance Sizing with Zero-Shot Foundation Models under Drift

author.name: Jack Bell, Giacomo Carfi, Gerlando Gramaglia, Andrea Simioni, Daniele Fontani, Vincenzo Lomonaco

entry.summary: CLOUDADV is an engineer-facing advisory system for cloud VM instance sizing under workload drift, combining zero-shot time-series forecasting with bounded LLM recommendation generation across day, week, and month horizons. It uses a higher-capacity offline LLM for references and evaluates a smaller production model for deployment-time alignment.

entry.title: Design and Implementation of Agentic Orchestrations and Orchestration of Agents

author.name: Stefanie Rinderle-Ma, Juergen Mangler, Johannes Loebbecke, Dominik Voigt, Nataliia Klievtsova, Matthias Ehrendorfer

entry.summary: This paper offers a classification framework for agentic orchestration options in business process management along properties like task specificity, traceability, autonomy, and correctness assurance, with qualitative decision criteria and quantitative metrics. It demonstrates these through different agentic implementations of a predictive sensing scenario.

entry.title: Adaptive Cluster-First Route-Second Decomposition for Industrial-Scale Vehicle Routing

author.name: Oguzhan Karaahmetoglu (Carnegie Mellon University), Hyong Kim (Carnegie Mellon University)

entry.summary: This paper proposes an adaptive cluster-first route-second system for industrial-scale capacitated vehicle routing that formulates decomposition as an iterative decision process, using an LLM as a high-level decision maker for tool selection and partitioning. It adapts to varying spatial, demand, and operational instance characteristics.

entry.title: Harnessing Textual Refusal Directions for Multimodal Safety

author.name: Moreno D'Inc\`a, Massimiliano Mancini, Nicu Sebe

entry.summary: This work compares two independent multi-agent RL approaches, contextual combinatorial bandits and policy gradients, for decentralized smart charging of large electric-vehicle fleets under grid constraints. Agents make local decisions from price signals and state-of-charge to enable implicit coordination.

entry.title: SwiftAudio: Data-Efficient Caption-Only Distillation for One-Step Text-to-Audio Diffusion-based Generation

author.name: Binh Mai, Tran Quoc Bao Le, Hung Dinh, Cong Tran

entry.summary: SwiftAudio distills a multi-step text-to-audio diffusion teacher into a one-step student using only text captions (no paired audio) via an audio-adapted Variational Score Distillation plus temporal smoothness regularization. Reduces inference latency while removing dependence on paired training data.

entry.title: Stage-Transition Dense Reward Modeling for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yang Yang, Bingjie Chen, Zihan Wang, Yizhe Li, Guoping Pan, Yi Cheng, Houde Liu

entry.summary: STDR converts unstructured expert videos into logically grounded dense rewards for long-horizon robotic manipulation by inferring task stage structure and providing stage-transition plus within-stage progress signals. Addresses sparse-reward RL without brittle manual reward shaping.

entry.title: DPPE: Rethinking Camera-Based Positional Encoding for Scaling Multi-View Transformers

author.name: Shun Kenney, Teppei Suzuki

entry.summary: DPPE investigates why camera-based relative positional encoding causes performance stagnation when scaling multi-view transformers for novel view synthesis, and proposes a redesigned positional encoding to overcome the bottleneck. Targets scalable 3D vision transformers.

entry.title: Token-Sparse Medical Multimodal Reasoning via Dual-Stream Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kaitao Chen, Weiqian Zhao, Jiamin Wu, Qihao Zheng, Shangquan Sun, Chunfeng Song, Xiaosong Wang, Mu Zhou, Mianxin Liu

entry.summary: ViToS is a dual-stream RL framework for medical vision-language models that jointly performs active visual token pruning and token-sparse reasoning, using one policy with grounding and sparse-reasoning branches to focus on sparse clinical visual evidence. Improves medical multimodal reasoning efficiency and accuracy.

entry.title: A Lifecycle and Application-Stack Survey of Large Language Model Vulnerabilities: Attacks, Risks, Defenses, and Open Problems

author.name: Seyed Bagher Hashemi Natanzi, Bo Tang

entry.summary: Systematizes LLM system vulnerabilities through a lifecycle and application-stack lens, organizing attacks across eight stages spanning data, prompts, outputs, tools, memories, and user authority as models become embedded in agents and pipelines. Surveys attacks, risks, defenses, and open problems.

entry.title: ShopX: A Foundation Model for Intent-to-Item Fulfillment in Agentic Shopping

author.name: Jiacheng Chen, Tao Zhang, Manxi Lin, Dunxian Huang, Teng Shi, Honghao Fu, Mengyan Li, Xinming Zhang, Chenchi Zhang, Xuan Lu, Xiaoxiong Du, Haibin Chen, Shaolin Ye, Hao Chang, Xiaoqi Li, Shuwen Xiao, Yujin Yuan, Jingxuan Feng, Shaopan Xiong, Huimin Yi, Ju Huang, Qiu Shen, Ying Chen, Junjun Zheng, Xiangheng Kong, Yuning Jiang

entry.summary: ShopX is proposed as a foundation model for agentic shopping that unifies intent understanding, execution planning, and semantic-ID-native item-space operations, translating flexible user intents directly into item-space outcomes rather than routing through low-bandwidth retrieval interfaces. Targets intent-to-item fulfillment for LLM shopping agents.

entry.title: Seeing Is Not Sharing: Some Vision-Language Models Overestimate Common Ground in Asymmetric Dialogue

author.name: Nan Li, Albert Gatt, Massimo Poesio

entry.summary: Formulates an interpretation-matching task on 13,077 annotated reference expressions from MapTask dialogues to test whether VLMs distinguish what could be shared from what has been shared through grounding in asymmetric dialogue. Finds providing map images improves accuracy but pushes models toward over-predicting alignment (assuming shared understanding).

entry.title: STEB: Style Text Embedding Benchmark

author.name: Rafael Rivera Soto, Anna Wegmann, Cristina Aggazzotti

entry.summary: STEB is an open-source Style Text Embedding Benchmark spanning 96 datasets across 7 languages covering authorship verification, retrieval, AI-text detection, and linguistic probing to standardize style-embedding evaluation. Finds semantic embeddings fail on stylistic tasks and no single style embedding dominates.

entry.title: CHERRY: Compressed Hierarchical Experts with Recurrent Representational Yield

author.name: Dohyeon Kwon, Youngjin Park

entry.summary: CHERRY studies compute-efficient language-model training via selective supervision on the roughly 15 percent of semantically-payload tokens, showing positive gradient coupling improves unsupervised tokens too, plus hierarchical experts and recurrent representations. Provides a proof that unsupervised-token improvement is guaranteed under a gradient-coupling condition.

entry.title: Breaking Failure Cascades: Step-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Medical Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Junha Jung, Minbyul Jeong, Suhyeon Lim, Sungwook Jung, Jaehoon Yun, Taeyun Roh, Mujeen Sung, Jaewoo Kang

entry.summary: MRPO is a step-aware RL algorithm for medical multimodal reasoning that assigns step-wise process rewards and, when the final answer is wrong, exponentially penalizes cascading early-stage reasoning failures identified as a leading cause of errors. Moves beyond outcome-only post-training for clinical VQA.

entry.title: Real-Time Source-Free Object Detection

author.name: Sairam VCR, Varun Gopal, Poornima Jain, Vineeth N Balasubramanian, Muhammad Haris Khan

entry.summary: Presents a real-time source-free object detection method built on the NMS-free YOLOv10 dual-head detector, addressing suboptimal mean-teacher self-training through improved pseudo-labeling for dual heads. Achieves state-of-the-art domain adaptation while being faster and more compact.

entry.title: Attend, Transform, or Silence: Operator-Level Visual Skipping for Efficient Multimodal LLM Inference

author.name: Zhaoyang Luo, Runmin Dong, Miao Yang, Fan Wei, Yushan Lai, Bin Luo, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: Analyzes multimodal LLM inference from an answer-observable view, finding late visual-token updates can be large yet barely affect answer tokens, and proposes operator-level (attention vs FFN) visual skipping to exploit this answer-silent redundancy rather than removing tokens or whole layers. Enables finer-grained inference acceleration.

entry.title: MECoBench: A Systematic Study of Multimodal Agent Collaboration in Embodied Environments

author.name: Qingyun Liu, Jiwen Zhang, Jingyi Hu, Siyuan Wang, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: MECoBench is a multimodal embodied cooperation benchmark spanning diverse real-world tasks, two cooperation structures, and three collaboration modes, evaluating whether MLLMs can collaborate in visually grounded environments. Finds collaboration helps but depends on balancing gains against coordination complexity and that communication is essential.

entry.title: Amplifying Membership Signal Through Chained Regeneration

author.name: Wojciech {\L}apacz, Stanis{\l}aw Pawlak

entry.summary: MADreMIA is a model-agnostic framework that amplifies membership-inference and dataset-inference signals for generative models via chained regeneration, iteratively feeding outputs back through the model (inspired by Model Autophagy Disorder) instead of relying on weak one-shot generations or infeasible shadow models. Enhances privacy auditing and copyright enforcement across modalities.

entry.title: SyncCache: Exploiting Asymmetric Dynamics for Fast Audio-Driven Portrait Animation

author.name: Juncheng Ma, Yuxuan Du, Yanan Sun, Zhening Xing, Changlin Li, Zhenyu Tang, Bo Li, Peng-Tao Jiang, Li Yuan, Daquan Zhou, Yonghong Tian

entry.summary: SyncCache is a training-free caching method that accelerates Diffusion Transformer-based audio-driven portrait animation by exploiting spatial and modality imbalances (high-frequency, human-region dynamics). It targets the inference latency problem that makes DiT talking-head models impractical.

entry.title: Anchoring on Reality: Breaking the Pseudo-Target Ceiling in Makeup Transfer

author.name: Bo Wei, Xianhui Lin, Yi Dong, Zhongzhong Li, Zonghui Li, Zirui Wang, Jiachen Yang, Xing Liu, Hong Gu, Xiaoming Li, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: ART tackles makeup transfer's lack of real paired data via a two-stage reality-anchored refinement cycle, first bootstrapping with pseudo-targets then shifting supervision toward real reference-derived signals. It aims to reduce synthetic artifacts, detail loss, and identity drift.

entry.title: AA: A Multi-view Multimodal Dataset for Screen-based Gaze Estimation

author.name: Chang Liu, Jiaqi Liu, Zhoutong Ye, Xinjie Shen, Chun Yu, Yuanchun Shi

entry.summary: AA is a multi-view, multimodal dataset for screen-based gaze estimation with eight screen-mounted and two side-view synchronized cameras and precise gaze targets. It enables robust modeling under viewpoint variation and occlusion with subject-independent evaluation splits.

entry.title: Investigating Multi-Agent Deliberation in Law

author.name: Cor Steging, Ludi van Leeuwen, Tadeusz Zbiegie\'n

entry.summary: The paper investigates multi-agent deliberation for legal reasoning, introducing two frameworks inspired by courtroom procedures and legal argumentation. Experiments show these approaches match rather than clearly beat baselines on legal and non-legal benchmarks.

entry.title: Dual Sparse Aggregation Transformer for Multispectral Object Detection

author.name: Wencong Wu, Xiuwei Zhang, Hanlin Yin, Hongxi Zhang, Yanning Zhang

entry.summary: DSAFormer introduces a dual sparse aggregation transformer for multispectral object detection, using sparse token selection to reduce redundant cross-modal interactions from irrelevant regions plus a learnable fusion block. It aims to improve accuracy over dense-attention multispectral detectors.

entry.title: Rethinking the Role of Feature Engineering and Learning Strategies in Few-Shot Hidden Emotion Recognition

author.name: Xiaochuan Guo, Jihao Gu, Haixu Liu, Yuxin Liu, Qi Wang, Yufei Wang, Fei Wang, Kun Li, Dan Guo

entry.summary: This competition-winning paper presents a compact multi-modal temporal framework for few-shot hidden emotion recognition, integrating skeletons, blendshapes, DINOv2/v3 features, X-CLIP, and Gemini semantic priors via cross-attention with static pose as query. It achieved first place in an IJCAI challenge track.

entry.title: Temporal Training Strategies for Left Atrium and Left Atrial Appendage Segmentation in Dynamic Contrast 4DCT

author.name: David Montalvo-Garc\'ia, Lauren Severance, Elliot R. McVeigh, Mar\'ia J. Ledesma-Carbayo

entry.summary: This study investigates temporal training-set design for nnUNet-based segmentation of the left atrium and left atrial appendage in dynamic contrast 4DCT, comparing minimal, physiological, and other frame-selection strategies. It examines the tradeoff between robustness and label noise given single annotations per sequence.

entry.title: Improving Certified Robustness via Adversarial Distillation

author.name: Matteo Melis, Jesus Martinez Del Rincon, Vishal Sharma

entry.summary: Improves the tradeoff between standard accuracy and certified adversarial robustness by combining adversarial distillation with certified-training relaxation bounds, producing models that are both empirically robust and verifiable. Targets the tension between certifiable networks and accuracy.

entry.title: FedXDS: Leveraging Model Attribution Methods to counteract Data Heterogeneity in Federated Learning

author.name: Maximilian Andreas Hoefler, Karsten Mueller, Wojciech Samek

entry.summary: FedXDS uses explainable-AI attribution methods to guide selective data sharing in federated learning, mitigating performance degradation from statistically heterogeneous client distributions. Presents the first application of XAI to counteract federated data heterogeneity.

entry.title: Belief Contraction in Dynamic Epistemic Logic

author.name: Gaia Belardinelli (Stanford University), Snow Zhang (University of Berkeley, California)

entry.summary: Extends dynamic epistemic logic to model belief contraction about factual propositions, showing that standard plausibility-ordering approaches cannot capture beliefs violating positive introspection or contraction from hedged announcements, and proposes an enriched formalism. Advances logical foundations of belief change.

entry.title: MVP-Nav: Multi-layer Value Map Planner Navigator

author.name: Wenyuan Xie, Shaokai Wu, Yijin Zhou, Yanbiao Ji, Guodong Zhang, Bayram Bayramli, Qiuchang Li, Xunchu Zhou, Yue Ding, Hongtao Lu

entry.summary: MVP-Nav is an RGB-only zero-shot object-goal navigation framework using a multi-layer value map planner that reconstructs explicit physical occupancy from monocular views via 3D foundation models, aligning perception, planning, and control to avoid physically unsafe but semantically plausible behavior. Addresses depth-free navigation uncertainty.

entry.title: Patient-Level Elbow Abnormality Detection: Leakage-Aware Evaluation of Learned Preprocessing, Calibration, and Triage-Oriented Operating Points

author.name: Ahmed Sallam, Ahmet Kaplan

entry.summary: This paper studies patient-level elbow abnormality detection on the MURA dataset under a leakage-aware protocol, evaluating learned DnCNN preprocessing, calibration, and triage-oriented operating points. It finds preprocessing differences are modest while emphasizing rigorous calibration and specificity-targeted evaluation.

entry.title: The consequences of locking intelligence away: an introduction to Claude relays in China

author.name: CMLKevin

entry.summary: This post documents how Chinese API relay stations resell Western VC-subsidized AI tokens (from Claude, ChatGPT, cloud credits, etc.) to the domestic market at a fraction of official prices, sometimes disguising cheaper models as premium ones. It illustrates the economic and geopolitical dynamics of restricting frontier model access.

entry.title: How should you slow down AI progress if it becomes necessary?

author.name: Felipe Calero-Forero

entry.summary: This post analyzes how the world could actually slow AI progress if needed, examining concrete instruments beyond commonly discussed blunt measures (token taxes, datacenter moratoriums, training pauses) and proposing a layered set of restrictions for catastrophic risk or a software intelligence explosion. It fills a gap by focusing on the how rather than the whether of slowdown.

entry.title: Revealing Safety-Critical Scenarios for UTM via Transformer

author.name: Huaze Tang, Bill Zeng, Chao Wang, Zhenpeng Shi, Qian Zhang, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: This work frames Unmanned Traffic Management vulnerability discovery as a sequence-modeling problem for transformer-based RL, using attention to model system states and predict failure-exposing actions. It targets the long-tail effect created by UTM self-healing.

entry.title: HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic: Multi-Hop Question Answering Corpus for Historical Research, Parliamentary Debates from the French Third Republic (1870-1940)

author.name: Aur\'elien Pellet (LRE), Julien Perez (EPITA, LRE), Marie Puren (LRE, CJM)

entry.summary: HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic is a French-language multi-hop QA dataset of 1782 questions derived from French Third Republic parliamentary debates and newspapers, designed with a historian to capture cross-source synthesis and temporal reasoning. It serves as a resource for evaluating retrieval-augmented and LLM systems in historical research.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Instrument QA: Probing Instrument Grounding in Music Audio-Language Models

author.name: Yujun Lee, Joonhyeok Shin, Hyoeun Kim, Kyuhong Shim

entry.summary: Introduces an OpenMIC-derived diagnostic benchmark showing that high binary instrument-presence QA accuracy in music audio-language models often masks shortcuts, position bias, and poor temporal localization. Argues instrument grounding needs harder, genre-prior-reduced and temporal evaluations.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Control: State-Aware Fine-Tuning for Transformer-based Models

author.name: Duc Anh Nguyen, Tien Ngoc Luu, Tung Pham, Toan Tran

entry.summary: Mixture-of-Control is a state-based fine-tuning method that adaptively integrates local per-block and global control signals for transformers, improving representational adaptation while avoiding the overhead of prior cross-block communication mechanisms. Offers memory-efficient parameter-efficient tuning.

entry.title: Preserve the Hard, Regenerate the Rest: Uncertainty-Guided Synthetic Training Data Augmentation with Diffusion Models

author.name: Nikolai R\"ohrich, Julian Glei{\ss}ner, Ahmed H. A. Ibrahim, Silvan Mertes, Tobias Huber

entry.summary: Proposes uncertainty-guided synthetic data augmentation for semantic segmentation that preserves hard regions while regenerating easy or uninformative ones with diffusion models, strictly maintaining label validity and maximizing pixel informativeness. Avoids external models and coarse augmentation heuristics.

entry.title: RCT: A Robot-Collected Touch-Vision-Language Dataset for Tactile Generalization

author.name: Jingbo He, Michael F\"arber, Roberto Calandra

entry.summary: RCT is a robot-collected touch-vision-language dataset with 29,279 tactile frames from full robot presses on 122 industrial materials using three DIGIT sensors, designed with contact-sequence-aware splits to enable held-out generalization across materials, sensors, and positions. Highlights how frame-random splits leak near-duplicate observations.

entry.title: A Technical Typology of AI Systems in Public Administration

author.name: Jonathan Rystr{\o}m, Chris Schmitz, Nathan Davies, Gerhard Hammerschmid, Albert Meijer, Chris Russell

entry.summary: Argues that public-administration research treats AI as a monolith and proposes a five-category technical typology (hand-coded, glass-box, black-box, general-purpose, agentic) calibrated to distinct implications for accountability, procedural justice, and non-discrimination. Aims to bring technical precision to public-sector AI governance.

entry.title: Hybrid Unet-Transformer Model for Generating Stress and Strain Fields from Composite Geometrics

author.name: Shrey Patel

entry.summary: A hybrid UNet-Transformer surrogate predicts stress and strain fields directly from composite microstructure images across ten field types and diverse tessellations, replacing computationally expensive finite element simulations. It targets fast physics-informed material design.

entry.title: Structural Proxies

author.name: Raymond Douglas

entry.summary: This post reflects on the fundamental challenge of AGI safety research lacking access to the superhuman systems it aims to study, categorizing current approaches (prosaic techniques, model organisms, control) by how they sidestep this access problem. It proposes thinking in terms of structural proxies for future systems.

entry.title: Temporal Preservation over Processing: Diagnosing and Designing Spatiotemporal Single-Stage Video Detectors

author.name: Karam Tomotaki-Dawoud, Anna Hilsmann, Peter Eisert, Sebastian Bosse

entry.summary: Introduces TemporalLens, a diagnostic framework using controlled perturbations (occlusions, temporal shuffling, redundancy, resolution degradation) to test whether single-stage video detectors truly reason over time or exploit a single frame. Also proposes design principles favoring temporal preservation over heavy processing.

entry.title: Mitigating Positional Leakage in 3D Masked Autoencoders for Robust Representation Learning

author.name: Xu Yan, Huiqun Wang, Chen Wang, Lei Ren, Di Huang

entry.summary: MPL-MAE identifies that decoders in 3D masked autoencoders over-rely on positional information (positional leakage), weakening semantic representation, and proposes recalibrated positional embeddings to mitigate this for point-cloud self-supervised learning. Improves feature quality on downstream 3D tasks.

entry.title: ZEBRA: Zero-Shot Entropy-Regularized Prompt Learning for Base-to-Novel Generalization in Audio-Language Models

author.name: Asif Hanif, Mohammad Yaqub

entry.summary: ZEBRA is a plug-and-play prompt-learning framework for audio-language models that fuses zero-shot and prompt-learning logits with self-entropy regularization to close the base-to-novel generalization gap where adaptation degrades novel-class accuracy. Improves few-shot adaptation without harming unseen classes.

entry.title: Histogram-constrained Image Generation

author.name: Haoming Liu, Yuanhe Guo, Yijia Cao, Shenji Wan, Hongyi Wen

entry.summary: Introduces Histogram-constrained Image Generation, a diffusion control mechanism occupying a middle granularity between global text prompts and dense ControlNet-style conditions, guiding generation via histogram constraints. Aims to balance global coherence with local precision.

entry.title: Bridging Local Observation and Global Simulation in Closed-Loop Traffic Modeling

author.name: Ziyan Wang, Tan Xiang, Peng Chen, Xintao Yan

entry.summary: CRAFT is a contextual preference alignment framework for closed-loop traffic simulation that addresses a local-to-global context mismatch, where ego-centric-trained simulators fail when surrounding agents become fully observable, causing unrealistic behaviors. It uses self-supervised failure discovery and preference-guided alignment.

entry.title: Modal CEGAR-tableaux with RECAR and resolution-based SAT-shortcuts

author.name: Rajeev Gor\'e (Faculty of Information Technology, Monash University, Australia), Cormac Kikkert (Cormac Kikkert Research)

entry.summary: Extends CEGAR-tableaux for modal satisfiability with SAT-shortcuts via both RECAR and a novel integration using the modal resolution prover KSP as an oracle, and reports the KSP-based CEGARBox++ outperforms its individual components on large satisfiable problems. Claims the first effective SAT-tableaux-resolution integration for modal logic.

entry.title: CLIMB: Centroid-Based Hierarchical Memory for Online Continual Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Julien Lefebvre, Stefan Duffner, Mathieu Lefort

entry.summary: CLIMB tackles online continual self-supervised learning under memory limits by combining a hierarchical centroid-based memory bank with knowledge distillation on replayed examples to reduce representation drift. The centroid memory supplies hard contrastive examples while covering data diversity.

entry.title: CVE-TTP KG: Knowledge Graph Linking Software Vulnerabilities to Attack Behaviors

author.name: Basant Agarwal, Dincy R. Arikkat, Swati Yadav, Serena Nicolazzo, Antonino Nocera, Vinod P

entry.summary: Constructs a CVE-TTP knowledge graph linking software vulnerabilities to MITRE ATT&CK tactics and techniques using transformer-based classification and relation extraction, with CySecBERT achieving high macro-F1. Bridges vulnerability databases and attacker behavior for better threat interpretation.

entry.title: Sparsity-Inducing Divergence Losses for Biometric Verification

author.name: Dimitrios Koutsianos, Ladislav Mo\v{s}ner, Yannis Panagakis, Themos Stafylakis

entry.summary: Proposes Q-Margin, an alpha-divergence loss for face and speaker verification that encodes the margin penalty into the reference measure (prior probabilities) rather than applying geometric penalties to logits, aligning margins with the generalized probabilistic framework and inducing sparse solutions. Offers a principled alternative to CosFace/ArcFace margins.

entry.title: Towards Inclusive Mobility Modeling: Characterizing and Evaluating Elderly Trajectory Patterns in Urban Systems

author.name: Zhengxuan Wang, Haohan He, Mengying Zhou

entry.summary: This study characterizes how underrepresentation of elderly riders in mobility datasets biases trajectory modeling and downstream urban planning, using Jersey City Citi Bike data and synthetic trajectory generation. It quantifies structurally distinct elderly mobility signatures like smaller activity spaces.

entry.title: Smart charging of large fleets of Electric Vehicles: Independent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approaches

author.name: Xavier Rate, Eloann Le Guern, Rapha\"el F\'eraud, Fatma Salem, Melissa Chiknoun, Eymeric Giabicani, Mehdi Feki, Patrick Maill\'e, Guy Camilleri, Anne Blavette, Hamid Benhamed

entry.summary: This survey classifies 78 joint OFDM waveform and RIS configuration works for 6G into four paradigms spanning convex relaxation, metaheuristics, deep RL, and emerging foundation-model, diffusion, and quantum methods. It highlights the absence of standardized benchmarks preventing cross-paper comparison.

entry.title: Learning Structurally Consistent Representations for Multi-View Radar Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Ali Zia, Muhammad Umer Ramzan, Abdelwahed Khamis, Usman Ali, Abdul Rehman

entry.summary: Introduces a higher-order structural alignment framework for multi-view radar semantic segmentation using learnable hypergraphs to capture dependencies among multiple radar returns from the same object, ensuring consistency across radar projections. Improves dense segmentation from sparse, noisy radar.

entry.title: JL1-CC&QA: Extending the JL1-CD Benchmark with Change Captioning and Question Answering

author.name: Ziyuan Liu, Ruifei Zhu, Ouqiao Ma, Yuantao Gu

entry.summary: JL1-CC&QA extends the JL1-CD remote-sensing change-detection dataset with 17,021 change captions and 20,060 question-answer pairs over 5,000 bi-temporal Jilin-1 satellite image pairs, moving beyond binary change segmentation to describe what and why changes occur. Enables multi-task, interactive change understanding.

entry.title: LeCropFollow: Latent Space Planning for Navigation in Unstructured Crop Fields

author.name: Felipe Tommaselli, Francisco Affonso, Arthur Pompeu, Gianluca Capezzuto, Arun Narenthiran Sivakumar, Girish Chowdhary, Marcelo Becker

entry.summary: LeCropFollow is a visual navigation framework for under-canopy agricultural robots that replaces explicit geometric modeling with a learned latent representation, combining a self-supervised semantic heatmap extractor with the TD-MPC2 model-based RL planner. Targets robust navigation in unstructured crop fields with irregular planting and discontinuities.

entry.title: PhotoQuilt: Training-Free Arbitrary-Resolution Photomosaics via Bootstrapped Tiled Denoising

author.name: Koorosh Roohi, Javad Rajabi, Andrew Fleet, Babak Taati

entry.summary: PhotoQuilt is a training-free framework that generates arbitrary-resolution photomosaics using bootstrapped tiled denoising, resolving the tension between global scene coherence and locally convincing tiles. It offers a creative-image application of diffusion models without additional training.

entry.title: RRT-Rope: A deterministic shortening approach for fast near-optimal path planning in large-scale uncluttered 3D environments

author.name: Louis Petit, Alexis Lussier Desbiens

entry.summary: RRT-Rope introduces a deterministic path-shortening method to produce near-optimal paths quickly in large-scale uncluttered 3D environments such as mining stopes explored by UAVs. It targets the slow convergence of RRT* variants by shortcutting feasible paths efficiently.

entry.title: Exponential-Family Tensor Completion via Nonconvex Dual Total-Variation Regularization

author.name: Wenfei Cao, Yang Chen, Qibin Zhao, Jinglai Li, Andrzej Cichocki

entry.summary: This paper provides a rigorous theoretical analysis of total-variation regularization for tensor completion under exponential-family noise, generalizing Gaussian and Poisson settings, and proposes nonconvex dual-TV regularizers based on a transformed L1 function. It advances theory for a widely used but underanalyzed regularization technique.

entry.title: When Regulation Has Memory: Hysteresis and Control Burden in Artificial Agency

author.name: Veronique Ziegler

entry.summary: This work studies whether the hidden regulatory effort keeping adaptive agents stable depends on their history, using a computational model of uncertainty regulation driven through and back from a changing target. It tests for hysteresis and carryover in control burden.

entry.title: A time-series classification framework for individual-level absenteeism prediction under severe class imbalance

author.name: Kwong Ho Li, Matthew Roughan, Wathsala Karunarathne

entry.summary: This paper proposes a time-series classification framework for individual-level absenteeism prediction under severe class imbalance, separating historical attendance sequences from future absence labels to enable genuine forecasting rather than reproducing realized outcomes. It targets workforce planning in high-demand sectors.

entry.title: Distilling Temporal Coherence into 2D Networks for Transrectal Ultrasound Prostate Video Segmentation

author.name: Dong Yeong Kim, JunGyu Lee, Jaewon Choi, June Young Seo, Myeongseop Kim, Jinwook Choi, Taek Min Kim, Young-Gon Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a training framework that distills temporal coherence from video into an efficient 2D network for real-time prostate segmentation in transrectal ultrasound, exploiting the observation that prostate geometry is stable while surrounding acoustics fluctuate. It aims to combine 3D temporal reasoning with fast single-frame inference for image-guided interventions.

entry.title: How Can AI Find My Model? A Model-Finding Experimental Study Considering Data Formats, Embeddings, and Retrieval Strategies

author.name: Jhon G. Botello, Jose J. Padilla, Erika Frydenlund, Krzysztof Rechowicz, Eric Weisel

entry.summary: An empirical study of how data formats, transformer embeddings, and retrieval strategies affect discovering reusable simulation models via natural-language queries. It measures recall and nDCG across query types in the modeling and simulation domain.

entry.title: Scientific Explanations in Health Sciences: Causality, Trust, and Epistemic Adequacy

author.name: Martina Mattioli, Marcello Pelillo

entry.summary: This paper critically reviews explainability in medical AI through the lens of philosophy of science and medicine, examining causality, trust, and epistemic adequacy that contemporary XAI research often overlooks. It argues foundational assumptions of medical explanation remain insufficiently examined.

entry.title: TDGT: A Tabular Data Generation Toolkit supporting adaptive GPU-accelerated Bayesian mixture models, diffusion-based models, and latent-space generative modeling

author.name: Vasileios C. Pezoulas, Nikolaos S. Tachos, Eleni Georga, Kostas Marias, Manolis Tsiknakis, Dimitrios I. Fotiadis

entry.summary: TDGT is a web-based toolkit for synthetic tabular data generation and fidelity assessment, featuring an Adaptive Bayesian Mixture Synthesizer that auto-selects mixture components, alongside diffusion and latent-space generators. It targets privacy-preserving data sharing with integrated multi-metric evaluation.

entry.title: From Materials Database to Materials Bank: Assetizing Data for AI Driven Materials Innovation

author.name: Chenyao Ma, Di Zhang, Weibo Gong, Wei Du, Rui Su, Yuhang Chen, Kan Xu, Huan Gu, Limin Li, Piao Ma, Zhenghao Li, Hao Li

entry.summary: Proposes a Materials Bank concept that adds a value-filtering and assetization layer on top of conventional materials databases, distinguishing high-potential materials from raw archived records to accelerate industrial translation. Reframes materials data as curated assets for AI-driven innovation.

entry.title: DA-Studio: An Agentic System for End-to-End Data Analysis

author.name: Yizhe Liu, Shaolei Zhang, Ju Fan

entry.summary: DA-Studio is an interactive web-based agentic system for end-to-end data analysis that autonomously organizes multi-step workflows, executes code in a sandbox, and remains inspectable via visible action traces. It targets complete execution-grounded analysis rather than isolated subtasks.

entry.title: Temperature Field Reconstruction of Tungsten Monoblock Divertor on EAST using Physics-aware Neural Operator Transformer

author.name: Zikang Yan, Xiao Wang, Qingquan Yang, Zhendong Yang, Gaoting Chen, Zehua Chen, Bo Jiang, Jin Tang, Guosheng Xu

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-aware neural operator transformer to reconstruct the divertor temperature field on the EAST tokamak in real time, modeling boundary heat-flux relations as a graph with graph attention. Provides a fast alternative to expensive finite-element methods for fusion device control.

entry.title: Automating Cause-Effect Specification with Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models

author.name: Javal Vyas, Milapji Singh Gill, Mehmet Mercang\"oz

entry.summary: Presents a semantic-AI framework combining a knowledge graph with a constrained LLM to automatically generate cause-and-effect matrices and operator-ready safety narratives plus SWRL rules for process control. Automates a traditionally manual, error-prone engineering-specification task.

entry.title: When to Truncate a Feature Ranking: A Residual-Overlap Stopping Rule for Subset Selection

author.name: Jesus S. Aguilar-Ruiz

entry.summary: Develops a distributional, risk-calibrated stopping rule for truncating supervised feature rankings based on accumulated class-separation evidence, replacing arbitrary cardinality thresholds or cross-validation. Provides an interpretable criterion for when to stop selecting features.

entry.title: Cross-lingual Relation Extraction with Large Language Models: Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, and Fine-Tuned Evaluation on Romanian

author.name: Dragos-Mitrut Vasile, Elena-Simona Apostol, Stefan-Adrian Toma, Adrian Paschke, Ciprian-Octavian Truica

entry.summary: Evaluates cross-lingual relation extraction for low-resource Romanian by translating SemEval-2010 Task 8 with an LLM pipeline and testing Gemma 4 31B under zero-shot, few-shot, and QLoRA fine-tuning against encoder baselines. Reports a modest performance drop from English to Romanian.

entry.title: Better Understanding, Understanding Better

author.name: Yu Wei (Department of Philosophy, East China Normal University)

entry.summary: Introduces a comparative epistemic logic of understanding with level-indexed understanding modalities and a connective for comparing how well agents understand why a proposition holds, addressing understanding's neglect in epistemic logic despite its centrality in epistemology and AI debates. Formalizes that understanding comes in degrees.

entry.title: Knowledge-Driven Dimension Estimation from a Single Image -3D Asset Generation Technology for Digital Twin Construction

author.name: Hidenori Sakaniwa, Akihito Akai, Akihiko Hyodo

entry.summary: This paper estimates real-world object scale from a single monocular image by decomposing objects into structural elements and integrating design-rule and geometric knowledge, targeting traffic-sign sizing for digital-twin/simulation construction. It addresses scale mismatch between virtual and real environments in in-vehicle camera verification.

entry.title: Horseshoe Priors for Spatial Small Area Estimation: Regular Variation, Tail Robustness, and Deep Learning

author.name: Dhiman Bhadra, Nicholas Polson

entry.summary: This paper studies horseshoe (heavy-tailed global-local) priors in the Fay-Herriot model for spatial small area estimation, analyzing regular variation, tail robustness, and connections to deep learning. It contributes theoretical characterizations of when heavy-tailed pooling outperforms Gaussian smoothing.

entry.title: Who Determines the Meaning of an Emotion? Affective Sovereignty as an Epistemic Consequence of Measurement Limits

author.name: Keito Inoshita

entry.summary: This philosophical paper asks who holds final authority to determine the meaning of one's own emotion as emotion-sensing AI becomes embedded in society, coining the term Affectosphere. It analyzes measurement limits by decomposing annotation uncertainty into reducible and irreducible components.

entry.title: PGUDA: Pressure-Guided Unsupervised Domain Adaptation with Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation for sEMG-Based Gesture Recognition

author.name: Yurui Liu, Xiao-Cong Zhong, Qisong Wang, Xuefu Wang, Dan Liu, Jinwei Sun

entry.summary: PGUDA is an unsupervised domain-adaptation framework for sEMG gesture recognition that uses stable pressure signals to guide cross-modal knowledge distillation, mitigating cross-subject and cross-session distribution shifts. Aims to improve deployment robustness of EMG-based human-computer interfaces.

entry.title: Von Mises Based Uncertainty Quantification for Closely Spaced Automotive Radar Targets

author.name: Vinay Kulkarni, V. V. Reddy

entry.summary: Compares a von Mises circular-statistics ensemble against evidential deep learning for uncertainty-aware direction-of-arrival estimation of closely spaced automotive radar targets. Reports the ensemble yields interpretable directional uncertainty and better out-of-distribution behavior.

entry.title: Improving multichannel speech enhancement through accurate room-acoustic simulations

author.name: Georg G\"otz, Alessia Milo, Steinar Gu{\dh}j\'onsson, Daniel Gert Nielsen, Jesper Pedersen, Finnur Pind

entry.summary: Studies how room-acoustic simulation fidelity affects multichannel speech enhancement, training SpatialNet on datasets from geometrical, wave-based, and hybrid acoustic modeling and evaluating on measured data. Finds higher-fidelity wave-based simulation improves real-world performance.

entry.title: A Tutorial on Autonomous Fault-Tolerant Control Using Knowledge-Grounded LLM Agents

author.name: Javal Vyas, Milapji Singh Gill, Artan Markaj, Felix Gehlhoff, Mehmet Mercang\"oz

entry.summary: A tutorial framework treating LLM agents as constrained supervisory planners for autonomous fault-tolerant control in process plants, proposing recovery actions that are validated by external symbolic or simulation-based checkers before actuation. Develops design dimensions for knowledge-grounded fault recovery.

entry.title: Agency is not a natural kind (and why that might matter for alignment)

author.name: SJ_Beard

entry.summary: This post argues that agency is not a natural kind, contending that humans and other systems we attribute agency to are really messy hierarchies of processes rather than unified thought-driven agents, and explores why this matters for alignment. It challenges folk-psychological framings underlying agent-based safety thinking.

entry.title: Q&A: What is agentic AI today, and what do we want it to be?

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: In this MIT News Q&A, MIT's Phillip Isola explains what agentic AI is (AI that takes actions in the world, physical or digital) versus generative AI, discussing the underlying models and mechanisms as businesses rapidly deploy AI agents. It provides accessible context on a fast-growing deployment trend.

entry.title: Team MKC at CLPsych 2026: Capturing and Characterizing Mental Health Changes through Social Media Timeline Dynamics

author.name: Kyomin Hwang, Hyeonjin Kim, Hyunho Lee, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: Describes a CLPsych 2026 shared-task LLM pipeline for capturing and characterizing mental-health changes across sequentially ordered social-media timelines, aiming to support early detection and continuous monitoring of psychological well-being. Focuses on temporal timeline dynamics for mental-health analysis.

entry.title: Neuro-Bayesian-Symbolic Residual Attention Shallow Network: Explainable Deep Learning for Cybersecurity Risk Assessment

author.name: Nicolaie Popescu-Bodorin, Madeleine Togher

entry.summary: NBS-RASN is a hybrid shallow neural architecture combining neural, Bayesian, and symbolic components for explainable cybersecurity risk assessment, enforcing epistemological axioms as hard constraints. It claims deep-learning behavior from a shallow interpretable network.

entry.title: From Idea to Prototype in an Afternoon: Scaffolded, AI-Assisted Rapid VA Prototyping

author.name: Gennady Andrienko, Natalia Andrienko

entry.summary: A case study showing that combining a workflow-scaffolding language (ATWL) with an AI assistant reduced visual-analytics prototyping from months to an afternoon. Derives lessons about the necessity of both structured scaffolds and human expertise for effective AI-assisted development.

entry.title: Cluelessness: Summary of the argument, why it matters, and counterarguments

author.name: Anthony DiGiovanni

entry.summary: This post summarizes the unawareness argument for cluelessness in effective altruism, breaking it into normative and epistemic premises and outlining the most productive lines of critique. It aims to orient participants in a critique competition on whether we can justifiably rank actions by long-run consequences.

entry.title: Why Prefer Any Decision Theory?

author.name: J Bostock

entry.summary: This post defends Functional Decision Theory, arguing that critics who construct scenarios where FDT fails are falling foul of symmetry arguments and applying inconsistent standards of rigor. It contends FDT ties or beats CDT across the abstract-to-practical spectrum.

entry.title: Information-Aided DVL Calibration

author.name: Zeev Yampolsky, Itzik Klein

entry.summary: Presents an information-aided method to calibrate Doppler velocity logs for underwater vehicle navigation when GNSS reference signals are unavailable, replacing conventional Kalman-filter calibration. Targets robustness of AUV navigation in GNSS-denied environments.

entry.title: Calibrating the Evaluator: Does Probability Calibration Mitigate Preference Coupling in LLM Agent Feedback Loops?

author.name: Zewen Liu

entry.summary: Investigates whether probability calibration of LLM evaluators can reduce evaluator preference coupling, where evaluator biases propagate into agent-learned strategies during feedback-loop training. Reports the first study comparing binary versus confidence-calibrated feedback in a small controlled experiment.

entry.title: Is it ethical to work on general-purpose robots given the risk of cyberhacking?

author.name: Master Chief

entry.summary: This post raises the ethical question of whether developing general-purpose robots is responsible given the risk that mass-deployed robots could be hacked and repurposed for repression, enabling totalitarian control. It notes the near-absence of assessments of this specific risk pathway.

entry.title: Minimizing Quantized Semantic Age of Information (QSAoI) in Foundation Model-Based Semantic Communications

author.name: Huanyu Zhang, Yulin Hu, Xiaopeng Yuan, Aydin Sezgin, Anke Schmeink

entry.summary: Introduces Quantized Semantic Age of Information, a metric capturing freshness versus semantic efficiency tradeoffs for foundation-model-based semantic communications in 6G finite-blocklength regimes, and a co-designed resource-allocation framework to minimize it. Bridges semantic and physical layers for low-latency transmission.

entry.title: Unjournal tool hub (finding & assessing high-impact research questions, cruxes, papers, etc.)

author.name: david reinstein

entry.summary: The Unjournal announces a hub of tools for finding and assessing high-impact research, including a prioritization dashboard, a cruxes and pivotal-questions explorer, and LLM-assisted evaluation guides. It aims to help researchers choose impactful questions and improve research evaluation.

entry.title: Expanding our Heat Resilience data to 50+ global cities

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google announces the expansion of its Heat Resilience dataset to more than 50 global cities, supporting climate adaptation efforts. The post is a brief update on applied climate and sustainability data infrastructure.

entry.title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning based Intrusion Detection in Realistic IoT Networks

author.name: Rana Alharbi, Chuadhry Mujeeb Ahmed

entry.summary: Compares machine-learning intrusion detection methods on the realistic Gotham2025 IoT dataset generated from 78 emulated devices across MQTT, CoAP, and RTSP protocols. Aims to help safeguard resource-constrained IoT networks against attacks.

entry.title: In partial defence of p(doom)

author.name: Mikhail Samin

entry.summary: Mikhail Samin defends p(doom) as a useful shorthand for surfacing disagreements and identifying whether someone is engaging with core AI risk arguments, while acknowledging it is less useful among informed rationalists. It advocates using the number as a communication and double-crux tool.

entry.title: Creating Intelligence: A Computational Foundation for AGI

author.name: Peter Overmann

entry.summary: This work proposes a computational theory of mind grounded in set theory and hyperdimensional computing, representing information as sparse binary sets with learning driven by topological plasticity rather than scalar weight updates. It claims associative memory emerges naturally from combinatorially expanded network topologies.

author.name: Shiyi Chen, Nicholas Saban, Collin Hargreaves, Huiqi Wang

author.name: Benjamin Breen, Austin Letson, Borja Requena Pozo, Leopoldo Sarra

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.32007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study agentic code generation in Dafny, where a model must generate both executable code and the proof artifacts for verification. We present AxDafn...

author.name: Sk Md Ahnaf Akif Alvi, Jan Janssen, Danny Perez, Douglas Allaire, Raymundo Arroyave

author.name: Chukwuemeka Ugwu, Oluwafemi Richard Oyeleke

author.name: Xinze Zhang

author.name: Carlos Eduardo Sanoja, Oscar Enrique Moreno Mayz

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.30650v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Educational support services often face a qualified-capacity problem: staff time is scarce, qualifications decay, new support needs can appear before...

author.name: Xinyu Qin, Vicky Ye, Ruiheng Yu, Lu Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.30651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Delirium is common in hospitalized patients and is often missed in routine care. We present a user-centered interactive machine learning (UC-iML) fra...

author.name: Muneera Bano, Didar Zowghi

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.30652v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transparency is increasingly mandated for public-sector AI systems, with organisations required to publish statements describing their AI use and ove...

author.name: Marina Mancoridis, Zo\"e Hitzig

author.name: Anshumali Shrivastava

entry.title: Separation of Knowledge and Reasoning?

author.name: HGross

entry.summary: This post asks whether AI research has attempted to surgically remove specific pretrained knowledge from a model without degrading reasoning, then retrain it to reacquire that knowledge via reasoning and tools, aiming for small models capable when tool-augmented. It probes the separation of memorized knowledge from reasoning.

entry.title: The Slogan Strikes Again

author.name: mrdodson

entry.summary: This essay examines the compression-is-intelligence slogan, framing LLM training as compressing the human text corpus into weights and using the compression of mathematics as an intuition for how learning arises when a model cannot simply memorize. It offers an information-theoretic perspective on why LLMs appear intelligent.

entry.title: That Which Cannot Be Poked With A Stick Is The Mind-Killer

author.name: Firinn

entry.summary: This rationalist essay extends the politics-as-mind-killer theme, arguing that empirically untestable disagreements (those that cannot be poked with a stick) are especially prone to distorted reasoning. It uses a parable of two rationalist houses debating prison abolition to illustrate the difficulty of resolving non-experimental cruxes.

entry.title: Interpersonalized recommendations

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Katja Grace muses on why recommendation services like Netflix do not offer joint recommendations for groups or pairs of users despite having individual profiles, noting how useful and seemingly feasible this would be. It is a light observation on a gap in recommender-system products.

entry.title: Connect to your past selves

author.name: PatrickDFarley

entry.summary: This personal-development post frames introspection as connecting to one's past selves for reflection, accountability, and consistency, treating identity as a four-dimensional entity. It offers a productivity-coaching perspective on self-understanding.

entry.title: Should authors or readers fill the gaps in mathematical arguments?

author.name: knowledgeMaintenance

entry.summary: This post argues about whether authors or readers should fill gaps in mathematical arguments, contending that large gaps increase total time cost across many readers while small one-line gaps are acceptable. It offers qualitative and quantitative reasoning about mathematical exposition norms.

entry.title: More Failed Eggless Choux

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: This post documents repeated failed attempts to make eggless choux pastry using vegan egg white protein, noting the batter looked right but did not puff, with a hypothesis about eggs' multiple proteins setting at different temperatures. It is a personal cooking experiment.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 30, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by reinforcement learning post-training theory and safety/interpretability, with strong data-centric and retrieval contributions.

Data, retrieval & multimodal

  • DataComp-VLM (DCVLM) extends the influential DataComp benchmark to vision-language models with 160 datasets for controlled data-centric experiments (Schmidt, Bethge, Jitsev).
  • PixelRAG shows representing websites as screenshots and retrieving in pixel space beats text-based RAG (Zaharia, Gonzalez, Min).

RL & post-training theory

  • A rigorous derivation of GRPO from the policy gradient theorem exposes credit-assignment failure, gradient sparsity, and rank collapse.
  • Analysis of online imitation learning (on-policy distillation) clarifies it beats offline SFT only under (non-)realizability conditions.
  • The Mirage of Optimizing Training Policies attributes RL instability to training-inference engine mismatch.
  • When More Sampling Hurts identifies modal and correlation ceilings limiting test-time scaling.

Safety & interpretability

  • Causal Perturbative Elicitation (CPE) surfaces hidden latent behaviors via low-rank adapters with high data efficiency.
  • Three negative results show internal-state probes read situational context, not upcoming agentic actions—undercutting pre-action misalignment monitoring.
  • Causal-register interventions test whether models actually compute from scratchpad reasoning.
  • A formal cryptographic study initiates proofs of ownership for ML models.
entry.content:
Today's research is dominated by reinforcement learning post-training theory and safety/interpretability, with strong data-centric and retrieval contributions.

Data, retrieval & multimodal

  • DataComp-VLM (DCVLM) extends the influential DataComp benchmark to vision-language models with 160 datasets for controlled data-centric experiments (Schmidt, Bethge, Jitsev).
