  • PixelRAG shows representing websites as screenshots and retrieving in pixel space beats text-based RAG (Zaharia, Gonzalez, Min).

RL & post-training theory

  • A rigorous derivation of GRPO from the policy gradient theorem exposes credit-assignment failure, gradient sparsity, and rank collapse.
  • Analysis of online imitation learning (on-policy distillation) clarifies it beats offline SFT only under (non-)realizability conditions.
  • The Mirage of Optimizing Training Policies attributes RL instability to training-inference engine mismatch.
  • When More Sampling Hurts identifies modal and correlation ceilings limiting test-time scaling.

Safety & interpretability

  • Causal Perturbative Elicitation (CPE) surfaces hidden latent behaviors via low-rank adapters with high data efficiency.
  • Three negative results show internal-state probes read situational context, not upcoming agentic actions—undercutting pre-action misalignment monitoring.
  • Causal-register interventions test whether models actually compute from scratchpad reasoning.
  • A formal cryptographic study initiates proofs of ownership for ML models.

entry.title: DataComp-VLM: Improved Open Datasets for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Matteo Farina, Vishaal Udandarao, Thao Nguyen, Selim Kuzucu, Maximilian B\"other, Andreas Hochlehnert, Adhiraj Ghosh, Marianna Nezhurina, Karsten Roth, Joschka Struber, Yuhui Zhang, Sebastian Dziadzio, Elaine Sui, Soumya Jahagirdar, Dhruba Ghosh, Hasan Hammoud, Thomas De Min, Simone Caldarella, Jehanzeb Mirza, Sedrick Keh, Mehdi Cherti, Hilde Kuehne, Bernt Schiele, Serena Yeung-Levy, Muhammad Ferjad Naeem, Federico Tombari, Ana Klimovic, Elisa Ricci, Matthias Bethge, Sewoong Oh, Ameya Prabhu, Alessio Tonioni, Jenia Jitsev, Massimiliano Mancini, Ludwig Schmidt, Nikhil Parthasarathy

entry.summary: Introduces DataComp-VLM (DCVLM), a large-scale benchmark for controlled data-centric experiments on vision-language model training, with 160 datasets and a 6T-token corpus across four data types, enabling systematic study of curation strategies across model and token-budget scales. This fills a gap in VLM data curation benchmarking. It is a major community resource.

entry.title: Proofs of Ownership for Machine Learning Models

author.name: Ran Canetti, Shafi Goldwasser, Or Zamir

entry.summary: Initiates a formal cryptographic study of proof of ownership for ML models, modeling it as a game among owner, thief, and judge to determine when a stolen model can be provably traced to its creator. Authored by leading cryptographers (Canetti, Goldwasser). This establishes theoretical foundations for model IP protection.

entry.title: Mechanistically Eliciting Latent Behaviors in Language Models

author.name: Andrew Mack, Nina Panickssery, Alexander Matt Turner

entry.summary: Causal Perturbative Elicitation (CPE) is an unsupervised method that discovers interpretable low-rank adapters via tensor decomposition to surface hidden behavioral modes in LLMs, learning many interpretable LoRAs from a single example. It can rival supervised elicitation for evaluating latent risks and reshaping model behavior.

entry.title: Internal-State Probes Read the Situation, Not the Action: Three Negative Results for Pre-Action Misalignment Monitoring

author.name: Max Fomin, Elad David, Amit LeVi

entry.summary: Reports three negative results showing that internal-state probes on LLMs read the situation or prompt context rather than predicting the actual upcoming harmful action, undermining their use as pre-action misalignment monitors. Tests span three model families and methods. This is a valuable cautionary finding for interpretability-based safety monitoring.

entry.title: On the Policy Gradient Foundations of Group Relative Policy Optimization: Credit Assignment, Gradient Sparsity, and Rank Collapse

author.name: Amritansh Mishra, Supriyo Chakraborty, Berkcan Kapusuzoglu

entry.summary: Rigorously derives GRPO from the policy gradient theorem, revealing a credit-assignment failure where output-only rewards give every token identical advantage, causing intensifying gradient sparsity and an intrinsic rank-2 gradient structure. Confirms effective rank around 2 via SVD on Nemotron-4B/GSM8K regardless of group size.

entry.title: Do Models Read What They Write? Causal Registers in Scratchpad Reasoning

author.name: Benjamin Shih, John Winnicki, Eric Darve

entry.summary: This work tests whether models actually compute from the intermediate states they write in scratchpad reasoning by editing internal representations while leaving visible text fixed, in a controlled state-tracking task with a known update rule. It matters for process supervision and alignment, since faithful chain-of-thought requires the written state to causally drive later computation.

entry.title: When Does Online Imitation Learning Help in LLM Post-Training? The Role of (Non-)Realizability Beyond Horizon

author.name: Huaqing Zhang, Jingchu Gai, Juno Kim, Bingbin Liu, Andrej Risteski

entry.summary: Analyzes when online imitation learning (on-policy distillation) beats offline SFT in LLM post-training, arguing the benefit hinges on realizability rather than error accumulation. Under realizability offline IL suffices, but in misspecified settings offline IL hits information barriers. This clarifies a key post-training design question.

entry.title: PIXELRAG: Web Screenshots Beat Text for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yichuan Wang, Zhifei Li, Zirui Wang, Paul Teiletche, Lesheng Jin, Matei Zaharia, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Sewon Min

entry.summary: Presents PixelRAG, a retrieval-augmented generation method that represents websites as screenshots and performs retrieval and reading entirely in pixel space, scaling to 30 million Wikipedia screenshots, and reportedly outperforms text-based RAG. This eliminates lossy HTML parsing. It matters for visually-grounded retrieval over the web.

entry.title: When More Sampling Hurts: The Modal Ceiling and Correlation Ceiling of Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Yong Yi Bay, Kathleen A. Yearick

entry.summary: Examines a fundamental limit of test-time scaling: while sampling more answers raises coverage (the chance at least one is correct), the ability to select the right one is capped, so extra samples can entrench confident mistakes. Introduces the notion of an identifiability gap between producible and pickable answers.

entry.title: The Mirage of Optimizing Training Policies: Monotonic Inference Policies as the Real Objective for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jing Liang, Hongyao Tang, Yi Ma, Yancheng He, Weixun Wang, Xiaoyang Li, Ju Huang, Wenbo Su, Jinyi Liu, Yan Zheng, Jianye Hao, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: The authors argue that LLM RL training instability stems from a mismatch between separate training and inference engines, and that the real objective should be monotonic improvement of the inference policy rather than the training policy. This reframing targets a fundamental source of RL post-training fragility and collapse.

entry.title: CAREBench: A Child-Safety Risk Benchmark for Language Models

author.name: Kaavya Krishna-Kumar, Elaine Lau, Vaughn Robinson, Jay Caldwell, Sheriff Issaka, Skyler Wang, Francisco Guzm\'an, Steven Kelling, Jonas Mueller

entry.summary: CAREBench is a benchmark of 500 prompts across twelve child-safety risk categories—including grooming, impersonation, surveillance, and emotional dependence—targeting upstream harms before explicit abuse. It addresses a gap in existing child-safety evaluations that focus narrowly on abuse material.

entry.title: Diffusion Fine-tuning with Rewarded Moment Matching Distillation

author.name: Alexis Jacq, Guillaume Couairon, Valentin De Bortoli, Quentin Berthet, Arnaud Doucet, Romuald Elie

entry.summary: Introduces Rewarded Moment Matching Distillation (RMMD), which jointly distills diffusion models and maximizes a reward while preserving generative naturalness via integral KL regularization. It studies the underexplored interaction between distillation and RL fine-tuning in diffusion post-training. This advances efficient, high-quality diffusion generation.

entry.title: The Fundamental Limits of Valid Transport Map Estimation

author.name: Sivaraman Balakrishnan

entry.summary: Formalizes the task of estimating any valid transport map (not necessarily optimal) in a minimax framework, yielding sample-complexity lower bounds applicable to flow matching and diffusion-based generative models. Single-authored by a respected statistician. This provides fundamental statistical limits for modern generative modeling.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction with Macro-Coverage Guarantees

author.name: Aabesh Bhattacharyya, Tiffany Ding, Rina Foygel Barber

entry.summary: Develops conformal prediction methods that guarantee macro-coverage (unweighted average of class-conditional coverage), a middle ground between marginal and class-conditional coverage that handles rare classes better. Authored by leading conformal-prediction researchers (Barber). This advances reliable uncertainty quantification for classification.

entry.title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Image: Advancing Masked Discrete Diffusion for High-Resolution Image Synthesis

author.name: Shufan Li, Greg Heinrich, Hanrong Ye, Yonggan Fu, Aditya Grover, Jan Kautz, Pavlo Molchanov

entry.summary: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Image is a masked discrete diffusion model for high-resolution text-to-image synthesis that tackles the lack of self-correction in discrete tokens and the sparse training signal from large tokenizer vocabularies. The work, from NVIDIA researchers, claims state-of-the-art results for masked image generation.

entry.title: When Can Conformal Risk Control Certify LLM Outputs? Bounds, Impossibility, and Adaptation for Structured Generation

author.name: Varun Kotte

entry.summary: Characterizes when conformal risk control can certify structured LLM outputs (NER, JSON, QA) and proves an impossibility result giving a closed-form feasibility test when base risk exceeds the target. Analyzes a certification hierarchy across Hoeffding, empirical Bernstein, and betting-based bounds.

entry.title: TraceLab: Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving

author.name: Kan Zhu, Mathew Jacob, Chenxi Ma, Yi Pan, Stephanie Wang, Arvind Krishnamurthy, Baris Kasikci

entry.summary: Releases TraceLab, a trace of roughly 4,300 real coding-agent sessions (~350k LLM steps, 430k tool calls) from Claude Code and Codex usage, analyzing workload patterns like long autonomous loops and long contexts with short outputs. This fills a gap for serving-system research. It enables realistic optimization of agentic LLM serving.

entry.title: Pessimism's Paradox: Conservative Offline Training Amplifies Reward Hacking During Online Adaptation in Reasoning Models

author.name: Subramanyam Sahoo, Aman Chadha, Vinija Jain, Divya Chaudhary

entry.summary: Empirically and mechanistically challenges the assumption that conservative offline training protects against reward hacking, finding that higher offline conservatism (via DPO beta) monotonically amplifies reward hacking during subsequent online adaptation on a Qwen3-14B policy. This is a counterintuitive safety-relevant result. It informs the offline-to-online RL pipeline.

entry.title: Meta-learning as a principle for human-like visual representations

author.name: Can Demircan, Marcel Binz, Alireza Modirshanechi, Eric Schulz

entry.summary: Proposes that human-like visual representations arise from meta-learning pressure to acquire new tasks from few observations, training a sequence model across thousands of image-to-concept tasks without human-data supervision and finding closer alignment to human representations than base encoders. This offers a principle for human-aligned vision. It bridges cognitive science and representation learning.

entry.title: On the Nonlinearity of Learning Rate Scaling for LLM Training

author.name: Zaiwen Yang, Huaqing Zhang, Jing Xu, Jingzhao Zhang

entry.summary: Empirically examines learning-rate transfer in LLM training (22M to 707M params), finding the optimal learning rate develops upward curvature at larger scales that breaks log-linear extrapolation. Shows curvature largely disappears when using effective learning rate in normalized weight space.

entry.title: MemLeak: Diagnosing Information Leaks in Multimodal Agent Memory

author.name: Kuan Wang, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: MemLeak shows that multimodal agents fail to truly forget facts even after text deletion because VLMs recover them from retained images via implicit visual cues. The Information Provenance Graph taxonomy and benchmark quantify multi-channel recovery, revealing that deletion success is illusory.

entry.title: Muon learns balanced solutions in matrix factorization without slow saddle-to-saddle dynamics

author.name: Mark Rhee, Jamie Simon, Dhruva Karkada

entry.summary: Studies how the Muon optimizer differs from gradient descent in matrix factorization, showing Muon avoids slow saddle-to-saddle dynamics, learns top modes simultaneously, and remains stable above the gradient-descent sharpness threshold. This deepens understanding of Muon's learning dynamics. It is timely given Muon's growing adoption.

entry.title: SWE-INTERACT: Reimagining SWE Benchmarks as User-Driven Long-Horizon Coding Sessions

author.name: Mohit Raghavendra, Anisha Gunjal, Aakash Sabharwal, Yunzhong He

entry.summary: Introduces SWE-Interact, a benchmark casting software engineering tasks as multi-turn, user-driven sessions where a simulator reveals requirements progressively, testing whether coding agents can discover intent and adapt. This contrasts with autonomous full-spec benchmarks. It better reflects real developer workflows.

entry.title: Scaling the Horizon, Not the Parameters: Reaching Trillion-Parameter Performance with a 35B Agent

author.name: Lei Bai, Zongsheng Cao, Yang Chen, Zhiyao Cui, Shangheng Du, Yue Fan, Shiyang Feng, Zijie Guo, Haonan He, Liang He, Xiaohan He, Shuyue Hu, Yusong Hu, Songtao Huang, Yichen Jiang, Hao Li, Xin Li, Dahua Lin, Weihao Lin, Fenghua Ling, Dongrui Liu, Zhuo Liu, Runmin Ma, Chunjiang Mu, Haoyang Peng, Tianshuo Peng, Jinxin Shi, Luohe Shi, Boyuan Sun, Zelin Tan, Shengji Tang, Qianyi Wang, Yiming Wu, Yi Xie, Xiangchao Yan, Jingqi Ye, Peng Ye, Fangchen Yu, Jiakang Yuan, Bihao Zhan, Bo Zhang, Chen Zhang, Shufei Zhang, Shuaiyu Zhang, Wenlong Zhang, Yiqun Zhang, Junpeng Zhao, Zhijie Zhong, Bowen Zhou, Yuhao Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Agents-A1, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model that reaches trillion-parameter-level performance by scaling the agent horizon via long trajectories (avg 45K tokens) and heterogeneous agent abilities. Uses a three-stage training recipe with knowledge-action infrastructure.

entry.title: Modification-Considering Value Learning for Reward Hacking Mitigation in RL

author.name: Evgenii Opryshko, Umangi Jain, Igor Gilitschenski

entry.summary: Proposes Modification-Considering Value Learning (MCVL) to mitigate reward hacking by treating each transition as a candidate modification, forecasting training paths with and without it and scoring both. Operationalizes current-utility optimization for value-based RL.

entry.title: Representational Depth of Evaluation Awareness Shifts With Scale in Open-Weight Language Models

author.name: Archit Manek

entry.summary: Finds that the layer at which evaluation-awareness is most linearly recoverable shifts from late layers in smaller models to early layers in larger ones across Qwen 2.5, Gemma 2, and Llama 3.2. Suggests scale changes both the strength and representational depth of evaluation-awareness.

entry.title: Building Multi-Task Agentic LLMs via Two-Phase Distillation

author.name: Huaijie Wang, Shusheng Xu, Yi Wu, Kaifeng Lyu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-phase distillation approach for building multi-task agentic LLMs by first training per-task RL experts then consolidating them, showing off-policy distillation degrades due to forward-KL mode-covering exceeding student capacity while on-policy is mode-seeking but needs strong initialization. It offers an alternative to directly training a single model on mixed tasks.

entry.title: Attractor States Emerge in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations

author.name: Ting-Wen Ko, Jonas Geiping

entry.summary: Studies long-run dynamics of multi-turn LLM-to-LLM conversations across 7 models and 20 topics, finding model-specific attractor states that asymmetrically draw conversation partners in mixed debates. This reveals stable behavioral patterns in model interactions. It matters for understanding multi-agent system dynamics.

entry.title: Generating in the Limit with Infinitely Many Hallucinations

author.name: Irene Strauss, Alexandra Butoi, Ryan Cotterell

entry.summary: Extends language generation in the limit theory by introducing a precision notion and recasting coverage-validity tension as a recall-precision tradeoff, analyzing generation under constraints on enumeration, novelty, and validity. Authored by a strong theory group (Cotterell). This deepens theoretical understanding of hallucination tradeoffs.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Theorem Discovery in a Formal Axiomatic System

author.name: Kazuki Ota, Takayuki Osa, Tatsuya Harada

entry.summary: Develops a self-supervised theorem-discovery agent that starts only from axioms and inference rules, alternating proof search with useful-theorem extraction to grow a theorem library without human mathematical priors. This probes whether agents can autonomously discover useful mathematics. It matters for autonomous mathematical reasoning research.

entry.title: On the Inseparability of Instructions and Data in Shared-Embedding Sequence Models

author.name: Dewank Pant, Shruti Lohani, Avijit Kumar

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical impossibility result proving that perfect prompt-injection prevention is mathematically unachievable in shared-embedding architectures lacking enforced control-data separation. It formalizes prompted systems and defines Semantic-Faithful Control, showing it cannot be achieved within the shared pipeline.

entry.title: HARD-KV: Head-Adaptive Regularization for Decoding-time KV Compression

author.name: Yuxuan Yang, Feiyang Ren, Bowen Zeng, Dalin Zhang, Jinpeng Chen, Gang Chen, Huan Li

entry.summary: Presents HARD-KV, a framework reconciling head-adaptive KV-cache compression (which improves accuracy but uses fluctuating memory) with rigid static memory requirements of engines like vLLM. Uses a cascade cache hierarchy and logits calibration for consistent top-p budgeting.

entry.title: Statistically Indistinguishable, Operationally Distinct: A Formal Barrier for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Tassilo Klein, Johannes Hoffart

entry.summary: Defines the Operational Turing Test showing tabular foundation models cannot distinguish legal from rule-violating database states whose marginals match closely, using Le Cam's lemma to bound any values-only classifier near chance. Demonstrates that only rule-derived audits close the gap.

entry.title: Few-Step Boltzmann Generators via Scalable Likelihood Flow Maps

author.name: RuiKang OuYang, Hanlin Yu, Xinyue Ai, Yutong He, Nicholas M. Boffi, Pradeep Ravikumar, Jose Miguel Hernandez-Lobato, Max Simchowitz, Benjamin Kurt Miller, Omar Chehab

entry.summary: Introduces SCALLOP, a scalable likelihood distillation for flow maps that improves density estimation in few-step generative models, replacing high-variance Hutchinson trace estimators. Builds on the F2D2 likelihood flow-map model for Boltzmann generators.

entry.title: Symbolic Mechanistic Data Attribution: Tracing Training Influence to Learned Behavioral Policies

author.name: Reza Habibi, Darian Lee, Magy Seif El-Nasr

entry.summary: Introduces Symbolic Mechanistic Data Attribution (SMDA), which attributes training examples to interpretable symbolic policies governing model behavior using ridge regression over sparse-autoencoder features. Distills a symbolic refusal-behavior policy in Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct.

entry.title: CRAFT: Counterfactual Credit Assignment from Free Sibling Rollouts for Self-Distilled Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zibin Meng, Kani Chen

entry.summary: Introduces CRAFT, a counterfactual credit-assignment scheme for self-distilled agentic RL that reuses the G-1 sibling GRPO rollouts as counterfactuals to overcome the retrospective and sign-blind limitations of single-scalar log-prob-gap gating. Importance-weights sibling rollouts for richer token-level credit.

entry.title: Reported Confidence in LLMs Tracks Commitment More Than Correctness

author.name: Dharshan Kumaran

entry.summary: Tests whether LLM verbal confidence reflects correctness using a two-stage abstention paradigm from perceptual decision-making neuroscience, finding verbal confidence predicts the commit/abstain decision far better than answer correctness. Calibrated token log-probabilities show the opposite, coupling abstention to correctness.

entry.title: The Joint Effect of Quantization and Sampling Temperature on LLM Safety Alignment: A Factorial Analysis

author.name: Hari Prasad, Ritam Pal

entry.summary: This factorial study evaluates how quantization precision and sampling temperature jointly affect LLM safety alignment across 9 models, 3 precisions, and 6 temperatures, generating ~322k responses judged by a six-model ensemble. It clarifies whether common deployment-time compression and sampling choices erode safety, contrary to broad concerns.

entry.title: Accelerating Q-learning through Efficient Value-Sharing across Actions

author.name: Prabhat Nagarajan, Brett Daley, Martha White, Marlos C. Machado

entry.summary: This paper introduces a mean-expansion layer that accelerates Q-learning by sharing value structure across actions within a state and reframing learning to avoid moving values far from near-zero initialization. It addresses fundamental inefficiencies in action-value learning from credible RL authors (White, Machado).

entry.title: Stabilizing Extrapolation in Looped Transformers via Learned Stochastic Stopping

author.name: Hsun-Yu Kuo, El Mahdi Chayti, Patrik Reizinger, Wieland Brendel, Martin Jaggi

entry.summary: This paper traces brittle length generalization in looped transformers to a spurious correlation between sequence length and loop count, and proposes injecting stochasticity into the number of loops during training plus a learned RL-based halting policy to stabilize extrapolation. It sharply reduces out-of-distribution variance on algorithmic tasks.

entry.title: Beyond IID: How General Are Tabular Foundation Models, Really?

author.name: Lennart Purucker, Andrej Tschalzev, Nick Erickson, Gioia Blayer, David Holzm\"uller, Alan Arazi, Alexander Pfefferle, Mustafa Tajjar, Ga\"el Varoquaux, Frank Hutter

entry.summary: Critiques how tabular foundation models are evaluated, arguing that fragmented benchmarks favor IID settings where these models already excel and exclude harder distribution-shift scenarios. It aims to broaden evaluation to assess true generality. This is important for honest assessment of tabular foundation model progress.

entry.title: Experience Augmented Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Jinda Lu, Kexin Huang, Junkang Wu, Shuo Yang, Jinghan Li, Chiyu Ma, Shaohang Wei, Xiang Wang, Guoyin Wang, Jingren Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes Experience-Augmented Policy Optimization (EAPO) for RLVR, expressing accumulated experience in a policy-adaptive manner rather than reusing fixed trajectories that suffer policy mismatch. This improves sample efficiency in LLM reasoning training. It matters for reducing the high cost of on-policy RL.

entry.title: C$^{2}$R: Cross-sample Consistency Regularization Mitigates Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Haoran Jin, Xiting Wang, Shijie Ren, Hong Xie, Defu Lian

entry.summary: Proposes C2R, a cross-sample consistency regularization that mitigates feature splitting and absorption in sparse autoencoders by enforcing consistent latent assignment across samples. This improves the reliability of SAE-extracted interpretable features at scale. It matters for trustworthy mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: Agentic Safety is an Epistemic Property, Not a Behavioral One

author.name: Charles L. Wang, Keir Dorchen, Peter Jin

entry.summary: Argues that agentic safety should be treated as an epistemic property of an evolving learner rather than a behavioral snapshot, introducing teachability as the capacity to preserve future corrective leverage as systems adapt. This reframes safety certification for dynamic, self-improving systems. It offers a conceptual foundation for corrigibility.

entry.title: FlipGuard: Defending Large Language Models Against Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks

author.name: Aoying Zheng, Anqi Du, Zizhuang Deng, Yuxuan Chen

entry.summary: Introduces FlipGuard, a proactive defense against quantization-conditioned backdoor attacks that selectively perturbs model weights before quantization to break the adversary's alignment between weight patterns and quantization boundaries, without needing training data or trigger samples, plus a Defense Effectiveness Ratio metric. This mitigates a stealthy LLM deployment vulnerability. It matters for secure model quantization.

entry.title: Smooth Scaling Laws Hide Stepwise Token Learning

author.name: Pingjie Wang, Zechen Hu, Peiru Yang, Fu Guo, Debing Zhang

entry.summary: Decomposes smooth language model scaling laws into localized per-token learning events fit with sigmoids, showing aggregate power-law loss arises from a spectrum of stepwise token-learning transitions. Provides a token-level mechanistic account of why scaling laws hold.

entry.title: DiScoFormer: One transformer for density and score, across distributions

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Allen AI introduces DiScoFormer, a transformer-based estimator that infers both density and score from a finite sample in a single forward pass, generalizing classical kernel density estimation. It is reported to remain accurate in high-dimensional and out-of-distribution settings without per-distribution retraining. A genuine architectural contribution to amortized statistical estimation.

entry.title: MALOQ: Massively Accelerated Learning of Operators for Quantum Transport

author.name: Manasa Kaniselvan, Alexander Maeder, Denghui Lu, Alexandros Nikolaos Ziogas, Mathieu Luisier

entry.summary: Introduces MALOQ, an application for training SO(2)-equivariant ML operators to predict DFT Hamiltonian/density matrices for quantum transport across systems up to 100k atoms. Provides custom data kernels and scalable edge-wise distribution to extend electronic-structure calculations.

entry.title: Bayesian Best-Arm Identification with Abstention: A Polynomial-to-Exponential Phase Transition

author.name: Yuqi Huang, Yunlong Hou, Vincent Y. F. Tan

entry.summary: Studies Bayesian fixed-budget best-arm identification with the option to abstain, proving that introducing any small abstention budget shifts undetected-error decay from polynomial to exponential in budget. Establishes matching information-theoretic lower and upper bounds for Gaussian priors.

entry.title: Fuzzing Large Language Models to Elicit Hidden Behaviours

author.name: Mohammed Abu Baker, Lakshmi Babu-Saheer

entry.summary: This paper studies fuzzing—injecting Gaussian noise into weights or activations—as a way to elicit hidden backdoor behaviors in sleeper-agent models without knowing the trigger, testing on six backdoored 7B-13B models. Fuzzing reveals hidden behaviors more often than temperature sampling, offering a practical safety-auditing tool.

entry.title: Arko-T: A Foundation Model for Text-to-Structured 3D Generation

author.name: Liang Wang, Zhaoyang Xi, Zekai Xiang, Heng Meng, Qishan Zhang, Pingyi Zhou, Jin Liu, Litao Chen

entry.summary: Presents Arko-T, a 4B-parameter text-to-design model that converts natural language into editable parametric CAD programs rather than static meshes, aligning the pipeline to a formal design-state notion. It outperforms seven frontier LLMs on most metrics at lower cost. This advances editable, manufacturing-relevant 3D generation.

entry.title: Convergence of Continual Learning in Homogeneous Deep Networks

author.name: Matan Schliserman, Gon Buzaglo, Itay Evron, Daniel Soudry

entry.summary: Characterizes weakly regularized continual classification in homogeneous deep networks as sequential projections onto task margin sets, showing global convergence generally fails but local linear convergence holds under regularity conditions. It unifies continual classification and regression analysis. This extends continual learning theory beyond linear models.

entry.title: One-Step Gradient Delay is Not a Barrier for Large-Scale Asynchronous Pipeline Parallel LLM Pretraining

author.name: Philip Zmushko, Egor Petrov, Nursultan Abdullaev, Mikhail Khrushchev, Samuel Horv\'ath

entry.summary: Challenges the belief that gradient staleness destabilizes asynchronous pipeline-parallel LLM pretraining, showing that one-step gradient delay (PipeDream-2BW) degradation depends strongly on optimizer choice and can be made stable. This enables bubble-free throughput at scale. It matters for efficient large-scale pretraining.

entry.title: The Voronoi Bottleneck: Capacity-Aware Dense Retrieval for Product Search

author.name: Charith Chandra Sai Balne, Rithwik Maramraju, Siddharth Pratap Singh, Rohit Upadhyay, Aditya Singh, Chittaranjan Tripathy, Yogananda Domlur Seetharama

entry.summary: Identifies a Voronoi Bottleneck limiting dense retrieval capacity, proving equivalence between Voronoi complexity and sign-rank for top-1 retrieval and introducing a label-free Capacity Utilization Score that predicts query failure. This gives a geometric theory of dense retrieval limits with diagnostics. It matters for understanding embedding-dimension constraints in product search.

entry.title: MACROCAST: A Vintage-Consistent Time Series Foundation Model for Real-Time Macroeconomic Forecasting

author.name: Andrea Carriero, Davide Pettenuzzo, Shubhranshu Shekhar

entry.summary: Introduces MACROCAST, a lightweight time series foundation model for real-time macroeconomic forecasting designed to rule out both temporal contamination and revision bias by never exposing the model to data unavailable to a real-time forecaster, trained on synthetic series then fine-tuned. This addresses leakage that inflates TSFM evaluations. It matters for credible economic forecasting.

entry.title: Does Verbose Chain-of-Thought Really Help? In-Distribution Evidence that Content, Not Length, Matters

author.name: Wenlong Wang, Fergal Reid

entry.summary: This study tests whether chain-of-thought helps due to useful semantic content or simply extra token computation, by comparing shorter and longer in-distribution generations from the same model on the same question. Across 25 models, extra tokens leave accuracy essentially unchanged, suggesting content rather than verbosity drives gains.

entry.title: A Path-Space Formulation of Prediction in World Models: From a Single Action to Prediction, Planning, and Irreversibility

author.name: Gunn Kim

entry.summary: Reframes world-model prediction as a probability measure over future trajectories, using the Onsager-Machlup path-space form to unify prediction, planning, and uncertainty as operations on a single action functional. Introduces entropy-production measures and irreversibility from model rollouts.

entry.title: DLR: Zero-Inference-Cost Latent Residuals for Low-Rank Pre-Training

author.name: Dong Wang, Wenwu Tang, Yun Cheng, Olga Saukh

entry.summary: Proposes DLR, a training-only, parameter-free residual that augments low-rank pretraining by replicating latent coordinates with a fixed structured residual, folded into weights after training for zero inference cost. Aims to close the quality gap between low-rank and full-rank pretraining.

entry.title: Invariant Reasoning Directions in Latent Trajectories of Language Models

author.name: Arun Vignesh Malarkkan, Manan Roy Choudhury, Utkarsh Byahut, Yash Ravindra Charde, Vivek Gupta, Yanjie Fu

entry.summary: Shows that contrastive refinement signals between stronger and weaker latent reasoning trajectories have a concentrated low-rank structure, while unconstrained updates are paraphrase-sensitive. Introduces TILR, a training-free method to identify and manipulate stable invariant reasoning directions.

entry.title: Multi-Block Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yijie Jin, Jiajun Xu, Yuxuan Liu, Chenkai Xu, Yi Tu, Jiajun Li, Dandan Tu, Xiaohui Yan, Kai Yu, Pengfei Liu, Zhijie Deng

entry.summary: Extends Block Diffusion Language Models from single-block to multi-block diffusion, decoding a running set of consecutive blocks concurrently for inter-block parallelism. Addresses the training-inference mismatch where teacher-forcing differs from bounded running-set inference with heterogeneous noise.

entry.title: Sample Complexity of Scientific Discovery: PAC Learnability of Compositional Function Trees

author.name: \c{S}uayp Talha Kocabay, Talha R\"uzgar Akku\c{s}, Kerem Yal\c{c}{\i}n

entry.summary: Analyzes the sample complexity of symbolic regression via PAC learning, proving that Rademacher complexity of compositional function trees need not blow up exponentially with structure count but is controlled by depth and base-operator Lipschitz constants. Offers a more optimistic view of scientific-discovery learnability.

entry.title: Interventional Flow Matching: Prospective Dose-Response Forecasting with Velocity-Field Jacobian Regularization

author.name: Amirreza Dolatpour Fathkouhi, Justin Lee, Heman Shakeri

entry.summary: Introduces Interventional Flow Matching (IFM), a continuous-time generative framework for prospective dose-response forecasting under planned treatment sequences, demonstrated in glucose management where drivers are policy-dependent. Conditions a velocity field on history and planned future drivers with Jacobian regularization in a bounded latent space.

entry.title: Interpretable Inverse Design of Metal-Organic Frameworks with Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Kyungmin Nam, Seunghee Han, Jihan Kim

entry.summary: Presents LLM4MOF, a closed-loop framework where LLM agents reason about chemistry, build candidate metal-organic frameworks, and test them in simulation over ten autonomous iterations, with one agent proposing interpretable design hypotheses and another translating them into selection constraints. Targets interpretable inverse MOF design.

entry.title: How AI settled the complexity of the oldest SGD algorithm

author.name: Micha{\l} Derezi\'nski, Xiaoyu Dong

entry.summary: This paper narrates how AI models were used to settle the worst-case complexity of the 1937 Kaczmarz algorithm, the earliest known instance of stochastic gradient descent. It is both a historical account and a demonstration of AI-assisted mathematical discovery.

entry.title: The Forgetting-Retention Dilemma: Certified Unlearning Theory in Continual Learning

author.name: Yiting Hu, Lingjie Duan, Qian Zhang

entry.summary: This paper establishes the first theoretical foundation bridging continual learning and certified machine unlearning, formulating the unlearning objective as minimizing post-unlearning excess risk and characterizing the forgetting-retention trade-off. It addresses how cumulative model evolution in CL complicates certified data deletion.

entry.title: Predict, Reuse, and Repair: Accelerating Dynamic Sparse Attention for Long-Context LLM Decoding

author.name: Tianyu Wang, Gourav Rattihalli, Aditya Dhakal, Junbo Li, Zhiwei Ren, Dejan Milojicic, Longfei Shangguan

entry.summary: Proposes PRR, a speculate-reuse-repair runtime that predicts likely KV blocks for dynamic sparse attention, overlapping selection and attention to remove a serialization bottleneck in long-context LLM decoding. It uses an EMA predictor plus a FlashAttention-based repair kernel to recover missed blocks. This matters for reducing inference latency in long-context serving.

entry.title: Turn-Averaged SAEs for Feature Discovery and Long-Context Attribution

author.name: Kevin Der, Harish Kamath, Ben Thompson

entry.summary: Introduces turn-averaged sparse autoencoders that represent each conversational turn with a fixed number of features by reconstructing average activations, avoiding the linear feature scaling with context length. This simplifies long-context attribution and feature discovery. It matters for interpreting long model transcripts.

entry.title: SIGNET: Motion-Level Knowledge Transfer for Cross-Language Sign Language Translation

author.name: Sobhan Asasi, Ozge Mercanoglu Sincan, Richard Bowden

entry.summary: Meshtryoshka is a differentiable rendering framework that combines an off-the-shelf triangle rasterizer with nested mesh shells resembling a matryoshka to reconstruct large-scale unbounded real-world scenes, unlike prior mesh-based methods limited to object-centric scenes. It bridges differentiable rendering and the mesh representations needed by downstream graphics tools.

entry.title: Walking in the Implicit: Interactive World Exploration via Neural Scene Representation

author.name: Zhiqi Li, Chengrui Dong, Zhenhua Du, Hangning Zhou, Cong Qiu, Hailong Qin, Mu Yang, Dongxu Wei, Peidong Liu

entry.summary: Walking in the Implicit proposes a scene-centric paradigm for interactive world exploration that changes the rollout variable from video frame latents to a fixed-length renderable implicit scene state (NIS), factorizing generation into stochastic state transition and deterministic pose-conditioned rendering. It is instantiated as NeuWorld using a transformer VAE and a diffusion transformer.

entry.title: DiLaServe: High SLO Attainment Serving for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Tzu-Tao Chang, Benjamin Yuanyang Hong, Kiet Pham, Shivaram Venkataraman

entry.summary: Presents DiLaServe, a serving system for diffusion language models addressing the speed-quality tradeoff of confidence-based denoising, dynamic parallelization under fluctuating load, and approximate KV caching with non-uniform per-step costs. Targets high SLO attainment.

entry.title: Depth Exploration for LLM Decoding

author.name: Weisi Yang, Zipeng Sun, Stephen Xia

entry.summary: Proposes Depth Exploration Decoding (DEX), a lossless decoding method that explores multiple candidate early-exit depths in parallel rather than selecting a single exit depth, validating against the final-depth model. Reduces wasted computation from too-late exits and fallback discards.

entry.title: Beyond Trajectory Matching: Reflow with Marginal Distribution Alignment

author.name: Chen Wang, Peiran Yun, Pan Xie, Ke Deng

entry.summary: Identifies a theoretical limitation of reflow-based distillation where trajectory matching can under-determine the student's endpoint distribution, allowing identical trajectory loss but different marginals. Proposes adding marginal-distribution alignment to improve few-step generation.

entry.title: Randomized neural operator for parametric PDEs with fast training and conformal uncertainty quantification

author.name: Zirui Deng, Jingbo Sun, Deyu Meng, Fei Wang

entry.summary: Introduces PCA-RaNN, a randomized latent neural operator combining PCA dimensionality reduction, fixed random features, and closed-form least-squares readout to solve parametric PDEs with one-to-three orders of magnitude faster training. Adds conformal uncertainty quantification and energy-matched scaling rules.

entry.title: Same Concept, Different Directions: Cross-Modal Feature Heterogeneity in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Chungpa Lee, Jihoon Kwon, Kyle Min, Jy-yong Sohn

entry.summary: This paper identifies cross-modal feature heterogeneity in vision-language models—the same concept occupies different directions across image and text modalities—challenging the implicit assumption underlying cross-modal sparse autoencoders. It demonstrates this discrepancy and its implications for interpreting joint embedding spaces.

entry.title: When Is a Draft Accepted? A Theory of Acceptance in Speculative Decoding

author.name: Aaryam Sharma

entry.summary: This paper develops a theory of acceptance in speculative decoding for practical regimes—greedy decoding, relaxed acceptance, and tree-based candidates—where success depends on local ranking and threshold events rather than exact distributional equality. It characterizes rejection regions as lower level sets and derives exact KL bounds.

entry.title: Illuminating Unified Multimodal Model for Free-form Interleaved Text-Image Generation

author.name: Chonghuinan Wang, Zhikai Chen, Chunwei Wang, Yecong Wan, Junwei Yang, Zhixin Wang, Wei Zhang, Jiaqi Xu, Renjing Pei, Xiaohe Wu, Fan Li, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: This work shows that a shared canonical object frame can emerge self-supervised from in-the-wild object-centric videos using only noisy Structure-from-Motion camera poses, by routing all training sequences through a shared coarse canonical mesh bottleneck. It removes the manual annotation bottleneck that limited category and instance diversity for cross-instance pose comparison.

entry.title: A Point Cloud Transformer for Remote Monitoring and Automated Assessment of Physical Rehabilitation Exercises

author.name: Kazi Rafat, Md. Ismail Hossain, M M Lutfe Elahi, Sifat Momen, Fuad Rahman, Nabeel Mohammed, Shafin Rahman

entry.summary: ViDiHand leverages representations of a pretrained video diffusion model to reconstruct 4D two-hand pose from egocentric video, adapting it via a hand-overlay rendering objective. It exploits the motion dynamics, occlusion reasoning, and hand-object interaction priors that internet-scale video generation models must implicitly acquire, overcoming the scarcity of hand-pose annotations.

entry.title: Internalizing the Future: A Unified Agentic Training Paradigm for World Model Planning

author.name: Xuan Zhang, Zhijian Zhou, Lingfeng Qiao, Yulei Qin, Ke Li, Xing Sun, Xiaoyu Tan, Chao Qu, Yuan Qi

entry.summary: Proposes training a single autoregressive LLM to internalize what-if planning by verbalizing prospective state rollouts plus a textual analogue of Q-values, addressing the reactive nature of agents in long-horizon tasks. Identifies a format-capability gap where naive fine-tuning yields superficial foresight mimicry.

entry.title: Tandem Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Difan Jiao, Raghav Singhal, Robert West, Ashton Anderson

entry.summary: Extends tandem training, where a stronger senior LLM co-generates rollouts with a frozen weaker junior so reasoning stays followable, to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). It addresses the compatibility problem of RLVR-trained models drifting into idiosyncratic, hard-to-follow reasoning.

entry.title: Constrained Tabular Diffusion for Finance

author.name: Michael Cardei, Jose M Munoz, Oscar Barrera, Shreyas K Chandrahas, Partha Saha

entry.summary: Introduces CTDF, which inserts a training-free feasibility operator into tabular diffusion sampling to enforce hard regulatory and economic constraints on generated financial data. Reports zero constraint violations and improved scarce-data utility.

entry.title: ReGuide: From Test-Time Guidance to Self-Improving Diffusion Policies

author.name: Tzu-Hsiang Lin, Srinivas Shakkottai, Dileep Kalathil, P. R. Kumar

entry.summary: Introduces ReGuide, a self-improving framework that reuses guided diffusion-policy rollouts as on-policy recovery data to combat covariate shift, via phase-conditioned guidance generating corrective trajectories. Avoids discarding corrected trajectories as prior test-time-guidance methods do.

entry.title: A Novel Latent-Class Attack and its Detection by Class Subspace Orthogonalization

author.name: Guangmingmei Yang, David J. Miller, George Kesidis

entry.summary: Proposes a novel latent-class data poisoning attack where poisoned examples from an unknown class are mislabeled to a target class so the model learns the novel class as a sub-class, threatening access-control systems. Also proposes a post-training defense via class subspace orthogonalization.

entry.title: GLACIER: Rethinking Mass Spectrum Prediction as an Object Detection Problem

author.name: Rui-Xi Wang, Runzhong Wang, Connor W. Coley

entry.summary: Reframes tandem mass spectrum prediction as object detection on molecular graphs, with GLACIER a single-stage transformer detecting fragment subgraphs and spectral contributions. Aims for higher accuracy and faster inference than two-stage fragment-scoring approaches.

entry.title: BaRA: Bayesian Adaptive Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Zhibin Duan, Yuhong Wang, Jiahong Fu, Zongsheng Yue, Bo Chen, Zongben Xu

entry.summary: Proposes BaRA, a Bayesian adaptive rank allocation method for parameter-efficient fine-tuning that models posterior distributions over adaptation parameters with context-dependent rank, inspired by probabilistic topic models. Aims to fix overconfidence and miscalibration of fixed-rank LoRA in low-data regimes.

entry.title: Towards Evaluating Data Priors for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Zeynep T\"urkmen, K\"ur\c{s}at Kaya, Alexander Pfefferle, Frank Hutter

entry.summary: Implements a unified interface to compare data-generating priors from recent tabular foundation models independently of their architectures and training protocols. Generates tasks from each prior and trains a fixed architecture to isolate prior effects on downstream behavior.

entry.title: Learning to Bid in Discriminatory Auctions with Budget Constraints

author.name: Negin Golrezaei, Sourav Sahoo

entry.summary: Studies repeated bidding in multi-unit discriminatory pay-as-bid auctions under budget constraints, developing polynomial-time learning algorithms via shortest paths in a DAG that exploit utility decomposition across units. Achieves sublinear regret under full-information and bandit feedback.

entry.title: Adaptive Block Diffusion: Resolving Training-Inference Mismatch in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Gagan Jain

entry.summary: Proposes Adaptive Block Diffusion (ABD) to resolve train-inference mismatch in diffusion language models by optimizing denoising risk over a distribution of prefix-window configurations treated as a stochastic variable. Trains a single model over the full configuration space without architectural changes.

entry.title: STEMGym: Benchmarking Sequential Decision-Making under Dose Budgets in Autonomous Electron Microscopy

author.name: Can Polat, Erchin Serpedin, Mustafa Kurban, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: STEMGym is an open-source Gymnasium benchmark of physics-simulated scanning transmission electron microscopy worlds, scoring agents by a dose-efficiency curve under realistic dose budgets. Surprisingly, it finds that smart adaptive navigation is not the dominant lever for sample-efficient atomic imaging, challenging a core premise of autonomous microscopy.

entry.title: IG-Lens: Exact Additive Probability Attribution Across Transformer Layers via Telescoping Integrated Gradients

author.name: Duc Anh Nguyen

entry.summary: IG-Lens uses telescoping integrated gradients to provide an exact additive decomposition, in probability space, of which transformer layers actually produce a predicted token's probability. It overcomes limitations of logit lens and direct logit attribution that are either non-additive or only additive in logit space.

entry.title: PS-PPO: Prefix-Sampling PPO for Critic-Free RLHF

author.name: Doo Hwan Hwang, Kee-Eung Kim

entry.summary: PS-PPO is a compute-efficient critic-free RLHF method that exploits temporal redundancy by sampling and updating from prompt-conditioned prefixes rather than full trajectories, reducing optimization cost for long reasoning traces. It addresses the inefficiency of propagating trajectory-level signals uniformly across all tokens.

entry.title: Theory of Continual Learning Against Data Poisoning Attacks

author.name: Yiting Hu, Lingjie Duan

entry.summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework for strategic data poisoning attacks and defenses in regularization-based continual learning, framing the adversary-defender interaction as an online zero-sum game and establishing a fundamental limit where no defense succeeds beyond a poisoning threshold. It fills a gap in principled CL security theory.

entry.title: Predictive Objectives Discard Exogenous Control-Relevant Features: A Controlled Mechanistic Study

author.name: Ayan Pendharkar

entry.summary: This controlled mechanistic study shows that predictive JEPA-style objectives discard exogenous yet control-relevant features because they optimize temporal predictability rather than control-relevance, even when those features are trivially encodable. A 2x2 design comparing six objectives isolates this failure mode.

entry.title: Beyond Drug Discovery: The Nanotechnology Molecular Optimization (NMO) Benchmark

author.name: Matthias Blaschke, Daniel Kienzle, Zsuzsanna Koczor-Benda, Julian Lorenz, Rainer Lienhart, Fabian Pauly

entry.summary: The Nanotechnology Molecular Optimization Benchmark replaces drug-discovery proxy oracles with quantum simulations to drive generative molecular design toward scientifically grounded quantum-materials targets. It serves as both a rigorous ML testbed and a discovery engine for nanotechnology, addressing transferability limits of pharma-centric benchmarks.

entry.title: B3O: Scalable Boltzmann Batch Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Maximilian Bloor, Liyuan Xu, Hrvoje Stojic, Victor Picheny

entry.summary: B3O reframes batch Bayesian optimization as sampling directly from a Boltzmann distribution defined by the acquisition function, avoiding the computational bottlenecks and diversity erosion of existing large-batch methods. It proves negligible additional regret and shows strong empirical performance for massively parallel simulation workflows.

entry.title: On the Vulnerability of Parameter-Level Defenses to Model Merging

author.name: Kuangpu Guo, Qingyan Zheng, Jian Liang, Yongcan Yu, Zilei Wang, Ran He, Tieniu Tan

entry.summary: This paper analyzes parameter-level defenses against unauthorized model merging and reveals that protected task vectors are inherently small in magnitude, leaving weights dominated by the pretrained model. The proposed Anchor-Guided Attack uses the pretrained model as a static reference to circumvent existing safeguards, exposing their vulnerability.

entry.title: MuonSSM: Orthogonalizing State Space Models for Sequence Modeling

author.name: Thai-Khanh Nguyen, Ngoc-Bich-Uyen Vo, Thieu N. Vo, Tan M. Nguyen, Cuong Pham

entry.summary: Introduces MuonSSM, which stabilizes state-space model training by conditioning the geometry of memory updates using a momentum pathway and Newton-Schulz orthogonalization on low-rank injections, preserving parallel scan complexity. It improves gradient propagation and long-horizon stability. This advances efficient long-sequence modeling architectures.

entry.title: Vision-driven Preference Synthesis for Mitigating Hallucinations in VLMs

author.name: Yunhun Nam, Jongheon Jeong

entry.summary: Introduces ViPSy, a vision-driven preference synthesis framework that constructs preference pairs that are both policy-aligned and visually grounded to reduce hallucinations in vision-language models, addressing limitations of intervention- and sampling-based methods. This improves visual faithfulness via better DPO-style data. It matters for trustworthy VLMs.

entry.title: Spectral phase transitions and trainability in neural network learning dynamics

author.name: Chanju Park, Dario Bocchi, Francesco D'Amico, Biagio Lucini, Gert Aarts

entry.summary: Frames neural network training as stochastic evolution of a random matrix ensemble, identifying a Baik-Ben Arous-Peche spectral phase transition during learning where signal eigenvalues detach from the random bulk, providing a dynamical account of representation formation. This links random matrix theory to trainability. It deepens theoretical understanding of learning dynamics.

entry.title: Neuromorphic Energy-Aware Learning for Adaptive Deep Brain Stimulation

author.name: Binh Nguyen, Colleen Josephson, Mircea Teodorescu, Gert Cauwenberghs, Jason Eshraghian

entry.summary: Introduces energy-aware learning that incorporates actuator energy directly into the RL reward, demonstrated with a deep spiking Q-network for closed-loop deep brain stimulation in a biophysical Parkinson's circuit model, recognizing that actuator energy can dominate controller inference cost. This broadens energy-efficient control beyond inference. It matters for neuromorphic medical devices.

entry.title: J-LAW: Joint Localization and Actionable World Modeling via Coupled Latent Factor Graphs

author.name: Guanqun Cao, Liang Chen

entry.summary: Proposes J-LAW, a coupled factor graph that jointly optimizes metric object poses, latent world states, and latent landmark embeddings, unifying classical SLAM localization with action-conditioned world modeling so each improves the other. This bridges metric consistency and learned latent dynamics for planning. It matters for robotics localization and world modeling.

entry.title: A Theoretical Interpretation of In-Context Learning via Probabilistic Modeling

author.name: Zhenyu Liu, Huaze Tang, Shao-Lun Huang

entry.summary: Presents a probabilistic model of in-context learning and derives ICL performance for general parametric distributions and exponential families, explaining the impact of number of demonstrations, model parameter sensitivity, and demonstration-query similarity. This provides theoretical grounding for ICL behavior. It matters for understanding why ICL works.

entry.title: Cybersecurity is the True Frontier for Generative AI Success or Failure

author.name: Edward Raff, Maor Ashkenazi, Sagar Samtani, David J. Elkind, Sven Krasser

entry.summary: A position and analysis paper arguing cybersecurity is the true frontier for generative AI, highlighting its extreme scale (billion-token malware), labeling difficulty, adversarial ground-truth ambiguity, and need to orchestrate hundreds of tools as agents. Authored by experienced security/ML researchers (Raff). It frames cybersecurity as a demanding multi-problem testbed for LLM agents.

entry.title: Why Struggle with Continuous Latents? Interpretable Discrete Latent Reasoning via Rendered Compression

author.name: Shuochen Chang, Qingyang Liu, Shaobo Wang, Bingjie Gao, Qianli Ma, Haonan Zhao, Yibo Miao, Yulin Sun, Zelin Peng, Jiangtong Li, Li Niu

entry.summary: Introduces Discrete Latent Reasoning (DLR), which converts continuous latent reasoning states into explicit discrete tokens via render-based compression to improve interpretability and training stability. Addresses the instability of continuous latent reasoning while reducing inference length.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Context Rot in Long-horizon Search

author.name: Shijie Xia, Yikun Wang, Zhen Huang, Pengfei Liu

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses context rot in long-horizon deep-search tasks, showing that as context grows, models prematurely give up or return uncertain answers. Through pruning experiments across four open-source models and three benchmarks it links accumulated context to degraded behavior and proposes mitigation strategies.

entry.title: DCGrasp: Distance-aware Controllable Grasp Generation

author.name: Hiroyasu Akada, Jes\'us P\'erez, Emre Aksan, Vasileios Choutas, Cristian Romero, Alberto Garcia-Garcia, Vladislav Golyanik, Christian Theobalt, Thabo Beeler

entry.summary: DCGrasp is a distance-aware controllable grasp generation system for 3D hand-object interactions, built on a novel grasp energy term using a signed distance profile from hand vertices to object surfaces with distance-aware weighting. It supports flexible controllability and generalization across diverse object geometries for robotics, XR, and synthetic data.

entry.title: From Accuracy to Visual Dependence: Auditing and Filtering Modality Collapse in Traffic VideoQA

author.name: Sena Korkut, Mar\'ia Alejandra Bravo Sarmiento, Sanghwan Kim, Zeynep Akata

entry.summary: This work audits modality collapse in traffic accident VideoQA, finding that several open-weight VLMs perform competitively or better without video input, and that adding more frames can degrade accuracy on the MM-AU benchmark. It introduces two diagnostics, Blind Gap and Visual Gain, to quantify genuine visual dependence and filter benchmarks accordingly.

entry.title: Dead-Direction Conditioners: Gauge-Equivariant Preconditioning for Deep Networks

author.name: Tejas Pradeep Shirodkar

entry.summary: Proposes DDC, a Dead-Direction Conditioner that lifts a base optimizer into a G-equivariant one respecting continuous parameter symmetries (logit shift, ReLU rescaling, LayerNorm scale, attention rotation). Keeps the trajectory on the symmetry quotient where optimization effectively lives.

entry.title: Uncertainty Estimation in Pathology Foundation Models via Deep Mutual Learning

author.name: Gb\`egninougbo Aurel Davy Tchokponhoue, Sevda \"O\u{g}\"ut, Ali Idri, Dorina Thanou, Pascal Frossard

entry.summary: DICE is a plug-and-play framework for uncertainty estimation in pathology foundation models that ensembles K frozen models and uses their disagreement as an uncertainty proxy, aligned via deep mutual learning with a theoretical guarantee that the objective upper-bounds model uncertainty. It addresses the lack of reliable confidence estimates that limits clinical adoption.

entry.title: Position: The Term "Machine Unlearning" Is Overused in LLMs

author.name: Sangyeon Yoon, Yeachan Jun, Albert No

entry.summary: This position paper argues that the term machine unlearning is overused in LLM research and should be reserved strictly for dataset-defined deletion that makes a model approximately indistinguishable from retraining without the forget set. It contends many tasks labeled unlearning pursue different policy-dependent objectives requiring distinct methods and metrics.

entry.title: SceneBot: Contact-Prompted General Humanoid Whole Body Tracking with Scene-Interaction

author.name: Sirui Chen, Shibo Zhao, Zhen Wu, Jiaman Li, Guanya Shi, C. Karen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces SceneBot, a unified humanoid whole-body motion-tracking framework conditioning a single policy on reference motions and per-link contact labels to handle locomotion, terrain traversal, and contact-rich manipulation. Uses hindsight scene reconstruction to infer scene-interaction graphs from retargeted human motion.

entry.title: Halt Fast! Early Stopping for Certified Robustness

author.name: Andrew C. Cullen, Paul Montague, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein

entry.summary: Presents a meta-learning framework for anytime-valid certified robustness via randomized smoothing, using a lightweight meta-learner to predict image-specific priors for a sequential E-process. Achieves a 20-fold reduction in sample complexity while maintaining rigorous statistical guarantees.

entry.title: Fisher-Routed Mixture of Experts for Federated Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Wenhao Yuan, Chenchen Lin, Jian Chen, Jinfeng Xu, Zewei Liu, Edith Cheuk Han Ngai

entry.summary: Proposes FedFMX, a Fisher-routed mixture-of-experts framework for federated class-incremental learning that addresses catastrophic forgetting, non-IID heterogeneity, and class misalignment via adaptive expert specialization. Routes samples to expert subsets balancing acquisition and retention.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Routing as Set-Valued Prediction: A WildChat Benchmark and Cost-Aware Evaluation

author.name: Ananto Nayan Bala, Faisal Muhammad Shah

entry.summary: Frames tool/agent routing from prompts as a set-valued prediction problem and introduces a 3,000-prompt WildChat-derived benchmark over a 12-agent catalog with cost-aware evaluation. Compares routing methods on set-level metrics, latency, and cost tiers.

entry.title: How Token Influence Decays with Distance: A Green-Function View of Trained Language Models

author.name: Matthias Br\"andel, Stephan K\"ohler, Oliver Rheinbach

entry.summary: Studies how next-token prediction in autoregressive Transformers responds to perturbations of earlier token embeddings, computing empirical distance-decay of token influence inspired by Green's functions in multilevel PDE solvers. Connects local-strong versus global-weak interaction structure.

entry.title: A Linear Matching Bandit Approach to Online Multi-Human Multi-Robot Teaming

author.name: Yaohui Guo, X. Jessie Yang, Cong Shi

entry.summary: Casts online multi-human multi-robot teaming as a linear matching bandit, proposing LinMatch which updates confidence intervals on unknown robot features and solves optimistic maximum-weighted matching via the Hungarian algorithm each round. Provides novel regret bounds for matching with linear features.

entry.title: PCGD: Physics-Guided Conditional Graph Diffusion for TCAD Device Simulation

author.name: Yihan Zhang, Zhiteng Zhang, Kun Chen, Chen Wang

entry.summary: Introduces PCGD, a physics-guided conditional graph diffusion framework operating on unstructured TCAD meshes to predict coupled electrostatic and carrier-density fields. Uses a condition-aware MeshGraphNet denoiser injecting boundary conditions and device structure via cross-attention.

entry.title: Deterministic Decisions for High-Stakes AI. A Zero-Egress Pipeline with the Deployability of RAG and the Accuracy of Machine Learning

author.name: Craig Atkinson

entry.summary: Identifies intervention bias as a failure mode of zero-shot LLM educational advisors, showing GPT-4o recommends action for 73 percent of students when an oracle deems 70 percent need none, a 43-point false-positive rate. Shows supervised policy learning eliminates this bias in a zero-egress deterministic pipeline.

entry.title: Optimizer Memory Makes Shuffle Order a First-Order Source of Fine-Tuning Noise

author.name: John Sweeney

entry.summary: This paper shows that data shuffle order can be a first-order rather than second-order source of fine-tuning noise because stateful optimizers like AdamW advance their moment buffers by step index, large enough to flip close A/B comparisons. It provides a fit-free way to estimate this noise, with implications for reproducibility of fine-tuning experiments.

entry.title: Towards Generalizable and Evidential Nuclear Magnetic Resonance-Based Molecular Structure Elucidation via Large Language Model Agent

author.name: Zheng Fang, Chen Yang, Yusen Tan, Yunpeng Zhao, Fanjie Xu, Hongxin Xiang, Hanyu Sun, Hanyu Gao, Xiaojian Wang, Wenjie Du, Yuqiang Li, Jun Xia

entry.summary: NMRAgent is an evidential reasoning LLM agent for NMR-based molecular structure elucidation that integrates specialized spectral analysis tools with chemical knowledge graphs to provide atom-level interpretability. It bridges database retrieval (which misses novel scaffolds) and black-box de novo elucidation models.

entry.title: DuoMem: Towards Capable On-Device Memory Agents via Dual-Space Distillation

author.name: Peyman Hosseini, Ondrej Bohdal, Ahmed Alajrami, Andrea Maracani, Ignacio Castro, Matthew Purver, Mete Ozay, Savas Ozkan, Taha Ceritli

entry.summary: DuoMem is a dual-space distillation framework that transfers procedural problem-solving from large teacher models to compact students via both context-space (better teacher-generated memories) and parameter-space (fine-tuning) distillation. It enables memory-augmented agents to run on resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: DRIFT: Difficulty Routing Self-DIstillation with Rhythm-Gated Exploration and Success BuFfer Training

author.name: Haisen Luo, Yiwei Liu, Haoning Wang, Dan Liu, Junxi Yin, Haotian Wang, Lei Zhang, Xiaoyu Tian, Shuaiting Chen, Yuansheng Song, Baoyan Guo, Xiongfei Yan, Bolan Yang, Chengwei Liu, Ming Cui, Jiong Chen

entry.summary: DRIFT is an online self-evolution policy optimization framework for LLM reasoning that combines difficulty routing and rhythm gating to track problem-level learning progress and adapt optimization, avoiding over-optimizing easy problems and under-exploring borderline cases. It enables stable self-improvement without external expert supervision.

entry.title: FlowAWR: Online Adaptive Flow Reinforcement via Advantage-Weighted Rectification

author.name: Zheming Fu, Ruizhe He, Wei Shang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Lei Wang, Chang Liu, Siming Fu

entry.summary: FlowAWR recasts online reinforcement learning for continuous generative flow models as advantage-weighted supervised regression toward rectified velocity targets, avoiding intractable trajectory likelihoods, stochastic SDE samplers, and the training-inference inconsistencies of prior density-approximated methods. It enables relative intra-group quality to modulate optimization strength unlike fixed-magnitude correction approaches.

entry.title: Exploring Differences Between Tabular Enterprise Data and Public Benchmarks

author.name: Myung Jun Kim, Maximilian Schambach, Frank Essenberger, Andre Sres, Johannes H\"ohne

entry.summary: Empirically contrasts enterprise tabular data with public benchmarks, showing that models like TabPFN and TabICL that excel on standard benchmarks can perform poorly on real business data and vice versa. This exposes a benchmark-reality gap. It matters for deploying tabular foundation models in industry.

entry.title: HSAP: A Hierachical Sequence-aware Parallelism for Hybrid-Context Generative Models

author.name: Songxin Zhang, Zejian Xie, Zhuoyang Song, Cong lin, Junyu Lu, Jiaxing Zhang, Bingyi Jing

entry.summary: Presents HSAP, a hierarchical sequence-aware parallelism framework that correctly computes causal attention on hybrid-context packed sequences while maintaining high parallelism degree. This solves cross-contamination problems in sequence parallelism for packed training. It matters for efficient large-scale LLM pretraining and fine-tuning.

entry.title: ReFreeKV: Towards Threshold-Free KV Cache Compression

author.name: Xuanfan Ni, Liyan Xu, Chenyang Lyu, Longyue Wang, Mo Yu, Lemao Liu, Fandong Meng, Jie Zhou, Piji Li

entry.summary: Proposes ReFreeKV, a threshold-free KV cache compression method that avoids the input/domain-specific budget tuning that limits prior pruning techniques on open-domain inputs. This improves robustness of memory reduction during inference. It matters for practical long-context deployment.

entry.title: A Neuroimaging Simulation Framework for Developing and Evaluating Causal AI

author.name: Eryn Libert-Scott, Emma A. M. Stanley, Vibujithan Vigneshwaran, Matthias Wilms, Erik Y. Ohara, Nils D. Forkert

entry.summary: Develops a neuroimaging simulation framework that generates synthetic T1-weighted MR images adhering to user-specified causal structures linking non-image variables to image biomarkers, providing ground-truth datasets for developing and evaluating causal AI. This overcomes the lack of causal ground truth in neuroimaging. It supports causal-AI methodology development.

entry.title: Timesteps of Mamba Align with Human Reading Times

author.name: Yuji Yamamoto, Shinnosuke Isono, Yoshinobu Kawahara, Sho Yokoi

entry.summary: Demonstrates that Mamba's dynamic discretization timestep correlates with human per-word reading times, remaining significant even controlling for GPT-2 surprisal. Proposes Mamba as a new lens for studying real-time human language processing.

entry.title: LatentRevise: Learning from Zero-Hit Reasoning

author.name: Yiqiu Guo, Xueting Han, Qi Jia, Guangtao Zhai, Jing Bai

entry.summary: LatentRevise recovers training signal for zero-hit RLVR prompts where correct trajectories are rarely sampled, by optimizing input embeddings of a failed reasoning prefix anchored on the gold answer. Targets the sampling frontier where new reasoning behavior is most valuable.

entry.title: Building artificial intelligence virtual tissue (AIVT) for tissue state representation, feature prediction, and dynamic simulation

author.name: Qiqi Lu, Qianjin Feng, Shaoqun Zeng, Shenghua Cheng

entry.summary: The paper proposes AI Virtual Tissue (AIVT), a conceptual AI framework grounded in spatial multimodal data to learn unified, spatially resolved, and dynamically manipulable representations of tissue states for health and disease modeling. It aims to capture tissues as multiscale spatially organized biological systems beyond conventional computational models.

entry.title: Explainability-Aware Frustum Attack: Exposing Structural Vulnerabilities in LiDAR-Based 3D Object Detectors

author.name: Chengzeng You, Binbin Xu, Soteris Demetriou

entry.summary: This work introduces an explainability-guided adversarial analysis for LiDAR-based 3D object detectors, using a Saliency-LiDAR method that aggregates integrated gradient attributions to identify spatial reliance patterns, then exploits them with a frustum attack to induce detector failures efficiently. It exposes structural vulnerabilities in point-cloud detectors used in driving.

entry.title: MuseBench: Benchmarking Intent-Level Audiovisual Arts Understanding in MLLMs

author.name: Yuxuan Fan, Gyusik Seo, Jing Hao, Jaemin Cho, Mohit Bansal, Jaehong Yoon

entry.summary: MuseBench is a benchmark for intent-level audiovisual arts understanding in multimodal LLMs, evaluating reasoning about why creative choices (framing, silence, lighting) express artistic meaning across cinema, visual arts, performance, and game design. It moves beyond perceptual recognition to assess understanding of creative intent.

entry.title: Argus: Metric Panoramic 3D Reconstruction for Indoor Scenes

author.name: Xi Li, Linyuan Li, Yan Wu, Tong Rao, Kai Zhang, Xinchen Hui, Cihui Pan

entry.summary: Argus is a feed-forward network for metric panoramic 3D reconstruction of indoor scenes, trained on Realsee3D, a new hybrid dataset of 10K scenes with 299K panoramic viewpoints and metric annotations. It uses a learned covisibility module to select an optimal reference view, avoiding global pose drift in sparse unordered captures.

entry.title: Hyper-Network Neural Functional Maps for Unsupervised Robust 3D Shape Matching

author.name: Dongliang Cao, Florian Bernard

entry.summary: This work introduces a hyper-network that predicts non-linear neural functional maps for unsupervised robust 3D shape matching, modeling the map as a skip-connection MLP whose weights are predicted to better align spectral bases under partiality and topological noise. It overcomes the limitation that linear functional maps fail under significant intrinsic distortion.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient Monocular 3D Gaussian SLAM for Kilometer-Scale Outdoor Scenes

author.name: Sicheng Yu, Dongxu Shen, Beizhen Zhao, Guanzhi Ding, Hao Wang

entry.summary: KiloGS-SLAM is a monocular 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM system designed for kilometer-scale outdoor scenes, jointly addressing fragile long-term pose tracking and excessive memory via a motion-adaptive hybrid tracking module that switches between Essential matrix and PnP models with an on-demand foundation model for trajectory rescue. It targets drift-free poses needed for high-fidelity large-scale mapping.

entry.title: NormAct: A Benchmark for Hidden Social Norm Compliance in Embodied Planning

author.name: Shiyun Zhao, Xinwei Song, Tianyu Guo, Xiaomeng Gao, Mingyuan Liu, Xu Han, Yuanyuan Zhang, Zhenliang Zhang, Xue Feng, Bo Dai

entry.summary: Introduces NormAct, a benchmark evaluating whether embodied MLLM planners infer and comply with hidden social norms embedded in ordinary tasks, scoring goal achievement, norm compliance, and task success. It uniquely tests implicit constraint inference rather than explicit norm knowledge.

entry.title: Large Language Model Teaches Visual Students: Cross-Modality Transfer of Fine-Grained Conceptual Knowledge

author.name: Thomas Shih-Chao Liang, Zhuoran Yu, Yong Jae Lee

entry.summary: Proposes LaViD, a language-to-visual knowledge distillation framework that transfers conceptual knowledge from an LLM teacher to a vision-only student without paired multimodal data, by prompting the LLM to generate MCQs probing semantic class distinctions used as soft labels. It enables cross-modality fine-grained knowledge transfer.

entry.title: Mitigating LLM-based p-Hacking by Preregistering for the Next LLM

author.name: Maria Thomas, Kristina Gligoric, Nihar B. Shah

entry.summary: Proposes a protocol to mitigate p-hacking in LLM-based research by preregistering the experiment and a set of eligible future models, then running confirmatory analysis on the first eligible LLM released after preregistration. Since that model does not exist at preregistration time, prompt-tuning to a desired result becomes infeasible.

entry.title: Bifocal Diffusion Language Models: Asymmetric Bidirectional Context for Parallel Generation

author.name: Yuhang Chen, Xianfeng Wu, Jinhao Duan, Mingfu Liang, Xiaohan Wei, Yunchen Pu, Fei Tian, Chonglin Sun, Parish Aggarwal, Frank Shyu, Luke Simon, Sandeep Pandey, Xi Liu, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: Introduces Bifocal diffusion language models, resolving the bidirectional-quality versus causal-cacheability dilemma in discrete diffusion LLMs through asymmetric bidirectional context that enables KV caching while retaining context access. Targets faster batch-serving inference without sacrificing generation quality.

entry.title: Hierarchical Decision Making with Structured Policies: A Principled Design via Inverse Optimization

author.name: Yuexuan Wang, Jingyuan Zhou, Kaidi Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a principled lower-level optimization formulation for hierarchical RL-optimal-control architectures using inverse optimization, addressing weaknesses of both constraint-violating RL and myopic optimal control. Targets complex constrained control tasks.

entry.title: Priced Motion Through Optimal Faces: A Normal-Fan Geometry for Non-Stationary Adversarial MDPs

author.name: Kai Hidajat

entry.summary: Develops a normal-fan polytope geometry for finite-horizon adversarial MDPs, arguing that the cost of non-stationarity should reflect changes in the optimal policy rather than mere loss movement. Loss vectors expose optimal faces of the occupancy-measure polytope.

entry.title: BrainRiem: Riemannian Prototype Learning for Source-Free Cross-Site Brain Network Diagnosis

author.name: Kunyu Zhang, Tianxiang Xu

entry.summary: Proposes BrainRiem, a source-free domain adaptation framework for cross-site fMRI brain-network diagnosis that learns Riemannian brain prototypes on the SPD manifold via Log-Euclidean metric. Addresses scanner heterogeneity while respecting clinical privacy and manifold geometry.

entry.title: KrishokChat: A Citation-Grounded Dataset and Benchmark for Bengali Agricultural Advisory

author.name: Khan Raiyan Ibne Reza, Omar Ibne Shahid

entry.summary: Presents KrishokChat, the first citation-grounded Bengali agricultural instruction-tuning dataset with 145,500 QA pairs derived from 290 hierarchical knowledge nodes and domain manuals, guaranteeing citation provenance. Includes safety and adversarial instances and a farmer-oriented benchmark for low-resource crop advisory.

entry.title: SP-CACW: Convergence-Aware Client Weighting for Selfish Personalized Learning

author.name: Yaron Kiselman, Kfir Y. Levy

entry.summary: Proposes SP-CACW, a convergence-aware client-weighting framework for selfish personalized federated learning that selects aggregation weights minimizing an upper bound on a target client's convergence error. Can assign zero weight to harmful peers, avoiding negative transfer.

entry.title: Prototype Latent World Model Replay for Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Weizhi Nie, Hui Wang, Weijie Wang, Yuting Su

entry.summary: Proposes Prototype Latent World Model Replay, a memory-free class-incremental learning method storing old classes as distributions over stable hidden states from a frozen encoder rather than as images. Samples old latent states to train a lightweight adapter and classifier alongside new-class features.

entry.title: Dual-Flow Reinforcement Learning with State-Aware Exploration

author.name: Qijun Li, Zheng Fu, Qi Song, Yifei He, Weitao Zhou, Kun Jiang, Diange Yang

entry.summary: Dual-Flow RL is a unified actor-critic framework that jointly models a continuous return distribution and a multimodal policy using conditional flow matching, addressing biased unimodal value estimates and mode collapse in continuous control. State-aware exploration targets high-value action regions.

entry.title: Exploiting Local Flatness for Efficient Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Seonghwan Park, Hyunji Jung, Dongyeop Lee, Namhoon Lee

entry.summary: This paper provides the first systematic investigation showing OOD inputs exhibit larger Hessian curvature than in-distribution data and exploits local flatness for efficient post-hoc out-of-distribution detection. It reduces the heavy computational cost of curvature-based OOD methods.

entry.title: Online Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Gaussian Processes

author.name: Jun Wang, Quoc Phong Nguyen, Julien Monteil, Vu Nguyen

entry.summary: GAIA reformulates online data selection for instruction tuning as a global estimation process using Gaussian Process regression to model continuous utility manifolds across semantic space, overcoming the batch-constrained local optimization of existing methods. An adaptive strategy-fusion mechanism dynamically prioritizes high-utility samples.

entry.title: FlexTab: A Flexible Encoder-Decoder Architecture for In-Context Learning Across Diverse Tabular Tasks

author.name: Marek Polewczyk, Maximilian Schambach, Marco Spinaci, Sam Thelin, Johannes H\"ohne

entry.summary: FlexTab is a flexible encoder-decoder architecture for in-context learning on tabular data that pairs a single task-agnostic encoder producing target-agnostic row embeddings with task-specific decoders, demonstrated across six tasks including classification, regression, anomaly detection, clustering, and entity matching. It disentangles feature representations from specific prediction targets.

entry.title: Depth-Staggered Fibonacci Spacing for Sparse Attention: Static Schedules Beat Learned Dilation and Extrapolate Where Dense Attention Fails

author.name: Chad A. Capps

entry.summary: Studies sparse attention with Fibonacci-spaced offsets and a per-layer scalar controlling spacing, finding that a static depth-staggered schedule beats both fixed and learned dilation and extrapolates where dense attention fails, across 21 small models under a matched recipe. This challenges learned sparsity in favor of structured static schedules. It matters for efficient long-context architectures.

entry.title: Can LLM-as-a-Judge Reliably Verify Rubrics in Agentic Scenarios?

author.name: Yangda Peng, Yunjia Qi, Hao Peng, Haotian Xia, Guanzhong He, Xintong Shi, Richeng Xuan, Songyuanyi Lu, Yixian Liu, Zhichao Hu, Yuhong Liu, Lei Hou, Bin Xu, Juanzi Li

entry.summary: Introduces RuVerBench, the first benchmark assessing LLM-as-a-Judge reliability for rubric verification in agentic deep-research and coding scenarios with 2,458 human-labeled instances. Systematically meta-evaluates whether LaaJ can reliably verify rubrics on long complex outputs.

entry.title: Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models

author.name: Disen Lan, Jianbin Zheng, Yuxi Ren, Xin Xia, Xuanda Wang, Xuefeng Xiao, Xipeng Qiu, Yu Cheng
