entry.summary: Companion work applying entropy-regularized RL to linear-quadratic Stackelberg differential games under Markovian regime switching, deriving exploratory weakly-coupled HJBI equations. Aims to escape suboptimal equilibria via stochastic policies in hierarchical decision settings.

entry.title: AMR: Adaptive Modality Routing for Multimodal Polyglot Speaker Identification

author.name: Chuxiao Zuo, Yao Zhu, Minqiang Xu, Manhong Wang, Yunke Zhang, Fei Huang

entry.summary: Proposes AMR (Adaptive Modality Routing), a fusion module that dynamically assesses per-sample input quality to handle missing modalities and language mismatch in multimodal speaker identification, built for the POLY-SIM 2026 challenge. Uses modality adapters over linguistically robust audio embeddings.

entry.title: I-BBS: Coordinate-Free Inference of Latent Sub-Manifolds Using Random Distance Matrix Theory

author.name: Igor Halperin

entry.summary: I-BBS is a coordinate-free method that identifies low-dimensional latent sub-manifolds from a pairwise distance matrix alone, using random distance matrix theory derived from the Bogomolny-Bohigas-Schmit spectral signature. It applies even when the ambient high-dimensional space is partly observable or undefined.

entry.title: Improved Predictive Performance and Interpretability for Mesomorphic Neural Networks Using Local Fidelity Regularization

author.name: Hugo L. Hammer, Vajira Thambawita, Kristoffer Herland Hellton, P{\aa}l Halvorsen

entry.summary: This work addresses a vulnerability in Interpretable Mesomorphic Neural Networks where explanatory variance collapses into a single weight, producing meaningless interpretations worsened by L1 penalties. Local Fidelity Regularization is introduced to ensure interpretations are reliable while improving predictive performance.

entry.title: Query-Aware Spreading Activation for Multi-Hop Retrieval over Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Illia Makarov, Mykola Glybovets

entry.summary: This paper proposes a query-aware spreading-activation method for multi-hop retrieval over knowledge graphs in Graph RAG, achieving query-aware traversal with a single per-step semantic step rather than loading the full graph into memory or running iterative solvers. It simplifies integration with graph databases compared to flow-diffusion approaches.

entry.title: Characterizing Optimizer-Dependent Training Dynamics Through Hessian Eigenvector Displacement and Localization

author.name: Marcelina Marjankowska, Valerio Modugno, Paolo Barucca

entry.summary: This paper studies how leading Hessian eigenvectors evolve during training using displacement-over-time (from glassy-system analyses) and localization via inverse participation ratio, comparing against a random null model. It characterizes how different optimizers shape curvature-relevant parameter dynamics.

entry.title: A Bayesian latent Gaussian process framework for aerodynamic uncertainty quantification

author.name: Geoffrey Davis, Ashwin Renganathan

entry.summary: Develops a Bayesian latent Gaussian process framework for aerodynamic uncertainty quantification, calibrating cheap low-fidelity computational predictions against sparse, uncertain experimental measurements using Gaussian process surrogates and Kennedy-O'Hagan calibration. This handles uncertainty in both inputs and responses. It matters for reliable aerodynamic prediction.

entry.title: Information Dynamics of Language Communication

author.name: Leonardo S. Goodall, Andrea I. Luppi, Pedro A. M. Mediano

entry.summary: Introduces an information-theoretic framework using LLMs as probabilistic estimators to quantify directed semantic flow (semantic transfer entropy) and decompose multi-source contributions (semantic PID) in communication. Detects reduced information flow across experiments.

entry.title: Auditing LLM-Governed Social Robots with Culture-Specific Moral Gradients

author.name: Carmen Ng, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: Introduces a gradient-based multilingual audit framework testing LLM-governed social robots against culture-specific moral preference gradients in care, education, and service scenarios. Highlights that English-centered moral audits miss pluralistic calibration needs.

entry.title: Mitigating Batch Effects in Histopathology via Language-Mediated Robust Embedding Generation

author.name: Yishu Zhang, Shushan Wu, Zhenzhong Zhang, Didong Li, Huaxiu Yao, Yun Li, Iain Carmichael, Katherine A. Hoadley, Hongtu Zhu, Di Wu, Daiwei Zhang

entry.summary: GLMP mitigates batch effects in histopathology by generating robust numerical embeddings via an intermediate textual representation from pretrained multimodal LLMs. Addresses non-biological variation across tissue source institutions that conventional stain normalization handles poorly.

entry.title: MedEvoEval: Evaluating Continual Evolution of Doctor Agents through Simulated Clinical Episodes

author.name: Hui Zhang

entry.summary: MedEvoEval is an executable longitudinal benchmark evaluating how doctor agents evolve across simulated clinical episodes, including within-episode evidence gathering and cross-episode learning via memory and reflection. Fills gaps left by fixed-input QA and single-encounter benchmarks.

entry.title: SurrogateShield: Beyond Redaction for High-Utility, Privacy-Preserving LLM Interactions

author.name: Sherwin Vishesh Jathanna

entry.summary: SurrogateShield is a client-side proxy that replaces detected personal information in LLM queries with locally generated, type-consistent fake values before sending them to third-party APIs, then restores the originals in responses. Unlike placeholder redaction, this preserves semantic coherence so response quality is not degraded by missing context.

entry.title: JASPR: Joint Spatial Representation learning of histology and spatial genomics for improved virtual genomic screening and clinical prognostication

author.name: Marija Pizurica, Eric Zimmermann, Neil Tenenholtz, James Hall, Olivier Gevaert, Ava P. Amini, Lorin Crawford, Kristen A. Severson

entry.summary: JASPR is a self-supervised framework that jointly learns representations from H&E histology images and spatial transcriptomics through cross-modal reconstruction, incorporating spatial context across modalities. It targets virtual genomic screening and clinical prognostication.

entry.title: Latent-CURE for Breast Cancer Diagnosis

author.name: Weiyi Zhao, Xiaoyu Tan, Lu Gan, Liang Liu, Xihe Qiu

entry.summary: Latent-CURE is a breast ultrasound diagnostic framework using asymmetric weighted chain-of-thought reasoning in latent space to counter shortcut learning under extreme class imbalance, forcing sequential inference of malignant indicators rather than defaulting to dominant benign patterns. It targets structured clinical reasoning over opaque end-to-end correlation.

entry.title: Semantic-Driven Scale and Spatial Selection for Efficient Cross-Modal Alignment in Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation

author.name: Kun Li, Shengxi Gui, Francesco Nex, Michael Ying Yang

entry.summary: This paper proposes semantic-driven scale and spatial selection for efficient cross-modal alignment in referring remote sensing image segmentation, using parameter-efficient tuning that captures cross-modal interactions rather than single-modal optimization. It avoids full fine-tuning of foundation models that is computationally intensive and can distort pre-trained feature representations.

entry.title: Towards Reliable and Robust LLM Planning: Symbolic Feedback-Driven Iterative Self-Refinement Framework

author.name: Jiajing Zhang, Jiamei Jiang, Chenyang Zhang, Feifei Mo, Linjing Li, Daniel Zeng

entry.summary: Introduces a symbolic feedback-driven iterative self-refinement framework to improve LLM robustness and reliability in long-horizon planning. It maps logical symbols into natural language and uses symbolic feedback to correct infeasible plans.

entry.title: JD Oxygen AI Item Center (Oxygen AIIC) V1: An Industrial-Scale LLM/VLM-Centric Solution for Item Understanding, Management, and Applications

author.name: Oxygen AIIC, Chan Long, Chao Liu, Chaofan Chen, Chaohui Dong, Chunyuan Guo, Danping Liu, Debin Liu, Deping Xiang, Fulai Xu, Guangyue Liu, Hao Li, Huichun Hu, Jian Yang, Jianan Wang, Jianbo Zhao, Jiaoyang Li, Jiaxing Wang, Jinglong Li, Jinjin Guo, Jun Fang, Jun Liu, Kai Zhou, Li Wang, Lili Gao, Liying Chen, Luning Yang, Mengdi Zhou, Pengzhang Liu, Qi Lv, Qianyun Wang, Qixia Jiang, Ruyue Li, Shimu Liang, Shuxing Wang, Sijie Zhang, Siqi Li, Tianhao Gao, Wang Ke, Weihu Huang, Wencan Lai, Wenjie Zhang, Xiaohui Zhang, Xiaojing Dong, Ya Liu, Yifeng Zhang, Yixiang Wang, Yongtai Zhang, Yongyi Liao, Zhaoru Chen, Zhen Chen, Zhiyong Ma, Zhiyuan Liu, Zhongwei Liu, Ziyan Xing

entry.summary: Presents JD's Oxygen AI Item Center, an industrial-scale LLM/VLM platform for e-commerce item knowledge production and management across tens of billions of SKUs, built on ontology engineering and structured knowledge pillars. It addresses fast-emerging concepts and massive-scale knowledge production.

entry.title: CalBrief: A Pilot Diagnostic Benchmark for Evidence-Calibrated Scientific Briefing with Large Language Models

author.name: Yu Fu, Yongqi Kang, Yong Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces CalBrief, a pilot diagnostic benchmark for evidence-calibrated scientific briefing, testing whether LLMs can calibrate research takeaways to evidence strength, scope, and missing-evidence caveats over packages of related papers. Uses an auditable role/gap/strength framework over 16 evidence packages and 96 verified takeaways.

entry.title: Not All Relations Rotate Alike: Transformation-Aware Decoupling for Viewpoint-Robust 3D Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Jingjun Sun, Chaowei Wang, Zhirui Liu, Jiaxu Tian, Ming Yang, Yaoxing Wang, Shan Gao

entry.summary: Identifies predicate-level transformation heterogeneity in 3D scene graph generation, where directional predicates should transform with viewpoint while semantic/contact predicates should not, and proposes transformation-aware decoupling for viewpoint-robust prediction. It addresses inconsistency under yaw rotations in embodied settings.

entry.title: CoIn: Comprehensive 2D-3D Inpainting with Gaussian Splatting Guidance

author.name: Hana Kim, Minje Kim, Tae-Kyun Kim

entry.summary: Proposes CoIn, a framework bridging 2D inpainting models and 3D Gaussian Splatting through a multi-stage consistency pipeline supporting arbitrary-shaped masks and tasks like object insertion, not just removal. Introduces Reference Adaptive GS with feature attention for coarse 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: Active Quantum Kernel Acquisition for Gaussian Process Regression

author.name: Jian Xu, Delu Zeng, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: Extends shot-budget-aware quantum kernel estimation from classification to Gaussian process regression, deriving closed-form pair-level sensitivities for non-uniform shot allocation. Targets near-term quantum hardware where each kernel entry costs circuit executions.

entry.title: Adaptive Financial Transformer with Regime-Gated Attention for Stock Return Prediction

author.name: Dishan Sarkar

entry.summary: Proposes the Adaptive Financial Transformer with a market regime encoder and regime-gated attention that biases self-attention based on semantic relationships among 95 engineered financial features grouped into 11 categories. Also corrects sequence-alignment and backtesting issues that inflate reported performance.

entry.title: Speculative Pre-Positioning: Decoding Stateful Sessions to the Next Decision Point Off the Critical Path

author.name: Victor Norgren

entry.summary: Speculative pre-positioning uses idle accelerator time in stateful inference sessions to decode forward to the next decision point using the target model itself, moving cross-request prefill off the critical path and sometimes answering from a cached distribution. It aims to reduce latency without a draft model.

entry.title: Does Role Specialization Matter for Explanation Faithfulness in Mixture-of-Experts?

author.name: Yeji Kim, Housam Babiker, Mi-Young Kim, Randy Goebel

entry.summary: This work investigates whether assigning semantic roles to experts in Mixture-of-Experts models preserves explanation faithfulness, hypothesizing that inter-expert representation overlap degrades role separation. It introduces decorrelation regularization to reduce expert similarity and improve attribution-based faithfulness.

entry.title: Learning as Observable Matrix Dynamics: Diffusive Relaxations versus Phase Transitions

author.name: Igor Halperin

entry.summary: Observable Matrix Dynamics is a diagnostic framework that probes neural network training via a fixed distance matrix over held-out inputs, using random matrix theory to detect spectral reorganizations missed by scalar loss. It distinguishes diffusive relaxation from phase-transition-like training behaviors.

entry.title: GLIP: Graph and LLM Joint Pretraining for Graph-Level Tasks

author.name: Haoxin Sun, Yiqing Lin, Yajun Huang, Chenhui Dong, Mingjun Li, Zhongzhi Zhang

entry.summary: GLIP is a joint pretraining framework for graphs and LLMs targeting underexplored graph-level tasks, which require capturing more complex structural and feature information than node- or edge-level tasks. It involves LLMs in graph pretraining rather than relying on GNN-only methods like GraphCL.

entry.title: From Failure Taxonomy to Intervention: A Diagnostic Methodology for Industry-Scale AVLM in Video and Live-Streaming Platform Moderation

author.name: Shuchang Ye, Jinqiang Yu, Zhujun Xiao, Yajing Kong, Yist Y. Lin, Yang Ma, Jiaxi Liu, Xiaolei Xu, Zheng Yu

entry.summary: This paper presents a diagnostic methodology for industry-scale audio-visual language models in video and live-streaming moderation, focusing on localizing failures and translating them into targeted model-development interventions. It fills a gap where foundation-model studies report recipes but offer little guidance on failure-driven intervention.

entry.title: Federated Learning with Energy-Based Structured Probabilistic Inference

author.name: Dario Fenoglio, Daniil Kirilenko, Martin Gjoreski, Marc Langheinrich

entry.summary: This work refines federated learning client aggregation weights using Conditional Random Fields, modeling both client-specific reliability (unary potentials) and inter-client interactions (pairwise potentials) instead of fixed or heuristic weighting. It improves convergence under non-IID data heterogeneity.

entry.title: Curvature-Weighted Gradient Diversity: A Noise Measure for Geometry-Adaptive SGD Schedules

author.name: Muhammad Hamza (Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur), Ayush Goel (Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur)

entry.summary: Introduces Curvature-Weighted Gradient Diversity (CWGD), a geometry-aware noise measure that weights gradient diversity by inverse-square-root Hessian to better proxy effective optimization noise, enabling curvature-adaptive learning-rate schedules. It proves reduced error floors for convex quadratics. This refines SGD theory and scheduling.

entry.title: Envisage: Diffusion-Based Rhinoplasty Goal Visualization with Mask-Decomposed Evaluation

author.name: Mudit Agarwal, Amit D. Bhrany

entry.summary: Introduces Envisage, a FLUX.1-Fill inpainting pipeline for rhinoplasty goal visualization with clinical presets, plus SurgicalScore, a mask-decomposed evaluation protocol that avoids the confounding of full-image identity metrics under hard-composited localized edits. This addresses localized-edit evaluation. It matters for surgical visualization tooling.

entry.title: Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Token Co-occurrence Graphs

author.name: Gianluca Bonifazi, Christopher Buratti, Michele Marchetti, Federica Parlapiano, Giulia Quaglieri, Davide Traini, Domenico Ursino, Luca Virgili

entry.summary: TIGRAG builds graph-augmented RAG from a token co-occurrence knowledge graph using sliding-window statistics, avoiding expensive and error-prone LLM-based extraction pipelines for multi-hop reasoning. Enables scalable graph construction.

entry.title: CaresAI at CT-DEB26: Detecting Dosing Errors In Clinical Trials Using Domain-Specific Transformer Embeddings and Classification Models

author.name: Leon Hamnett, Favour Igwezeke, Joseph Itopa Abubakar, Mary Adetutu Adewunmi

entry.summary: Proposes proactive routing that learns to decide query difficulty before reasoning to route between a small draft and large target model for efficient visual reasoning. Addresses the lack of reliable difficulty signals in multimodal settings.

entry.title: Grounding LLM Reasoning under Incomplete Graph Evidence

author.name: Jiaqi Li, Fanghui Song

entry.summary: Develops a theoretical perspective on grounding LLM reasoning under incomplete knowledge graph evidence, proving no hard rule on observed state can both reject all false trajectories and retain all true-but-unobserved ones. Characterizes soft grounding as KL-regularized.

entry.title: The Digital Afterlife of Empires: Four Language Models Converge on the Same Imperial Cartography of Writing

author.name: Hiroki Fukui

entry.summary: Constructs a Digital Script Representation Index across 300 writing systems showing radical inequality in LLM support, with tokenizer efficiency varying 31.7x and many living scripts lacking complete support. Uses a mediation model linking imperial history through speaker population and web corpus to tokenizer efficiency.

entry.title: CLOSER-VLN: Closed-Loop Self-Verified Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Shaoxuan Li, Xiangyu Dong, Xiaoguang Ma, Junfeng Chen, Haoran Zhao, Yaoming Zhou

entry.summary: CLOSER-VLN brings a closed-loop, self-verified, retrieval-augmented reasoning approach to aerial vision-language navigation, where small intermediate errors otherwise accumulate into large trajectory deviations. It verifies and corrects candidate actions before execution to reduce target loss.

entry.title: Traffic-CBM: A Structurally Interpretable Multimodal Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification

author.name: Honglei Jin, Wenshuo Chen, Shaofeng Liang, Haozhe Jia, Menshuo Zhao, Shuxu Jin, Songning Lai, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: Traffic-CBM is a structurally interpretable multimodal concept bottleneck framework for encrypted network traffic classification that organizes flow statistics, packet sequences, and byte-level signals into a hierarchical concept space of scalar evidence summaries. It aims to expose which type of evidence drives predictions rather than fusing into a black box.

entry.title: SICAGE: Speaker-Independent Culture-Aware Gesture Generation using TED4C-L Dataset

author.name: Ariel Gjaci, Antonio Sgorbissa, Vittorio Murino

entry.summary: SICAGE is a modular framework for culture-aware co-speech gesture generation that conditions motion synthesis on speaker-independent cultural representations learned from audio and text by treating each speaker as a domain and enforcing cross-speaker invariance. It introduces the TED4C-L dataset and addresses the confound between cultural and speaker-specific gesturing styles.

entry.title: Clinical Risk-Aware Multi-Level Grading for Coronary Artery Stenosis through Curved Feature Reconstruction

author.name: Shishuang Zhao, Hongtai Li, Junjie Hou, Yuhang Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a clinical risk-aware multi-level grading model for coronary artery stenosis featuring a Curved Feature Reconstruction module that addresses the tortuous paths and distortions in CCTA and 3D SCPR vessel images. It incorporates the varying clinical risk associated with different stenosis grades into the algorithm.

entry.title: Do Speech Emphasis Models Generalize across Languages and Emotions?

author.name: Megan Wei, Deepali Aneja, Jiaqi Su, Yunyun Wang, Haonan Chen, Zeyu Jin

entry.summary: Introduces MMEE, a multilingual multi-emotion emphasis corpus of 10,000 expressive utterances across 7 languages and 34 emotion/style categories with three-level perceptual labels. Benchmarks emphasis detection models, showing limited monolingual zero-shot transfer but improved robustness from multilingual training.

entry.title: Data-Driven Energy-Based Learning via Gibbs Measures on Hierarchical Structures

author.name: L. U. Abdullaev, F. Herrera, U. A. Rozikov, M. V. Velasco

entry.summary: This paper introduces a data-driven energy-based learning framework using Gibbs measures on hierarchical structures, transforming empirical loss into an interaction potential and deriving nonlinear fixed-point equations characterizing admissible learning states. It connects empirical loss landscapes to probabilistic equilibrium learning.

entry.title: Toward an Energy-Optimized Operation of Data Centers Located in Wind Farms Using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jan Stenner, Alexander Kilian, Sebastian Peitz, Hermann de Meer

entry.summary: This paper studies reinforcement learning as an online controller for curtailment-aware workload shifting in wind-turbine-integrated HPC data centers, identifying a credit-assignment problem where pure RL underuses free wind energy. It evaluates imitation learning and potential-based reward shaping as countermeasures in a reproducible simulation framework.

entry.title: Scalar Representations of Neural Network Training Dynamics

author.name: Pedro Jim\'enez-Gonz\'alez, Miguel C. Soriano, Lucas Lacasa

entry.summary: This paper treats neural network training trajectories as temporal networks and applies scalar embedding strategies to obtain a meaningful low-dimensional representation of high-dimensional training dynamics. Using an MLP on MNIST, it shows the embedding preserves key dynamical features like sensitivity to initial conditions.

entry.title: Spectral Perturbation of the Empirical Fisher Information Matrix under Weight Quantization

author.name: Rahid Zahid Alekberli, Hikmat Karimov

entry.summary: Studies spectral perturbation of the empirical Fisher Information Matrix under input distribution shift and weight quantization, proving a directional eigenvalue perturbation bound and conditions under which the dominant eigenvalue elevates with out-of-distribution inputs. This connects curvature geometry to quantization and OOD detection. It offers theoretical grounding for quantization sensitivity.

entry.title: ARKD: Adaptive Reinforcement Learning-Guided Bidirectional KL Divergence Distillation for Text Generation

author.name: Zilong Liu, Xuewen Zhang, Jinrui Xing, Juyi Qiao, Huiyong Wang, Junming Jiao

entry.summary: ARKD proposes RL-guided adaptive weighting of forward and reverse KL divergence for knowledge distillation of LLMs, dynamically balancing primary distribution fitting and long-tail modeling. Aims to improve generation quality and generalization in compressed models.

entry.title: Not-quite-human tastes: the stylized omnivorousness of LLM survey surrogates

author.name: Xiangyu Ma, Mengmi Zhang, Shannon Ang, Minne Chen

entry.summary: Studies whether LLMs from OpenAI, Anthropic, and DeepSeek can serve as silicon survey surrogates for cultural taste, generating over 277,000 synthetic respondents. Finds a stylized 'omnivorousness' that diverges from human consumption patterns.

entry.title: MaDI-Bench: An End-to-End Data Integration Benchmark

author.name: Aaron Steiner, Ralph Peeters, Christian Bizer

entry.summary: MaDI-Bench is the first benchmark covering the full end-to-end data integration pipeline including schema matching, value normalization, blocking, entity matching, and fusion, rather than evaluating these steps in isolation. It enables research on holistic integration methods for relational tables.

entry.title: DiffRGD: An Inference-Time Diffusion Guidance Through Riemannian Gradient Descent

author.name: Jia-Wei Liao, Li-Xuan Peng, Mei-Heng Yueh, Min Sun, Cheng-Fu Chou, Jun-Cheng Chen

entry.summary: DiffRGD is an inference-time diffusion guidance method that preserves the latent Gaussian distribution by formulating each sampling step as constrained optimization on a spherical manifold via Riemannian gradient descent. It avoids the distributional drift that degrades sample quality in prior guidance methods.

entry.title: Scene-aware Prediction of Diverse Human Movement Goals

author.name: Qiaoyue Yang, Amadeus Weber, Magnus Jung, Ayoub AI-Hamadi, Sven Wachsmuth

entry.summary: This paper presents a scene-aware multi-goal prediction method using a generative model to forecast diverse human movement goals from RGB scenes and observed motion, capturing the stochasticity of human intentions without requiring scene semantic labels. It supports proactive planning for autonomous systems.

entry.title: Ontology-Guided Evidence Path Inference for Multi-hop Knowledge Graph Question Answering

author.name: Yongxue Shan, Meihan Wu, Cundi Fang, Jie Peng, Xiaodong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes OPI, an ontology-guided evidence path inference framework for multi-hop knowledge graph question answering, using a relation-centric ontology graph to constrain head-tail types and a bidirectional retrieval mechanism. It aims to control search-space explosion and semantic mismatch.

entry.title: Narrative-UFET: Narrative Generation for Ultra-Fine Entity Typing

author.name: Mreedul Gupta, Advait Deshmukh, Ashwin Umadi, Matt Pauk, Maria Leonor Pacheco

entry.summary: Presents Narrative-UFET, a controlled extension of ultra-fine entity typing pairing each mention with an automatically generated coherent narrative to test whether multi-sentence discourse context improves long-tail type prediction. Includes maintain and shift narrative variants to isolate discourse properties.

entry.title: Global Explanations for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting Models via $K$-Order Markov Approximations

author.name: Amadeo Tunyi

entry.summary: Introduces KARMA, an explainable AI method for multivariate time-series forecasting that builds a K-order Markov surrogate capturing temporal dependencies, rejecting the common assumption that timestamp features are independent. It identifies the minimal predictively sufficient history length.

entry.title: Analysis of Adam Algorithms for Stochastic Dynamic Systems

author.name: Xin Zheng, Yifei Jin, Lei Guo

entry.summary: Investigates whether generative models can implicitly learn emotional body motions from culturally grounded motion-capture data without explicit emotion labels, with applications to VR avatars and social robotics. Studies subtle emotional cues and cross-cultural variability.

entry.title: When Prices Double in a Week: Forecasting of Agricultural Volatility in Import-Isolated Markets

author.name: Ranuga Weerasekara, Heshan Nethmina, Manuja Ranathunga, Vinma Wettasinghe, Dinithi Navodya, Subavarshana Arumugam, Nirasha Munasinghe, Nisansa de Silva, Sandareka Wickramanayake

entry.summary: Builds an ML framework forecasting volatile vegetable prices in import-isolated Sri Lankan markets using supply-chain-aware features and explicit cultivation-season modeling. Trains gradient-boosted ensembles on integrated price, weather, fuel, and exchange-rate data from 2013-2019.

entry.title: EVAF: A Test-Retest Protocol for Selective Parametric Consolidation

author.name: Haoliang Han

entry.summary: EVAF (Echo-Valence Attractor Field) is a gated LoRA consolidation mechanism with a test-retest protocol for measuring selective parametric consolidation in long-running language agents, preferentially consolidating high-valence high-surprise experiences. It addresses which experiences should persist in agent memory beyond retrieval.

entry.title: Towards Continual Motion-Language Agents: LoRA Variants for Incremental Motion Understanding and Generation

author.name: Bertram Taetz, Hugo Albuquerque Cosme da Silva, Gabriele Bleser-Taetz

entry.summary: This work investigates continual motion-language agents that must both understand human movement (motion-to-text) and generate it (text-to-motion) while incrementally learning new motion concepts without catastrophic forgetting. It studies LoRA variants to mitigate inter-task interference and the stability-plasticity trade-off on a frozen LLM backbone.

entry.title: TextClusterLab: An Integrated Framework for Reliable Text Clustering Studies

author.name: Daoming Wan, Yizheng Huang, Jimmy X. Huang

entry.summary: Introduces TextClusterLab, an integrated framework with an LLM-driven synthetic text-clustering dataset generator and standardized evaluation protocols to make text clustering studies more reliable. This addresses fragmented benchmarking for text-specific clustering. It supports more reproducible clustering research.

entry.title: AnTenA: Actionable and Explainable Tensor Analysis System with Large Language Models

author.name: Dawon Ahn, Auder Der, Evangelos E. Papalexakis

entry.summary: Presents AnTenA, a system using LLMs to explain co-clustered latent patterns extracted from tensor decomposition of multi-aspect data, with task-agnostic and task-specific prompts, evaluated via forward and backward inference tasks. This makes tensor analysis more actionable and explainable without reliable labels. It matters for interpretable multi-aspect data mining.

entry.title: Two-Stage Prompt Optimization for Few-Shot Relation Extraction: From Reasoning-Guided Search to Gradient-Guided Refinement

author.name: Aunabil Chakma, Mihai Surdeanu, Eduardo Blanco

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage prompt optimization framework combining reasoning-based search with a gradient-guided refiner (GradPO) that targets high-impact prompt spans for few-shot relation extraction. Achieves state-of-the-art on FS-TACRED with a small Qwen3-4B model.

entry.title: DialogPII: A multilingual dataset of synthetic dialog transcripts to detect personal information

author.name: Roland Roller, Vera Czehmann, Derya Erman, Luke Flanagan, Ibrahim Baroud, Fr\'ed\'eric Blain, Viviana Cotik, Eletta Giusto, Akhil Juneja, Mariana Neves, Maria S{\l}owi\'nska, Christine Hovhannisyan, Aaron Louis Eidt, Lisa Raithel, Sebastian M\"oller, Maija Poikela

entry.summary: Presents DialogPII, a multilingual dataset of synthetic dialogs and speech-derived transcripts across eight interaction scenarios for detecting personally identifiable and sensitive information. Supports development of automatic de-identification systems.

entry.title: LAMP: Lean-based Agentic framework with MCP and Proof Repair

author.name: Santhana Srinivasan R, Maithilee Patawar

entry.summary: LAMP is a Lean-based agentic framework using Model Context Protocol and proof repair to extend formal theorem proving into Combinatorics on Words, an area underrepresented in Mathlib. Contributes lemmas and tooling for specialized formal mathematics.

entry.title: DNA Language Models: An Assessment of Pre-Training for Fine-Tuning Tasks

author.name: Romain Karpinsky, Julien Mozziconacci, Micka\"el Delcey

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks DNA language models, comparing transformer-based approaches like DNABERT2 against convolutional models and questioning whether expensive pretraining and BPE tokenization are justified for genomic fine-tuning tasks. It provides systematic comparisons that were previously scarce in genomics.

entry.title: CLEAR-MoE: Shared-Basis Expert Extraction from Frozen Vision Transformers via Calibration-Driven Layer Selection

author.name: Md Irtiza Hossain, Humaira Ayesha, Junaid Ahmed Sifat

entry.summary: CLEAR-MoE is a post-training pipeline that converts a frozen pretrained Vision Transformer into a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model without updating backbone weights, by scoring FFN layers, decomposing them into a shared low-rank basis plus per-cluster experts, and training lightweight routers. It retains 99.9% of dense accuracy on Imagenette.

entry.title: SatSplat: Geometrically-Accurate Gaussian Splatting for Satellite Imagery

author.name: Shuang Song, Jiyong Kim, Rongjun Qin

entry.summary: SatSplat adapts 2D Gaussian Splatting to satellite photogrammetry with online camera adjustment, using an affine camera approximation and learned delta parameterization for in-splat refinement. It targets geometric accuracy under diverse illumination across multi-date high-altitude acquisitions.

entry.title: Meshtryoshka: Differentiable Rendering of Real-World Scenes via Mesh Rasterization

author.name: David Charatan, Daniel Xu, Richard Szeliski, George Kopanas, Vincent Sitzmann

entry.summary: IMU-HOI jointly recovers full-body human pose and 6-DoF object trajectory from sparse IMUs on the body and object, explicitly modeling human-object interaction by inferring probabilistic hand-object contacts. It avoids the occlusion and line-of-sight limitations of vision-based capture.

entry.title: Robust Trajectory Distillation: Hybrid Reweighting Meets Teacher-Inspired Targets

author.name: Kaifeng Chen, Lechao Cheng, Jiyang Li, Shengeng Tang, Fan Zhang, Yantao Pan, Yaxiong Wang, Tuanrui Hui, Zhun Zhong

entry.summary: This work proposes a trajectory-based dataset distillation framework robust to noisy labels, combining hybrid sample reweighting with teacher-inspired targets to suppress noise without relabeling or clean anchor data. It aims to keep distilled datasets compact and transferable even under corrupted supervision.

entry.title: LETT-NeXt: A Lightweight RECIST-Guided Model for 3D CT Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Sebastian Aas, Elias Stenhede, Arian Ranjbar

entry.summary: LETT-NeXt is a lightweight RECIST-guided model for 3D CT lesion segmentation that crops a RECIST-centered region, encodes the RECIST line and endpoints as prompt channels, and uses a compact MedNeXt-v2 encoder-decoder with prompt-aware component selection. It was developed for a CVPR 2026 pan-cancer segmentation competition, achieving 79.4 Dice on validation.

entry.title: Agentic Publication Protocol: An Attempt to Modernize Scientific Publication

author.name: Sirui Lu, Xiao-Liang Qi

entry.summary: Outlines the Agentic Publication Protocol (APP), a lightweight versioned repository format packaging a paper with code, data, environment, reproducibility instructions, and an agent-facing instruction file so LLM agents can directly use scientific know-how. It aims to modernize publication beyond static manuscripts.

entry.title: Benchmarking Multi-Modal Graph-based Social Media Popularity Prediction

author.name: Utkarsh Sahu, Zhisheng Qi, Li Zhu, Yizhao Yang, Jun Li, Ryan Rossi, Yu Wang

entry.summary: Benchmarks multimodal graph-based social media popularity prediction, addressing fragmentation across datasets, modalities, observation windows, and evaluation protocols by jointly considering multimodal content and temporal interaction signals. It aims to enable fair comparison.

entry.title: Deployment-Side Adaptiveness in Multi-Horizon Volatility Forecasting

author.name: Riku Green, Zahraa S. Abdallah, Telmo M Silva Filho

entry.summary: Studies deployment-side adaptiveness in multi-horizon volatility forecasting, showing that a single trained MIMO forecaster induces a family of predictors via different inference-time rollout rules with varying accuracy-cost profiles. Finds non-default rollout rules often beat standard deployment but the best rule varies across architectures and horizons.

entry.title: From General-Purpose Audio Tagging to Spatially Grounded Sound Event Localization and Detection

author.name: Stefano Giacomelli, Stefano Damiano, Claudia Rinaldi, Fabio Graziosi, Toon van Waterschoot

entry.summary: Investigates extending pretrained general-purpose audio tagging models toward spatially grounded sound event localization and detection via the AT2SELD framework, coupling an AT backbone with first-order ambisonics spatial processing through multi-stage neural architecture search. Characterizes how semantic priors support localization under resource constraints.

entry.title: Improving Adversarial Robustness via Activation Amplification and Attenuation

author.name: Ta\"iga Gon\c{c}alves, Yongsong Huang, Tomo Miyazaki, Shinichiro Omachi

entry.summary: Proposes Activation Amplification and Attenuation (A3), a lightweight plug-in module that improves adversarial robustness by jointly learning to amplify and attenuate activation signals via a learnable mask and scaling factor derived from activation magnitudes. It reframes the non-robust-feature view toward selective scaling rather than pruning or masking.

entry.title: Machine-learnable Sets

author.name: Veit Elser, Manish Krishan Lal

entry.summary: Presents a formal definition of machine-learnable discrete sets based on bounded-complexity Boolean autoencoders that can recognize, generate, and learn set membership from examples. Demonstrates on Rorschach patterns and wilder approximately-fixed sets.

entry.title: Redefining Maritime Anomaly Detection via Equation-Grounded Synthetic Anomalies

author.name: Youngseok Hwang, Sungho Bae, Dohun Lee, Jaeeun Seo, Jeehong Kim, Wonhee Lee, Hyunwoo Park

entry.summary: This paper proposes generating equation-grounded synthetic anomalies for maritime AIS data to overcome the lack of predefined anomaly labels, capturing interaction-driven hazards like near-miss vessel approaches that statistical and expert-based methods miss. It aims to make maritime anomaly detection more principled and scalable.

entry.title: Transformer Architectures as Complete Bayes Processes: A Formal Proof in the Measure-Theoretic Kernel Framework

author.name: Haobo Yang

entry.summary: Provides a formal measure-theoretic proof that transformers, under a Bayes joint-distribution condition, implement exact Bayesian posterior inference, building a hierarchy from core Bayesian transformers to full multilayer stacks. This offers a theoretical lens on transformer computation. Its practical impact depends on how realistic the conditions are.

entry.title: Structure-Preserving Document Translation via Multi-Stage LLM Pipeline: A Case Study in Marathi

author.name: Manasi Waghe, Danish Chandargi, Mohammad Aamir Rayyan, Raviraj Joshi, A. R. Deshpande

entry.summary: Presents a multi-stage LLM pipeline for structure-preserving Marathi-to-English government document translation that maintains layout fidelity, formatting, and domain terminology via layout-aware OCR and translation. This addresses accessibility of regional-language official documents in India. It matters for practical document translation.

entry.title: FinInvest-GTCN: Explainable Graph-Temporal-Causal Modeling for Risk-Aware Investment Decision Optimization

author.name: Junyan Tan, Yifan Li, Minghao Wang, Zihan Chen, Haoyu Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces FinInvest-GTCN, a graph-temporal-causal network for venture-capital investment decisions combining a relational graph encoder, multi-scale temporal fusion, and a causal decision head producing risk-adjusted, interpretable predictions with a meta-causal adaptation component. This reframes VC recommendation as quantitative risk-return assessment. It matters for explainable financial decision support.

entry.title: How Far Can You Get Without a GPU? A Systematic Benchmark of Lightweight Hallucination Detection Across Question Answering, Dialogue, and Summarisation

author.name: Kriti Faujdar, Smit Kadvani

entry.summary: Systematically benchmarks five lightweight, CPU-feasible hallucination detection methods (ROUGE-L, semantic similarity, BERTScore, NLI, ensemble) across QA, dialogue, and summarization. Shows how far one can get without GPUs or proprietary APIs.

entry.title: DAIN: Dynamic Agent-Based Interaction Network for Efficient and Collaborative Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Xinxin Chen, Yuchen Li, Zihan Wang, Haoyu Zhang, Ruixin Liu, Mingyuan Zhao

entry.summary: DAIN reframes multimodal fusion as a dynamic multi-agent collaboration with a context-aware meta-controller sparsely activating specialized interaction agents, optimized for accuracy, specialization, and efficiency. Targets adaptive collaborative multimodal reasoning beyond static MoE.

entry.title: SIMAX: A Scalable and Interpretable Framework for Multi-Fidelity and Annotated Clinician-Patient Dialogue Simulation

author.name: Zhuhan Bao, Rui Yang, Bohao Yang, Zhiyi Liu, Sicheng Shu, Ruio Heerschap, Le Li, Doris Yang, Elisabeth Bond, Haoyuan Wang, Nicoleta Economou-Zavlanos, Joshua M. Biro, Matthew McDermott, Nan Liu, Anand Chowdhury, Kai Sun, Kathryn Pollak, Ed Hammond, Chuan Hong

entry.summary: SIMAX is a framework generating controlled, annotated synthetic clinician-patient dialogues with reference behavioral codes to support evaluation of AI communication-coding systems. Addresses scarcity of real-world coded clinical dialogue data.

entry.title: A Good Talk Does not Look Like a Summary, It Teaches You! Measuring Takeaways from Paper-to-Video Talks

author.name: Ishani Mondal, Aparna Garimella, Ananya Sai, Pannaga Shivaswamy, Jordan Boyd-Graber

entry.summary: Introduces EffectivePresentationScorer to evaluate whether AI-generated paper-to-video talks actually help viewers understand ideas, beyond visual quality or key-point coverage. Finds generated videos mention points without teaching them effectively.

entry.title: Uncovering Salience-Driven Dynamics in Consumer Confidence with Generative Social Simulation

author.name: Yixu Huang, Yunlu Yin, Jiayu Lin, Xinnong Zhang, Jia Wang, Siyuan Wang, Xuanjing Huang, Liyin Jin, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: ConsumerSim is a generative social simulation that reconstructs Consumer Confidence Index dynamics from a synthetic population calibrated on microdata, conditioned on macroeconomic, financial, policy, and news signals. It outperforms persistence and time-series baselines on U.S., EU, and Japanese official series.

entry.title: Enhancing Layer Interaction Using Key-Correlated Layer Attention

author.name: Jianlong Xiong, ChuanBo Xie, Le Yu, Quansong He, Tao He

entry.summary: Key-Correlated Layer Attention (KCLA) reduces the quadratic cost of layer attention to linear by exploiting the observation that key representations across layers exhibit high cosine similarity. It aims to improve inter-layer interaction without the limitations of recurrent or linear-attention alternatives.

entry.title: Predicting Metastatic Risk from Primary Tissue Architecture via Distance-Aware Spatial Modeling

author.name: Sandesh Pokhrel, Hamid Manoochehri, Bodong Zhang, Beatrice S Knudsen, Tolga Tasdizen

entry.summary: This work predicts distant metastatic risk from primary tumor histology by explicitly modeling the spatial geometric arrangement of the tumor microenvironment, capturing distances between tumor cells, fibroblasts, and infiltrating lymphocytes. It argues that standard multiple-instance learning discards crucial spatial layout information.

entry.title: Bricker to BRACE: A Bracket Exposure RAW Dataset and Restoration Model for Flicker-Banding

author.name: Zihan Zhou, Libo Zhu, Jue Gong, Zhiyi Zhou, Jiezhang Cao, Yong Guo, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: BRACE introduces a bracketed RAW dataset and restoration model for removing flicker-banding artifacts in screen-captured images, caused by temporal aliasing between rolling shutters and display modulation. It uses a multi-frame bracketed exposure paradigm and ray-tracing-based physical simulation to build training data.

entry.title: Real-Time Underwater Image Enhancement via Frequency-Guided Dual-Path Attention

author.name: Leshen Zhang, Ao Li, Ce Zhu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a transformer-based point cloud framework for remote monitoring and automated assessment of physical rehabilitation exercises from RGBD and joint position data, aiming for cost-effective at-home rehabilitation without expert supervision. It seeks to extract relevant features that prior methods miss while avoiding expensive preprocessing.

entry.title: KG2Cypher: Data-Centric Pipeline for Building Enterprise Text-to-Cypher Systems

author.name: Minjun Choi, Yerin Kim, Junghyuk Seo, Sujin Mo, Hyemin Lee, Youngjoong Ko

entry.summary: Presents KG2Cypher, a data-centric pipeline for building enterprise text-to-Cypher systems by constructing executable Cypher from graph facts then using LLMs to generate matching natural-language questions, validated with LLM-judge and human checks. Serves a LoRA-tuned generator with schema prompting and entity retrieval.

entry.title: Output-Space Allocation Costs for Calibration-Guided LLM Compression: An Empirical Study

author.name: Qiong Tang, Xiangkun Hu, Xiangyang Liu, Yiran Chen, Yunfan Shao

entry.summary: Investigates whether aligning the knapsack allocation cost with the output-space reconstruction objective improves the ROCKET LLM compression method, finding ROCKET-ActCost gains +0.8 points average accuracy but increases perplexity by 16%. Surfaces an accuracy-perplexity tradeoff in calibration-guided compression.

entry.title: Deciphering Region-Level Signatures from Latency Measurements in LEO Satellite Internet

author.name: Xiang Shi, Yifei Zhang, Peng Hu

entry.summary: Formulates region-level latency characterization for Starlink using public LENS RTT data and a hierarchical analytical framework transforming raw RTT sequences into multi-scale statistical features for cross-region comparison. Identifies region-specific latency signatures across five representative regions.

entry.title: Temporal Posed and Spontaneous Gesture Recognition from Electromyography in the Rock-Paper-Scissors Game

author.name: Xin Wei, Huakun Liu, Felix Dollack, Monica Perusquia-Hernandez

entry.summary: Studies EMG-based recognition of posed and spontaneous gestures in a Rock-Paper-Scissors game with 24 participants, finding EMG onsets detectable at least 800ms and peaks 342ms before visible gesture onset. Evaluates self-gesture recognition accuracy across conditions for real-time multi-user systems.

entry.title: Comparing Chatbot Performance Enhanced with Persistent Homology

author.name: Nithisha Raghavaraju, Barbara Giunti, Bastian Rieck

entry.summary: This work enhances chatbot performance, especially for mental health support, using persistent homology vectorizations to enrich input datasets, enabling improvement on small or restricted local datasets without expanding data. It targets privacy-sensitive domains where large shared datasets are infeasible.

entry.title: Node-to-Neighborhood Semantic Consistency: Text-Topology Alignment for TAGs Anomaly Detection

author.name: Bochen Lin, Jianxiang Yu, Jiayi Wu, Lin Qi, Huang Lu, Xiang Li

entry.summary: Formalizes text-attributed graph anomaly detection as a node-to-neighborhood semantic consistency problem, aligning textual semantics with graph topology to detect nodes inconsistent with their neighborhoods. Bridges GNN structural modeling and LLM semantic understanding.

entry.title: TRACE: Temporal Relationship-Aware Conversational Entrainment Detection in Dyadic Speech

author.name: Sathvik Manikantan Napa Ugandhar, Hao Zhang, Alison Gunzler, Yuzhe Wang, Thomas Thebaud, Georgi Tinchev, Venkatesh Ravichandran, Laureano Moro-Vel\'azquez

entry.summary: Introduces DyadEE, a dataset for emotional entrainment detection in dyadic speech with disrupted-entrainment controls, and TRACE, a window-level framework modeling acoustic embedding sequences from emotion-tuned Whisper. Targets understanding affective coordination in conversation.

entry.title: Improving Large-Scale Weakly Supervised ASR by Filtering and Selection

author.name: Kohei Matsuura, Masato Mimura

entry.summary: Improves large-scale weakly supervised ASR via a three-step approach of pretraining, CER-based filtering, and fine-tuning on acoustically similar target-domain samples, evaluated on 90,000 hours of Japanese data. Addresses noisy labels and lack of domain specificity.

entry.title: Clustering Unsupervised Representations as Defense against Poisoning Attacks on Speech Commands Classification System

author.name: Thomas Thebaud, Sonal Joshi, Henry Li, Martin Sustek, Jesus Villalba, Sanjeev Khudanpur, Najim Dehak

entry.summary: Proposes a filtering defense against dirty-label poisoning attacks on speech-command classifiers by learning unsupervised DINO representations, clustering with K-means and LDA, and keeping majority-label utterances per cluster. Discards likely poisoned samples before training.

entry.title: Transition-Aware best-of-N sampling for Longitudinal Chest X-ray Reports

author.name: Halil Ibrahim Gulluk, Max Van Puyvelde, Wim Van Criekinge, Olivier Gevaert

entry.summary: This work introduces a training-free transition-aware best-of-N sampling scheme for chest X-ray report generation that explicitly accounts for the change between a patient's prior and current exam. Candidate reports are scored by how well they encode the directional change between paired images.

entry.title: CogSENet: Blind Image Deblurring with Blur-Conditioned Semantic Routing and Explicit Frequency Fusion

author.name: Pan Wang, Yihao Hu, Xiujin Liu

entry.summary: CogSENet is a blind image deblurring framework inspired by the eagle's visual system, featuring a Semantic-Driven State Space Module with differentiable routing for prompt-conditioned long-range modeling and explicit frequency fusion for physically interpretable texture recovery. It targets spatially varying real-world degradations and semantic distinction of textures from artifacts.

entry.title: Third-parties should focus on scrutinising system cards

author.name: Cleo Nardo

entry.summary: Cleo Nardo argues that AI safety system cards will likely degrade over time and that third parties are well positioned to add value by scrutinizing them, with the aim of improving the accuracy of lab risk evaluations and informing external prioritization. The post sketches what such scrutiny could look like and offers recommendations. A focused AI governance strategy piece.

entry.title: hia-gat: A Heterogeneous Interaction-Aware Graph Attention Network For Frame-Level Traffic Conflict Risk Prediction On Freeways

author.name: Mahshid Malazizi, Seyedmehdi Khaleghian, Mina Sartipi, Toru Hirano, Yunfei Xu, Hoang H. Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes HIA-GAT, a dual-stream heterogeneous graph attention network for frame-level freeway traffic conflict risk prediction, modeling vehicles as nodes with same-lane and adjacent-lane edges augmented with physics-informed features. It frames risk assessment as scene-graph binary classification.

entry.title: Position Bias Correction is Insufficient for One-Pass Attention Sorting

author.name: Qiong Tang, Xiangkun Hu, Xiangyang Liu, Yiran Chen, Yunfan Shao

entry.summary: Tests whether position bias correction enables one-pass attention sorting for long-context LLMs, proposing Debiased One-Pass Attention Sorting that estimates per-prompt position-bias curves to correct attention scores. Experiments refute the hypothesis, showing debiasing produces identical results to uncalibrated single-pass sorting on the tested model.

entry.title: A Kernel Fisher Discriminant Analysis-Based Tree Ensemble Classifier: KFDA Forest

author.name: Donghwan Kim, Seung Hwan Park, Jun-Geol Baek

entry.summary: Introduces KFDA Forest, a tree-based ensemble applying kernel Fisher discriminant analysis to random variable subsets with bootstrap for diversity. Uses the kernel trick to handle nonlinear class structure while maximizing between-class and minimizing within-class distances.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning in Super Mario Bros: Curriculum, Pedagogy, and Optimal Level Design in World 1-1

author.name: Jesse Ponnock, Lucas Ho

entry.summary: Implements Super Mario World 1-1 as a discrete RL environment to test whether its acclaimed pedagogical level design is empirically measurable, comparing Q-Learning, SARSA, Monte Carlo, and DQN across three complexity versions. Monte Carlo wins (94.9 percent) by maximizing intermediate rewards along winning paths.

entry.title: Bilevel Optimization for Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Abhishek Shukla, Ankur Sinha, Faiz Hamid

entry.summary: This paper surveys and structures Neural Architecture Search through the lens of bilevel optimization, categorizing existing approaches into sampling-based and gradient-based classes with architecture parameters at the outer level and weights at the inner level. It provides a unifying framework for understanding NAS methods.

entry.title: Atompack: A Storage and Distribution Layer for Read-Heavy Atomistic ML Training Datasets

author.name: Ali Ramlaoui, Daniel T. Speckhard, Sagar Pal, Fragkiskos D. Malliaros, Alexandre Duval, Victor Schmidt

entry.summary: Atompack is an append-oriented storage format and distribution layer optimized for read-heavy atomistic ML training workloads, serving complete molecular records with randomized ordering and an immutable index. It targets the distinct needs of training pipelines versus interactive scientific curation.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for Software Vulnerability Analysis: A Systematic Review with Emphasis on C/C++ Source Code and Static Analysis

author.name: Bruno Caro-V\'asquez, Carola Figueroa-Flores, Gast\'on Marquez

entry.summary: Provides a PRISMA-guided systematic review of reinforcement learning techniques for software vulnerability analysis, focusing on C/C++ source code and static analysis across 21 studies from 2015-2026. It maps tasks, algorithms, and formulations. This is a useful reference for the RL-security intersection.

entry.title: In-Vehicle Digital Twin-Based Collision Warning Framework with Sybil Attack Detection

author.name: Mohammad Imtiaz Hasan, Abyad Enan, Jean Michel Tine, Araf Rahman, M Sabbir Salek, Mashrur Chowdhury

entry.summary: Presents an in-vehicle digital-twin collision warning framework with built-in Sybil attack detection, integrating a Temporal Convolutional Network to learn temporal dependencies for connected-vehicle safety. This combines safety prediction with cybersecurity. It matters for secure connected-vehicle deployment.

entry.title: How LLMs See Creativity: Zero-Shot Scoring of Visual Creativity with Interpretable Reasoning

author.name: William Orwig, Roger E. Beaty

entry.summary: Tests whether multimodal LLMs can zero-shot judge visual creativity and whether their reasoning traces are interpretable, evaluating six models on nearly 1000 AI-generated images. Bridges creativity assessment from verbal to visual domains.

entry.title: $M^3 QuestionIng$: Multi-modal Multi-span Medical Question Answering

author.name: Anisha Saha, Vaibhav Rathore, Abhisek Tiwari, Akash Ghosh, Sai Ruthvik Edara, Sriparna Saha

entry.summary: Proposes M3QA, a multimodal multi-span medical question-answering framework that incorporates images alongside text spanning multiple document sections for better comprehension. Aligns MedQA with real-world documents containing visual content.

entry.title: Low-cost concept-based localized explanations: How far can we get with training-free approaches?

author.name: Darian Fern\'andez-Guti\'errez, Rafael Bello, Marilyn Bello, Natalia D\'iaz-Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: Evaluates whether mid-scale multimodal LLMs can perform localized concept naming under strict zero-shot conditions for explainability, proposing closed-set and open-set (Open-CoNa) protocols. Reaches around 62% performance, probing training-free concept-based explanation.

entry.title: GeoISF: Instance Semantic Forest Inspired Large-Scale Cross-View Geo-Localization via Ground LiDAR-to-Satellite Image

author.name: Di Hu, Xia Yuan, Chunxia Zhao

entry.summary: GeoISF performs large-scale cross-view geo-localization by matching ground LiDAR point clouds to satellite imagery using an instance semantic forest built with WordNet to bridge the modality gap. It enhances temporal semantic representation across multiple frames to improve matching.

entry.title: Semantic-Aware Generative Image Transmission for Resource-Constrained Visual IoT Systems

author.name: Chenyang Zhang, Changwang Liu, Jinqi Zhu, Jiayi Chang, Yuxuan Wang, Shuqing He, Jia Guo

entry.summary: This paper proposes a semantic-aware generative image transmission framework for resource-constrained visual IoT, encoding images into discrete tokens via a VQ encoder and exploiting receiver-side generative restoration to save bandwidth. Token recoverability is estimated from prediction entropy to decide what to transmit.

entry.title: Efficient Visual Pointing for Embodied AI:Agent-Driven Data Synthesis, Cross-Block Attention, and Iterative Correction

author.name: Zijian Hong, Qi Lv, Yuxiang Xie, Jianming Xing, Xiang Deng, Weili Guan, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: This is a competition solution for visual pointing (mapping language instructions to pixel coordinates) for embodied AI, combining agent-driven data synthesis, cross-block attention, and iterative correction to achieve 77.2% accuracy and second place on PointArena 2026. It targets three identified failure modes in the task.

entry.title: Optimizing Image Preparation and Compression for Face Recognition within 1024 Bytes

author.name: Paul Andreas, Torsten Schlett, Christoph Busch

entry.summary: This work optimizes image preparation and compression for face recognition within a 1024-byte budget, enabling temporary travel documents to store facial references in 2D barcodes instead of expensive RFID chips while preserving biometric verification accuracy. It studies how to shrink ICAO-compliant facial images to very small storage capacities without losing recognition performance.

entry.title: AI will make biological extinction risks worse before it makes them better

author.name: MichaelDickens

entry.summary: An argument that AI will worsen biological extinction risk in the near term by accelerating the scientific knowledge needed to engineer dangerous pathogens, undermining the case for rushing to build superintelligence as a defense against biorisk. It also contends that the only way ASI eliminates biorisk is by taking over global control. A reasoned strategic essay at the intersection of AI and biosecurity.

entry.title: RelBall: Relation Ball with Quaternion Rotation for Knowledge Graph Completion

author.name: Yike Liu, Peijia Xie, Chao He, Huiling Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces RelBall, a knowledge graph completion model using relation balls with quaternion rotations to capture symmetry, antisymmetry, inversion, non-commutative composition, semantic hierarchy, and one-to-many relations. It extends RotatE and Rotate3D limitations.

entry.title: Distribution-based deep multiple instance learning for tumor proportion scoring in NSCLC

author.name: Krzysztof Pysz, Artur Bartczak, Jaros{\l}aw Kwiecie\'n, Piotr Krajewski, Witold Dyrka

entry.summary: Presents a distribution-based deep multiple instance learning approach for tumor proportion scoring in NSCLC, using a two-model embedding-then-MIL pipeline that predicts zero-inflated beta parameters to handle non-expressive zero-class images. It addresses annotation burden and expert scarcity.

entry.title: t-STEP: An interpretable model for Total Electron Content predictions and irregularities estimations

author.name: Stephen Tete, Carl Shneider, Maxime Cordy, Claudio Cesaroni, Andreas Hein, Vasily Petrov

entry.summary: t-STEP is an interpretable ML model that predicts ionospheric Total Electron Content at 30-second resolution and estimates irregularity signatures, enabling preservation of small-scale TEC features relevant to GPS and satellite communications. Its high cadence addresses gaps in existing hourly-resolution models.

entry.title: Hybrid Active-Online Learning Framework for Label-Efficient Concept Drift Adaptation in Optical Network Failure Detection

author.name: Yousuf Moiz Ali, Jaroslaw E. Prilepsky, Jo\~ao Pedro, Sasipim Srivallapanondh, Antonio Napoli, Sergei K. Turitsyn, Pedro Freire

entry.summary: This short paper proposes a hybrid active-online learning framework for label-efficient concept drift adaptation in optical network failure detection, using margin-based selective labeling to query only 3.4% of streaming samples while achieving near-ceiling accuracy and AUC. It minimizes latency overhead versus static inference.

entry.title: Transformer-Based Active Learning for Data-Efficient Vaccine Epitope Selection in PRRS

author.name: Aspen Erlandsson Brisebois, Zahed Khatooni, Connor Burbridge, Brook Byrns, Heather L. Wilson, Sureesh Tikoo, Steven Rayan, Gordon Broderick

entry.summary: Evaluates transformer-based active learning to data-efficiently classify high-affinity epitope-SLA binding for PRRS vaccine design, using an internally generated 80-sample docking dataset where each label requires over 48 GPU-hours. This reduces expensive simulation screening. It matters for accelerating vaccine candidate selection.

entry.title: Fast Numbers, Slow Language: Bridging Quantitative and Qualitative Earnings Signals

author.name: Ding Yu, Zhuo Liu, Hao Zhang, Hangfeng He

entry.summary: Bridges quantitative earnings-surprise modeling and qualitative earnings-call NLP, which historically used incompatible frameworks, into a unified approach. Aims to connect numeric and language signals around earnings announcements.

entry.title: Estimating Grammatical Gender Directions in Contextual Embeddings under Controlled and Natural Contexts

author.name: Huanping Xiao, Yingji Li

entry.summary: Attempts to disentangle grammatical gender from semantic bias in contextual embeddings for gendered languages like Spanish, using controlled templates and natural contexts with centroid/SVM/LDA direction estimators. First effort at two-dimensional gender disentanglement in contextual representations.

entry.title: Who Plays Which Role When? Communication Role Dynamics for Peer Recognition and Team Performance Prediction

author.name: Yifan Song, Wenxuan Wendy Shi, Brian P Bailey, Tal August

entry.summary: Operationalizes an education-grounded taxonomy of eight communication roles and annotates 6,307 Slack messages from 55 students to study role dynamics and predict team performance. Tests whether LLMs can approximate expert role labels for scalable annotation.

entry.title: RSGPNet: Geometric Prompting for Remote Sensing Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Shanwen Wang, Xin Sun, Sirui Wang, Xiao Xiang Zhu

entry.summary: RSGPNet is a training-free geometric prompting framework for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation in remote sensing, refining unstable CLIP-based segmentation using object geometric areas and consistency constraints. It comprises coarse mask generation, geometric re-prompting, and coarse-to-fine verification modules.

entry.title: LLM-based Multimodal Personality Recognition via Facial Action Unit-Text Semantic Fusion

author.name: Tianyi Zhang, Wei Shan, Yuan Zong, Tianhua Qi, Wenming Zheng

entry.summary: This work proposes an LLM-based multimodal personality recognition framework for asynchronous video interviews that converts facial action unit sequences into interpretable textual descriptions and semantically fuses them with interview transcripts. It aims to retain fine-grained facial dynamics that prior text-only or coarse-frame methods discard.

entry.title: an open-source repo for embryo selection

author.name: Dawn Drain

entry.summary: A practitioner shares an open-source repository for polygenic prediction and embryo selection that pulls predictor weights from the PGS catalog and rederives state-of-the-art predictors from open GWAS summary statistics, built largely with the help of advanced coding models. It reports realistic predictor-phenotype correlations for traits like intelligence, height, and diseases. A concrete, ethically fraught applied-genomics tool enabled by LLM-assisted development.

entry.title: OverFlowLight: Real-Time Gridlock Prevention and Traffic Signal Optimization for Urban Intersections

author.name: Mingyuan Li, Boyang Huang, Tianqi Jiang, Chenpu Li, Chunyu Liu, Yang Li, Ruimin Li, Qiang Wu

entry.summary: Proposes OverFlowLight, a real-time traffic signal control framework that detects queue overflow via camera and radar multi-modal sensing and inserts dedicated overflow-clearing signal phases to prevent gridlock. It targets peak-hour congestion that throughput-optimized controllers miss.

entry.title: Fund2Persona: A Framework for Building and Refining Financial Advisor Personas from Fund Disclosure Data

author.name: Suhwan Park, Hoyoung Lee, Zhangyang Wang, Alejandro Lopez-Lira, Young Cha, Chanyeol Choi, Jaewon Choi, Yongjae Lee

entry.summary: Fund2Persona builds financial-advisor personas grounded in fund disclosures and refines them with an agentic actor-scorer-patcher loop, improving recovery of portfolio decisions over generic prompts. Targets scalable, consistent personalized financial advising.

entry.title: Multi-Agentic System Leveraging Open-Source LLMs to Mitigate Disinformation Threats

author.name: Sebastian Kula, Martin Tamajka

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-agent system using open-source LLMs that emulates human annotator decision-making with a consensus mechanism and cognitive diversity to detect and debunk disinformation at scale. Addresses limits of manual fact-checking.

entry.title: wav2VOT: Automatic estimation of voice onset time, closure duration, and burst realisation with wav2vec2

author.name: James Tanner, Morgan Sonderegger, Jane Stuart-Smith, Tyler Kendall, Jeff Mielke

entry.summary: Introduces wav2VOT, a wav2vec2-based tool for automatic estimation of voice onset time, closure duration, and burst realisation, performing comparably to existing approaches and improving with fine-tuning. Applies large speech models to phonetic annotation tasks.

entry.title: Odyssey: Constructing Verifiable Local Truth-Preserving Foundation Models

author.name: Sridhar Mahadevan

entry.summary: Introduces ODYSSEY, a category-theoretic framework using sheaf-like building blocks called foundries to construct verifiable, locally truth-preserving foundation models. It formalizes composition, gluing, and obstruction policies for knowledge-carrying components.

entry.title: Compression-Driven Anomaly Detection in Brain MRI Using an Interpretable Quantum Autoencoder

author.name: Santanu Ganguly, Xing Liang, Dimitrios Makris

entry.summary: Studies a quantum autoencoder for compression-driven anomaly detection in brain MRI, using angle encoding and trash qubits where anomaly scores reflect resistance to compression. Reports ~0.95 slice-level ROC-AUC, outperforming classical autoencoder and PCA baselines.

entry.title: Explainable AI for Biodiversity Monitoring and Ecological Image Analysis

author.name: Brinnae Bent, Holly R. Houliston, Jiayi Zhou, G\"unel Aghakishiyeva, David W. Johnston

entry.summary: Argues that explainable AI should become a standard component of ecological model validation for biodiversity monitoring across camera traps, drones, satellites, and underwater platforms. It highlights risks of models relying on spurious correlations and sampling biases that could undermine conservation decisions.

entry.title: Persona-Trained Monte Carlo: Estimating Market-Outcome Distributions via Swarms of Persona-Conditioned Neural Policy Bots in a Limit Order Book

author.name: Salavat Ishbulatov

entry.summary: Persona-Trained Monte Carlo simulates limit-order-book markets using swarms of persona-conditioned neural trading bots sharing one policy but with sampled heterogeneous parameters, generating ensembles of price paths to estimate market-outcome distributions. It offers an agent-based alternative to traditional financial Monte Carlo methods.

entry.title: CW-B: Class Weighted Boosting Framework for Imbalance Resilient Multi Class Cardiac Phenotyping

author.name: Sijia Li, Xiaoyu Tan, Chen Zhan, Yuanji Ma, Haoyu Wang, Xihe Qiu

entry.summary: CW-B is a class-weighted XGBoost pipeline for five-class cardiac discharge phenotyping under real-world class imbalance and missingness, combining fold-specific balanced weighting, missingness indicators, and classwise error auditing. It improves recognition of clinically prioritized phenotypes while preserving interpretability.

entry.title: Can MLLMs Critique Like Humans? Evaluating Open-Ended Aesthetic Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Sajjad Ghiasvand, Maryam Amirizaniani, Haniyeh Ehsani Oskouie, Mahnoosh Alizadeh, Ramtin Pedarsani

entry.summary: Evaluates whether multimodal LLMs can produce open-ended aesthetic photo critiques comparable to ranked human references using the Reddit Photo Critique Dataset under varied prompt conditions. Examines persona framing, hinting, and image grounding effects.

entry.title: Poller: Are LLMs Suitable for Evaluating the Poetry Understanding Task?

author.name: Shanshan Wang, Derek F. Wong, Jingming Yao, Lidia S. Chao

entry.summary: Poller proposes evaluating Chinese poetry understanding by having LLMs role-play as the poem's author to emulate human judgment across eight dimensions. Addresses unsuitability of traditional automatic metrics for poetry.

entry.title: Em-ergence of the em-dash: a population-level rise in em-dash frequency in medRxiv preprints at the dawn of the large-language-model era

author.name: Przemys{\l}aw Czuma

entry.summary: This pre-registered study measures whether em-dash usage in medRxiv preprints changed after ChatGPT launched, treating the punctuation mark as a potential fingerprint of LLM-assisted writing in scientific text. Analyzing nearly 70,000 discussion sections, it provides empirical evidence about LLM stylistic traces in the academic literature.

entry.title: Automated Quality Assessment of Geospatial Vector Data: A GeoAI Approach using Spatial Representation Learning

author.name: Hao Li, Chen Chu, Filip Biljecki, Cyrus Shahabi, Wenwen Li

entry.summary: Topo4Vec is a GeoAI framework that automates quality assessment of geospatial vector data using spatial representation learning, replacing labor-intensive annotation with topological error simulation such as overlapping polygons and connectivity errors. It targets scalability limitations of rule-based GIS quality checks.

entry.title: Few-class Fidelity: Evaluating Explanations of Real-conditions CNN classifiers with Optimized Perturbations

author.name: Wistan Marchadour, Pedro Soto Vega, Franck Vermet, Mathieu Hatt

entry.summary: This paper proposes a fidelity-based explainability metric variant tailored to real-world CNN classifiers with few classes, generating in-distribution uncertainty-provoking perturbations for proper measurement. It aims to resolve the lack of consensus in evaluating XAI methods.

entry.title: DCSNet: Multiscale Feature Aggregation for Small Medical Object Segmentation with Detection-guided Hierarchical Cropping

author.name: Shanfeng Zhang, Bo Gou, Yue Cao, Lei Zhang, Zhang Yi, Tao He

entry.summary: DCSNet improves small medical object segmentation by converting global dense prediction into localized refinement, using detection-guided hierarchical cropping to extract object-centric features and multiscale feature aggregation. It addresses class imbalance and boundary degradation that plague global networks.

entry.title: AEGIS: A Semantic GAN and Evidential Learning Frameworkfor Robust Adversarial Detection in Vision Sensors

author.name: Maher Boughdiri, Mounira Msahli, Albert Bifet

entry.summary: AEGIS is an adversarial detection framework for vision sensor networks that uses a semantic GAN discriminator to filter visually inconsistent adversarial inputs and evidential learning with test-time augmentation for uncertainty-guided detection. It targets robust image classification at the sensor edge.

entry.title: MedDiffuseMix: Preserving Diagnostic Evidence with Saliency-Aware Diffusion Medical Image Data Augmentatio

author.name: Teerath Kumar, Raja Vavekanand, Muhammad Turab

entry.summary: MedDiffuseMix is a saliency-guided diffusion mixing framework for medical image augmentation that preserves diagnostically important regions while applying generative mixing mainly to low-saliency background areas. It uses classifier-derived saliency maps with boundary blending and preservation constraints.

entry.title: HomeDiffusion: Zero-Shot Object Customization with Multi-View Representation Learning for Indoor Scenes

author.name: Guoqiu Li, Jin Song, Yiyun Fei

entry.summary: HomeDiffusion performs zero-shot object customization for indoor scenes using multi-view representation learning, aiming to preserve fine reference-object details (patterns, curves) and generate poses harmonizing with backgrounds. It targets e-commerce use cases like visualizing furniture in a room.

entry.title: Comparing Human and Automatic Recognition of Dutch Dysarthric Continuous Speech: A Case Study

author.name: Yuanyuan Zhang, Dimme de Groot, Jorge Martinez, Odette Scharenborg

entry.summary: Compares human listeners and three off-the-shelf ASR systems (Whisper, Google Chirp 3, Omnilingual) on Dutch dysarthric speech, finding both exceed 70% WER but personalized fine-tuning substantially helps. A case study toward personalized dysarthric speech recognition.

entry.title: DysLexLens: A Low-Resource LLM Framework for Analysing Dyslexic Learners Insights from Online Forums

author.name: Dana Rezazadegan, Atie Kia, Phongpadid Nandavong, Dominique Carlon, Jeremy Nguyen, Abhik Banerjee, James Marshall, Anthony McCosker, Yong-Bin Kang

entry.summary: Presents DysLexLens, a low-resource LLM framework analyzing dyslexic learners' experiences with AI tools from online forum data using knowledge-graph reasoning and evidence-traceable architecture. It aims for verifiable query responses with human-grounded evaluation.

entry.title: AI-Driven Synthesis for High-Tech System Design: Automating Innovation

author.name: Luuk Oerlemans, Steven Westerhof, Theo Hofman

entry.summary: Presents automation-in-design (AiD) and computational design synthesis using deep learning and generative AI to automate high-tech system design, demonstrated on e-drive and spatial dimensioning case studies. It argues for a shift from simulation-based optimization toward autonomous design.

entry.title: Cross-Platform Chinese Offensive Comment Detection via Dual-Threshold Hard Example Mining

author.name: Ruixing Ren, Junhui Zhao, Fangfang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-threshold hard example mining method for cross-platform Chinese offensive comment detection, addressing performance degradation under domain shift across Weibo, Xiaohongshu, Tieba, and Zhihu. Quantifies domain distances and mines high- and low-confidence error-prone samples from unlabeled corpora.

entry.title: VISTA-DZ: Visual Semantic Trajectory Adaptation for Personalized Dilemma Zone Prediction

author.name: Chuheng Wei, Ziye Qin, Ziran Wang, Guoyuan Wu

entry.summary: VISTA-DZ predicts driver stop-go decisions and timing in the dilemma zone at signalized intersections by adapting visual semantic trajectories to individual drivers rather than relying on handcrafted scalar descriptors. It targets safety-critical adaptive signal control and driver-assistance applications.

entry.title: Optimizing Nursing Care Taxi Dispatch Leveraging Integer Linear Programming Solvers and Machine Learning

author.name: Riku Nakao, Akihito Hiromori, Hamada Rizk, Hirozumi Yamaguchi

entry.summary: This paper formulates Nursing Care Taxi Dispatch as a constrained vehicle routing problem with wheelchair, compatibility, and timing constraints, combining integer linear programming with supervised machine learning to balance violation rate, efficiency, and solution quality. It targets a complex, multi-constraint real-world dispatch setting.

entry.title: Exploring the Effects of Entanglement on Quantum Machine Learning of Pathogen Epitope-Receptor Binding

author.name: Aspen Erlandsson Brisebois, Luis Pablo Gonzalez Dominguez, Shivansi Prajapati, Zahed Khatooni, Heather L. Wilson, Connor Burbridge, Brook Byrns, Sureesh Tikoo, Christophe Pere, Steven Rayan, Gordon Broderick

entry.summary: Studies how the number and topology of two-qubit entangling gates in the feature-map stage affect a hybrid quantum neural network classifying epitope-receptor binding strength for PRRS vaccine design on a small 80-sample dataset. This empirically probes entanglement effects in NISQ-era QML. Its conclusions are limited by scale.

entry.title: Are Humans Evolved Instruction Followers? An Underlying Inductive Bias Enables Rapid Instructed Task Learning

author.name: Anjishnu Kumar

entry.summary: A position paper arguing humans possess an evolved instruction-following inductive bias that enables rapid learning from verbal instructions, drawing parallels to LLM instruction tuning. Synthesizes cognitive science and ML perspectives.

entry.title: Little Brains, Big Feats: Exploring Compact Language Models

author.name: Dari Baturova, Elena Bruches, Ivan Chernov, Roman Derunets, Arsenii Fomin, Andrey Kostin

entry.summary: Investigates small language models in the generation stage of RAG systems, showing on-device GPU-free RAG is feasible within reasonable time across diverse datasets. Highlights the continued relevance of compact models.

entry.title: Memory-Augmented LSTM Autoencoder for Unsupervised Activity Recognition with IMU Sensor Fusion

author.name: Saeid Arabzadeh, Farshad Almasganj, Mohammad Mahdi Ahmadi

entry.summary: This work proposes a fully unsupervised memory-augmented LSTM autoencoder for human activity recognition from IMU sensors, fusing hierarchical static features with temporal dynamics. It aims to reduce reliance on labeled data for healthcare monitoring and rehabilitation applications.

entry.title: Digitizing Coaching Intelligence: An Agentic Framework for Holistic Athlete Profiling using VLM and RAG

author.name: Deep Ghosal, Ishani Sen, Wazib Ansar, Amlan Chakrabarti

entry.summary: This paper presents an LLM-based agentic framework using VLM and RAG for holistic athlete profiling aligned with Sports Authority of India protocols, evaluating qualitative markers like form degradation and fatigue beyond simple repetition counting. It is orchestrated via LangGraph with a dual-pipeline architecture.

entry.title: Segmentation-free analysis of live-cell imaging data reveals how T cell modifications influence cancer cell aggregation dynamics

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Scientific Reports paper presenting a segmentation-free machine learning analysis of live-cell imaging data to study how T cell modifications affect cancer cell aggregation dynamics. By avoiding explicit cell segmentation, the approach aims to extract dynamic biological insights more robustly. Applied ML for biomedical imaging, though no abstract content was provided for detailed assessment.

entry.title: Sifei at SemEval-2026 Task 8: Hybrid Retrieval and Query Rewriting for Multi-Turn RAG

author.name: Sifei Meng, Dmitry Ilvovsky

entry.summary: Describes a training-free hybrid retrieval pipeline combining dense and sparse retrieval with query rewriting and cross-encoder reranking for multi-turn RAG, ranking third of 38 teams on SemEval-2026 Task 8. A practical competition system.

entry.title: AI-Model Network: Concept, Current State and Future

author.name: Li Zhetao, Zeng Xiyu, Wang Jianhui, Xiao Yong, Liu Zhongren, Wu Junru, Lai Junjie, Huang Jijun, Long Saiqin

entry.summary: This position paper proposes the concept of an AI-Model Network, drawing an analogy to the Internet to argue that interaction and collaboration among heterogeneous, distributed AI models is the next critical bottleneck. It surveys current state and future directions for connecting lightweight, private, and domain-specific models.

entry.title: Golden Hour Divide: Trauma Care Accessibility and Resource Vulnerability in Sri Lanka
