entry.summary: Mean-Field PhiBE addresses model-free continuous-time mean-field control where population dynamics follow an unknown McKean-Vlasov SDE but only discrete-time data are available. It introduces a formulation that avoids the non-identifiability of HJB coefficients while preserving differential-equation structure lost by direct Bellman discretization.

entry.title: ProtoKV: Streaming Video Understanding under Delayed Query with Summary-State Memory

author.name: Le Tu Ngoc Minh (KAIST), Jinyeong Lim (KAIST), Dongsu Han (KAIST)

entry.summary: ProtoKV is a constant-footprint streaming video understanding memory that represents far history as a fixed-capacity summary state with a semantic-spatial prototype bank rather than retaining token instances. It addresses delayed queries where decisive cues appear briefly but risk eviction under bounded GPU memory before the query arrives.

entry.title: Forecasting With LLMs: Improved Generalization Through Feature Steering

author.name: Humzah Merchant, Bradford Levy

entry.summary: Uses sparse autoencoders to inspect LLM internal features during forecasting tasks, distinguishing time-aware reasoning from look-ahead-biased reasoning. Shows that amplifying time-awareness features reduces look-ahead bias while preserving general reasoning.

entry.title: OPID: On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shuo Yang, Jinyang Wu, Zhengxi Lu, Yuhao Shen, Fan Zhang, Lang Feng, Shuai Zhang, Haoran Luo, Zheng Lian, Zhengqi Wen, Jianhua Tao

entry.summary: Proposes OPID, an on-policy skill distillation framework for agentic RL that extracts dense token-level skill supervision directly from completed on-policy trajectories rather than external skill memories. Aims to bridge sparse outcome rewards with dense guidance for language agents.

entry.title: Axon: A Synthesizing Superoptimizer for Tensor Programs

author.name: Akash Kothari, Shaowei Zhu, Daniel Kroening, Chungha Sung

entry.summary: Introduces Axon, a synthesizing superoptimizer for tile-based AI accelerator tensor programs that uses program synthesis and SMT over unbounded tensors to generate and verify semantically equivalent kernel variants. Automates tiling, instruction selection, and operator fusion to relieve programmer burden.

entry.title: What Do Deepfake Benchmarks Measure? An Audit Using Frozen Self-Supervised Representations

author.name: Samuel Pagon, Yixuan Shen, Vishal Asnani, Feng Liu

entry.summary: Audits deepfake benchmarks by testing whether a linear probe on frozen self-supervised representations matches bespoke detectors, arguing such cases mean benchmarks reward generic features rather than real-world deepfake detection. Questions what current benchmarks actually measure.

entry.title: Neural Voxel Dynamics: Learning Implicit 3D Physics via Volumetric Feature Advection

author.name: Zican Wang, Niloy Mitra

entry.summary: Presents Neural Voxel Dynamics, a self-supervised framework that lifts V-JEPA semantic features into a depth-grounded voxel grid and learns an action-conditioned volumetric advection operator to model implicit 3D physics from video. Aims to give generative video models a 3D geometric foundation for object permanence.

entry.title: Do Image Editing Models Understand Lighting?

author.name: Tim K\"uchler, Johann-Friedrich Feiden, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner, Carsten Rother

entry.summary: This work introduces the 3DLP benchmark with a new HDR dataset of 1K real-world image pairs of indoor scenes with physically toggled light probes, to test whether generative image editing models truly understand lighting. It provides granular evaluation of light transport rather than relying on synthetic or perceptual judgments.

entry.title: See & Sniff: Learning Visuo-Olfactory Representations

author.name: Seongyu Kim, Seungwoo Lee, Hyeonggon Ryu, Joon Son Chung, Arda Senocak

entry.summary: See & Sniff introduces SmellNet-V, a visuo-olfactory dataset built by synthetically pairing smell-only samples with semantically aligned web images, exploiting odor invariance to visual transformations. The self-supervised framework learns joint representations via dense local alignment and produces smell saliency maps.

entry.title: PhysiFormer: Learning to Simulate Mechanics in World Space

author.name: Yiming Chen, Yushi Lan, Andrea Vedaldi

entry.summary: PhysiFormer is a diffusion transformer for physically-plausible 3D object motion that represents objects as world-coordinate 3D meshes rather than view-dependent pixels, predicting future vertex trajectories from initial positions, velocities, and material type. It achieves good results without explicit rigidity or causality inductive biases.

entry.title: Ask, Solve, Generate: Self-Evolving Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation via Self-Consistency Rewards

author.name: Ritesh Thawkar, Shravan Venkatraman, Omkar Thawakar, Abdelrahman Shaker, Fahad Khan, Hisham Cholakkal, Salman Khan, Rao Muhammad Anwer

entry.summary: This proposes a self-evolving training framework where a unified multimodal model improves both understanding and generation using only unlabeled images, via three internal roles (Proposer, Solver, Generator) and self-consistency rewards without human annotations or external reward models. It introduces Solver Token Entropy to stabilize learning.

entry.title: Revealing Mammographic Phenotypes in Deep Learning Breast Cancer Risk Models

author.name: Ruiyu Jia, Yanqi Xu, Yuxuan Chen, Yiqiu Shen, Laura Heacock

entry.summary: This work clusters patch embeddings from a pretrained breast cancer risk model (Mirai) to isolate recurring mammographic phenotypes linked to 5-year cancer risk, going beyond single-image saliency maps. It reveals both clinically meaningful structures and shortcut artifacts like surgical clips.

entry.title: World Action Models Enable Continual Imitation Learning with Recurrent Generative Replays

author.name: Manish Kumar Govind, Dominick Reilly, Smit Patel, Hieu Le, Srijan Das

entry.summary: REGEN is a continual imitation learning framework that uses World Action Models to synthesize pseudo-replay trajectories conditioned on prior task instructions and current observations, enabling robots to rehearse learned tasks without storing original demonstrations. It reduces catastrophic forgetting by up to 50% versus sequential fine-tuning.

entry.title: Scaling Nonlinear Optimization: Many Problems One GPU

author.name: John Viljoen, Johanna Haffner, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Negar Mehr

entry.summary: This work scales mature nonlinear program solvers like IPOPT to solve many robotics problems in parallel on a single GPU, bridging the gap between CPU-bound exact solvers and GPU-batched learning pipelines. It enables hard constraint satisfaction and optimality guarantees within GPU-accelerated workflows.

entry.title: Exploring the Intrinsic Geometry of Diffusion Models with Constrained Inverse Kinematics

author.name: Miguel Angel Rogel Garcia, Phone Thiha Kyaw, Jonathan Kelly

entry.summary: This studies whether diffusion models recover the intrinsic geometry of data manifolds in the analytically tractable setting of constrained inverse kinematics, where each task constraint defines a configuration manifold with known intrinsic dimension. It provides ground truth for evaluating the geometry learned by conditional diffusion models on UR5 and Franka robots.

entry.title: Tactile-WAM: Touch-Aware World Action Model with Tactile Asymmetric Attention

author.name: Siyu Wu, Linjing You, Junjie Zhu, Yaozu Liu, Changhao Zhang, Jian Liu, Weiqiang Wang, Qi Li, Jituo Li, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: Tactile-WAM augments world action models with tactile prediction for contact-rich manipulation, identifying a failure mode called tactile pollution where naive tactile-token injection degrades video and action prediction. It introduces an asymmetric attention mechanism to integrate sparse contact signals without corrupting visual dynamics. The identified failure mode and targeted fix are a genuine conceptual contribution.

entry.title: ForesightSafety-VLA: A Unified Diagnostic Safety Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Mingyang Lyu, Yinqian Sun, Yiyang Jia, Sicheng Shen, Moquan Sha, Huangrui Li, Feifei Zhao, Yi Zeng

entry.summary: ForesightSafety-VLA introduces a diagnostic safety benchmark for vision-language-action models with a 13-category taxonomy spanning physical, instruction-side, and perception-side safety, evaluated under controlled scene, language, and visual variations. It makes safety the primary evaluation target for embodied policies. As VLA deployment grows, dedicated safety benchmarks are increasingly important.

entry.title: Continual Robot Policy Learning via Variational Neural Dynamics

author.name: Jiaxu Xing, Zhiyuan Zhu, Yunfan Ren, Ismail Geles, Yifan Zhai, Rudolf Reiter, Davide Scaramuzza

entry.summary: Also from Scaramuzza's group, this continual learning framework improves robot policies online using real-world experience under hidden, recurring dynamics by combining an analytical physics prior with a neural residual and a recurrent encoder that infers current conditions. It addresses the gap where controllers are trained once and never adapt to wind, payload, wear, or battery drain. Condition-aware continual adaptation is a practically important and underexplored direction.

entry.title: Introspection or entropy? Re-examining concept-injection “introspection” in open models

author.name: agastyasridharan

entry.summary: This post critically re-examines Anthropic's claim that language models can introspect, showing in open-source replications that concept injection raises the YES logit on unrelated questions (like whether the Earth is flat), implying the introspection-prompt yes is not by itself evidence of detecting an injected thought. The author argues the effect may reflect distributional perturbation (entropy) rather than genuine introspection. This is a valuable critical replication challenging a high-profile interpretability claim.

entry.title: Beyond the Hard Budget: Sparsity Regularizers for More Interpretable Top-k Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Nathana\"el Jacquier, Maria Vakalopoulou, Mahdi S. Hosseini

entry.summary: This work introduces sparsity regularizers for Top-k sparse autoencoders to overcome the fixed budget k and overfitting limitations, improving interpretability of vision foundation model representations. It combines explicit regularization with architectural Top-k sparsity in a way prior work avoided.

entry.title: Empirical Software Engineering TerraProbe: A Layered-Oracle Framework for Detecting Deceptive Fixes in LLM-Assisted Terraform

author.name: Manar Alsaid, Chimdumebi Nebolisa, Faris Abbas

entry.summary: TerraProbe is a five-layer oracle framework for evaluating LLM-assisted security repair of Terraform infrastructure-as-code, checking planning validity, behavioral change, and security intent rather than just whether a static-analysis finding disappears. Applied to 288 repairs from Gemini, GPT-4o, and Claude, it shows that targeted finding removal substantially overstates true repair success.

entry.title: Latent Diffusion Posterior Sampling with Surrogate Likelihood Guidance for PDE Inverse Problems

author.name: Yuanzhe Wang, Alexandre M. Tartakovsky

entry.summary: L-DPS is an approximate Bayesian framework for high-dimensional PDE-governed inverse problems combining a variational autoencoder, an unconditional latent diffusion prior, diffusion posterior sampling, and a differentiable neural surrogate. It tackles implicit sample-based priors, high-dimensional spatial parameters, and costly repeated forward evaluations.

entry.title: The Riddle Riddle: Testing Flexible Reasoning in Large Language Models and Humans

author.name: Bella Fascendini, Kathryn McGregor, Max D. Gupta, Thomas L. Griffiths

entry.summary: Introduces the riddle riddle paradigm, presenting LLMs and humans with riddle-like questions whose answers require only literal interpretation, to test whether models flexibly reason or pattern-match on surface form. Probes the source of LLM cognitive-task performance.

entry.title: TaskNPoint: How to Teach Your Humanoid to Hit a Backhand in Minutes

author.name: Blake Werner, Ilona Demler, Pietro Perona, Aaron D. Ames

entry.summary: TaskNPoint is a training protocol for teaching humanoid robots dynamic skills like a tennis backhand quickly, exploiting the insight that dynamic skill outcomes are decided by a short crucial interaction window requiring whole-motion coordination. It frames learning as mastering a handful of actions and practicing the key window.

entry.title: Improving Vision-Language-Action Model Fine-Tuning with Structured Stage and Keyframe Supervision

author.name: Yuan Xu, Yixiang Chen, Kai Wang, Jiabing Yang, Peiyan Li, Qisen Ma, Yan Huang, Liang Wang

entry.summary: StaKe is a plug-in auxiliary supervision framework for fine-tuning Vision-Language-Action models that derives a stage classifier and keyframe predictor from demonstration gripper states without manual annotation. It addresses failures concentrated around challenging gripper-event transitions.

entry.title: WatchAct: A Benchmark for Behavior-Grounded Robot Manipulation

author.name: Baiqi Li, Ce Zhang, Yu Fang, Yue Yang, Shangzhe Li, Mingyu Ding, Gedas Bertasius

entry.summary: Introduces WatchAct, a benchmark of 3,000 long-horizon instances pairing real human-action videos with language instructions, simulator scenes, and executable LIBERO tasks to evaluate robot reasoning over observed human behavior. Addresses the gap where current benchmarks pair instructions with single static images.

entry.title: Localizing RL-Induced Tool Use to a Single Crosscoder Feature

author.name: Andrii Shportko, Shubham Bhokare, Ahmed Zeyad A Alzahrani, Bowen Cheng, Gustavo Mercier, Jessica Hullman

entry.summary: Shows that Dedicated Feature Crosscoders isolate a compact set of RL-specific features mediating tool-calling capability in Qwen2.5-3B, with encode-decode reconstruction improving tool correctness and enabling retraining-free behavioral control. Provides mechanistic insight into how RL reshapes representations for agentic behavior.

entry.title: Discovering Millions of Interpretable Features with Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: XinYang He, Wei Wang, Bing Zhao, Xuan Ren, WenBo Li, WeiXu Qiao, Hu Wei, Lin Qu

entry.summary: Introduces Qwen3-Instruct SAE, a comprehensive suite of sparse autoencoders trained on Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B at residual, MLP, and attention sites, discovering millions of interpretable features. Releases open SAE models to address the scarcity of available trained SAEs.

entry.title: TGHE: Template-based Graph Homomorphic Encryption for Privacy-Preserving GNN Inference in Edge-Cloud Systems

author.name: Ngoc Bao Anh Le, Thai T. Vu, John Le, Heath Cooper, Jun Shen

entry.summary: TGHE proposes an ego-centric homomorphic encryption framework for privacy-preserving GNN inference, exploiting recurring structural templates in transaction graphs to pack identical computation trees into shared CKKS ciphertexts. This decouples per-query cost from global graph size, enabling encrypted inference on large dynamic financial graphs that previously capped at ~20k nodes.

entry.title: SamaVaani: Auditing and Debiasing Multilingual Clinical ASR for Indian Languages

author.name: Subham Kumar, Prakrithi Shivaprakash, Abhishek Manoharan, Astut Kurariya, Diptadhi Mukherjee, Prabhat Chand, Pratima Murthy, Koustav Rudra, Lekhansh Shukla, Animesh Mukherjee

entry.summary: SamaVaani audits multilingual clinical ASR across Kannada, Hindi, and Indian English on real psychiatric interview data, comparing eight models and fine-tuning two open-source ones to reduce bias. It reveals substantial performance disparities across languages and demographics.

entry.title: In-Context Model Predictive Generation: Open-Vocabulary Motion Synthesis from Language Models to Physics

author.name: Xiaomeng Fu, Junfan Lin, Yang Liu, Yaowei Wang, Guanbin Li, Liang Lin, Ziliang Chen

entry.summary: ICMPG combines LLM-based high-level motion planning with inference-time physical feedback to synthesize human motion that is both semantically faithful and physically realistic. It bridges open-vocabulary instruction interpretation with physics-aware control.

entry.title: Learning to Fold: prizewinning solution at LeHome Challenge 2026 (1st place online, 2nd offline)

author.name: Ilia Larchenko

entry.summary: This report describes a prizewinning solution to the LeHome Challenge 2026 bimanual garment-folding competition, improving a vision-language-action policy with an RL loop where the policy serves as its own value function predicting success and progress. It recombines existing RL ideas with engineering contributions like AWR plus RECAP for flow-matching VLA.

entry.title: E-TTS: A New Embodied Test-Time Scaling Framework for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Wen Ye, Peiyan Li, Tingyu Yuan, Yuan Xu, Xiangnan Wu, Chaoyang Zhao, Jing Liu, Nianfeng Liu, Yan Huang, Liang Wang

entry.summary: E-TTS is a modular embodied test-time scaling framework for robotic manipulation that unifies reasoning and action scaling via history-aware iterative refinement with vision-language verifiers. It addresses the lack of studied scaling mechanisms and underuse of historical context in long-horizon embodied tasks.

entry.title: High-Probability PL-SGD with Markovian Noise: Optimal Mixing and Tail Dependence

author.name: Dhruv Sarkar, Aprameyo Chakrabartty, Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: This paper establishes high-probability convergence bounds for SGD on PL-condition objectives with Markovian noise, closing the gap between prior bounds and expectation results via a lag-blocking argument and proving the optimal linear dependence on mixing time with a matching lower bound. It extends results to the light-tailed setting.

entry.title: Does Aurora Encode Atmospheric Structure? Latent Regime Analysis and Attribution

author.name: Emma Kasteleyn, Ana Lucic

entry.summary: This work probes the internal representations of the Aurora weather foundation model using spatially pooled PCA and layer-wise relevance propagation, finding the latent space is primarily organized by seasonal cycles while extreme storms are not linearly separable. Perturbation tests show masking relevant regions degrades forecasts much more than random masking.

entry.title: Rethinking Training & Inference for Forecasting: Linking Winner-Take-All back to GMMs

author.name: Qiyuan Wu, Katie Z Luo, Bharath Hariharan, Wei-Lun Chao, Mark Campbell

entry.summary: This work traces uninformative trajectory-forecasting posteriors in autonomous driving to a mismatch between conditional GMM modeling and winner-take-all training loss, which over-segments trajectory space. It proposes post-hoc treatments linking WTA back to GMMs to recover informative mode probabilities.

entry.title: When Does Quality-Aware Multimodal Fusion Matter? A Leakage-Safe Diagnostic for Decision-Level Dependence

author.name: Jaden Moon, Arvind Pillai, Andrew Campbell

entry.summary: This paper introduces a leakage-safe diagnostic that permutes modality reliability scores at test time to check whether quality-aware multimodal fusion actually uses reliability information or merely correlates with it. Experiments on stress and sentiment datasets show predictions are often unchanged, revealing that reliability weighting frequently has no causal effect.

entry.title: Explaining Temporal Graph Neural Networks via Feature-induced Information Flow

author.name: Ping Xiong, Thomas Schnake, Klaus-Robert M\"uller, Shinichi Nakajima

entry.summary: This work proposes a novel attribution method for event-based temporal graph neural networks that captures information flow through event-induced variables, not just direct event-embedding-to-output contributions. It addresses how mediating variables enable long-range temporal dependencies, improving explainability.

entry.title: Tailor Made Embeddings for Quantum Machine Learning

author.name: Aldo Lamarre, Dominik \v{S}afr\'anek

entry.summary: Note: the listed item is 'Asymptotically Optimal Learning for Parametric Prophet Inequalities' which characterizes the optimal full-information competitive ratio for exponential-type reward families and proposes a confidence-based dynamic-programming policy achieving it from online observations alone. It provides closed-form competitive ratios for unbounded and bounded support cases.

entry.title: LearniBridge: Learnable Calibration of Feature Caching for Diffusion Models Acceleration

author.name: Xuyue Huang, Zhe Chen, Wang Shen, Xiao-Ping Zhang

entry.summary: LearniBridge is a learnable calibration mechanism for feature caching in diffusion transformers that addresses severe error accumulation at high acceleration ratios. Observing that the optimal calibration update lies in a shared low-rank subspace across prompts, it uses lightweight LoRA-style modules to bridge multiple timesteps.

entry.title: Scalable Message-Passing Quantum Graph Neural Networks in the Weisfeiler-Leman Hierarchy

author.name: Snehal Raj, Brian Coyle, L\'eo Monbroussou, Andr\'e J. Ferreira-Martins, Renato M. S. Farias, Elham Kashefi

entry.summary: This work presents a scalable message-passing quantum graph neural network with expressivity guarantees in the Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy and demonstrable scalability, addressing trainability bottlenecks via pre-training. It connects quantum GNNs to the message-passing primitive while providing performance and scalability assurances.

entry.title: Jailbreaking for the Average Jane: Choosing Optimal Jailbreaks via Bandit Algorithms for Automatically Enhanced Queries

author.name: Prarabdh Shukla, Ritik, Suhas Rao, Arpit Agarwal, Arjun Bhagoji

entry.summary: Proposes using multi-armed bandit algorithms to efficiently select optimal jailbreaks for a target LLM from a large set with few queries, examining whether non-expert attackers can reliably elicit harmful responses. Combines this with curated effective malicious queries to assess real-world threat models.

entry.title: Hierarchical Muon: Tiled Newton-Schulz Updates for Efficient Muon Optimization

author.name: Ziyuan Tang, Tianshi Xu, Yousef Saad, Yuanzhe Xi

entry.summary: Proposes Hierarchical Muon, which partitions momentum-gradient matrices into tiles and applies Newton-Schulz independently per tile to reduce the cubic-scaling cost of Muon optimization. Trades exact orthogonalization for a local matrix-function approximation.

entry.title: Soft Token Alignment for Cross-Lingual Reasoning

author.name: Jiayi He, Jungsoo Park, Wei Xu, Alan Ritter

entry.summary: Introduces SOLAR, an auxiliary supervised fine-tuning objective that aligns soft-token representations across languages using English as a pivot, aiming to reduce cross-lingual reasoning inconsistency. Addresses divergence caused by language-specific discrete token commitments.

entry.title: Multilingual Reasoning Cascades Need More Context

author.name: Arnav Mazumder, Dengjia Zhang, Shuyue Stella Li, Yulia Tsvetkov, Niyati Bafna

entry.summary: Shows that translation cascades for multilingual reasoning lose cultural and disambiguation cues, and proposes a training-free context-aware cascade that passes the original question, translation, and reasoning trace to the final translation step. Evaluates gains across nine benchmarks and three models.

entry.title: DocArena: Turning Raw Documents into Controllable Training Environments for Document Search Agents

author.name: Jiamian Wang, Ruiyi Zhang, Tong Yu, Jing Shi, Samyadeep Basu, Rajiv Jain, Zhiqiang Tao, Tong Sun

entry.summary: Proposes DocArena, an automated pipeline that turns raw documents into controllable, scalable, multimodal training environments for RL-trained document search agents. Generates (question, answer, evidence) tuples to shape agent search strategies and generalization.

entry.title: GeMoE: Gating Entropy is All You Need for Uncertainty-aware Adaptive Routing in MoE-based Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Chaoxiang Cai, Minghe Weng, Jie Li, Yibo Jiang, Longrong Yang, Zequn Qin, Xi Li

entry.summary: Proposes GeMoE, framing MoE token routing in vision-language models as a Minimum Description Length problem and using gating entropy for uncertainty-aware adaptive expert selection. Replaces static Top-k routing with input-dependent dynamic expert counts.

entry.title: Position Rebinding Cache Reuse: Replay-Free Visual Revisiting for Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Mengzhao Wang, Yanli Ji, Wangmeng Zuo, Peng Ye, Chongjun Tu

entry.summary: Identifies that reusing historical visual KV cache in interleaved multimodal reasoning fails because cached keys are bound to stale positional context, causing decoding collapse, and proposes Position Rebinding Cache Reuse to reconstruct visual evidence under current positions. Enables replay-free visual revisiting.

entry.title: Event-based Gaze Control System for Accurate Real-time Spin Estimation in Professional Ball Games

author.name: Yunpu Hu, Fabian Schilling, Valentina Cavinato, Asude Aydin, Agis Politis, Ricardo Tapiador Morales, Kirk Y. W. Scheper, Peter D\"urr, Naoya Takahashi

entry.summary: This presents an event-based active vision system that tracks unmodified balls and measures their spin in real-time during ball games, combining an event camera, galvanometer mirror gaze control, and a focus-tunable telephoto lens. It addresses the challenge of small, fast-rotating balls for sports analytics.

entry.title: SpatialFlow-GRPO: Where Spatial Credit Drives Image Editing

author.name: Yankai Yang, Yancheng Long, Wei Chen, Xingyu Lu, Hongyang Wei, Bin Wen, Fan Yang, Tingting Gao, Han Li, Shuo Yang

entry.summary: SpatialFlow-GRPO introduces spatially fine-grained reward feedback for image editing reinforcement learning, converting region-aware rewards into semantic-region-level optimization signals aligned with latent positions. It addresses the limitation of whole-image rewards that cannot distinguish regional quality contributions.

entry.title: LISA: Likelihood Score Alignment for Visual-condition Controllable Generation

author.name: Yanghao Wang, Hongxu Chen, Jiazhen Liu, Zhenqi He, Rui Liu, Zhen Wang, Long Chen

entry.summary: LISA revisits the dual-branch paradigm for visual-condition controllable generation through score-based modeling, showing the main network provides an unconditional prior score and the side network contributes a likelihood score. It proposes a likelihood score alignment regularization for more efficient training.

entry.title: RoPEMover: Depth-Aware Object Relocation via Positional Embeddings

author.name: Ipek Oztas, Duygu Ceylan, Aybars Bugra Aksoy, Aysegul Dundar

entry.summary: RoPEMover performs depth-aware object relocation in single images by manipulating rotary positional embeddings in diffusion transformers, extending 2D RoPE to a depth-aware 3D formulation. It maintains scene-level consistency including occlusions, shadows, and reflections during object motion.

entry.title: Rendering Novel Views of MRI Using 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Robin Y. Park, Mark C. Eid, Rhydian Windsor, Amir Jamaludin, Ana I. L. Namburete, Jo\~ao F. Henriques, Andrew Zisserman

entry.summary: This adapts 3D Gaussian Splatting to reconstruct volumes from sparse anisotropic spinal MRIs, resampling new view planes better aligned with target anatomy for improved radiological grading of stenosis. It outperforms voxel interpolation for downstream ordinal severity prediction.

entry.title: PressMimic: Pressure-Guided Motion Capture and Control for Humanoid Robot Imitation

author.name: Yi Lu, Shenghao Ren, Tianyu Xiong, Zhaoxiang Li, Jiaqi Li, He Zhang, Tao Yu, Qiu Shen, Xun Cao

entry.summary: PressMimic integrates pressure as a unified modality across perception and control for humanoid motion imitation, using a multimodal model (FRAPPE++) for pressure-guided motion capture to address contact dynamics. It reduces artifacts like foot sliding and floor penetration ignored by vision-only pipelines.

entry.title: Inference-Time Robot Behavior Steering through Physically-Aware Reconfiguration of Task-Structure

author.name: Yiyuan Pan, Hanjiang Hu, Shangtao Li, Xusheng Luo, Changliu Liu

entry.summary: ReStruct enables inference-time robot behavior steering by reconfiguring task structure in a physically-aware manner, building on a neural automaton policy that decomposes a visuomotor policy into a high-level state-machine skeleton and a low-level residual controller. It avoids retraining while ensuring physically feasible plan edits unlike pure neuro-symbolic methods.

entry.title: HumanoidUMI: Bridging Robot-Free Demonstrations and Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation

author.name: Hongwu Wang, Chenhao Yu, Youhao Hu, Jiachen Zhang, Yuanyuan Li, Shaqi Luo

entry.summary: HumanoidUMI is a portable, robot-free framework for collecting humanoid whole-body manipulation data using lightweight VR devices and UMI-inspired grippers to capture sparse keypoint trajectories, wrist-view observations, and gripper actions. A high-level policy predicts future keypoints that are then retargeted to the robot. It extends the influential UMI paradigm to whole-body humanoid behaviors.

entry.title: VibeAct: Vibration to Actions for Contact-Rich Reactive Robot Dexterity

author.name: Yuemin Mao, Uksang Yoo, Jean Oh, Jonathan Francis, Jeffrey Ichnowski

entry.summary: VibeAct bridges real vibrotactile sensing and simulation-based RL for dexterous contact-rich manipulation by embedding piezoelectric microphones in a robot hand, collecting vibro-acoustic data via teleoperation, and replaying it in a calibrated digital twin to label per-finger contact and slip. This creates a shared physical representation enabling sim-to-real policy learning. Using audio-band contact sensing for occluded, fast contact events is a novel sensing modality for dexterity.

entry.title: Eval-Awareness Steering detects the Test, Not the Sabotage

author.name: sahilraut

entry.summary: This independent alignment study tests whether an internal eval-awareness direction in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct causally drives sandbagging or merely correlates with it, reusing Apollo's deception-detection harness on a confound-controlled dataset. It finds the direction is a valid detector of evaluation framing (about 0.81 AUROC) but is neither a causal driver nor a per-item predictor of sandbagging. The careful causal-vs-correlational distinction is a valuable contribution to deception/sandbagging research.

entry.title: ConflictScore: Identifying and Measuring How Language Models Handle Conflicting Evidence

author.name: Siyi Liu, Aaron Halfaker, Dan Roth, Patrick Xia

entry.summary: Introduces ConflictScore and ConflictBench to measure how well LLM responses acknowledge conflicting evidence in grounding documents, decomposing answers into atomic claims labeled against sources. Provides count- and ratio-based metrics beyond standard factuality measures.

entry.title: scBench-Long: Verifiable Benchmarking of Long-Horizon Single-Cell Biology

author.name: Ian Diks, Zhen Yang, Arjun Banerjee, Tim Proctor, Kenny Workman

entry.summary: Introduces scBench-Long, a benchmark of 21 long-horizon single-cell biology evaluations requiring agents to recover scientific conclusions from raw or near-raw data without prescribed methods, spanning melanoma T-cell reactivity, regulatory inference, and COVID-19 lung pathology. Goes beyond broad-knowledge or local-step benchmarks.

entry.title: ReasonCLIP-58M: Visually Grounded Commonsense Reasoning Supervision for CLIP

author.name: Sicheng Zhang, Muzammal Naseer, Binzhu Xie, Naufal Suryanto, Shi Qiu, Jamal Bentahar, Naveed Akhtar, Mubarak Shah

entry.summary: ReasonCLIP-58M is a continual pretraining framework that injects large-scale visually grounded commonsense reasoning supervision into CLIP-style encoders while preserving descriptive alignment. It tests whether CLIP encoders can support compositional reasoning without architectural changes.

entry.title: Heavy-Ball Q-Learning with Residual Weighting Correction

author.name: Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: This paper proposes a corrected heavy-ball Q-learning method with convergence guarantees and identifies conditions where it provably converges faster than standard Q-learning, extending to linear function approximation. The analysis uses a switched linear system representation and joint spectral radius.

entry.title: Automating Potential-based Reward Shaping with Vision Language Model Guidance

author.name: Henrik M\"uller, Daniel Kudenko

entry.summary: VLM-PBRS automates potential-based reward shaping by learning the potential function directly from vision-language-model preference feedback over image pairs, preserving the optimal policy while avoiding reward hacking. It addresses sparse-reward RL exploration challenges.

entry.title: Equivariance and Augmentation for Bayesian Neural Networks

author.name: Miaowen Dong, Axel Flinth, Jan E. Gerken

entry.summary: This work studies data augmentation for Bayesian neural networks trained with variational inference, building on results that augmented infinite deep ensembles are exactly equivariant, to compare imposing symmetry via architecture versus learning it from augmented data. It focuses on exponential-family variational distributions.

entry.title: Learning Probabilistic Filters with Strictly Proper Scoring Rules

author.name: Eviatar Bach, Ricardo Baptista, Jochen Br\"ocker, Bohan Chen, Andrew Stuart

entry.summary: The proper scoring ensemble filter (PSEF) is a data assimilation method that trains a permutation-invariant analysis map to approximate Bayesian filtering distributions using only synthetic state-observation trajectories and strictly proper scoring rules. It targets uncertainty quantification in partially observed dynamical systems.

entry.title: Symplectic Neural Networks for learning Generalized Hamiltonians

author.name: Harsh Choudhary, Vyacheslav Kungurtsev, Chandan Gupta, Melvin Leok, Georgios Korpas

entry.summary: This paper introduces symplectic neural networks for learning generalized Hamiltonians from noisy state observations, leveraging the fact that symplectic discretizations of the adjoint system yield the same sensitivities to make backpropagation through implicit symplectic integrators tractable. This preserves geometric structure and energy conservation in long-term simulation.

entry.title: The Geometry of Updates: Fisher Alignment at Vocabulary Scale

author.name: John Sweeney

entry.summary: This paper addresses training-free source selection among LLM families sharing a tokenizer (e.g., SMILES, protein, genomic sequences) and shows that representation-similarity metrics like CKA are non-identifiable for transfer. It proposes head Fisher alignment, computed as a cosine at vocabulary scale, as the correct update-geometry metric.

entry.title: Interpreting "Interpretability" and Explaining "Explainability" in Machine Learning in Physics

author.name: Rikab Gambhir, Luisa Lucie-Smith, Jesse Thaler

entry.summary: This review clarifies the concepts of interpretability (structural transparency of a model) and explainability (mapping a model onto domain knowledge) as applied to machine learning in physics. It discusses the trade-offs of each, the contexts requiring them, and the intrinsic versus post-hoc tools available.

entry.title: Evaluation Pitfalls and Challenges in Multimedia Event Extraction

author.name: Philipp Seeberger, Steffen Freisinger, Tobias Bocklet, Korbinian Riedhammer

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic analysis of evaluation pitfalls in multimedia event extraction, identifying inconsistent data processing, inconsistent task assumptions, and overly relaxed evaluation settings. Controlled experiments under a strict framework show minor evaluation choices cause large performance differences, undermining comparability.

entry.title: Accelerated sampling using SamAdams variable timesteps and position-adaptive Langevin dynamics

author.name: Benedict Leimkuhler, Peter A. Whalley

entry.summary: This paper introduces SamAdams adaptive timestepping and position-adaptive Langevin (PAL) dynamics for accelerated sampling, combining a relaxed stiffness monitor that shrinks steps in stiff regions with friction concentrated along the local force direction while preserving the canonical invariant measure. The combined SA-PAL scheme uses a palindromic integrator requiring only one force evaluation per iteration.

entry.title: Fast algorithms for learning a Gaussian under halfspace truncation with optimal sample complexity

author.name: Haitong Liu, Deepak Narayanan Sridharan, David Steurer, Manuel Wiedmer

entry.summary: Provides a fast algorithm with optimal sample complexity for learning a high-dimensional Gaussian truncated to an unknown halfspace, improving on prior polynomial-time results. The runtime is dominated by empirical covariance computation.

entry.title: DanceOPD: On-Policy Generative Field Distillation

author.name: Wei Zhou, Xiongwei Zhu, Zelin Xu, Bo Dong, Lixue Gong, Yongyuan Liang, Meng Chu, Leigang Qu, Lingdong Kong, Wei Liu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Introduces DanceOPD, an on-policy generative field distillation framework for flow-matching image models that routes samples to capability-specific fields to unify text-to-image, local editing, and global editing without their usual conflicts. Trains with a simple velocity MSE objective.

entry.title: SocialPersona: Benchmarking Personalized Profiling and Response with Multimodal Social-Media Context

author.name: Qinkai Zhang, Yanyan Zhao, Xin Lu, Yulin Hu, Pengtao Han, Bing Qin

entry.summary: Introduces SocialPersona, a benchmark testing whether multimodal LLMs can infer users' revealed preferences from longitudinal social-media timelines rather than just recalling stated preferences. Built from 171 real users with human-verified preference tags across seven domains.

entry.title: HarmVideoBench: Benchmarking Harmful Video Understanding in Large Multimodal Models

author.name: Jiajun Wu, Haoyu Kang, Yining Sun, Jiacheng Hou, Heng Zhang, Danyang Zhang, Zhenjun Zhao, Haochi Zhang, Leixin Sun, Eric Hanchen Jiang, Yushan Li, Ruiyu Li, Mengkai Huang, Yan Gao, Xu Zhang, Guancheng Wan

entry.summary: Introduces HarmVideoBench, a benchmark for harmful-video understanding in large multimodal models that moves beyond binary classification to capture multi-layered harms and require explanatory rationales. Addresses superficial shortcut-based evaluation in content moderation.

entry.title: PhysRAG: Enhancing Physics-Awareness in Video Generation via Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Kexu Cheng, Zicheng Liu, Mingju Gao, Chunhe Song, Hao Tang

entry.summary: PhysRAG enhances physical awareness in video generation through retrieval-augmented generation, building a physical video database and injecting physical knowledge into a video diffusion model via learnable queries. It uses a two-stage data filtering pipeline to curate high-quality physics videos.

entry.title: Focusing on What Matters: Saliency-Harnessing Accurate Routing for Diffusion MoE

author.name: Haoyou Deng, Keyu Yan, Chaojie Mao, Xiang Wang, Yu Liu, Changxin Gao, Nong Sang

entry.summary: This work identifies a routing failure in diffusion Mixture-of-Experts models where noise-corrupted latents prevent routers from allocating compute to salient tokens, and proposes a saliency-harnessing routing method. It improves expert allocation for efficient visual generation.

entry.title: SubdivAR: Autoregressive Next-Scale Prediction for Neural Mesh Subdivision

author.name: Huipeng Guo, Zikai Song, Hang Long, Jielei Zhang, Wenbing Li, Junkai Lin, Tianhao Zhao, Jinshen Zhang, Tianle Guo, Wei Yang

entry.summary: SubdivAR reformulates neural mesh subdivision as autoregressive next-scale prediction using a Mesh Autoregressive Representation that arranges meshes at different subdivision levels into an ordered scale sequence. It improves detail synthesis and generalizability over local rule-based and neural methods.

entry.title: Not All Actions Are Equal: Rethinking Conditioning for Dexterous World Model

author.name: Zizhao Yuan, Zhengtu Liang, Taowen Wang, Qiwei Liang, Yichi Wang, Yunheng Wang, Yuetong Fang, Lusong Li, Zecui Zeng, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: This work rethinks action conditioning in dexterous world models, observing that high-DoF actions are heterogeneous spanning multiple magnitude scales, and proposes a conditioning scheme that avoids uniformly aggregating the whole action sequence. It improves modeling of subtle but important control signals.

entry.title: SAM2Matting: Generalized Image and Video Matting

author.name: Ruiqi Shen, Guangquan Jie, Chang Liu, Henghui Ding

entry.summary: SAM2Matting is a tracker-to-matting framework that advances VOS trackers like SAM2/SAM3 to high-fidelity video matting by adding a region-proposal bridge and dedicated matting heads, decoupling high-level tracking from low-level fine detail extraction. It avoids dependence on narrow video matting datasets.

entry.title: Don't Settle at the Mode! Mitigating Diversity Collapse in Pretrained Flow Models via Feature Self-Guidance

author.name: Pradhaan S Bhat, Rishubh Parihar, Abhijnya Bhat, R. Venkatesh Babu

entry.summary: This work introduces a training-free feature self-guidance mechanism to mitigate diversity collapse in pretrained flow models when generating multiple samples under the same conditioning, dispersing internal features during batch generation with manifold regularization. It avoids external reward models and their inference overhead.

entry.title: RMTL: Reinforced Micro-task Learning for Long-Horizon Manipulation with VLM Rewards

author.name: An{\i}l Can Ate\c{s}, Orhan Kahraman, Cihan Topal

entry.summary: RMTL decomposes long-horizon manipulation tasks into micro-tasks with per-stage VLM-generated reward prompts, addressing the problem that single global VLM prompts produce near-flat rewards making early progress undetectable. It improves reinforcement learning for randomized-initial-condition manipulation.

entry.title: MPC-Injection: Biasing Off-Policy Locomotion RL Toward Controller-Induced Behavior Basins

author.name: Roy Xing (Dartmouth College), Seyoung Ree (Harvard University), Brian Plancher (Dartmouth College)

entry.summary: MPC-Injection steers off-policy locomotion RL toward designer-preferred gaits by inserting transitions from a model predictive controller solving the same MDP into the replay buffer, avoiding undeployable local optima like vibrating limbs. Unlike reward shaping or adversarial imitation it adds no discriminator or auxiliary objective.

entry.title: Exploration: fine-tuning with parameter decomposition

author.name: Lucius Bushnaq

entry.summary: Lucius Bushnaq reports that fine-tuning a single scalar prefactor on one German-related rank-1 parameter subcomponent can destroy a 67M-parameter model's German prediction while beating rank-1 and rank-4 LoRA on the trade-off between German removed and English retained at small token budgets. This explores parameter decomposition for targeted, interpretable fine-tuning and unlearning. The single-scalar surgical intervention is a striking interpretability and model-editing result.

entry.title: The Open Source Economic Index of AI Adoption and Capability

author.name: Seamus Somerstep, Aritra Guha, Divesh Srivastava, Yuekai Sun

entry.summary: Develops an open-source economic index measuring AI adoption from user-LLM chat data mapped to O*NET tasks, plus a capability benchmark using MCP servers to test Kimi-k2.5 across 9 occupations. Replicates frontier-lab labor studies in an open framework.

entry.title: Sampling sea state using a diffusion model

author.name: Jiarong Wu, Bertrand Chapron, Laure Zanna

entry.summary: Proposes a diffusion-based generative model for probabilistic global sea state estimation conditioned on five days of wind forcing history, moving beyond deterministic bulk-variable wave models. Enables ensemble predictions and online coupling to climate simulations.

entry.title: AXLE: A Cloud Infrastructure for Lean 4 Theorem Proving Utilities

author.name: Jimmy Xin, Alex Schneidman, Chris Cummins, Karun Ram, Srihari Ganesh, Jannis Limperg

entry.summary: Presents AXLE, a cloud service offering 14 Lean 4 metaprogramming tools for scalable proof verification, manipulation, repair, and metadata extraction to support AI-for-math workflows like RL pipelines and dataset curation. Scales to millions of requests with per-request isolation.

entry.title: Robust Onion: Peeling Open Vocab Object Detectors Under Noise

author.name: Priyank Pathak, Mukilan Karuppasamy, Aaditya Baranwal, Shruti Vyas, Yogesh S Rawat

entry.summary: Robust Onion is an empirical study dissecting how open-vocabulary object detectors degrade under synthetic visual noise, attributing robustness primarily to vision backbone feature collapse rather than pretraining or caption supervision. It offers a layer-by-layer diagnostic of robustness failure.

entry.title: Confidence-Aware Tool Orchestration for Robust Video Understanding

author.name: Yangfan He, Yujin Choi, Jaehong Yoon

entry.summary: Robust-TO is an agentic video understanding framework that integrates per-frame trustworthiness into reasoning, addressing the Blind Trust Problem where models suffer large accuracy drops under perturbations like motion blur or occlusion without awareness. It orchestrates perception tools under a unified evidence interface.

entry.title: Safe Autoregressive Image Generation with Iterative Self-Improving Codebooks

author.name: Yunqi Xue, Zhijiang Li, Philip Torr, Jindong Gu

entry.summary: This work proposes iterative self-improving codebooks for safe autoregressive image generation, leveraging the unified multimodal model's own understanding to refine discretized visual token codebooks toward safer outputs. It investigates the safety properties of autoregressive image generation.

entry.title: Fast LeWorldModel

author.name: Yuntian Gao, Xiangyu Xu

entry.summary: Fast-LeWM accelerates JEPA-based latent world models for visual planning by replacing repeated local one-step rollouts with action-prefix prediction, reducing compute and accumulated latent errors over long horizons. It encodes action prefixes to directly predict future latents.

entry.title: Mesh-RL: Coupled subgrid reinforcement learning

author.name: Behnam Gheshlaghi, Bahador Rashidi, Shahin Atakishiyev

entry.summary: Mesh-RL is a spatial domain-decomposition RL framework inspired by finite element methods that partitions environments into overlapping subgrids with boundary-consistent temporal-difference updates to accelerate long-range credit assignment. It avoids modifying the reward function, Bellman operator, or adding explicit planning.

entry.title: Can Large Language Models Reliably Code Qualitative Humanitarian Data? A Benchmark Study Against Human Expert Adjudication

author.name: Jerome Marston, Tino Kreutzer, Salom\'e Garnier, Ella Boone, Phuong N Pham, Patrick Vinck

entry.summary: This benchmark study compares 46 LLMs against a human gold standard for coding qualitative humanitarian data, using 150 synthetic transcripts evaluated with inter-rater reliability metrics and discrepancy analysis. It establishes whether LLMs can reliably interpret nuanced accounts of need to scale humanitarian response.

entry.title: Finding Stationary Points by Comparisons

author.name: Helin Wang, Chenyi Zhang, Xiwen Tao, Yexin Zhang, Tongyang Li

entry.summary: This work studies finding stationary points of non-convex functions using only a comparison oracle (which point has the larger value), giving an algorithm that visits an epsilon-stationary point in O(n^2/epsilon^1.5) queries. It also develops the first quantum comparison-oracle algorithm for this problem.

entry.title: Cross-Head Attention Uplift Network with Inverse Propensity Score under Unobserved Confounding

author.name: Haoran Zhang, Chuanpu Li, Yuxin Fu, Bin Tong, Guan Wang, Bo Zheng, Feng Zhou

entry.summary: The Cross-Head Attention Uplift Network (CHAUN) plus Robust Adversarial Inverse Propensity Score method estimates individual treatment effects under unobserved confounding by sharing feature embeddings and using cross-head attention to integrate treatment and control representations. It proves ITE identifiability with true propensity scores even under hidden confounders.

entry.title: Designing Reward Signals for Portable Query Generation: A Case Study in Industrial Semantic Job Search

author.name: Ping Liu, Qianqi Shen, Jianqiang Shen, Wenqiong Liu, Rajat Arora, Yunxiang Ren, Chunnan Yao, Dan Xu, Baofen Zheng, Wanjun Jiang, Andrii Soviak, Kevin Kao, Jingwei Wu, Wenjing Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents an RLAIF framework for generating portable job-search queries that abstract away seeker-specific identifiers while preserving qualifications, confronting a highly adversarial reward surface where policies exploit LLM-judge rubric flaws. It compares optimization mechanics against structured reward engineering for industrial semantic search.

entry.title: The Role of Input Dimensionality in the Emergence and Targeted Control of Adversarial Examples

author.name: Nasrin Malekzadeh Goradel, Niccolo Pancino, Yaser Gholizade Atani, Benedetta Tondi, Giovanni Bellettini, Mauro Barni

entry.summary: This study systematically examines the role of input dimensionality in both the emergence and targeted control of adversarial examples, testing concentration-of-measure theories empirically. It shows real image classes exhibit strong empirical localization beyond what such theories assume, across hierarchical image datasets.

entry.title: Where Larger Models Excel: The Primacy of Constraint-Guided Reasoning

author.name: Guan-Yi Lin, Hen-Hsen Huang

entry.summary: Studies why larger models outperform smaller ones on reasoning, introducing AdvCluster to extract and cluster fine-grained advantages from paired reasoning traces. Finds constraint-guided reasoning as a primary driver of the gap.

entry.title: GAVEL: Grounded Caption Error Verification and Localization

author.name: Zixian Gao, Atsushi Hashimoto, Kuniaki Saito

entry.summary: Introduces GAVEL, a task and dataset for jointly verifying, explaining, and localizing caption errors in image-text pairs to address VLM hallucinations. Shows even strong closed-source models struggle on grounded error localization.

entry.title: Forget, Anticipate and Adapt: Test Time Training for Long Videos

author.name: Rajat Modi, Sebastian Noel, Xin Liang, Yogesh Singh Rawat

entry.summary: Introduces the Frame Forgetting Network for efficient test-time training on hour-long videos, operating on only three frames within a sliding window and skipping updates when frames are similar to avoid linear compute growth. Addresses computational intractability of existing long-video TTT.

entry.title: LogicIR: Logic Gate Networks for Image Restoration

author.name: Hongjae Lee, Myungjun Son, Jaeseong Yu, Seung-Won Jung

entry.summary: Introduces LogicIR, the first logic gate network designed for image restoration, using a UNet-inspired architecture composed entirely of NAND/XOR-style logic operations for highly efficient inference. Brings extremely efficient computation to the image restoration domain.

entry.title: PhysEditWorld: A Large-Scale Dataset Toward Physics-Editable World Models

author.name: Bin Hu, Yanwen Ma, Jiehui Huang, Ziliang Zhang, Haoning Wu, Ruicheng Zhang, Yaokun Li, Zijun Wang, Yuechen Zhang, Chun-Mei Tseng, Hanhui Li, Shengju Qian, Jun Zhou, Kaipeng Zhang, Xiaodan Liang, Jiaya Jia, Xiu Li

entry.summary: Introduces PhysEditWorld, a large-scale multimodal dataset built via a UE5 replay-and-rendering pipeline that records action-conditioned rollouts with explicit physical parameters (initially gravity) for physics-editable game world models. Aims to make physical dynamics controllable variables rather than implicit correlations.

entry.title: Capacity-Controlled Multi-View Stylization of 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zhihao Wen, Yixin Yang, Bojian Wu, Yang Zhou, Dani Lischinski, Daniel Cohen-Or, Hui Huang

entry.summary: This work proposes a capacity-controlled framework for multi-view stylization of 3D Gaussian Splatting grounded in optimal transport, reformulating style matching as a semi-balanced optimal transport problem. It mitigates many-to-one feature reuse and improves cross-view stylistic consistency.

entry.title: TMP: Tree-structured Mixed-policy Pruning for Large-scale Image Generation and Editing

author.name: Peizhen Zhang, Yang Li, Xunsong Li, Songtao Liu, Zewen Liu, Qiangqiang Hu, Guotong Guo, Jupeng Ding, Yifu Sun, coopersli, Jian Zhang, Zhao Zhong, Liefeng Bo

entry.summary: TMP is a tree-structured mixed-policy pruning framework that generalizes across image generation tasks and architectures including MoE and diffusion transformers, applicable to step-distilled models as a final compression stage. It demonstrates compression on SOTA open-source image models.

entry.title: FlameVQA: A Physically-Grounded UAV Wildfire VQA Benchmark with Radiometric Thermal Supervision

author.name: Mobin Habibpour, John Spodnik, Niloufar Alipour Talemi, Fatemeh Afghah

entry.summary: FlameVQA is a physically-grounded visual question answering benchmark for UAV wildfire monitoring built on FLAME 3, pairing RGB imagery with radiometric thermal data for temperature-grounded safety-critical reasoning. It includes 34 multiple-choice questions per image across six operational capability groups.

entry.title: Sculpting NeRF Geometry: Human-Preference Fine-Tuning of a 3D-Aware Face GAN

author.name: Archer Moore, Mingming Gong, Liam Hodgkinson

entry.summary: This work fine-tunes a pretrained 3D-aware face GAN (EG3D) directly from a learned reward over radiance-field density values using RLHF, without requiring meshes or shape priors. The reward model trains on a small set of preference samples and improves 3D geometry.

entry.title: Paying More Attention to Visual Tokens in Self-Evolving Large Multimodal Models

author.name: Shravan Venkatraman, Ritesh Thawkar, Omkar Thawakar, Rao Muhammad Anwer, Hisham Cholakkal, Salman Khan, Fahad Khan

entry.summary: This work identifies visual under-conditioning in self-evolving large multimodal models, where decoders rely on language priors rather than image content, and proposes a method to increase attention to visual tokens. It targets failures in image captioning and visual question answering under unsupervised self-play.

entry.title: Dual-Prior Guided Null-Space Learning with Mixture-of-Splines for Arbitrary Medical Slice Super-Resolution

author.name: Haofei Song, Siyuan Xu, Xintian Mao, Shaojie Guo, Qingli Li, Yan Wang

entry.summary: DP-NSL reformulates arbitrary medical slice super-resolution as a constrained recovery process using a measurement-consistent projection that reproduces acquired slices with zero error, plus a mixture-of-splines prior. It avoids hallucinating anatomically implausible structures while preserving observed data.

entry.title: Neural Texture Compression using Hypernetworks

author.name: Belcour Laurent

entry.summary: This work trains a single hypernetwork that outputs both latent features and MLP weights for neural texture compression, eliminating the need for per-material gradient-descent optimization while matching reference quality. It extends to interpolation across materials.

entry.title: NavIsaacLab: Generating Realistic Crowd via Parallel Robot Learning for Benchmarking Human-aware Navigation

author.name: Bingyi Xia, Han Bao, Jingyu Zhu, Hanjing Ye, Yuhan Pang, Guangcheng Chen, Liang Lin, Wenjun Xu, Jiankun Wang

entry.summary: NavIsaacLab generates realistic crowds via parallel robot learning in Isaac Lab for benchmarking human-aware navigation, addressing the scarcity of diverse high-quality scene data and the reliance on handcrafted pedestrian rules. It provides extensive sensor signals for training and evaluating navigation policies.

entry.title: Bridging Handheld and Teleoperated Supervision for Contact-Rich Manipulation via State-Gated Experts

author.name: Vidullan Surendran, Neehar Peri, David Watkins

entry.summary: This paper combines scalable handheld data collection (UMI-style) with teleoperation by recognizing that handheld trajectories are valid in free-space phases but dynamically infeasible in contact-sensitive phases. It proposes state-gated experts that switch supervision types per task phase to enable safe contact-rich manipulation. The framing of action validity across task phases is a useful conceptual contribution for data-efficient robot learning.

entry.title: Humanoid-DART: Humanoid Loco-Manipulation using Diffusion-guided Augmentation through Relabeling and Tracking

author.name: Pranav Debbad, Kanish Thiagarajan, Victor Dh\'edin, Shafeef Omar, Majid Khadiv

entry.summary: Humanoid-DART is a self-supervised framework that bootstraps humanoid loco-manipulation from sparse demonstrations by combining diffusion-based trajectory generation with RL tracking, automatically expanding the behavioral repertoire. It reduces the need for continual human intervention in data collection. The diffusion-plus-RL relabeling loop is a practical approach to scaling humanoid policy learning.

entry.title: PRISM: Efficient and Locally Optimal Probabilistic Planning with Reachability Guarantees

author.name: Alex Rose, Christopher Jewison, Jonathan P. How

entry.summary: PRISM is a multi-query belief-space motion planner from Jonathan How's lab that provides reachability guarantees under motion uncertainty and state/control constraints, addressing the difficulty of belief-space coverage and completeness in prior sampling-based planners. It aims for efficient, locally optimal probabilistic planning with finite-time guarantees. The reachability-guaranteed formulation is a meaningful theoretical advance for constrained belief-space planning.

entry.title: All you need is log

author.name: Akshay Balsubramani

entry.summary: This theoretical paper characterizes the unique multi-distribution generalization of the Rényi divergence family, showing that any functional of W-tuples of distributions that is monotone under data processing and additive on independent products is a positive integral of multi-way coincidence divergences. It resolves an open question relevant to multi-population fairness, multi-prior PAC-Bayes bounds, and multi-hypothesis testing. The axiomatic characterization is an elegant and potentially foundational result.

entry.title: Which tokens does a hybrid model predict better?

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: An Ai2 blog post presenting token-level analyses of Olmo 3 and an Olmo Hybrid model, finding that hybrid (attention plus state-space style) models predict meaning-bearing, context-dependent tokens better while pure transformers retain an edge on verbatim copying. This offers concrete insight into the trade-offs of hybrid architectures. It is substantive empirical analysis grounded in open models.

entry.title: Deterministic Pareto-Optimal Policy Synthesis for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Aniruddha Joshi, Niklas Lauffer, Sanjit Seshia

entry.summary: Introduces a preference-conditioned Bellman operator motivated by Chebyshev scalarization to compute deterministic Pareto-optimal policies for multi-objective MDPs, proving an enveloping upper-bound property on the true Pareto frontier. Advances theory for multi-objective RL.

entry.title: Adaptive Evaluation of Out-of-Band Defenses Against Prompt Injection in LLM Agents

author.name: Praneeth Narisetty, Shiva Nagendra Babu Kore, Uday Kumar Reddy Kattamanchi, Jayaram Kumarapu

entry.summary: Organizes out-of-band prompt-injection defenses (CaMeL, FIDES, Progent, RTBAS, FORGE) as instances of classical security principles (Biba integrity, reference monitoring, least privilege) and provides adaptive evaluation revealing coverage gaps. Offers a structured security-theory comparison of agent defenses.

entry.title: Learning Motion Feasibility from Point Clouds in Cluttered Environments

author.name: Sajid Ansari, Arthi, Girish Varma, Antony Thomas

entry.summary: This paper learns motion feasibility prediction directly from raw RGB-D observations for a 7-DOF manipulator in cluttered scenes, introducing a large-scale benchmark. It targets reducing the computational cost of infeasible planning attempts in realistic robotics settings.

entry.title: NaviCache: Test-Time Self-Calibration Caching for Video Generation

author.name: Zheqi Lv, Zhibo Zhu, Jinke Wang, Qi Tian, Shengyu Zhang, Zhengyu Chen, Chengxi Zang, Zhou Zhao, Fei Wu

entry.summary: NaviCache is a plug-and-play test-time self-calibration caching method for accelerating video diffusion models, reframing feature evolution as an inertial navigation problem to counter observational noise and momentum. It avoids the data dependency of offline calibration methods.

entry.title: Parametric Open Source Games

author.name: Aleksandar Todorov, Jesse ten Napel, Alexander M\"uller

entry.summary: This paper introduces parametric open-source games, a continuous analogue of program equilibria where players choose parameter vectors mapped to mixed actions, establishing equilibrium existence and an exact coupling threshold for cooperation in symmetric 2x2 games. It extends the framework to neural semantics.

entry.title: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning

author.name: Tianyi Men, Zhuoran Jin, Pengfei Cao, Yubo Chen, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: PEEU empowers GUI agents through autonomous environment exploration to discover experiences and hindsight experience utilization to synthesize aligned high-level training data, improving planning and cross-website generalization for small open-source MLLMs. It also proposes a task-decomposition hierarchy for analyzing generalization.

entry.title: Sketched Linear Contrastive Learning: Approximation, Optimization, and Statistical Scaling

author.name: Ziyan Chen, Zhongzhu Zhou, Ding-Xuan Zhou

entry.summary: This paper develops scaling-law theory for sketched linear contrastive learning under a paired Gaussian latent-variable setup, deriving a risk decomposition into irreducible risk, approximation error, and gradient-descent bias/variance under power-law spectra. It extends scaling-law understanding from regression to contrastive representation learning.

entry.title: Just how sure are you? Improving Verbalized Uncertainty Calibration in Medical VQA

author.name: Eren Senoglu, Federico Toschi, Nicolo Brunello, Andrea Sassella, Mark James Carman

entry.summary: This work proposes a training-based framework to improve verbalized uncertainty calibration in medical visual question answering, using a composite loss combining Brier calibration, an anchor regularizer against confidence collapse, contrastive image-text alignment, and KL stabilization. It addresses overconfidence in multimodal medical LLMs.

entry.title: Effective Covariance Dynamics in Solvable High-Dimensional GANs

author.name: Andrew Bond, Zafer Do\u{g}an

entry.summary: This work analyzes a solvable high-dimensional GAN model where a linear generator learns a low-dimensional subspace from data with structured, class-dependent latent covariance, extending prior diagonal-covariance analyses. It proves the stochastic training process converges to deterministic ODEs governed by an effective second moment.

entry.title: Generative Models on Analog Hardware with Dynamics

author.name: Yu-Neng Wang, Sara Achour

entry.summary: Introduces Analog Interaction Systems, a framework for implementing generative models on analog hardware like coupled oscillators and Ising machines, characterizing the expressivity gap versus neural baselines. Proposes mechanisms to narrow that gap for low-power generation.

entry.title: PhyEditBench: A Real-World Multi-Stage Benchmark for Physics-Aware Image Editing

author.name: Shengbin Guo, Shaokang He, Chaoyue Meng, Shengpeng Xiao, Xunzhi Xiang, Shaofeng Zhang, Qi Fan

entry.summary: Introduces PhyEditBench, a real-world multi-stage benchmark for physics-aware image editing with a hierarchical taxonomy of 4 classes and 12 subclasses, plus anti-physics synthetic cases. Reveals substantial limitations of SOTA editing models in physical reasoning.

entry.title: Full spectrum Unlearnable Examples via Spectral Equalization

author.name: Jiale Cai, Gezheng Xu, Zhihao Li, Ruiyi Fang, Ruizhi Pu, Di Wu, Qicheng Lao, Charles Ling, Boyu Wang

entry.summary: FUSE generates full-spectrum unlearnable examples that remain effective even after low-pass filtering, addressing a key vulnerability where existing data-protection perturbations concentrate in high frequencies. It uses spectral equalization and cross-band consistency for more robust data protection.

entry.title: LiveEdit: Towards Real-Time Diffusion-Based Streaming Video Editing

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Chongbo Zhao, Fangneng Zhan, Yue Ma

entry.summary: LiveEdit is a streaming video editing framework that performs causal frame-by-frame editing with strong content preservation and real-time latency, using a three-stage distillation pipeline from a bidirectional teacher. It targets practical interactive editing scenarios.

entry.title: PortraitGen: Exemplar-Driven GRPO with Dual-Reward Guidance for Photorealistic Portrait Generation

author.name: Xiaomin Li, Qian Liang, Yinan Li, Ying Zhang, Chen Li, Jing Lyu, Huchuan Lu, Xu Jia

entry.summary: PortraitGen is a GRPO-based framework for photorealistic portrait generation that uses exemplar-driven real images during post-training and dual-reward guidance targeting fine-grained AI artifacts like oily skin and biological implausibilities. It addresses superficial-aesthetics bias in existing RL image methods.

entry.title: PanoImager: Geometry-Guided Novel View Synthesis and Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramic Views

author.name: Zhisong Xu, Takeshi Oishi

entry.summary: PanoImager is an SfM-free framework for novel view synthesis and reconstruction from sparse panoramic images under rotation-dominant weak-parallax motion, combining feed-forward pose/depth priors, geometry-conditioned diffusion view completion, and depth-guided 3DGS optimization. It stabilizes reconstruction under extreme sparsity.

entry.title: Proposal-Conditioned Latent Diffusion for Closed-Loop Traffic Scenario Generation

author.name: Shubham Vaijanath Phoolari, Aleyna Kara, Christoph Lauer, Steven Peters

entry.summary: This presents a diffusion-based closed-loop traffic scenario generation framework conditioned on instance-centric scene context and multimodal proposal priors, with a compact action-latent representation for sampling efficiency. It targets time-constrained replanning loops for autonomous vehicle simulation.

entry.title: Racing a Wheeled Quadruped: Active Load Transfer Mitigation via Model Predictive Control

author.name: Marla Eisman, Brian Lam, Samuel Sonnino, Francesco Borrelli

entry.summary: This presents a hierarchical MPC and RL control framework for active roll control of a wheeled quadruped during autonomous racing, minimizing lateral load transfer with knee joints generating anti-roll torque as active suspension. Physical track experiments demonstrate reduced load transfer ratio.

entry.title: From Hallucination to Grounding: Diagnosing Visual Spatial Intelligence via CRISP

author.name: Zhixing Li, Yinan Yu

entry.summary: Introduces CRISP, a structural-diagnostic evaluation paradigm for visual spatial intelligence in VLMs that uses metric 3D scene graphs and oracle intervention to decouple latent reasoning from perceptual bottlenecks. Reveals a systematic perception-reasoning disconnect where proprietary models have strong latent reasoning but poor metric estimation.

entry.title: SharQ: Bridging Activation Sparsity and FP4 Quantization for LLM Inference

author.name: Haoqian Meng, Yilun Luo, Yafei Zhao, Wenyuan Liu, Huaqing Zheng, Xindian Ma, Peng Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces SharQ, a training-free LLM inference method bridging activation sparsity and FP4 quantization via an online sparse-dense decomposition that extracts an outlier-dominated sparse backbone quantized to FP4 plus a dense residual. Tackles input-dependent outliers that break FP4 activation compression.

entry.title: Anatomy-Guided Residual Motion Diffusion for Controllable 4D Cardiac MRI Synthesis

author.name: Yiheng Cao, Gustavo Andrade-Miranda, Jiatian Zhang, Lingxiao Zhao, Xin Gao

entry.summary: This work presents an anatomy-guided cascaded latent diffusion framework for controllable 4D cardiac MRI synthesis, disentangling static anatomy from temporal motion. It targets data augmentation under limited annotations, domain shift, and privacy constraints.

entry.title: A Deterministic Control Plane for LLM Coding Agents

author.name: Padmaraj Madatha

entry.summary: This study analyzes 10,008 GitHub repositories to characterize how LLM coding agent configuration files propagate as undeclared shared components, finding high cross-organization duplication and rare permission declarations. It proposes a deterministic control plane for managing these unmanaged configs.

entry.title: Data-Free Reservoir Features for Efficient Long-Horizon Cold-Start Continual Learning

author.name: Augustinas Ju\v{c}as, Yangchen Pan

entry.summary: CIRCLE proposes a feature extractor never fit to image data for cold-start exemplar-free class-incremental learning, using data-free reservoir features to avoid the cost of repeated backbone training and the bias of frozen backbones. It targets long-horizon continual learning without replay or pretraining.

entry.title: \chisao{}: A GPU-Native Parallel Optimizer for Multimodal Black-Box Functions via Convergence-Anticonvergence Oscillation

author.name: Ira Wolfson

entry.summary: CHISAO is a GPU-native parallel population optimizer for finding all modes of multimodal black-box functions, using a deliberate convergence-anticonvergence oscillation cycle to escape local traps while freezing confirmed modes. It exploits GPU parallelism unlike sequential methods like basin-hopping and CMA-ES.

entry.title: PersistentKV: Page-Aware Decode Scheduling for Long-Context LLM Serving on Commodity GPUs

author.name: Muhammad Ahmed

entry.summary: PersistentKV is a native block-table decode attention engine and page-aware scheduling study for grouped-query attention, targeting KV-cache-movement-bound LLM serving on commodity GPUs. It maps work by KV-head group to better utilize hardware for low-active long-context decode and mixed sequence lengths.

entry.title: RSPC: A Benchmark for Modeling Stress and Psychiatric Conditions in Digitally Mediated Relationships using Psychiatrist Annotations

author.name: Parmitha Vangapandu, Sai Ganesh Mokkapati, Sathwik Narkedimilli, MSVPJ Sathvik, Timothy Liu, Simon See, Johannes C. Eichstaedt

entry.summary: RSPC is a corpus of 1,799 Reddit posts about long-distance relationships, annotated by psychiatrists for diagnostic categories, relational stressor triggers, and relationship phase, modeling mental health within interpersonal context. It benchmarks transformer models and LLMs across multi-label disorder classification, trigger detection, and temporal phase prediction.

entry.title: ProfileFoundry: A Synthetic Person-Object Substrate for Privacy, Memory, and Tool-Use Evaluation in LLM Agent

author.name: Sriram Selvam, Anneswa Ghosh

entry.summary: Releases ProfileFoundry, a deterministic generator and fixed dataset of 100,000 synthetic person objects with consistent cross-field and temporal structure for privacy, memory, and tool-use evaluation in LLM agents. Provides relational and longitudinal structure that random fake data lacks.

entry.title: DinoLink: A Token-Centric Representation Compression Framework for Bandwidth-Constrained Collaborative V2X Perception

author.name: Tianle Zhu, Haohua Que, Handong Yao, Hongyi Xu, Zhipeng Bao

entry.summary: Proposes DinoLink, a token-centric compression framework using saliency-aware token pruning and residual vector quantization to enable bandwidth-constrained V2X collaborative perception via semantic communication. Achieves 139x bitrate reduction while maintaining competitive mAP on nuScenes.

entry.title: Identifying the Unknown: Prompt-Free Open Vocabulary Anomaly Recognition for Robot-Object Interaction

author.name: Philipp Allgeuer, Jan-Gerrit Habekost, Stefan Wermter

entry.summary: AnomNOVIC is a prompt-free open-vocabulary anomaly recognition framework for robot-object interaction, combining a masked autoencoder for object-agnostic bounding boxes with a real-time open-vocabulary classifier. It enables recognition of unseen objects without predefined class lists.

entry.title: Modeling Local, Global, and Cross-Modal Context in Multimodal 3D MRI

author.name: Minh Duc Do, Tillmann Rheude, Noel Kronenberg, Roland Eils, Benjamin Wild

entry.summary: MICViT is a 3D vision transformer for multimodal brain MRI that explicitly models modality-specific representations and cross-modal interactions across local and global contexts via four attention mechanisms. It targets the challenge of limited sample sizes in high-dimensional neuroimaging.

entry.title: Ordinal Neural Collapse as a Representation Prior for Visual Navigation

author.name: E-In Son, Jung-Taak Kim, Seung-Woo Seo

entry.summary: This proposes using ordinal neural collapse as a representation prior for visual navigation, addressing the problem that jointly optimizing visual encoders and action decoders with a single action loss produces ambiguous, action-agnostic representations. It improves robustness against scene variation and visual distractors.

entry.title: Hardware Design for Table Tennis Robot Capable of Beating Professional Players

author.name: Nobuhiko Mukai, Pavel Adodin, Stefan Heusser, Alexander Sigrist, Divij Grover, Guillem Torrente, Farshad Khadivar, Takekazu Kakinuma, Peter D\"urr

entry.summary: Describes the hardware design of Ace, a custom 8-DoF table tennis robot engineered to meet specifications derived from elite players, using topology optimization and inverse-dynamics motor selection plus an RL control policy. It is an engineering-heavy systems paper rather than an algorithmic advance. The benchmark goal of beating professionals makes it attention-grabbing.

entry.title: RelAfford6D: Relational 6D Affordance Graphs for Constraint-Driven Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Guodong Zhang, Qichen He, Wenyuan Xie, Shaokai Wu, Yanbiao Ji, Qiuchang Li, Bayram Bayramli, Yue Ding, Hongtao Lu

entry.summary: RelAfford6D is a training-free framework that builds a Relational 6D Affordance Graph linking interacting parts to physical anchors, elevating topological nodes into metric SE(3) poses via vision foundation models and formulating execution as kinematic constraints. It targets open-world manipulation of articulated objects. The training-free, constraint-driven formulation leveraging foundation models is an appealing direction.

entry.title: PhysReflect-VLA: Physical Feasibility and Self-Reflective Regulation for Reliable Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Jiayu Yang, Tao Yang, Weijun Li, Xiang Chang, Fei Chao, Changjing Shang, Qiang Shen

entry.summary: PhysReflect-VLA adds execution-time reliability to VLA policies via a Feasibility Operator that checks whether candidate actions induce dynamically consistent transitions plus structured self-reflection in a closed-loop pipeline. It targets long-horizon manipulation sensitive to infeasible transitions and contact disturbances. The closed-loop feasibility check and self-correction are practical reliability additions.

entry.title: Thinking Like a Scientist? A Structural Study of LLM-Generated Research Methods

author.name: Francesca Carlon, Brecht Verbeken, Vincent Ginis, Andres Algaba

entry.summary: Compares default methodological suggestions from GPT-5.1, Gemini 3 Pro, and DeepSeek-V3.2 against actual methods in 1,000 recent CS papers, quantifying divergence across taxonomy dimensions. Examines whether LLMs 'think like scientists' under minimal prompting.

entry.title: CascadeFormer: Depth-Tapered Transformers Motivated by Gradient Fan-in Asymmetry

author.name: Huzama Ahmad, Cao Viet Hai Nam, Se-Young Yun

entry.summary: Presents CascadeFormer, which tapers transformer width with depth to match uneven information flow (motivated by Gradient Fan-in Asymmetry), plus CascadeFlow Pruning that removes layers via accumulated gradients. Achieves comparable perplexity with 8.6% lower latency and 9.4% higher throughput.

entry.title: Perception, Verdict, and Evolution: Hindsight-Driven Self-Refining Forensics Agent for AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Yangjun Wu, Keyu Yan, Yu Liu, Jingren Zhou, Fei Huang, Rong Zhang, Zhou Zhao, Fei Wu

entry.summary: Proposes ForeAgent, an agentic forensics framework for AI-generated image detection using a Perception-Verdict architecture with hindsight-driven iterative self-evolution to reduce reliance on costly static frontier-model supervision. Improves sensitivity to fine-grained forensic artifacts.

entry.title: CAT-Q: Cost-efficient and Accurate Ternary Quantization for LLMs

author.name: Shigeng Wang, Chao Li, Yangyuxuan Kang, Jiawei Fan, Anbang Yao

entry.summary: Presents CAT-Q, a cost-efficient post-training ternary quantization scheme for LLMs using learnable modulation and softened ternarization, avoiding the data-intensive quantization-aware training that prior ternary methods require. Applicable across diverse architectures and model sizes.

entry.title: Bridging Vision and Language Concepts through Optimal Transport Semantic Flow

author.name: Chenyang Zhang, Anqi Dong, Guangming Zhu, Nuoye Xiong, Siyuan Wang, Lin Mei, Liang Zhang

entry.summary: OTF-CBM rethinks concept alignment in Concept Bottleneck Models as a dynamic optimal-transport process, learning a data-driven semantic cost via inverse optimal transport and performing unbalanced transport. It improves fine-grained concept localization over global cosine similarity.

entry.title: Scaling Multi-Reference Image Generation with Dynamic Reward Optimization

author.name: Wenwang Huang, Yusen Fu, Junjie Wang, Mengfei Huang, Yulin Li, Gan Liu, Jing Cai, Yancheng He, Zhuotao Tian

entry.summary: This work introduces OmniRef-Bench for complex multi-reference image generation and DyRef, a two-stage training framework with dynamic reward optimization to handle combinations of many mixed-type reference images. It addresses the degradation of existing models as reference count grows.

entry.title: AI Healthcare Chatbots as Information Infrastructure: A Large-Scale Study of User-Reported Breakdowns

author.name: Muhammad Hassan, Ramazan Yener, Ece Gumusel, Masooda Bashir

entry.summary: This study analyzes over 15,000 user reviews from 59 AI healthcare chatbot apps, framing them as information infrastructure and identifying recurring breakdowns in access, interaction quality, and billing, with privacy concerns linked to the most negative experiences. It highlights real-world reliability failures.

entry.title: Clue-Guided Money Laundering Group Discovery

author.name: Boyang Wang, Jianing Cao
