entry.summary: This work proposes Clue-Guided Group Discovery for anti-money-laundering, progressively recovering a laundering group from an initial clue set through analyst interaction, better matching real investigation workflows than node-level alerts or global group search. It introduces the Clue2Group framework.

entry.title: Reproducibility Study of "AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models"

author.name: Ananth K S, Arya Hariharan

entry.summary: This is a reproducibility study of AlphaEdit, a null-space-constrained knowledge editing method, confirming its reported metrics on the original models while extending evaluation to new architectures, benchmarks, and longer sequential editing horizons. It identifies a discrepancy in reported fluency consistency.

entry.title: fTNN: a tensor neural network for fractional PDEs

author.name: Qingkui Ma, Hehu Xie, Xiaobo Yin

entry.summary: fTNN is a deterministic tensor neural network subspace method for solving fractional-Laplacian PDEs on bounded domains, using a geometry-adapted integration split into singular near-field, regular interior far-field, and analytical exterior far-field contributions. It applies tailored quadrature to each component for the fractional Poisson and advection-diffusion equations.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Tree-level Biomass Estimation in Urban Environments From Airborne LiDAR and Optical Observations

author.name: Jose Bermudez (McMaster University, Hamilton, Ontario, Canada), Zilong Zhong (McMaster University, Hamilton, Ontario, Canada), Dominic Cyr (, Environment and Climate Change Canada, Montreal, Quebec, Canada), Camile Sothe (Planet Labs PBC, San Francisco, California, USA), Alemu Gonsamo (McMaster University, Hamilton, Ontario, Canada)

entry.summary: This paper presents a self-supervised, crown-level above-ground biomass estimation framework for an 810 km2 urban landscape using leaf-off airborne LiDAR and near-infrared orthophotography. A dual-stream cross-attention network trained on rule-based pseudo-labels delineates individual tree crowns and assigns functional types.

entry.title: Attributed, But Not Incremental: Cannibalization-Corrected Attribution for Large-Scale Advertising

author.name: Donghui Li, Bowen Yuan, Zili Yang, Qinxin Chen, Lijing Song

entry.summary: This paper proposes an experiment-calibrated attribution correction framework that uses incrementality experiments as causal anchors to convert sparse lift measurements into daily corrections for large-scale advertising. It addresses how paid-attributed conversions overstate true incremental growth when paid channels cannibalize organic demand.

entry.title: Tractography-Driven Synthetic Data Generation for Fiber Bundle Segmentation in Tracer Histology

author.name: Kyriaki-Margarita Bintsi, Sparsh Makharia, Ya\"el Balbastre, Joselyn Romero Avila, Julia F. Lehman, Suzanne N. Haber, Anastasia Yendiki

entry.summary: This work proposes a synthetic-data augmented framework for automated fiber bundle segmentation in macaque tracer histology, using ex vivo dMRI tractography as a generative prior to synthesize realistic 2D training patches composed with blockface backgrounds. It reduces reliance on time-consuming manual annotation for validating dMRI tractography.

entry.title: MinGram: A Minimalist Unigram Tokenizer with High Compression and Competitive Morphological Alignment

author.name: Sander Land

entry.summary: Introduces MinGram, a minimalist Unigram tokenizer that keeps editable token-list representation but simplifies training using a BPE seed, hard EM, and a single pruning step. Achieves high compression with competitive morphological alignment while removing heavy training machinery.

entry.title: Mapping Political-Elite Networks in Europe with a Multilingual Joint Entity-Relation Extraction Pipeline

author.name: Kirill Solovev, Jana Lasser

entry.summary: Presents a fully open-weight multilingual joint entity-relation extraction pipeline that builds signed, temporal knowledge graphs of European political-elite networks from large news corpora. Moves beyond simple co-occurrence to capture adversarial and informal ties at scale.

entry.title: Exact and Deterministic Patch Descriptor Retrieval via Hierarchical Normalization

author.name: Koichi Sato

entry.summary: This presents a patch descriptor retrieval method using Hierarchical Normalization that returns the provably exact nearest neighbor while evaluating only a fraction of the database, and does so deterministically across runs and hardware. It contrasts with approximate methods like HNSW that trade exactness for speed.

entry.title: SSI-Policy: Learning Structured Scene Interfaces for Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Kaijun Wang, Zikai Ouyang, Xuping Wu, Jinyi Hong, Wei Pan, Haibo Lu, Jia Pan, Wei Zhang, Linfang Zheng

entry.summary: SSI-Policy introduces a unified RGB-only Structured Scene Interface encoding monocular depth, language-grounded object layouts, and instruction-conditioned trajectories as an intermediate representation for vision-language manipulation. It aims to retain geometric structure without depth sensors while supporting task-level reasoning. The modular RGB-only representation is a sensible engineering middle ground for low-data regimes.

entry.title: PAMAE: Phase-Aware-MoE Action Experts Towards Reliable Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Jiayu Yang, Tao Yang, Xiang Chang, Fei Chao, Changjing Shang, Qiang Shen

entry.summary: PAMAE replaces the single shared action expert in flow-matching VLA policies with a sparse mixture-of-experts routed by execution-phase cues, enabling phase-specific control patterns while preserving the pretrained backbone. It is a plug-and-play module for multi-stage manipulation reliability. The phase-aware MoE routing is a reasonable refinement of flow-matching action heads.

entry.title: Improving the speed and energy-efficiency of AI agents

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT News describes a system from MIT and Microsoft that lets developers specify agentic workflows in plain language and then automatically selects the best models, tools, hardware configuration, and resource allocation, adjusting on the fly to optimize for cost or speed. Tests on agentic workloads reduced computation, energy, and cost. This addresses real efficiency problems in increasingly common agentic AI systems.

entry.title: Helpfulness Hurts: Domain-Dependent Degradation of Mid-Trained Compassion Values Under Post-Training

author.name: Jasmine Brazilek, Juliana Seawell

entry.summary: Investigates how post-training (SFT and GRPO) degrades 'compassion values' instilled during mid-training in a Llama 3.1 8B model, finding helpfulness training erodes animal-welfare values more than coding training. It highlights domain-dependent value degradation during alignment pipelines.

entry.title: LCG: Long-Context Consistent Image Generation with Sparse Relational Attention

author.name: Zihao Wang, Yijia Xu, Haoze Zheng, Xuran Ma, Haokun Gui, Harry Yang

entry.summary: Proposes LCG, a long-context multi-image text-to-image generation framework using Sparse Relational Attention and a Routing Consistency Constraint to maintain consistency across sequential outputs for comics, storyboards, and visual narratives. Targets identity and layout consistency at scale.

entry.title: TEMPO-Diffusion: Temporally Exposed Malicious Poisoning of Diffusion Models

author.name: William Aiken, Paula Branco, Guy-Vincent Jourdan, Iosif-Viorel Onut

entry.summary: Introduces TEMPO-Diffusion, a targeted backdoor attack framework for diffusion models that localizes malicious distribution shifts to temporal in-distribution exposures, supporting class-targeted attacks, multiple sub-image backdoors, and time-conditioned in-painting triggers. Improves stealthiness over input-time triggers.

entry.title: EVOM: Agentic Meta-Evolution of Actor-Critic Architectures for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Boyun Zhang, Chao Wang, Kai Wu

entry.summary: Introduces EVOM, an agentic meta-evolution framework that uses an LLM-based design agent to discover actor-critic RL architectures via bi-level optimization with low-fidelity PPO inner loops. Automates open-ended neural architecture design for RL.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of LLM-Generated Specifications for VeriFast

author.name: Wen Fan, Minh Tran, Sanya Dod, Xin Hu, Marilyn Rego, Danning Xie, Jenna DiVincenzo, Lin Tan

entry.summary: Empirically evaluates how well ten LLMs generate separation-logic specifications for the VeriFast verifier across 303 C functions, exploring eight prompting approaches. Addresses the gap where prior LLM-for-verification work targeted non-SL verifiers.

entry.title: Agents That Know Too Much: A Data-Centric Survey of Privacy in LLM Agents

author.name: Nada Lahjouji, Ashwin Gerard Colaco

entry.summary: Surveys privacy in LLM agents from a data-centric perspective, organizing risks around the data an agent touches (queries, intermediate results, memory writes, inter-agent messages) rather than by attack type. Highlights how multi-step, stateful, delegated-permission agents leak sensitive information beyond final answers.

entry.title: Disco-LoRA: Disentangled Composition of Content, Style, and Motion for Multi-concept Video Customization

author.name: Xuancheng Xu, Gengyun Jia, Bing-Kun Bao

entry.summary: Disco-LoRA introduces a framework for multi-concept video customization that disentangles and recombines content, style, and motion using LoRA-based decomposition. It includes a new benchmark for jointly controlling these concepts in text-to-video generation.

entry.title: Event-Aware Instructed Assistant for Referring Video Segmentation

author.name: Jinyu Liu, Henghui Ding, Shuting He, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: This work decomposes videos into simple events via learnable Event Queries for referring video segmentation, addressing confusion and hallucination from treating videos as single events. It aligns text-related segments with distinct events in an event-by-event manner.

entry.title: Beyond Global Divergences: A Local-Mass Perspective on Bayesian Inference

author.name: Hanli Xu, Fengxiang He, Sarat Moka

entry.summary: This work introduces a local-mass perspective on Bayesian inference via a Mass Index and a regularized extended KL divergence, capturing local behavior not reflected by global objectives like KL divergence and ELBO. It characterizes how Bayesian updating changes local mass under singular components.

entry.title: Implementation of reinforcement learning in chemical reaction networks: application to phototaxis as curiosity-driven exploration

author.name: Ruyi Tang (LCQB-AG), Gr\'egoire Sergeant-Perthuis (LCQB-AG), David Colliaux

entry.summary: This work proposes a framework linking a POMDP with biochemical reaction-network dynamics to implement reinforcement learning in chemical systems, reframing algal phototaxis as curiosity-driven, information-seeking sensorimotor behavior. The cell updates a minimal internal state via memoryless Bayesian steps.

entry.title: Embedding Foundation Model Predictions in Discrete-Choice Models with Structural Guarantees

author.name: Yingshuo Wang, Xian Sun, Yanhang Li, Zhichao Fan, Zexin Zhuang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage adapter that embeds tabular foundation model predictions inside a multinomial logit utility framework, enforcing economic constraints like positive willingness-to-pay and zero probability for unavailable options. It combines maximum-likelihood structural fitting with a small neural correction, bridging deep learning accuracy and economic interpretability.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Neural Predictivity from Language Models During Naturalistic Comprehension

author.name: Xiao Jia

entry.summary: Note: the listed item FracEvent is an event-camera simulator that models pixel-level lifecycle dynamics via fractional-relaxation pixel dynamics, going beyond contrast-threshold generation that simplifies temporal structure. It aims to produce more realistic event timing for better downstream transfer in event-based vision.

entry.title: Ribbon: Scalable Approximation and Robust Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Graham Gibson, John Tipton, Kellin Rumsey, Natalie Klein

entry.summary: Introduces Ribbon, a scalable approximation to Bayesian bootstrap uncertainty using influence-function linearization around a single fitted model rather than repeated refitting. Aims to provide cheap, principled predictive uncertainty for complex models.

entry.title: Improving General Role-Playing Agents via Psychology-Grounded Reasoning and Role-Aware Policy Optimization

author.name: Zhenhua Xu, Dongsheng Chen, Jian Li, Yitong Lin, Zhebo Wang, Jiafu Wu, Yizhang Jin, Chengjie Wang, Meng Han, Yabiao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Psy-CoT, a psychology-grounded chain-of-thought framework decomposing role-playing reasoning into perception, empathy, and logical construction, plus role-aware policy optimization. Aims for general role-playing agents that think from a profile rather than mimic surface patterns.

entry.title: DiCoBench: Benchmarking Multi-Image Fine-Grained Perception via Differential and Commonality Visual Cues

author.name: Geng Li, Yuxin Peng

entry.summary: Introduces DiCoBench, a multi-image high-resolution benchmark for cross-image fine-grained perception via differential and commonality visual cues, with 765 samples across 8 tasks. Evaluates whether MLLMs can autonomously perceive implicit visual cues without explicit textual hints.

entry.title: DeCoFlow: Structural Decomposition of Normalizing Flows for Continual Anomaly Detection

author.name: Hun Im, Jungi Lee, Subeen Cha, Pilsung Kang

entry.summary: Proposes DeCoFlow for continual anomaly detection with normalizing flows, decomposing coupling-layer subnets into a frozen universal base and task-specific low-rank adapters to prevent catastrophic forgetting while preserving invertibility. Exploits affine coupling's parameterization invariance.

entry.title: TraMP-LLaMA: Generative Interpretability with Decoupled Instruction Tuning for Facial Expression Quality Assessment

author.name: Shuchao Duan, Alan Whone, Hossein Rahmani, Jun Liu, Majid Mirmehdi

entry.summary: TraMP-LLaMA is a multimodal framework for facial expression quality assessment in Parkinson's disease that jointly predicts severity scores and generates structured textual reports from facial motion cues. It uses decoupled instruction tuning to reduce interference between scoring and language generation.

entry.title: SatSplatDiff: Geometry-preserving generative refinement for high-fidelity satellite Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jiyong Kim, Shuang Song, Ronjgun Qin

entry.summary: SatSplatDiff uses geometry-preserving generative refinement to improve satellite Gaussian Splatting reconstructions, addressing insufficient supervision on building facades from top-down satellite views. It mitigates hallucinations and photo-consistency breaks that arise from refining each view independently.

entry.title: DnA: Denoising Attention for Visual Tasks

author.name: Ron Campos, Subhajit Maity, Xin Li, Srijan Das, Aritra Dutta

entry.summary: DnA (Denoising Attention) replaces standard softmax attention with a scheme using positive and negative queries to separate relevant from closely-associated irrelevant features in distinct subspaces with larger principal angles. It yields modest accuracy gains on ImageNet-1K with a ViT-B backbone.

entry.title: Morphology-Specific Closed-Loop Control of Logarithmic-Spiral Continuum Arms via Online Jacobian Error Compensation

author.name: Partha Datta (Laboratory for Soft Machines and Electronics, Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland, OH, USA, Department of Electrical, Computer and Systems Engineering, Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland, OH, USA), Yi Jin (Laboratory for Soft Machines and Electronics, Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland, OH, USA), Wei Lin (Department of Electrical, Computer and Systems Engineering, Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland, OH, USA), C. Chase Cao (Laboratory for Soft Machines and Electronics, Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland, OH, USA, Department of Electrical, Computer and Systems Engineering, Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland, OH, USA, Advanced Platform Technology)

entry.summary: This presents the first morphology-specific closed-loop task-space control framework for logarithmic-spiral continuum arms, deriving an analytical task-space Jacobian from spiral kinematics combined with online Jacobian error compensation. It enables reaching, wrapping, and grasping for bio-inspired soft manipulators.

entry.title: RouterVLA: Turning Smoke Tests into Supervision for Heterogeneous VLA Selection

author.name: Xingyu Ren, Chugang Yi, Ge Ma, Youran Sun

entry.summary: RouterVLA studies reusing pre-deployment smoke-test rollouts to supervise selection among heterogeneous frozen VLA experts, using outcome-disjoint cross-fitting where probes profile each expert and a separate trial scores the selection. Across 34,752 LIBERO-Plus records a simple probe-success rule raises held-out success by 14.6 points, and learned scorers were statistically indistinguishable from this rule. The finding that commissioning trials carry most of the routing value is a useful, honest negative-ish result.

entry.title: KG-TRACE: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Mechanistic Grounding in Antimicrobial Resistance Prediction

author.name: Naman Garg, Sarika Jain, Sourav Yadav, Bharat K. Bhargava, Ghanapriya Singh, Abhishek Srivastava, Parimal Kar

entry.summary: Presents KG-TRACE, a neuro-symbolic framework integrating the WHO mutation knowledge graph as a biological constraint on a neural genomic model for antimicrobial resistance prediction, using a learned epistemic trust gate. Achieves 0.976 AUROC for isoniazid with mechanistic grounding.

entry.title: SSM Adapters via Hankel Reduced-order Modeling: Injection Site Determines Task Suitability in Long-Context Fine-Tuning

author.name: Omanshu Thapliyal

entry.summary: Introduces the HRM adapter, an SSM-based PEFT module initialized via balanced truncation of Hankel Grammians with FFT-based parallel scanning for parity with LoRA, finding that MLP injection sites suit sequential state-accumulation tasks. Outperforms LoRA on LongBench with Mistral-7B.

entry.title: Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory: Eliminating Stale-Fact Errors for AI Agents over Evolving Knowledge

author.name: Neeraj Yadav

entry.summary: Identifies that RAG has no model of time, retrieving stale and current facts with near-identical embedding similarity (AUROC 0.59 for distinguishing contradicted from duplicated facts), and presents MemStrata, a retrieval memory that tracks temporal validity to eliminate stale-fact errors. Addresses evolving knowledge in agent memory.

entry.title: VoiceTTA: Enhancing Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech via Reinforcement Learning-Based Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Tianxin Xie, Chenxing Li, Dong Yu, Li Liu

entry.summary: Introduces VoiceTTA, a reinforcement-learning test-time adaptation method for zero-shot TTS that improves imitation of unseen speaking styles using F0/energy coefficient-of-variation rewards plus speaker similarity and intelligibility, optimizing learnable prefixes via GRPO. Enables rapid personalization without large datasets.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Size Transfer for Neural ODEs on Sparse Random Graphs: Graphon Limits and Adjoint Convergence

author.name: Mingsong Yan, Zhida Wang, Sui Tang

entry.summary: Develops a quantitative theory for zero-shot size transfer of Graph Neural ODEs on sparse random graphs sampled from graphons, proving trajectory-wise and adjoint convergence to graphon limits. Justifies training on small graphs and deploying on larger similar graphs without retraining.

entry.title: NuclearQAv2: A Structured Benchmark for Evaluating Domain-Science Competence in Large Language Models

author.name: Henry Shaowu Yuchi, Michal Kucer, Benjamin H. Sims, Selma Peterson, Emily Taylor

entry.summary: NuclearQAv2 is a structured benchmark of roughly 1,240 question-answer pairs across boolean, numeric, and verbal categories for evaluating LLMs on nuclear engineering knowledge and quantitative reasoning. It uses a hybrid pipeline combining expert authoring, datasets, and LLM-assisted generation.

entry.title: Uncertainty quantification via conformal prediction in data assimilation

author.name: Catherine George, Alireza Javanmardi, Tijana Janji\'c, Eyke H\"ullermeier

entry.summary: This study investigates applying conformal prediction to uncertainty quantification in data assimilation for numerical weather prediction, using a 1D modified shallow water model that mimics convection. It compares standard, normalized, and quantile-regression CP variants across coverage, interval length, and interval-score metrics.

entry.title: A probabilistic framework for online test-time adaptation

author.name: Daniel Corrales, David R\'ios Insua

entry.summary: This paper presents a probabilistic state-space modeling framework for online test-time adaptation, where a model trained on labeled data must adapt to unlabeled data under distributional shift. It characterizes parameter learning, time evolution, prior tuning, and prediction within the architecture.

entry.title: Cascaded Multi-Granularity Pruning for On-Device LLM Inference in Industrial IoT

author.name: Jinghan Wang, Yanjun Chen, Wei Zhang, Xiaotong Huang, Tianchen Liu, Gaoliang Peng

entry.summary: Presents a cascaded multi-granularity pruning framework removing layers, heads, and channels coarse-to-fine with low-rank recovery between stages for extreme LLM compression on Industrial IoT edge devices. Formalizes a checkable Structural Independence Assumption to predict pruning reliability.

entry.title: Towards Explainable Adjudicative Variance: Quantifying Judicial Discretion via Gated Multi-Task Learning

author.name: Stanis{\l}aw S\'ojka, Felix Steffek, Matthias Grabmair

entry.summary: Proposes a judge-aware gated multi-task learning architecture to disentangle objective case facts from judicial discretion in legal outcome prediction, evaluated on nearly 14,000 UK Employment Tribunal decisions. Models when outcomes hinge on judge identity versus merits.

entry.title: Layer-Specific Prompt Fusion Discovery via Differentiable Search in Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Xi Xiao, Xingjian Li, Yunbei Zhang, Cheng Han, Tianming Liu, Tianyang Wang, Runmin Jiang, Jihun Hamm, Xiao Wang, Min Xu

entry.summary: Formulates visual prompt fusion in Vision Transformers as a bi-level optimization solved via differentiable architecture search to discover layer-specific hybrid fusion schemes beyond simple concatenation or addition. Studies whether hybrid fusion improves prompt tuning.

entry.title: TaskTok: Delving into Task Tokens for Task-driven Image Restoration

author.name: Hongjae Lee, Sojung Kang, Jaeseong Yu, Seung-Won Jung

entry.summary: Proposes TaskTok, which observes that task-relevant cues are unevenly distributed across latent tokens in task-driven image restoration and selectively refines only a relevant token subset rather than all tokens. Improves downstream high-level vision performance while reducing computation.

entry.title: Liquid Fusion of Heterogeneous Representations Towards General Salient Object Detection

author.name: Ke Chen, Ling Zhou, Guangqi Jiang, Gengshen Wu, Yi Liu, Shoukun Xu

entry.summary: This proposes a method for general salient object detection that harmonizes complementary spectral biases of CNNs and State Space Models via a dynamic liquid fusion mechanism. It leverages frequency-domain analysis showing CNN and SSM representations are complementary.

entry.title: Appearance-Preserving Refinement of Generated 3D Assets for Monochromatic Fabrication

author.name: Chentao Shen, Chen Jia, Mingjie Huang, Zhuang Zhang, Haisen Zhao, Xiangru Huang

entry.summary: GenMF is an appearance-oriented geometry refinement framework that recovers texture-dependent appearance cues in geometry for monochromatic fabrication of generated 3D assets, where texture information is lost. It balances appearance recovery against fabrication risks from sharp local features.

entry.title: Surviving by Serving: Functional Relevance Drives Self-Organization in Complex Adaptive Systems

author.name: Claus Metzner, Ali Ghebleh, Achim Schilling, Andreas Maier, Thomas Kinfe, Patrick Krauss

entry.summary: This proposes Surviving by Serving as a general self-organization principle where system components persist only if their outputs are utilized by others, otherwise adapting and exploring. A minimal multi-agent model shows spontaneous emergence of functional organization without global objectives.

entry.title: KRVF: A Source-Aware Semantic Voxel World Representation for Edge Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Runfeng Ling

entry.summary: KRVF is a source-aware semantic voxel world representation for edge mobile manipulation that encodes occupancy, color, semantic evidence, temporal freshness, and evidence source as task-oriented voxels. It separates measured occupancy from semantic-prior hypotheses to enable depth-failure-aware reasoning.

entry.title: PlanRL: A Trajectory Planning Architecture for Reinforcement Learning-based Driving Experts

author.name: Joonhee Lim, Yongjae Lee, Jangho Shin, Dongsuk Kum

entry.summary: PlanRL integrates an RL driving policy with a polynomial trajectory planner in a Frenet-frame coordinate system, outputting interpretable trajectories rather than raw control commands. This improves interpretability and compatibility with end-to-end planning architectures. The architecture is a thoughtful bridge between RL experts and structured planning for autonomous driving.

entry.title: LiMoDE: Rethinking Lifelong Robot Manipulation from a Mixture-of-Dynamic-Experts Perspective

author.name: Zhihao Gu, Lin Wang

entry.summary: Introduces LiMoDE, a lifelong robot manipulation framework using a Mixture-of-Dynamic-Experts with a two-stage learning scheme to extract reusable skills and mitigate catastrophic forgetting. Offers an architectural alternative to prompt-learning approaches.

entry.title: ProvenAI: Provenance-Native Traces of Evidence in Generated Answers

author.name: Mohammad Faizan, Dalal Alharthi

entry.summary: Introduces ProvenAI, a framework decomposing RAG transparency into answer correctness, citation fidelity, and per-document influence via leave-one-resource-out interventions on the HotpotQA distractor benchmark. Distinguishes superficial citations from sources that genuinely shaped outputs.

entry.title: Speaking Numbers to LLMs: Multi-Wavelet Number Embeddings for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Defu Cao, Zijie Lei, Muyan Weng, Jiao Sun, Yan Liu

entry.summary: Proposes TempoWave, a plug-and-play temporal wavelet digit interface that maps scalar observations into digit-wise multi-wavelet embeddings to fix the misalignment between LLM tokenization and continuous numerical values for time series forecasting. Preserves numerical ordering and exposes local and global structure.

entry.title: LAMP: Lane-Aligned Motion Primitives for Feasible Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Sangjin Han, Hoseong Jung, Jeongtae Her, Changhyun Choi, H. Jin Kim

entry.summary: Proposes LAMP, a topology-aware motion forecasting framework that anchors multimodal trajectory predictions to lane-aligned motion primitives learned via VQ-VAE, ensuring predictions adhere to lane topology even for low-probability modes. Improves feasibility for safety-critical autonomous driving planning.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Selective Multimodal Driver Monitoring with Driver-State World Modeling

author.name: Daosheng Qiu, Haozhuang Chi, Hao Su, Shu Long, Xinyue Miao, Yongle Dong, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: This work proposes a cost-aware selective inference framework for multimodal driver monitoring, pairing a lightweight RGB-physiological student model with a learned gate that decides whether to accept fast predictions or abstain for safety. It targets low-latency, reliable in-cabin monitoring.

entry.title: ReaORE: Reasoning-Guided Progressive Open Relation Extraction Empowered by Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Xin Lin, Liang Zhang, Guoqi Ma, Hongyao Tu, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: ReaORE is a reasoning-guided progressive framework for open relation extraction that performs coarse-to-fine relation reasoning using large reasoning models to generalize to unseen relation types. It addresses limitations of clustering-based and direct LLM-generation approaches.

entry.title: Physics-guided Convolutional Neural Network for Domain Growth Prediction in Systems with Conserved Kinetics

author.name: Vijay Yadav, Madhu Priya, Manish Dev Shrimali, Prabhat K. Jaiswal

entry.summary: This work proposes an attention-based physics-guided CNN surrogate model to predict microstructural evolution governed by the Cahn-Hilliard equation, achieving stable accurate long-time rollouts for phase separation in binary mixtures. It targets conserved-kinetics systems.

entry.title: A General Framework for Learning Algebraic Properties from Cayley Graphs using Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Tal Weissblat

entry.summary: This work generalizes a GNN framework to learn arbitrary algebraic properties of finite groups directly from their Cayley graph representations, demonstrating recovery of abelianity, nilpotency, and solvability. It uses a common architecture and pipeline across property types.

entry.title: EMA-FS: Accelerating GBDT Training via Gain-Informed Feature Screening

author.name: Yan Song

entry.summary: EMA-FS accelerates gradient-boosted decision tree training by maintaining an exponential moving average of per-feature split gains and restricting histogram construction to top-K high-gain features after warmup. Unlike random subsampling, it screens features based on predictive utility.

entry.title: Asymptotically Optimal Learning for Parametric Prophet Inequalities

author.name: Jung-hun Kim, Anna Grebennikova, Vianney Perchet

entry.summary: Note: this position contains 'Asymptotically Optimal Learning for Parametric Prophet Inequalities' content mismatch; the listed item is a safe transfer RL framework for autonomous highway lane changing using adaptive reward shaping and policy-ratio reweighting. It introduces a teacher intervention mechanism to ensure safety and mitigate distribution-shift-induced training oscillation.

entry.title: Kolmogorov Arnold networks (KAN) for aerodynamic prediction: a comparison with MLPs and GNNs

author.name: Miguel Jaraiz, Fermin Gutierrez, Pablo Yeste, Miguel S\'anchez-Dom\'inguez, Eusebio Valero, Gonzalo Rubio, Lucas Lacasa

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks against MLPs and GNNs for aerodynamic prediction, contributing to the ongoing debate about whether KANs outperform MLPs in classic ML tasks. It assesses KAN performance specifically in the aerodynamics domain.

entry.title: BetXplain: An Explanation-Annotated Dataset for Detecting Manipulative Betting Advertisements on Social Media

author.name: MSVPJ Sathvik, Parmitha Vangapadu, Nishit Rane, Sathwik Narkedimilli, Mark Lee, Akrati Saxena

entry.summary: BetXplain is an explanation-annotated dataset of manipulative betting advertisements collected from Instagram and Reddit, manually labeled for deceptive advertising practices alongside human explanations. It targets the underexplored automated detection of misleading gambling promotions on social media.

entry.title: Syntactic Belief Update as the Driver of Garden Path Processing Difficulty

author.name: Alan Zhou, Milo\v{s} Stanojevi\'c, John T. Hale

entry.summary: Proposes that garden-path processing difficulty is driven by syntactic belief updates over a distribution of parse trees, measured via a generalized Renyi divergence, rather than lexical surprisal which fails in these cases. Offers a psycholinguistic model of human parsing difficulty.

entry.title: Beyond Surface Forms: A Comprehensive, Mechanism-Oriented Taxonomy of Indirect Linguistic Encoding for LLM-Based Coded Language Detection

author.name: Hamid Reza Firoozfar, Mohammadsadegh Abolhasani, Reza Mousavi, Paul Jen-Hwa Hu

entry.summary: Proposes a comprehensive mechanism-oriented taxonomy of indirect linguistic encoding (algospeak, euphemisms, obfuscation) for LLM-based coded language detection, categorizing by encoding operations rather than communicative goals. Evaluated against four prior taxonomies on 2,000 annotated TikTok and Bluesky posts.

entry.title: Coarse-to-Fine: A Hybrid Self-Supervised Method for Non-rigid 3D Shape Matching

author.name: Feifan Luo, Ting Li, Zhao Li, Hongyang Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid self-supervised coarse-to-fine method for non-rigid 3D shape matching with a dual-branch design using Laplacian and elastic functional-map bases. Achieves SOTA on non-isometric deformations and topological noise while staying efficient.

entry.title: Intracranial Aneurysm Classification and Segmentation via Tri-Axial ROI and Multi-Task Learning

author.name: Pengcheng Shi, Kaiyuan Yang, Houjing Huang, Jiawei Chen, Yan Lu, Jiaqi Liu, Murong Xu, Bjoern Menze, Xinglin Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a multi-task framework for intracranial aneurysm analysis performing multi-label classification, multi-class aneurysm segmentation, and vessel segmentation across 13 anatomical locations and four imaging modalities. Combines fast 2D tri-axial ROI extraction with a 3D multi-task nnU-Net and dual-decoder design.

entry.title: Calibrated Harmonic Overlaid Implicit Neural Representations for Multi-Dimensional Data

author.name: Honghang Chen, Xiujun Zhang, Xiaoli Sun, Mingqing Xiao

entry.summary: CHOIR is an implicit neural representation that uses coordinated harmonic superposition inspired by Fourier series instead of deep function composition, to improve optimization stability and reduce spectrum bias for multi-dimensional data. It targets multispectral images and videos.

entry.title: Pseudo-Text-Conditioned 3D Grounding DINO for Organ Localization in Abdominal CT

author.name: Siqi Chen, Han Gong, Keyi Hou, Jingxuan Yang, Sheethal Bhat, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: CT-3GDINO is a lightweight 3D detector adapting a Grounding-DINO-style architecture for organ localization in abdominal CT, using frozen pseudo-text class tokens instead of a real text encoder. It provides spatial priors for downstream trauma analysis with a Swin3D backbone.

entry.title: A System for Fast, Resilient, and Adaptable Loco-Manipulation Behaviors on Humanoid Robots

author.name: Duncan William Calvert

entry.summary: This thesis presents a robot-local, runtime-editable behavior authoring and execution system for fast, resilient, adaptable loco-manipulation on humanoid robots, combining object-centric Affordance Templates, Behavior Tree logic, and operator supervision following Coactive Design principles. It maintains continuous operator-robot synchronization for runtime repair.

entry.title: BOWConnect: Parallel Bayesian Optimization over Windows with Learned Local Cost Maps for Sample-Efficient Kinodynamic Motion Planning

author.name: Sourav Raxit, Abdullah Al Redwan Newaz, Jose Fuentes, Leonardo Bobadilla

entry.summary: BOWConnect is a bidirectional parallel kinodynamic motion planner that integrates Bayesian Optimization over Windows as a learned steering function, with each worker learning local cost maps to guide sampling toward feasible controls. It targets sample inefficiency, unreliable heuristics, and narrow passages in high-dimensional planning. The learned local cost-map steering within a parallel tree search is a creative blend of optimization and sampling-based planning.

entry.title: $\lambda$-PSD: Scalable Approximate SNR-Optimised Polynomial Stein Discrepancies

author.name: Minh-Long Nguyen, Thanh-Long Vu, Christopher Drovandi, Leah F. South, Trung-Tin Nguyen

entry.summary: This work analyzes polynomial Stein discrepancies and shows that increasing polynomial degree amplifies signal without controlling variance, potentially causing exponential SNR-squared decay, then reformulates discrepancy construction as explicit SNR-squared maximization via a Rayleigh quotient over Stein features. It introduces a scalable lambda-PSD method. The SNR-driven reformulation is a clarifying theoretical insight for goodness-of-fit testing.

entry.title: Divergent Recommendations, Convergent Diagnoses: Cross-Provider Failure-Mode Convergence in AI Commercial Recommendation

author.name: Will Jack, Noah Lehman, Keller Maloney, Sarah Xu

entry.summary: Studies how ChatGPT and Claude diverge on product recommendations (only ~35% overlap) yet converge on diagnosing why brands fail to be recommended across discoverability, compellingness, and positioning failure modes. Analyzes 215 prompts and 7,763 joint failures.

entry.title: Hybrid privacy-aware semantic search: SVD-truncated document geometry and CKKS-encrypted query reranking under a restricted threat model

author.name: Sergey Kurilenko

entry.summary: Studies a hybrid privacy-aware semantic search method protecting document collections geometrically via SVD-truncation plus secret orthogonal rotation while protecting queries cryptographically with CKKS homomorphic encryption reranking. Exploits asymmetry between static collections and dynamic queries against embedding-inversion attacks.

entry.title: XMSE-Aware Adaptive Empirical Bayes Estimation

author.name: Minghao Chen, Jiale Zheng

entry.summary: This paper proposes an XMSE-aware mixed estimator that interpolates between maximum likelihood and empirical Bayes shrinkage, with a closed-form oracle mixing weight provably no worse than either at second order. It turns recent excess-MSE diagnostics into a design principle.

entry.title: The Spec Growth Engine: Spec-Anchored, Code-Coupled, Drift-Enforced Architecture for AI-Assisted Software Development

author.name: Hartwig Grabowski

entry.summary: The Spec Growth Engine is a framework for AI-assisted software development that uses a machine-readable spec graph, a context-scoping assembler, and drift enforcement to combat context explosion and silent spec-code drift in coding agents. It enforces alignment between specifications and code.

entry.title: Bridging Talk and Thought: Understanding Dialogue Dynamics Across Collaborative Problem-Solving Contexts

author.name: Zhengyuan Liu, Stella Xin Yin, Min-Yen Kan, Nancy F. Chen

entry.summary: This work presents a conceptual two-layer hierarchical coding framework for analyzing dialogue in collaborative problem-solving, integrating cognitive, non-cognitive, and metacognitive mechanisms across human-AI and multi-agent settings. It is validated across nine datasets spanning multiple contexts.

entry.title: Federated Hash Projected Latent Factor Learning

author.name: Jialan He

entry.summary: This work integrates hash learning into federated learning via federated hash-projected latent factor learning, transmitting compact binary codes to reduce communication overhead and privacy risk while improving binary-code representational capacity. It addresses limitations of real-valued gradient transmission.

entry.title: Stochastic Gradient Optimization with Model-Assisted Sampling

author.name: Jonne Pohjankukka, Jukka Heikkonen

entry.summary: This paper proposes a model-assisted sampling framework that reinterprets mini-batch stochastic gradients through survey sampling theory, treating the dataset as a fixed finite population and gradients as sample-based estimates. The aim is to reduce gradient variance and bridge ML optimization with classical sampling methods.

entry.title: A Multi-Fidelity Convolutional Autoencoder-Transfer Learning Framework for Guided-Wave-Based Damage Diagnosis Using Large Simulated and Limited Experimental Datasets

author.name: Santosh Kapuria, Abhishek

entry.summary: This study presents a multi-fidelity convolutional autoencoder transfer-learning framework combining large physics-based simulation data with limited experimental measurements for guided-wave structural health monitoring. It enables accurate damage localization and sizing in plate-like structures with piezoelectric transducers.

entry.title: State-Specific Respiratory Signatures for Affective and Stress Recognition: Interpretable Respiratory Markers, Autocorrelation Lags, and Compact CNN Models

author.name: Andrei Velichko, Mehmet Tahir Huyut

entry.summary: This work reframes respiratory-signal-based stress and affective-state recognition as a joint predictive and explanatory problem, combining compact 1D-CNNs with physically grouped handcrafted respiratory signatures on the WESAD dataset. It identifies which interpretable respiratory properties and autocorrelation lags separate stress from non-stress states.

entry.title: Compiler-Driven Approximation Tuning for Hyperdimensional Computing

author.name: Xavier Routh, Abdul Rafae Noor, Akash Kothari, Zheyu Li, Mahbod Afarin, Tajana Rosing, Vikram Adve

entry.summary: Presents a compiler-driven approach to automatically tune approximation in Hyperdimensional Computing workloads across heterogeneous hardware including CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, and in-memory technologies. Exploits HDC's intrinsic noise tolerance for performance gains.

entry.title: Adversarial Diffusion Across Modalities: A Fusion Survey of Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluation for Text, Vision, and Vision-Language Models

author.name: Abrar Alotaibi, Moataz Ahmed

entry.summary: A meta-research survey integrating four disconnected adversarial-evaluation tracks (diffusion attacks on text/LLMs, image classifiers, VLM jailbreaks, and diffusion purification defenses) into a unified taxonomy and research agenda. Highlights denoising diffusion as a shared generative mechanism across communities.

entry.title: Methane-Plume Segmentation From Hyperspectral Satellite Imagery Via Multimodal Deep Learning

author.name: Brayan Quintero, Jeferson Acevedo, Samuel Traslavi\~na, Hoover Rueda-Chac\'on

entry.summary: Proposes a multimodal deep learning model with a feature-guided methane enhancement mechanism that injects physical methane cues into transformer RGB representations for plume segmentation in hyperspectral satellite imagery. Outperforms SOTA on MPDataset at lower computational cost.

entry.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction

author.name: Jinhyung Lee, Haeun Yun, Siwon Kim, Gihyun Baek, Sungho Moon, Sehyun Hwang, Sunghoon Im

entry.summary: RobOralScan presents what the authors claim is the first RL-based pipeline for robotic automatic intraoral scanning, using a geometric memory-based observation space that accumulates partial scans into a tri-state representation. It aims to automate labor-intensive dental scanning with limited field-of-view. The geometric memory representation for active scanning is a notable application-specific design.

entry.title: Assert, don't describe: Linguistic features that shift LLM reasoning about animal welfare

author.name: Jasmine Brazilek, Harper Dunn

entry.summary: Examines how ten linguistic features in fine-tuning data shift Llama-3.2-1B's reasoning about animal welfare, finding assertive certainty and moral vocabulary push toward stronger pro-welfare stances while hedging weakens them. Demonstrates how stylistic choices in training text influence model values.

entry.title: From Structure to Synergy: A Survey of Vision-Language Perception Paradigm Evolution in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Haoxiang Sun, Tao Wang, Li Yuan, Jian Zhao, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic survey of vision-language perception in multimodal LLMs from a unified perspective treating vision and language as inseparable, tracing the paradigm shift toward perception-centric intelligence. References O-series and R-series models.

entry.title: Retrieval-Warmed Energy-Based Reasoning: A Five-Arm Ablation Methodology for Diffusion-as-Inference on Structured Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Libo Sun, Po-Wei Harn, Zewei Zhang, Peixiong He, Xiao Qin

entry.summary: Studies retrieval-warmed energy-based reasoning (an IRED diffusion model with Hopfield trajectory memory) and contributes a five-arm ablation methodology to disentangle class-prior bias, stochastic warm-starting, and graph-aligned value reuse. Diagnoses which pipeline component drives gains on structured reasoning tasks.

entry.title: \textsc{DiARC}: Distinguishing Positive and Negative Samples Helps Improving ARC-like Reasoning Ability of Large Language Models

author.name: Yuxuan Yang, Feiyang Li, Yile Wang

entry.summary: Proposes DiARC, arguing that solving ARC-like abstraction-reasoning tasks requires distinguishing positive from negative samples rather than only positive-sample supervision, improving open-source LLM reasoning. Moves beyond pure data-augmentation approaches.

entry.title: AIGP: An LLM-Based Framework for Long-Term Value Alignment in E-Commerce Pricing

author.name: Chennan Ma, Yanning Zhang, Siqi Hong, Xiuchong Wang, Fei Xiao, Keping Yang

entry.summary: AIGP is an LLM-based framework for e-commerce dynamic pricing that integrates domain knowledge and a Long-Term Value Estimator trained via offline RL to align decisions with long-term business objectives like GMV and ROI. It uses supervised fine-tuning for efficient deployment.

entry.title: On-board Remote-Sensing Foundation Models for Unsupervised Change Detection of Disaster Events

author.name: S. Ram\'irez-Gallego

entry.summary: This work presents an unsupervised change detection method using remote-sensing foundation models with a ResNet plus FPN architecture for on-board disaster monitoring, enabling satellites to autonomously trigger captures without expensive labels. It optimizes limited onboard power and compute.

entry.title: Revisiting Action Factorization for Complex Action Spaces

author.name: Timothy Flavin, Sandip Sen

entry.summary: This paper revisits action factorization for hybrid discrete-continuous action spaces (e.g., steering+signaling, aim+fire) and notes that standard RL benchmarks use uniform action configurations while hybrid benchmarks are heavyweight or archival. It systematically compares factorization methods for complex action spaces.

entry.title: RecallRisk-BERT: A Multi-Task Framework for Post-Report Medical Device Recall Triage

author.name: Ali Semih Atalay, Sevgi Yigit-Sert

entry.summary: RecallRisk-BERT is a multi-task framework for post-report medical device recall triage that jointly predicts recall severity and root-cause categories from 54,165 FDA recall records spanning 2002-2025. It compares classical and boosting models before introducing the BERT-based multi-task model.

entry.title: Listening Like a Judge: A Music-Aware Framework for Automatic Singing Performance Evaluation

author.name: Neelam Saini, Sourav Ghosh

entry.summary: MusicJudge is a modality-guided framework for automatic singing quality assessment that performs block-aligned multimodal analysis coupling lyric correctness with pitch-rhythm fidelity. It detects semantically meaningful lyric blocks via multi-signal matching to handle melisma, vibrato, and tempo elasticity.

entry.title: HierBias: Context-Conditioned Hierarchical Media Bias Detection with Multi-Task Type Classification

author.name: Kaining Li, Ruichen Yan, Yuxin Dong

entry.summary: Presents HierBias, a hierarchical context-conditioned media bias detector that models document context and proves theoretically that leveraging inter-sentence context reduces Bayes error. Adds multi-task type classification of bias.

entry.title: Term-Centric Hierarchy Induction from Heterogeneous Corpora

author.name: Elena Senger, Yuri Campbell, Jan-Peter Bergmann, Rob van der Goot, Barbara Plank

entry.summary: Proposes a term-centric framework for inducing hierarchical taxonomies from heterogeneous corpora by mapping documents into a shared concept space via automatic term extraction. Scales to massive collections for policy and innovation mapping.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Source Cognitive Taskonomy:Multi-Source Task Relations through fMRI Transfer Learning

author.name: Junfeng Xia, Wendu Li, Mengjiao Zhang, Jie Guo

entry.summary: Extends fMRI cognitive taskonomy from single-source to multi-source transfer across 23 Human Connectome Project task states using masked reconstruction and Boolean Integer Programming for budget-constrained task allocation. Trains over 1,100 task-specific and transfer models.

entry.title: LayersReg: A Layer-by-Layer Progressive Regressor for Reliable Intraoperative 3D/2D Registration

author.name: Xiyuan Wang, Zhenchao Wang, Xinran Chen, Junkai Liu, Chuan Chen, Feng Yin

entry.summary: Proposes LayersReg, a layer-by-layer progressive regression paradigm for intraoperative 3D/2D registration that endows the model with 3D anatomical awareness rather than memory-driven pose retrieval. Aims to improve generalization over existing learnable registration methods.

entry.title: Depth-Semantic Alignment and Affinity-Guided Fusion for Structured Radar Point Cloud Generation

author.name: Amjad Hussain, Xin Qiu, Fuyuan Ai, Yuchen Tan, Zecheng Li, Chunyi Song, Wenjie Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a vision-radar fusion method to generate denser, structurally complete radar point clouds by using image semantics for spatial alignment and sparse completion. The generated point clouds improve downstream object detection and tracking.

entry.title: Multi-modality Image Fusion under Adverse Weather: Mask-Guided Feature Restoration and Interaction

author.name: Xilai Li, Xiaosong Li, Haishu Tan, Tao Ye, Huafeng Li, Hongbin Wang

entry.summary: This proposes a mask-guided multi-modality image fusion method that jointly performs feature restoration and cross-modal interaction under adverse weather, using a pseudo ground truth strategy and a mask generation mechanism. It targets robust scene representation in degraded conditions.

entry.title: OSC2Runner: OpenSCENARIO 2.x Compliant High-Fidelity AV Simulation in CARLA

author.name: Thoshitha Gamage, Lasanthi Gamage

entry.summary: OSC2Runner is the first orchestration framework that natively maps the OpenSCENARIO v2.x domain-specific language to the CARLA simulator via a multi-pass transpiler architecture, avoiding spatiotemporal drift and kinematic snapping from adapting legacy v1.x interpreters. It treats scenario translation as a compilation pipeline.

entry.title: Know2Guess: A Contamination-Aware Multi-Zone Benchmark for Knowledge-Boundary Evaluation in Large Language Models

author.name: Renwei Meng, Bowen Zhang, Jian Wang, Xican Wang, Haoyi Wu, Xuanyan Qiu, Shengan Yang

entry.summary: Introduces a contamination-aware, multi-zone benchmark of 1,200 items across five domains to evaluate when LLMs should answer versus abstain, distinguishing supported knowledge from unsupported guessing. It tests FLAN-T5, Qwen2.5, and Llama-3 under locked answer-or-abstain prompts with dual parsing strategies.

entry.title: Reducing Redundancy in Whole-Slide Image Patching for Scalable Indexing and Retrieval

author.name: Jialiang Geng, Ghazal Alabtah, Saghir Alfasly, Wataru Uegami, H. R. Tizhoosh

entry.summary: Proposes ARReST, a redundancy-reduction strategy for whole-slide image patching to reduce storage demands while preserving retrieval accuracy for digital pathology indexing and RAG workflows. Addresses scalability and storage cost barriers in clinical imaging.

entry.title: Evaluation-Strategy Gap in Fault Diagnosis of Deep Learning Programs

author.name: Sigma Jahan

entry.summary: Investigates the gap between within-program cross-validation and cross-program deployment in fault diagnosis of deep learning training programs, using DynFault, a corpus of 5,542 fault-injected traces from 38 real programs. Finds a 0.190 drop in balanced accuracy when generalizing to unseen programs.

entry.title: HiLSVA: Design and Evaluation of a Human-in-the-Loop Agentic System for Scientific Visualization

author.name: Kuangshi Ai, Patrick Phuoc Do, Chaoli Wang

entry.summary: Presents HiLSVA, a human-in-the-loop agentic system for scientific visualization with a plan-first multi-agent architecture, stepwise provenance tracking, learn-at-test-time adaptation, and sandboxed execution. Reframes SciVis agents to prioritize human analytical control over full autonomy.

entry.title: Inverse Design of Compact and Wideband Inverted Doherty Power Amplifiers Using Deep Learning

author.name: Han Zhou, Haojie Chang, David Widen, Christian Fager

entry.summary: This paper presents a deep-learning-assisted inverse design methodology for compact wideband inverted Doherty power amplifiers, jointly using CNNs and genetic algorithms to generate pixelated combiner networks. A fabricated GaN HEMT prototype validates the approach with measured efficiency results.

entry.title: State Representation Matters in Deep Reinforcement Learning: Application to Energy Trading

author.name: Jesper Klicks, Sander Vr\v{z}ina, Vincent Fran\c{c}ois-Lavet

entry.summary: This paper studies how state representation choices affect deep RL performance in energy trading, comparing absolute, relative, forecast, and combined market features within a fixed Double DQN agent on a pumped-storage arbitrage environment. It isolates feature design as the key variable.

entry.title: Application of LLMs to Threat Assessment of Foreign Peacekeeping Missions

author.name: Gerhard Backfried, Christian Schmidt, Diego Pilutti, Michael Suker

entry.summary: This work applies LLMs to threat assessment for foreign peacekeeping missions, combining an interdisciplinary risk model with OSINT-based media collection and LLM-supported threat extraction, demonstrated on the EU Monitoring Mission in Georgia. Evaluation shows high agreement with human judgment on core threat aspects.

entry.title: Topology-Informed Neural Networks for Flood Detection in Optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar Imagery

author.name: Sophia Li, Max Zhao, Raghu G. Raj, Tianyu Chen

entry.summary: This work proposes topology-informed neural networks for flood detection in optical and SAR satellite imagery, building on the SEN12-FLOOD dataset to improve detection where cloud cover obscures optical imagery. It incorporates topological features for environmental hazard monitoring.

entry.title: Batch-Invariant Spectral Intelligence for Robust and Explainable Insect Authentication

author.name: Majharulislam Babor, Giacomo Rossi, Annalisa Altavilla, Oliver Schl\"uter, Marina M. -C. H\"ohne

entry.summary: The Batch-Invariant Spectral Network (BISN) combines a learnable Savitzky-Golay-initialized preprocessing module with entropy-regularized adversarial training to authenticate edible insect species via near-infrared spectroscopy across unseen production batches. It targets robustness to batch-to-batch spectral variation for food-supply regulatory compliance.

entry.title: Neural Speaker Diarization via Multilingual Training: Evaluation on Low-Resource Nepali-Hindi Speech

author.name: Samip Neupane, Sandesh Pokhrel, Sandesh Pyakurel, Basanta Joshi

entry.summary: This paper investigates neural speaker diarization for low-resource Nepali-Hindi speech via multilingual training, comparing EEND with encoder-decoder attractors and Perceiver-based attractors. It evaluates whether end-to-end diarization can transfer to underrepresented languages with scarce annotated data.

entry.title: Closing the Quality Gap in Low-Resource Text-to-Speech: LoRA Fine-Tuning of VoxCPM2 for Khmer and Korean

author.name: Phannet Pov, Sovandara Chhoun, Hyun Woo Park, Wan-Sup Cho, Saksonita Khoeurn

entry.summary: Closes the TTS quality gap for low-resource Khmer and Korean by applying a single zero-initialized LoRA adapter to the 2.4B VoxCPM2 model trained jointly on both languages. Achieves substantial MOS improvements from a small shared corpus.

entry.title: How Surprising Is Historical Italian to Language Models? Tokenization Tax, Comprehension Tax, and a Simple Mitigation

author.name: Maria Levchenko

entry.summary: Proposes a diagnostic framework decomposing historical-language difficulty for LLMs into tokenization cost, surprisal, semantic robustness, and context sensitivity, evaluated on 17th- and 19th-century Italian. Offers a simple mitigation for the resulting tokenization and comprehension taxes.

entry.title: Beyond Aesthetics: Quantifying Information Loss in Turbid Scenes

author.name: Vasiliki Ismiroglou, Stefan H. Bengtson, Tasos Benos, Thomas B. Moeslund, Malte Pedersen

entry.summary: Introduces the Turbid Underwater Baseline dataset of 1,320 real extreme-turbidity images with 16,000+ ground-truth masks and PCD, a contrast-invariant metric quantifying structural information loss. Shows PCD correlates with segmentation performance better than synthetic turbidity.

entry.title: Temporally Consistent Label Interpolation for Robust Surgical Multi-Task Learning under Challenging Conditions

author.name: Garam Kim, Juyoun Park

entry.summary: Proposes FAROS, a flow-guided label interpolation framework that propagates sparse keyframe spatial annotations across frames to balance dense temporal and sparse spatial supervision in surgical multi-task learning. Addresses annotation granularity mismatch under challenging conditions.

entry.title: Scalable Operator Learning via Nystr\"om Approximation With Denoising Applications

author.name: Naveen Gupta, Vaibhav Silmana, S. Sivananthan

entry.summary: This paper studies Nyström subsampling for vector-valued regression in vector-valued RKHS, proposing a scalable operator learning algorithm that handles functional outputs and establishing minimax-optimal convergence rates under general source conditions. It applies the framework to denoising. The generalized source conditions extending beyond classical frameworks are a solid theoretical contribution.

entry.title: Dream machine -- the next creative economy

author.name: Peter Woodbridge, John J. O'Hare

entry.summary: Analyzes the structural transformation of creative industries under generative AI using 374 primary sources, introducing the Human-AI Agency Continuum and the 'slop ceiling' concept whereby AI content stays at 1-3% of streams despite being 44% of uploads. Offers an empirical framework on creative economy disruption.

entry.title: Active Adversarial Perturbation-driven Associative Memory Retrieval for RGB-Event Visual Object Tracking

author.name: Xiao Wang, Xufeng Lou, Zikang Yan, Lan Chen, Sibao Chen, Yaowei Wang, Yonghong Tian, Jin Tang

entry.summary: Presents APRTrack, a hierarchical perturbation-and-retrieval framework for RGB-Event visual object tracking robust to partial target missing and modal degradation, using active adversarial perturbations and associative memory retrieval. Targets harsh real-world conditions with occlusion and clutter.

entry.title: Multipath Adaptive Gated Bottleneck Latent ODE with Raman Data Fusion for Cell Culture Process Forecasting

author.name: Johnny Peng, Thanh Tung Khuat, Ellen Otte, Katarzyna Musial, Bogdan Gabrys

entry.summary: Proposes a Gated Bottleneck Latent ODE with multi-path just-in-time fine-tuning and Raman data fusion for forecasting mammalian cell-culture bioprocesses from sparse, irregularly sampled measurements. Enables early multi-day forecasts to guide intervention in biopharmaceutical manufacturing.

entry.title: Quantization in Federated Learning: Methods, Challenges and Future Directions

author.name: Farwa Ikram, Dipanwita Thakur, Antonella Guzzo, Giancarlo Fortino

entry.summary: This survey provides the first federated-learning-centric systematic review of quantization, organizing methods around FL-specific dimensions like client heterogeneity, aggregation consistency, non-IID robustness, and privacy/hardware co-optimization. It introduces a novel taxonomy to address communication and computation bottlenecks.

entry.title: ConvMemory v3: A Validity Context Layer for Conversational Memory via Target-Conditioned Relation Verification

author.name: Taiheng Pan

entry.summary: Presents ConvMemory v3, a validity context layer for conversational memory that detects when retrieved memories are outdated using target-conditioned relation verification and a dual-evidence gate. Surfaces update evidence to handle superseded information.

entry.title: Layered Outer-Loop Control for Disturbance-Robust Multi-Waypoint UAV Arrival

author.name: Runfeng Ling

entry.summary: This presents a layered terminal-control architecture for disturbance-robust multi-waypoint UAV position regulation, with staged evaluation across PyBullet, PX4/Gazebo, and hardware. It separates smooth approach generation, persistent-bias compensation, and supervised near-target terminal regulation.

entry.title: UAV-MapFusion: RTK-Aligned Uncertainty-Aware Coarse-to-Fine Multi-Session UAV Mapping

author.name: Feng Pan, Chunran Zheng, Bing Xue, Yukang Cui, Jiayu Wen, Zhiyu Chen, Wei Wang

entry.summary: UAV-MapFusion proposes an uncertainty-aware, RTK-aligned coarse-to-fine system for merging multi-session UAV point cloud maps, using a scene graph for initial alignment and RTK observations to suppress long-range drift while preserving local geometry. It targets large-scale aerial mapping constrained by flight endurance. The contribution is a solid but specialized mapping pipeline.

entry.title: Dot-Flik: A Scalable Edge AI Architecture for Distributed Insect Monitoring

author.name: Mattia Consani, Denisa-Andreea Constantinescu, {\AA}se H{\aa}tveit, Titus Venverloo, Fabio Duarte, Carlo Ratti, David Atienza

entry.summary: Presents Dot-Flik, a scalable edge-AI architecture for distributed insect monitoring using motion-informed frame filtering and a hierarchical IoT design that reduces compute and bypasses cloud reliance. Targets cost-effective ecological monitoring of insect declines.

entry.title: Beyond Logical Forms: LLM-Extracted Patterns for Fallacy Classification

author.name: Eleni Papadopulos, Firoj Alam, Giovanni Da San Martino

entry.summary: This work uses LLMs to inductively extract reasoning patterns combining abstract logical structures and linguistic cues for classifying logical fallacies. It shows statistically significant improvements over zero-shot baselines across multiple LLMs.

entry.title: Transformer-Based Classification of Bacterial Raman Spectra with LOOCV

author.name: Jamile Mohammad Jafari, Thomas Bocklitz

entry.summary: This study evaluates a transformer-based classifier for bacterial Raman spectra using nested leave-one-replicate-out cross-validation on 5,417 single-cell spectra from six species, comparing against PCA/ICA combined with LDA, SVM, and Random Forest. The transformer consistently outperforms conventional pipelines across independent test replicates.

entry.title: Geometric Gradient Rectification for Safe Open-Set Semi-Supervised Learning

author.name: Jiahe Chen, Qian Shao, Qiyuan Chen, Jiaying He, Jintai Chen, Jian Wu, Hongxia Xu

entry.summary: Introduces Geometric Gradient Rectification for open-set semi-supervised learning, shifting from sample filtering to gradient-level control using the supervised gradient as an anchor. Aims to prevent harmful auxiliary gradients while retaining informative hard samples.

entry.title: LLM-Based Examination of Eligibility Criteria from Securities Prospectuses at the German Central Bank

author.name: Serhii Hamotskyi, Akash Kumar Gautam, Christian H\"anig

entry.summary: First case study applying LLMs to verify securities-collateral eligibility against legal criteria in lengthy bilingual prospectuses at the German Central Bank, shifting from NER to generative information extraction. Addresses OCR noise and rigid span constraints.

entry.title: Learning Adversarial Augmentation Policies for Robust Garlic Seedling Detection

author.name: Soeun Lee, Chanho Kim, Yeji Kang, YoungKi Hong, Byeongkeun Kang

entry.summary: This work learns adversarial augmentation policies for robust garlic seedling detection under severe, heterogeneous outdoor illumination, and introduces a new garlic seedling dataset for ground-based precision agriculture. It avoids inference-time overhead from extra enhancement modules.

entry.title: A Closed-Form 4-DoF Inter-Robot Pose Estimator using Bearing-only Measurements

author.name: Qixin De, Ao Zhuang, Yechen Zhang, Zhuozhou Qian, Danping Zou

entry.summary: Proposes a closed-form 4-DoF inter-robot pose estimator using bearing-only measurements, relaxing nonlinear rotation constraints and analyzing observability degeneracy. It targets cooperative multi-robot localization with minimal infrastructure and bandwidth. The closed-form solution and observability analysis are solid but the contribution is narrow.

entry.title: Exploring Generalization in NLA's

author.name: Kamesh R

entry.summary: A LessWrong post reproducing and extending Anthropic's work on natural language autoencoders (activation verbalizers and reconstructors), describing the author's replication using FineWeb activations and external labeler checkpoints. It explores generalization of these interpretability components. The post offers hands-on replication insight relevant to activation interpretation and steering.

entry.title: AI #174: You’re It

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's regular AI roundup (#174) covering recent developments including the open model GLM-5.2, Anthropic's Claude Tag Slack integration, Dean Ball joining OpenAI policy, and ongoing debates, plus capability and economics notes. It aggregates and editorializes on a wide range of current AI news. As a curation it is useful for situational awareness but is commentary rather than original research.

entry.title: Reducing Conversational Escalation in Large Language Model Dialogue with Nonviolent Communication Constraints

author.name: Zhixing Sun, Shenghe Xu, Tao Li

entry.summary: Explores whether lightweight prompt-level constraints derived from Nonviolent Communication can reduce conversational escalation in emotionally charged LLM dialogues. Reframes safety beyond toxic content toward de-escalation behaviors.

entry.title: From Lexicon to AI: A Structured-Data Pipeline for Specialized Conversational Systems in Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Siddhant Hitesh Mantri, Dhara Gorasiya, Malhar Kulkarni, Pushpak Bhattacharya

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline that converts Hindi WordNet into 1.25 million instruction-response pairs to fine-tune a 12B model via LoRA with 4-bit quantization, demonstrating structured lexical databases as foundations for low-resource conversational AI. Evaluated through a Hindi language-learning chatbot.

entry.title: SpaceRipple: Lightweight Semantic Delivery for Mission-Oriented LEO Earth Observation Satellite Networks

author.name: Ziyi Yang, Hao Yuan, Yunxiang Yi, Wenbo Wang, Xing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes SpaceRipple, a lightweight framework for mission-oriented semantic delivery in LEO Earth-observation satellite networks, using adaptive compression and on-board edge processing to deliver task-relevant semantic information rather than full raw imagery under limited bandwidth. Coordinates compression across sensing and edge-computing satellites.

entry.title: Understanding Domain-Aware Distribution Alignment in Budgeted Entity Matching

author.name: Nicholas Pulsone, Gregory Goren, Roee Shraga

entry.summary: This paper investigates the state-of-the-art low-resource domain-aware entity matching method BEACON, studying how its performance varies under different data constraints, supervision levels, and algorithmic choices. It provides targeted experiments to understand distribution alignment behavior.

entry.title: Graph Neural Networks Applications Across Domains: All Insights You Need

author.name: Abderaouf Bahi

entry.summary: This is a broad survey organizing graph neural networks around a single design space, deriving spectral and spatial formulations from shared principles and connecting expressivity to the Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy. It examines twelve application domains to identify where graph structure justifies its computational cost.

entry.title: Enabling self-supervised learned primal dual with Noise2Inverse

author.name: Antti S\"allinen, Siiri Rautio, Santeri Kaupinm\"aki, Andreas Hauptmann

entry.summary: Extends the Noise2Inverse self-supervised framework to the Learned Primal-Dual algorithm for CT reconstruction without ground-truth images. Targets low-dose and sparse-angle settings where clean references are unavailable.

entry.title: Zero-shot Tweet-Level Stance Detection Enhanced by External Knowledge and Reflective Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Yiju Huang, Wenxian Wang, Lijun Zhou, Rui Tang, Xiao Lan, Tao Zhang, Haizhou Wang

entry.summary: Proposes zero-shot tweet-level stance detection enhanced by external knowledge and reflective chain-of-thought, and constructs the first Japanese multi-topic tweet stance dataset. Addresses context sparsity and distinguishing neutral from irrelevant stances.

entry.title: Computer Vision for MOBA Analytics: A Dataset and Baseline for Visibility Analysis in Dota 2

author.name: Ricardo da Rocha Carvalho, Elo\'isa Oliveira, Luiz Bernardo Martins Kummer, Emerson Cabrera Paraiso, Rayson Laroca

entry.summary: This introduces Dota2-Vis, a video-based dataset of 288 Full HD videos from The International 2025 with annotated minimaps, plus a baseline pipeline for visibility analysis in professional Dota 2 matches. It enables vision-based MOBA analytics beyond structured game data.

entry.title: Unsupervised Memory-Enhanced Video Transformers: Obstacle Detection for Autonomous Agricultural Rover

author.name: Th\'eo Biardeau (XLIM-ASALI, UFR SFA), Anne-Sophie Capelle-Laiz\'e (UP, XLIM-ASALI, XLIM-ASALI), Salwan Alwan (UFR SFA), David Helbert (UFR SFA)

entry.summary: Introduces VMTAD, a fully unsupervised video memory transformer for real-time obstacle/anomaly detection on autonomous agricultural rovers, addressing failures of LiDAR below plant canopies and supervised methods on unseen obstacles. Designed for dynamic moving-camera scenes.

entry.title: From Clicks to Intent: Cross-Platform Session Embeddings with LLM-Distilled Taxonomy for Financial Services Recommendations

author.name: Dianjing Fan, Yao Li, Kyaw Hpone Myint, Dwipam Katariya, Alexandre G. R. Day, Pranab Mohanty, Giri Iyengar

entry.summary: Proposes cross-platform session embeddings using LLM-distilled taxonomy to bridge pre-login web browsing intent and authenticated in-app behavior for financial services recommendations. Addresses cross-channel entity resolution challenges.

entry.title: AnySimLite: A Lightweight Few-Shot Similarity Encoder for On-Device Speech-Adjacent Classification

author.name: Sourav Ghosh, Yash Bhatia, Keshav Goyal, Sahil Singh Bagri, Mohamed Akram Ulla Shariff, Saravana Balaji Shanmugam

entry.summary: Proposes AnySimLite, a lightweight few-shot similarity encoder combining word- and character-level channels to solve multiple on-device speech-adjacent classification tasks via a single text-similarity formulation. Targets memory-constrained edge deployment.

entry.title: Context Recycling for Long-Horizon LLM Inference

author.name: Derek Thomas

entry.summary: Presents ContextForge, a context-recycling system that maintains task-relevant info across long conversational turns via structured query generation, external memory retrieval, and controlled synthesis. Evaluated on a 15-turn multi-turn reasoning benchmark for healthcare queries.

entry.title: Privacy-Aware Agent Collaboration for Dynamic VR Slice Management in 6G SD-RAN

author.name: Khaled M. Naguib, Soumaya Cherkaoui, Mahmoud M. Elmesalawy, Ahmed M. Abd El-Haleem, Ibrahim I. Ibrahim

entry.summary: Proposes a mobility-driven, privacy-aware multi-agent RL framework for VR network slice management in 6G SD-RAN, using mobility prediction and an information-bottleneck encoder for secure agent collaboration. Reports up to 34% throughput improvement in simulation.

entry.title: Statistical and Structural Approaches to Algorithmic Fairness

author.name: Antonio Ferrara

entry.summary: A thesis on statistical and structural approaches to algorithmic fairness, arguing that early fairness mitigation strategies relied on fragile simplifications inadequate for complex socio-technical environments. Develops more robust framings of fairness.

entry.title: MLFFM-SegDiff: A Multi-Level Feature Fusion Diffusion Model for Skin Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Jingjun Gu, Chaojie Shen, Yifeng Cao, Wei Zhang, Yiliu Li, Aobo Fan

entry.summary: MLFFM-SegDiff is a multi-level feature fusion diffusion model for skin lesion segmentation that addresses blurred boundaries and artifacts in dermoscopic images. It improves cross-level feature interaction and boundary detail recovery.

entry.title: Comparing BERT Sentence-Pair Classification and Few-Shot LLM Prompting for Detecting Threat and Solution Framing in German Climate News

author.name: Raven Adam, David Maier, Marie Kogler

entry.summary: Systematically compares fine-tuned BERT sentence-pair classification against few-shot prompting with Llama 4 Maverick for detecting threat versus solution framing in German climate news. Provides a practical methods comparison for applied media analysis.

entry.title: Compositionality and the lexicon in evolutionary semantics

author.name: Fausto Carcassi

entry.summary: Presents an evolutionary semantics framework where lexical meanings and a composition function co-evolve under pressures for simplicity and accuracy, applied to quantifier meaning. Finds the conservativity universal emerges as an efficient system-wide abstraction.

entry.title: RIS-Assisted Proactive Handover for Reliable mmWave Wireless Networks

author.name: Alaa Adnan, Mohammad Al-Quraan, Ahmed Zoha, M. Majid Butt, Sami Muhaidat, Muhammad Ali Imran, Marco Di Renzo, Lina Mohjazi

entry.summary: This proposes a RIS-assisted proactive handover approach for mmWave networks that optimizes the number of allocated reconfigurable intelligent surface elements to balance processing complexity and link quality under handover timing constraints. It uses vision-aided communications to mitigate line-of-sight blockages.

entry.title: Random Walk on B\'ezier Curves for Global Optimization

author.name: Jinpeng Wang, Xingguo Xu, Yujing Sun, Jiguang Yu, Kaichen Ouyang, Yuansheng Gao

entry.summary: Bezier Walk Evolution is a geometry-driven metaheuristic optimization framework that reformulates evolutionary search as adaptive trajectory construction using Bezier curves with a distance-aware random walk. Varying curve order enables a smooth transition from global exploration to local exploitation.

entry.title: Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data

author.name: Catarina P. Loureiro, M. Ros\'ario Oliveira, Paula Brito, Lina Oliveira

entry.summary: This paper extends an outlier-detection framework based on the Interval Minimum Covariance Determinant estimator with Shapley-value explanations for interval-valued data, deriving a closed-form Shapley value for the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance. It enables fine-grained decomposition of outlyingness into centers, ranges, and cross-terms. The closed-form attribution for interval data is a neat but niche statistical contribution.

entry.title: Alignment & Succession: The Ideology of Successionism

author.name: L Rudolf L

entry.summary: L Rudolf L's essay analyzes successionism, the ideology (named by Andrew Critch) that humanity should be willing to be replaced by AI, tracing examples from Silicon Valley figures and situating it among debates about goodness, risk, and governance. It is a substantive intellectual examination of an emerging ideology relevant to AI alignment discourse. The piece is conceptual rather than empirical.

entry.title: Geometric Fairness-Aware Routing for Federated Edge Networks

author.name: Ratun Rahman

entry.summary: Introduces Geo-FairFed, a routing framework combining hyperbolic graph neural networks and federated optimization to enforce fairness across edge nodes in 6G networks using curvature-regularized objectives. Learns topology-aware representations on negatively-curved manifolds.

entry.title: Charting the Growth of Social-Physical HRI (spHRI): A Systematic Review Pipeline Augmented by Small Language Models

author.name: Mayumi Mohan, Ju-Hung Chen, Alexis E. Block

entry.summary: Evaluates whether small language models (<1.5B params) can assist title/abstract screening for a large systematic review of social-physical human-robot interaction. Finds SLMs augment but don't match human reviewers, while operating locally and faster, identifying papers reviewers missed.

entry.title: FBK's Long-form SpeechLLMs for IWSLT 2026 Instruction Following

author.name: Zhihang Xie, Marco Gaido, Sara Papi, Matteo Negri, Luisa Bentivogli

entry.summary: Describes FBK's submission to the IWSLT 2026 instruction-following task using SpeechLLMs for short- and long-form speech, exploring segmentation methods and introducing the HIFS metric for unstable long-form generation. Finds fixed 30-second segmentation most robust.

entry.title: The Governance Inversion Hypothesis: Why More AI Regulation May Produce Less Organisational Control

author.name: Victor Frimpong

entry.summary: Introduces the Governance Inversion Hypothesis, arguing that increasing AI regulation and formalization may paradoxically reduce organizations' operational control over AI systems. Draws on institutional and accountability theory.

entry.title: Multiscale Exit-Join Dynamics: Tactical Consensus and Strategic Coalition Formation

author.name: Quanyan Zhu

entry.summary: Develops a multiscale game-theoretic model coupling strategic coalition exit-and-join decisions with tactical within-coalition consensus dynamics, characterizing joint equilibria, polarization, and cognitive barriers. A fast-slow architecture with DeGroot-style consensus.

entry.title: Utilizing Cognitive Signals Generated during Human Reading to Enhance Keyphrase Extraction from Microblogs

author.name: Xinyi Yan, Yingyi Zhang, Chengzhi Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates whether EEG signals can complement eye-tracking signals to improve keyphrase extraction from noisy microblog text, using the ZuCo cognitive corpus. Incorporates cognitive features into AKE models.

entry.title: DanceDuo: Bridging Human Movement and AI Choreography

author.name: Gia-Cat Bui-Le, Tuong-Vy Truong-Thuy, Hai-Dang Nguyen, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: DanceDuo is a diffusion-based platform that generates AI-choreographed dance synchronized with various music genres and integrates pose estimation to let users compare their performances with AI sequences. It aims to encourage dance practice through interactive comparison.

entry.title: RoboTales: ROBOTic Anthropomorphic LEarning Systems

author.name: Andrew Chen, Ju-Hung Chen, Phurinat Pinyomit, Alexis E. Block

entry.summary: RoboTales is a low-cost robotic storytelling system that animates narratives using expressive sock puppetry on a Baxter robot, synchronizing narration, gestures, and mouth movements. A pilot study found puppet-based storytelling improved engagement and story recall over gesture-only mode.

entry.title: Data-Driven Duration Management -- Term Structure Forecasting Using Machine Learning

author.name: Tobias Lausser, Joao Eduardo Vuolo, Rudi Zagst
